title: Sarvavedāntasiddhāntasārasaṅgraha — Complete Five-Part Reader
subtitle: A summary of Vedānta in five parts

sections.title: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
You are Only that Ultimate Reality

units.label: Verse 1
units.deva:
अखण्डानन्द-सन्दोहो वन्दनाद् यस्य जायते।
गोविन्दं तम् अहं वन्दे चिदानन्द-तनुं गुरुम्॥
units.translation: By bowing to whom an abundance of undivided bliss arises, I bow to that Govinda, the teacher whose form is consciousness-bliss.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: Invocation By salutation to whom one attains the consciousness of undivided bliss, to Govinda, the Guru, who is the embodiment of pure consciousness and bliss, I offer my salutation.
units.iast:
akhaṇḍānanda-sandoho vandanād yasya jāyate|
govindaṃ tam ahaṃ vande cidānanda-tanuṃ gurum||

units.label: Verse 2
units.deva:
अखण्डं सच्-चिद्-आनन्दम् अवाङ्मनस-गोचरम्।
आत्मानम् अखिलाधारम् आश्रयेऽभीष्ट-सिद्धये॥
units.translation: For the accomplishment of the desired end, I take refuge in the undivided Self: Being-Consciousness-Bliss, beyond speech and mind, the support of all.

gloss.en: for accomplishment of the desired end

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: I take shelter in the infinite Ātman, who is existence, knowledge and bliss absolute, who is beyond thought and expression, and who is the support of the universe, for the accomplishment of the desired object.
units.iast:
akhaṇḍaṃ sac-cid-ānandam avāṅmanasa-gocaram|
ātmānam akhilādhāram āśraye’bhīṣṭa-siddhaye||

units.label: Verse 3
units.deva:
यदालम्बो दरं हन्ति सतां प्रत्यूह-सम्भवम्।
तद् आलम्बे दयालम्बं लम्बोदर-पदाम्बुजम्॥
units.translation: The refuge of whom destroys the fear born of obstacles for the good: I take refuge in that compassionate support, the lotus feet of Lambodara.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: I seek shelter at the lotus feet of Gaṇeśa, the abode of kindness. If a virtuous person seeks shelter there, the fear that arises out of the obstacles is removed.
units.iast:
yadālambo daraṃ hanti satāṃ pratyūha-sambhavam|
tad ālambe dayālambaṃ lambodara-padāmbujam||

units.label: Verse 4
units.deva:
वेदान्त-शास्त्र-सिद्धान्त-सार-सङ्ग्रह उच्यते।
प्रेक्षावतां मुमुक्षूणां सुख-बोधोपपत्तये॥
units.translation: This is called a collection of the essence of Vedānta-śāstra doctrine, so that discerning seekers of liberation may understand easily.

gloss.en: collection of the essence of Vedānta-śāstra doctrine

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: This work is entitled, ‘The Quintessence of Vedānta’. It is specially written in order that it might be easily comprehended by the wise seekers after liberation.
units.iast:
vedānta-śāstra-siddhānta-sāra-saṅgraha ucyate|
prekṣāvatāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ sukha-bodhopapattaye||

units.label: Verse 5
units.deva:
अस्य शास्त्रानुसारित्वाद् अनुबन्ध-चतुष्टयम्।
यदेव मूलं शास्त्रस्य निर्दिष्टं तद् इहोच्यते॥
units.translation: Because this [work] follows śāstra, the four preliminaries, stated as the foundation of śāstra, are explained here.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: Textual connections Every Śāstra must deal with the four following constituents. This work which is in conformity with, and is based upon the Śāstras, follows the same principle.
units.iast:
asya śāstrānusāritvād anubandha-catuṣṭayam|
yadeva mūlaṃ śāstrasya nirdiṣṭaṃ tad ihocyate||

units.label: Verse 6
units.deva:
अधिकारी च विषयः सम्बन्धश्च प्रयोजनम्।
शास्त्रारम्भ-फलं प्राहुर् अनुबन्ध-चतुष्टयम्॥
units.translation: They call the qualified student, the subject, the relation, and the purpose the fourfold preliminaries and the fruit of beginning a śāstra.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: The preliminary considerations for the study of the Śāstras are the fitness of the person (adhikārī), the nature of the subject matter (viṣaya), how far a particular text is relevant (sambandha), and the benefit (prayojana) to be derived from it.
units.iast:
adhikārī ca viṣayaḥ sambandhaśca prayojanam|
śāstrārambha-phalaṃ prāhur anubandha-catuṣṭayam||

units.label: Verse 7
units.deva:
चतुर्भिः साधनैः सम्यक् सम्पन्नो युक्ति-दक्षिणः।
मेधावी पुरुषो विद्वान् अधिकार्यत्र सम्मतः॥
units.translation: Here the qualified person is considered to be intelligent and learned, fully endowed with the four means and skilled in reasoning.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: Whoever is endowed in full measure with the ‘four noble qualities,’ who is dexterous in reasoning, who is gifted with mental power, and who is learned is eminently fit to study this Śāstra.
units.iast:
caturbhiḥ sādhanaiḥ samyak sampanno yukti-dakṣiṇaḥ|
medhāvī puruṣo vidvān adhikāryatra sammataḥ||

units.label: Verse 8
units.deva:
विषयः शुद्ध-चैतन्यं जीव-ब्रह्मैक्य-लक्षणम्।
यत्रैव दृश्यते सर्व-वेदान्तानां समन्वयः॥
units.translation: The subject is pure consciousness, marked by the unity of the individual self and Brahman, in which alone the synthesis of all Vedānta is seen.

gloss.en: marked by the unity of the individual self and Brahman

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: The pure consciousness, that is marked by the unity that underlies Ātman and Brahman, forms the subject matter. It is at this point and at this point alone that there is a synthesis of all the Vedantic texts.
units.iast:
viṣayaḥ śuddha-caitanyaṃ jīva-brahmaikya-lakṣaṇam|
yatraiva dṛśyate sarva-vedāntānāṃ samanvayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 9
units.deva:
एतदैक्य-प्रमेयस्य प्रमाणस्यापि च श्रुतेः।
सम्बन्धः कथ्यते सद्भिर् बोध्य-बोधक-लक्षणः॥
units.translation: The wise describe the relation between this unity, which is to be known, and śruti, the means of knowledge, as that between what is to be known and what makes it known.

gloss.en: of the unity as the thing to be known
having the character of what is to be known and what makes it known

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: This unity has to be proved and the Śruti offers the proof of it. Therefore the unity to be proved stands in relation to the Śruti as what is taught in relation to that which teaches it.
units.iast:
etadaikya-prameyasya pramāṇasyāpi ca śruteḥ|
sambandhaḥ kathyate sadbhir bodhya-bodhaka-lakṣaṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 10
units.deva:
ब्रह्मात्मैकत्व-विज्ञानं सन्तः प्राहुः प्रयोजनम्।
येन निःशेष-संसार-बन्धात् सद्यः प्रमुच्यते॥
units.translation: The wise call knowledge of the unity of Brahman and the Self the purpose; by it one is immediately freed from the entire bond of saṃsāra.

gloss.en: knowledge of the unity of Brahman and the Self

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: The utility of knowledge lies, according to the learned, in the realization of this unity, the unity of Ātman and Brahman. By means of such realization one becomes freed immediately and once for all from the bonds of Saṃsāra, the cycle of birth and death.
units.iast:
brahmātmaikatva-vijñānaṃ santaḥ prāhuḥ prayojanam|
yena niḥśeṣa-saṃsāra-bandhāt sadyaḥ pramucyate||

units.label: Verse 11
units.deva:
प्रयोजनं सम्प्रवृत्तेः कारणं फल-लक्षणम्।
प्रयोजनम् अनुद्दिश्य न मन्दोऽपि प्रवर्तते॥
units.translation: Purpose, marked by a result, is the cause of undertaking. Even a fool does not act without aiming at a purpose.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: Some purpose in the form of fruit is the cause of action. No one, not even a fool, ever takes up anything without thinking of the benefit to be derived from it.
units.iast:
prayojanaṃ sampravṛtteḥ kāraṇaṃ phala-lakṣaṇam|
prayojanam anuddiśya na mando’pi pravartate||

units.label: Verse 12
units.deva:
साधन-चतुष्टय-सम्पत्तिर् यस्यास्ति धीमतः पुंसः।
तस्यैवैतत्-फल-सिद्धिर् नान्यस्य किञ्चिद्-ऊनस्य॥
units.translation: This result is attained only by the wise person who has the full endowment of the four means, and not by anyone deficient in even a little.

gloss.en: full endowment of the four means

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: The four means of realization This benefit is gained only by one who is wise and who is fully endowed with the ‘four noble qualities;’ but it cannot be gained by one who is wanting in anyone one them, however slight the flaw may be.
units.iast:
sādhana-catuṣṭaya-sampattir yasyāsti dhīmataḥ puṃsaḥ|
tasyaivaitat-phala-siddhir nānyasya kiñcid-ūnasya||

units.label: Verse 13
units.deva:
चत्वारि साधनान्यत्र वदन्ति परमर्षयः।
मुक्तिर्येषां तु सद्भावे नाभावे सिध्यति ध्रुवम्॥
units.translation: The highest sages say that there are four means here. Liberation surely succeeds when they are present, and not when they are absent.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: The great sages say that there are four means of realization. Where they are to be found in plenitude, liberation is attained. It is certain that it cannot be attained otherwise.
units.iast:
catvāri sādhanānyatra vadanti paramarṣayaḥ|
muktiryeṣāṃ tu sadbhāve nābhāve sidhyati dhruvam||

units.label: Verse 14
units.deva:
आद्यं नित्यानित्य-वस्तु-विवेकः साधनं मतम्।
इहामुत्रार्थ-फल-भोग-विरागो द्वितीयकम्॥
units.translation: The first means is held to be discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things. Dispassion toward enjoying the results of things here and hereafter is the second.

gloss.en: discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things
enjoyment of the results of things

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: Of these, the first is discrimination between what is eternal and what is not eternal. The second constituent is the lack of attachment for such of the objects of enjoyment as may be gained either here or hereafter.
units.iast:
ādyaṃ nityānitya-vastu-vivekaḥ sādhanaṃ matam|
ihāmutrārtha-phala-bhoga-virāgo dvitīyakam||

units.label: Verse 15
units.deva:
शमादि-षट्क-सम्पत्तिस् तृतीयं साधनम् मतम्।
तुरीयं तु मुमुक्षुत्वं साधनं शास्त्र-सम्मतम्॥
units.translation: The endowment of the six qualities beginning with calmness is held to be the third means. The fourth is desire for liberation, the means approved by śāstra.

gloss.en: endowment of the six qualities beginning with calmness

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: The six noble qualities, such as calmness of mind and the like, when taken together, form the third constituent. According to the Śāstras the fourth and final constituent is the desire for liberation.
units.iast:
śamādi-ṣaṭka-sampattis tṛtīyaṃ sādhanam matam|
turīyaṃ tu mumukṣutvaṃ sādhanaṃ śāstra-sammatam||

units.label: Verse 16
units.deva:
ब्रह्मैव नित्यम् अन्यत् तु ह्यनित्यम् इति वेदनम्।
सोऽयं नित्यानित्य-वस्तु-विवेक इति कथ्यते॥
units.translation: Knowing that Brahman alone is eternal and everything else is non-eternal is called discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things.

gloss.en: discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: Discrimination It is only Brahman, the Absolute, that is eternal; nothing else is eternal. To be aware of this distinction between the eternal and the non-eternal is known as ‘discrimination (viveka).’
units.iast:
brahmaiva nityam anyat tu hyanityam iti vedanam|
so’yaṃ nityānitya-vastu-viveka iti kathyate||

units.label: Verses 17–18
units.deva:
मृदादि-कारणं नित्यं त्रिषु कालेषु दर्शनात्।
घटाद्यनित्यं तत्-कार्यं यतस् तन्-नाश ईक्ष्यते॥
तथैवैतज् जगत् सर्वम् अनित्यं ब्रह्म-कार्यतः।
तत्-कारणं परं ब्रह्म भवेन् नित्यं मृदादिवत्॥
units.translation: Cause material such as clay is eternal, because it is seen in the three times; its effect, such as a pot, is non-eternal, because its destruction is seen. In the same way, this whole world, as an effect of Brahman, is non-eternal; its cause, the supreme Brahman, is eternal like clay.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: For instance, none of the objects that are made of clay, such as pots and jugs are eternal; for they perish and cease to be. But the clay out of which they are made remains at all times, and therefore it is said to be eternal. What the clay is to the pot, the Brahman is in relation to the world. That is why it is said that Brahman alone is eternal. ((ChanU.6.1.4-6) (Chāndogya Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
mṛdādi-kāraṇaṃ nityaṃ triṣu kāleṣu darśanāt|
ghaṭādyanityaṃ tat-kāryaṃ yatas tan-nāśa īkṣyate||
tathaivaitaj jagat sarvam anityaṃ brahma-kāryataḥ|
tat-kāraṇaṃ paraṃ brahma bhaven nityaṃ mṛdādivat||

units.label: Verse 19
units.deva:
सर्गं वक्त्यस्य तस्माद् वा एतस्माद् इत्यपि श्रुतिः।
सकाशाद् ब्रह्मणस् तस्माद् अनित्यत्वे न संशयः॥
units.translation: Śruti also speaks of this creation, saying “from that” and “from this.” Since it comes from Brahman, its non-eternity is not in doubt.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: According to the Śruti all that is manifest has proceeded from the Absolute, Brahman. Apart from Brahman they cease to be. That is the reason why they are not eternal. ((TaitU.2.1.1) (Taittirīya Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
sargaṃ vaktyasya tasmād vā etasmād ityapi śrutiḥ|
sakāśād brahmaṇas tasmād anityatve na saṃśayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 20
units.deva:
सर्वस्यानित्यत्वे सावयवत्वेन सर्वतः सिद्धे।
वैकुण्ठादिषु नित्यत्व-मतिर् भ्रम एव मूढ-बुद्धीनाम्॥
units.translation: Since the non-eternity of everything is established by its having parts, the belief that Vaikuṇṭha and the like are eternal is only a delusion of foolish minds.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: Whatever consists of parts and whole cannot be eternal. This truth holds good even if it is (the heaven called) Vaikuṇṭha. Therefore, to consider any particular object to be eternal would be an error of the imagination.
units.iast:
sarvasyānityatve sāvayavatvena sarvataḥ siddhe|
vaikuṇṭhādiṣu nityatva-matir bhrama eva mūḍha-buddhīnām||

units.label: Verse 21
units.deva:
अनित्यत्वं च नित्यत्वम् एवं यच् छ्रुति-युक्तिभिः।
विवेचनं नित्यानित्य-विवेक इति कथ्यते॥
units.translation: Discerning, through śruti and reasoning, what is non-eternal and what is eternal is called discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: To distinguish, in the light of what the Śruti says, and with the help of one’s own power of reasoning between that which is eternal and that which is not eternal is therefore known as ‘discrimination.’
units.iast:
anityatvaṃ ca nityatvam evaṃ yac chruti-yuktibhiḥ|
vivecanaṃ nityānitya-viveka iti kathyate||

units.label: Verse 22
units.deva:
ऐहिकामुष्मिकार्थेषु ह्यनित्यत्वेन निश्चयात्।
नैःस्पृह्यं तुच्छ-बुद्ध्या यत् तद् वैराग्यम् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: Because worldly and otherworldly objects are known to be non-eternal, the lack of desire for them, from seeing them as trivial, is called dispassion.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: Desirelessness Inasmuch as all possessions that may be gained either here or hereafter are by their very nature transient, and are of no lasting value, not to feel any yearning for them is known as ‘non-attachment (vairāgya).’
units.iast:
aihikāmuṣmikārtheṣu hyanityatvena niścayāt|
naiḥspṛhyaṃ tuccha-buddhyā yat tad vairāgyam itīryate||

units.label: Verse 23
units.deva:
नित्यानित्य-पदार्थ-विवेकात् पुरुषस्य जायते सद्यः।
स्रक्-चन्दन-वनितादौ सर्वत्रानित्य-वस्तुनि विरक्तिः॥
units.translation: From discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things, dispassion arises at once toward every non-eternal object, such as garlands, sandal paste, women, and the rest.

gloss.en: from discrimination between eternal and non-eternal things

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: As the immediate consequence of practising discrimination between what is eternal and what is not, there arises an absence of desire; and this desirelessness is felt towards all transient objects, such as a garland, a paste of sandalwood, or a young woman and so on.
units.iast:
nityānitya-padārtha-vivekāt puruṣasya jāyate sadyaḥ|
srak-candana-vanitādau sarvatrānitya-vastuni viraktiḥ||

units.label: Verse 24
units.deva:
काकस्य विष्ठावद् असह्य-बुद्धिर्
भोग्येषु सा तीव्र-विरक्तिर् इष्यते।
विरक्ति-तीव्रत्व-निदानम् आहुर्
भोग्येषु दोषेक्षणम् एव सन्तः॥
units.translation: That unbearable view of objects of enjoyment, like a crow’s excrement, is held to be intense dispassion. The wise say that seeing the defects in objects of enjoyment is the cause of intense dispassion.

gloss.en: the view that it is unbearable

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: The culmination of desirelessness is attained when one turns away with disgust from all the objects of desire, as though they were as abominable as the excrement of a crow. The wise say that this feeling comes as a result of the perception of the defects that are inherent in all the objects of enjoyment.
units.iast:
kākasya viṣṭhāvad asahya-buddhir
bhogyeṣu sā tīvra-viraktir iṣyate|
virakti-tīvratva-nidānam āhur
bhogyeṣu doṣekṣaṇam eva santaḥ||

units.label: Verse 25
units.deva:
प्रदृश्यते वस्तुनि यत्र दोषो
न तत्र पुंसोऽस्ति पुनः प्रवृत्तिः।
अन्तर्महारोगवतीं विजानन्
को नाम वेश्याम् अपि रूपिणीं व्रजेत्॥
units.translation: When a defect is seen in an object, a person does not engage with it again. Who would approach even a beautiful courtesan, knowing that she has a great disease within?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: No one would ever seek an object in which one perceives inherent defects; for there is none who would ever seek that which may seem to be attractive, when one knows that it conceals hidden deformities.
units.iast:
pradṛśyate vastuni yatra doṣo
na tatra puṃso’sti punaḥ pravṛttiḥ|
antarmahārogavatīṃ vijānan
ko nāma veśyām api rūpiṇīṃ vrajet||

units.label: Verse 26
units.deva:
अत्रापि चान्यत्र च विद्यमान-
पदार्थ-सम्मर्शनम् एव कार्यम्।
यथा-प्रकारार्थ-गुणाभिमर्शनं
सन्दर्शयत्येव तदीय-दोषम्॥
units.translation: Here and elsewhere, one should examine the objects that are present. Examining their nature, purpose, and qualities shows their defects.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: It therefore behoves us that we should investigate into the nature of all objects, whether they concern this world or the next world. It is only by means of investigation that we may perceive the inherent defects.
units.iast:
atrāpi cānyatra ca vidyamāna-
padārtha-sammarśanam eva kāryam|
yathā-prakārārtha-guṇābhimarśanaṃ
sandarśayatyeva tadīya-doṣam||

units.label: Verse 27
units.deva:
कुक्षौ स्वमातुर् मल-मूत्र-मध्ये
स्थितिं तदा विट्क्रिमि-दंशनं च।
तदीय-कौक्षेयक-वह्नि-दाहं
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Thinking of the state in one’s mother’s womb, amid feces and urine, of being bitten by worms, and of the burning heat of the womb, who would not become dispassionate?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion at the contemplation of one’s own existence in one’s mother’s womb, in the midst of ordure, bitten by germs, and roasted in the furnace heat of the body?
units.iast:
kukṣau svamātur mala-mūtra-madhye
sthitiṃ tadā viṭkrimi-daṃśanaṃ ca|
tadīya-kaukṣeyaka-vahni-dāhaṃ
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||

units.label: Verse 28
units.deva:
स्वकीय-विण्मूत्र-विसर्जनं तच्
चोत्तान-गत्या शयनं तदा यत्।
बाल-ग्रहाद्याहति-भाक् च शैशवं
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate on considering the discharge of one’s own feces and urine, the face-up posture of lying then, and infancy spent subject to childhood afflictions?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
svakīya-viṇmūtra-visarjanaṃ tac
cottāna-gatyā śayanaṃ tadā yat|
bāla-grahādyāhati-bhāk ca śaiśavaṃ
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion when contemplating one’s ante-natal life, in the midst of one’s own filth and urine, with one’s feet up, or when one contemplates the stage of infancy, when one was subject to the diseases caused by the influence of evil stars?

units.label: Verse 29
units.deva:
स्वीयैः परैस् ताडनम् अज्ञ-भावम्
अत्यन्त-चापल्यम् असत्-क्रियां च।
कुमार-भावे प्रतिषिद्ध-वृत्तिं
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate on considering how, in boyhood, one is beaten by one’s own people and by others, is ignorant and extremely fickle, engages in wrong acts, and follows prohibited conduct?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
svīyaiḥ parais tāḍanam ajña-bhāvam
atyanta-cāpalyam asat-kriyāṃ ca|
kumāra-bhāve pratiṣiddha-vṛttiṃ
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion when one recalls how as a child one was beaten by one’s own relations and also by others, and how ignorant one was, how very fickle, addicted to evil ways and to forbidden conduct?

units.label: Verse 30
units.deva:
मदोद्धतिं मान्य-तिरस्कृतिं च
कामातुरत्वं समयातिलङ्घनम्।
तां तां युवत्योदित-दुष्ट-चेष्टां
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate on considering the arrogance of youth, disrespect toward the worthy, being overcome by desire, transgressing proper limits, and wicked conduct prompted by young women?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
madoddhatiṃ mānya-tiraskṛtiṃ ca
kāmāturatvaṃ samayātilaṅghanam|
tāṃ tāṃ yuvatyodita-duṣṭa-ceṣṭāṃ
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion when one thinks over one’s own arrogance during one’s youth; and how disrespectful one was towards those worthy of honour; or how under the influence of lust one transgressed the established laws of conduct or was given to the vices of youth?

units.label: Verse 31
units.deva:
विरूपतां सर्व-जनाद् अवज्ञां
सर्वत्र दैन्यं निज-बुद्धि-हैन्यम्।
वृद्धत्व-सम्भावित-दुर्दशां तां
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate after considering ugliness, contempt from everyone, misery everywhere, weakness of one’s own judgment, and the wretched condition brought on by old age?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
virūpatāṃ sarva-janād avajñāṃ
sarvatra dainyaṃ nija-buddhi-hainyam|
vṛddhatva-sambhāvita-durdaśāṃ tāṃ
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of disgust at the contumely of others, it may be because one is not good looking, or because one has lost one’s command over reason as old age advances?

units.label: Verse 32
units.deva:
पित्तज्वरार्शः-क्षय-गुल्म-शूल-
श्लेष्मादि-रोगोदित-तीव्र-दुःखम्।
दुर्गन्धम् अस्वास्थ्यम् अनून-चिन्तां
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate after considering the intense suffering caused by bilious fever, piles, consumption, abdominal swellings, colic, diseases involving phlegm and the like, foul smell, ill health, and unceasing worry?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
pittajvarārśaḥ-kṣaya-gulma-śūla-
śleṣmādi-rogodita-tīvra-duḥkham|
durgandham asvāsthyam anūna-cintāṃ
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of disgust when one sees how life is ever fraught with disease, such as fever, piles, phthisis, enlargement of spleen, colic, and cough? With the advance of old age, ill health sets in, causes the body to emit a bad smell, and troubles the mind with grief.

units.label: Verse 33
units.deva:
यमावलोकोदित-भीति-कम्प-
मर्म-व्यथोच्छ्वास-गतीश्च वेदनाम्।
प्राण-प्रयाणे परिदृश्यमानां
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate after considering the fear and trembling brought on at the sight of Yama, pain in the vital parts, gasping breaths, and the pain seen as life departs?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yamāvalokodita-bhīti-kampa-
marma-vyathocchvāsa-gatīśca vedanām|
prāṇa-prayāṇe paridṛśyamānāṃ
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Then there arises fear; trembling in the body, pain in the vital organs, and there is a gasping for breath, as Yama, the god of death approaches. There is also the experience of an agonizing sense of pain at the moment of death. Would not one who thinks over all this feel a sense of disgust with life?

units.label: Verse 34
units.deva:
अङ्गार-नद्यां तपने च कुम्भी-
पाकेऽपि वीच्याम् असि-पत्र-कानने।
दूतैर् यमस्य क्रियमाण-बाधां
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate after considering the torment inflicted by Yama’s messengers in Aṅgāra River, Tapana, Kumbhīpāka, Avīci, and the forest of sword-leaves?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
aṅgāra-nadyāṃ tapane ca kumbhī-
pāke’pi vīcyām asi-patra-kānane|
dūtair yamasya kriyamāṇa-bādhāṃ
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion when one contemplates how the departed suffer under the orders of Yama, it may be in the boiling waters of Aṅgāra-nadī, or in Kumbhī-pāka where one is baked alive, or in Asi-patra-kānana where one is compelled to walk on the blades of swords?

units.label: Verse 35
units.deva:
पुण्य-क्षये पुण्य-कृतो नभः-स्थैर्
निपात्यमानान् शिथिली-कृताङ्गान्।
नक्षत्र-रूपेण दिवश् च्युतांस् तान्
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate after considering those who performed meritorious acts, cast down from heaven when their merit is exhausted, their limbs limp, falling like stars from the sky?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
puṇya-kṣaye puṇya-kṛto nabhaḥ-sthair
nipātyamānān śithilī-kṛtāṅgān|
nakṣatra-rūpeṇa divaś cyutāṃs tān
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion when, as a result of investigation one finds that whatever stock of merit one might have acquired might be exhausted, and then one would be hurled down from heaven, only to fall below with mangled limbs, like fallen stars which have lost their lustre? ((ChanU.5.10.5) (Chāndogya Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 36
units.deva:
वाय्वर्क-वह्नीन्द्र-मुखान् सुरेन्द्रान्
ईशोग्र-भीत्या ग्रथितान्तर्-अङ्गान्।
विपक्ष-लोकैः परिदूयमानान्
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate after considering the chief gods—Vāyu, the Sun, Fire, and Indra—bound within by fear of the mighty Lord and tormented by hostile groups?

gloss.en: headed by Vāyu, the Sun, Fire, and Indra
from fear of the mighty Lord

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
vāyvarka-vahnīndra-mukhān surendrān
īśogra-bhītyā grathitāntar-aṅgān|
vipakṣa-lokaiḥ paridūyamānān
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion when one contemplates that not even the mighty Devas such as Vāyu, Āditya, Agni and Indra are exempt either from the fear of the Lord, or from the fear of their enemies? ((TaitU.2.8.1) (Taittirīya Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 37
units.deva:
श्रुत्या निरुक्तं सुख-तारतम्यं
ब्रह्मान्तम् आरभ्य मही-महेशम्।
औपाधिकं तत् तु न वास्तवं चेद्
आलोच्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate after considering the gradations of happiness described in scripture, from the mighty lord of earth up to Brahmā, as dependent on limiting adjuncts and therefore not real?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śrutyā niruktaṃ sukha-tāratamyaṃ
brahmāntam ārabhya mahī-maheśam|
aupādhikaṃ tat tu na vāstavaṃ ced
ālocya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion when one contemplates that the graduated scale of happiness beginning with Brahmā and coming down to the mighty rulers of the earth, inasmuch as it is based upon the assumption of a body must necessarily be transient, and therefore not real?

units.label: Verse 38
units.deva:
सालोक्य-सामीप्य-सरूपतादि-
भेदस्तु सत्-कर्म-विशेष-सिद्धः।
न कर्म-सिद्धस्य तु नित्यतेति
विचार्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate after considering that differences such as dwelling in the same world as the Lord, being near Him, or having His form are achieved through particular meritorious acts, and that what action achieves is not eternal?

gloss.en: of what is achieved by action

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sālokya-sāmīpya-sarūpatādi-
bhedastu sat-karma-viśeṣa-siddhaḥ|
na karma-siddhasya tu nityateti
vicārya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion when one realizes that nothing that has been acquired could be eternal, even if one should acquire as the reward of merit the privilege of living in the same region, in close proximity, with and invested in a form similar to that of the Lord? ((MunU.1.2.10) (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 39
units.deva:
यत्रास्ति लोके गति-तारतम्यं
उच्चावचत्वान्वितम् अत्र तत् कृतम्।
यथेह तद्वत् खलु दुःखम् अस्तीति
आलोच्य को वा विरतिं न याति॥
units.translation: Who would not become dispassionate after considering that wherever a world has a hierarchy of higher and lower states, suffering exists there too, just as it does here?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yatrāsti loke gati-tāratamyaṃ
uccāvacatvānvitam atra tat kṛtam|
yatheha tadvat khalu duḥkham astīti
ālocya ko vā viratiṃ na yāti||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who does not feel a sense of revulsion when on examination one finds that wherever there is a gradation of high and low, there must needs be misery also; for it is as true of those regions as here on earth? ((BrhUEng.4.3.33) (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad))
units.sourceNote: The source prints इस्तीत्य्; normalized to अस्तीति (“there is”) for grammar and meaning.

units.label: Verse 40
units.deva:
को नाम लोके पुरुषो विवेकी
विनश्वरे तुच्छ-सुखे गृहादौ।
कुर्याद् रतिं नित्यम् अवेक्षमाणो
वृथैव मोहान् म्रियमाण-जन्तून्॥
units.translation: Which discerning person in the world would delight in the fleeting, trivial pleasure of a home and the like while constantly watching deluded beings die in vain?

gloss.en: in a home and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ko nāma loke puruṣo vivekī
vinaśvare tuccha-sukhe gṛhādau|
kuryād ratiṃ nityam avekṣamāṇo
vṛthaiva mohān mriyamāṇa-jantūn||
units.editionTranslation: Which person who is endowed with discrimination would ever seek happiness in such transient objects as one’s abode when one sees day by day how those who are deluded and who pin their faith in these low pleasures pass away and cease to be?
units.sourceNote: The verse reads मोहान्; the edition’s Sanskrit prose order has मोहात्. This reader preserves the verse and translates मोहान् as “deluded beings.”

units.label: Verse 41
units.deva:
सुखं किम् अस्त्यत्र विचार्यमाणे
गृहेऽपि वा योषिति वा पदार्थे।
मायातमोऽन्धीकृत-चक्षुषो ये
त एव मुह्यन्ति विवेक-शून्याः॥
units.translation: What pleasure is there in a home, a woman, or any object when examined? Only those whose sight is blinded by māyā’s darkness, and who lack discernment, are deluded.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sukhaṃ kim astyatra vicāryamāṇe
gṛhe’pi vā yoṣiti vā padārthe|
māyātamo’ndhīkṛta-cakṣuṣo ye
ta eva muhyanti viveka-śūnyāḥ||
units.editionTranslation: What pleasure is there in the possession of a home or of the company of a young woman? It is only those who are devoid of discrimination, and who become blinded on account of ignorance become deluded.

units.label: Verse 42
units.deva:
अविचारित-रमणीयं
सर्वम् उदुम्बर-फलोपमं भोग्यम्।
अज्ञानाम् उपभोग्यं न तु
तज्-ज्ञानां योषिति वा पदार्थे॥
units.translation: Everything enjoyable is attractive when unexamined, like an udumbara fruit; the ignorant enjoy it, but the wise do not, whether it is a woman or another object.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
avicārita-ramaṇīyaṃ
sarvam udumbara-phalopamaṃ bhogyam|
ajñānām upabhogyaṃ na tu
taj-jñānāṃ yoṣiti vā padārthe||
units.editionTranslation: The wild fig may seem attractive to look at, but it is only so long as it is not examined closely. It is the same with all other objects of enjoyment; they too seem attractive to the ignorant, though the wise know that they are worthless.
units.sourceNote: Restored the opening pāda अविचारित-रमणीयम् from the cited edition, which was missing from the reader text.

units.label: Verse 43
units.deva:
गतेऽपि तोये सुषिरं कुलीरो
हातुं ह्यशक्तो म्रियते विमोहात्।
यथा तथा गेह-सुखानुषक्तो
विनाशम् आयाति नरो भ्रमेण॥
units.translation: Just as a crab dies from delusion, unable to leave its hole even after the water is gone, so a person attached to the pleasures of home reaches destruction through error.

gloss.en: attached to the pleasures of home

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
gate’pi toye suṣiraṃ kulīro
hātuṃ hyaśakto mriyate vimohāt|
yathā tathā geha-sukhānuṣakto
vināśam āyāti naro bhrameṇa||
units.editionTranslation: Like the crab that remains in its hole after the water in it has all evaporated, and out of a false sense of attachment perishes, the man who is drawn by the pleasures of the home lingers there and meets his end.

units.label: Verses 44–45
units.deva:
कोशकृमिः तन्तुभिर् आत्म-देहम्
आवेष्ट्य चावेष्ट्य च गुप्तिम् इच्छन्।
स्वयं विनिर्गन्तुम् अशक्त एव संस्
ततस् तद्-अन्ते म्रियते च लग्नः॥
यथा तथा पुत्र-कलत्र-मित्र-
स्नेहानुबन्धैर् ग्रथितो गृहस्थः।
कदापि वा तान् परिमुच्य गेहाद्
गन्तुं न शक्तो म्रियते मुधैव॥
units.translation: Just as a silk worm wraps its own body in threads again and again, seeking protection, but cannot emerge and dies trapped, so a householder bound by affection for sons, wife, and friends cannot leave them and go from home; he dies in vain.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kośakṛmiḥ tantubhir ātma-deham
āveṣṭya cāveṣṭya ca guptim icchan|
svayaṃ vinirgantum aśakta eva saṃs
tatas tad-ante mriyate ca lagnaḥ||
yathā tathā putra-kalatra-mitra-
snehānubandhair grathito gṛhasthaḥ|
kadāpi vā tān parimucya gehād
gantuṃ na śakto mriyate mudhaiva||
units.editionTranslation: The silk worm draws the filament from its body, and wraps itself again and again in order to protect itself. Unable to come out of it, it lingers there and dies. The householder also fares in the same way. He becomes bound by the ties of affection, whether it is for his family, or his friends and relations. He then becomes unable to give them up, and perishes in vain.
units.sourceNote: Normalized कोशक्रिमिस् to कोशकृमिः, the standard Sanskrit form for “silk worm,” consistent with the edition’s prose order.

units.label: Verse 46
units.deva:
कारागृहस्यास्य च को विशेषः
प्रदृश्यते साधु विचार्यमाणे।
मुक्तेः प्रतीपत्वम् इहापि पुंसः
कान्ता-सुखाभ्युत्थित-मोह-पाशैः॥
units.translation: On proper examination, what difference is there between this home and a prison? Here too, the bonds of delusion arising from pleasure with a beloved person turn one away from liberation.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kārāgṛhasyāsya ca ko viśeṣaḥ
pradṛśyate sādhu vicāryamāṇe|
mukteḥ pratīpatvam ihāpi puṃsaḥ
kāntā-sukhābhyutthita-moha-pāśaiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: If one should examine properly, what difference is there between one’s home and a prison house? If one should be bound by one’s desire, and if one should remain in one’s home, out of attachment to it, even that is a kind of bondage and it becomes a hindrance to the attainment of liberation.

units.label: Verse 47
units.deva:
गृह-स्पृहा पाद-निबद्ध-शृङ्खला
कान्ता-सुताशा पटु-कण्ठ-पाशः।
शीर्षे पतद्भूर्यशनिर् हि साक्षात्
प्राणान्त-हेतुः प्रबला धनाशा॥
units.translation: Longing for a home is a chain bound to the feet; desire for a wife and children is a tight noose around the neck. Powerful desire for wealth is a heavy thunderbolt falling on the head, directly causing the end of life.

gloss.en: a chain bound to the feet
a tight noose around the neck

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
gṛha-spṛhā pāda-nibaddha-śṛṅkhalā
kāntā-sutāśā paṭu-kaṇṭha-pāśaḥ|
śīrṣe patadbhūryaśanir hi sākṣāt
prāṇānta-hetuḥ prabalā dhanāśā||
units.editionTranslation: The ties which bind a man to his house are like the chains round his feet. The affection that he feels for his wife and children is like a halter round his neck. Inordinate desire for wealth is like the fall of a heavy thunderbolt that brings about one’s death.

units.label: Verse 48
units.deva:
आशा-पाश-शतेन पाशित-पदो नोत्थातुम् एव क्षमः
काम-क्रोध-मदादिभिः प्रतिभटैः संरक्ष्यमाणोऽनिशम्।
संमोहावरणेन गोपनवतः संसार-कारागृहान्
निर्गन्तुं त्रि-विधेषणा-पर-वशः कः शक्नुयाद् रागिषु॥
units.translation: Among those attached, who could leave the prison-houses of saṃsāra, covered by delusion, when his feet are bound by hundreds of hope-fetters, he cannot even rise, is constantly hemmed in by adversaries such as desire, anger, and pride, and is controlled by the threefold desire?

gloss.en: by desire, anger, pride, and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
āśā-pāśa-śatena pāśita-pado notthātum eva kṣamaḥ
kāma-krodha-madādibhiḥ pratibhaṭaiḥ saṃrakṣyamāṇo’niśam|
saṃmohāvaraṇena gopanavataḥ saṃsāra-kārāgṛhān
nirgantuṃ tri-vidheṣaṇā-para-vaśaḥ kaḥ śaknuyād rāgiṣu||
units.editionTranslation: Discerning the problem of desire If one should be bound by hundreds of false hopes as though they are so many fetters, and if one should be unable to stand, and if one should be always under the surveillance of enemy soldiers, the representatives of lust, anger and arrogance, and in addition to it if one should be the victim of the three kinds of desire, is it ever possible that such a person could ever come out a free man from the prison house of the world encircled and entrenched as it is by delusion?

units.label: Verse 49
units.deva:
कामान्धकारेण निरुद्ध-दृष्टिर्
मुह्यत्य् असत्य् अप्य् अबला-स्वरूपे।
न ह्यन्ध-दृष्टेर् असतः सतो वा
सुखत्व-दुःखत्व-विचारणास्ति॥
units.translation: With sight blocked by the darkness of desire, one is deluded even by a woman’s unreal form. A person with blinded sight does not consider whether something is real or unreal, pleasure or pain.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kāmāndhakāreṇa niruddha-dṛṣṭir
muhyaty asaty apy abalā-svarūpe|
na hyandha-dṛṣṭer asataḥ sato vā
sukhatva-duḥkhatva-vicāraṇāsti||
units.editionTranslation: If one should become blinded by lust, even the picture of a woman, unreal as it is, is enough to cause delusion. One who is deprived of one’s judgement becomes incapable of discrimination, and becomes unable to find out how far one’s pleasure and pain are real, or are otherwise.

units.label: Verse 50
units.deva:
श्लेष्मोद्गारि मुखं स्रवन्मलवती नासाश्रुमल् लोचनं
स्वेद-स्रावि मलाभिपूर्णम् अभितो दुर्गन्ध-दुष्टं वपुः।
अन्यद् वक्तुम् अशक्यम् एव मनसा मन्तुं क्वचिन् नार्हति
स्त्री-रूपं कथम् ईदृशं सुमनसां पात्रीभवेन् नेत्रयोः॥
units.translation: The mouth emits phlegm, the nose drains filth, and the eyes shed tears; the body streams sweat, is full of filth, and stinks all over. Other faults are too many to speak of or even conceive. How could such a woman’s form be worthy of the eyes of the wise?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śleṣmodgāri mukhaṃ sravanmalavatī nāsāśrumal locanaṃ
sveda-srāvi malābhipūrṇam abhito durgandha-duṣṭaṃ vapuḥ|
anyad vaktum aśakyam eva manasā mantuṃ kvacin nārhati
strī-rūpaṃ katham īdṛśaṃ sumanasāṃ pātrībhaven netrayoḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Is there any wise man who would ever feel attracted at the spectacle of one whose mouth, nose and eyes are exuding phlegm, filth and tears, whose body is full of perspiration and hides many other shortcomings, too numerous to be mentioned, only because it happens to be a woman’s (i.e. an opposite sex) body?

units.label: Verse 51
units.deva:
दूराद् अवेक्ष्याग्नि-शिखां पतङ्गो
रम्यत्व-बुद्ध्या विनिपत्य नश्यति
यथा तथा नष्ट-दृग् एष सूक्ष्मं
कथं निरीक्षेत विमुक्ति-मार्गम्॥
units.translation: Just as a moth sees a flame from afar, falls into it thinking it beautiful, and perishes, so how could this person, blinded to what is subtle, perceive the path to liberation?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
dūrād avekṣyāgni-śikhāṃ pataṅgo
ramyatva-buddhyā vinipatya naśyati
yathā tathā naṣṭa-dṛg eṣa sūkṣmaṃ
kathaṃ nirīkṣeta vimukti-mārgam||
units.editionTranslation: Just as moths are drawn from afar at the sight of a flame, and attracted by it they fall in it and perish, so also the man who is under the spelt of delusion falls a victim to it; for he becomes incapable of perceiving the subtle path to salvation.

units.label: Verse 52
units.deva:
कामेन कान्तां परिगृह्य तद्वज्
जनोऽप्ययं नश्यति नष्ट-दृष्टिः।
मांसास्थि-मज्जा-मल-मूत्र-पात्रं
स्त्रियं स्वयं रम्यतयैव पश्यति॥
units.translation: Driven by desire, a person takes a beloved woman and perishes in the same way, his discernment lost; he himself sees as beautiful a woman who is only a vessel of flesh, bone, marrow, filth, and urine.

gloss.en: a vessel of flesh, bone, marrow, filth, and urine

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kāmena kāntāṃ parigṛhya tadvaj
jano’pyayaṃ naśyati naṣṭa-dṛṣṭiḥ|
māṃsāsthi-majjā-mala-mūtra-pātraṃ
striyaṃ svayaṃ ramyatayaiva paśyati||
units.editionTranslation: Although woman’s body is but an assemblage of flesh, fat and bones, that man who is lured by lust regards it as the abode of beauty. Such a man loses his insight and is destroyed.

units.label: Verse 53
units.deva:
काम एव यमः साक्षात् कान्ता वैतरणी नदी।
विवेकिनां मुमुक्षूणां निलयस् तु यमालयः॥
units.translation: For discerning seekers of liberation, desire itself is Yama; the beloved woman is the river Vaitaraṇī; the dwelling, indeed, is Yama’s abode.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kāma eva yamaḥ sākṣāt kāntā vaitaraṇī nadī|
vivekināṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ nilayas tu yamālayaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: There is therefore no death other than lust; nor is there any river of hell, Vaitaraṇī, other than woman. Let the wise aspirant after liberation look upon his home as though it were the receptacle of death.

units.label: Verse 54
units.deva:
यमालये वापि गृहेऽपि नो नृणां
ताप-त्रय-क्लेश-निवृत्तिर् अस्ति।
किञ्चित् समालोक्य तु तद्-विरामं
सुखात्मना पश्यति मूढ-लोकः॥
units.translation: Neither in Yama’s abode nor at home do people find relief from the distress of the threefold suffering. The deluded person sees a brief pause in that suffering as happiness.

gloss.en: relief from the distress of the threefold suffering

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yamālaye vāpi gṛhe’pi no nṛṇāṃ
tāpa-traya-kleśa-nivṛttir asti|
kiñcit samālokya tu tad-virāmaṃ
sukhātmanā paśyati mūḍha-lokaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: No one can ever escape suffering pain as a result of the three-fold ills of life either in the abode of Yama, or in one’s own home. The man who is deluded imagines that the brief interval between two successive periods of pain is full of bliss.

units.label: Verse 55
units.deva:
यमस्य कामस्य च तारतम्यं
विचार्यमाणे महद् अस्ति लोके।
हितं करोत्यस्य यमोऽप्रियः सन्
कामस् त्वनर्थं कुरुते प्रियः सन्॥
units.translation: On examination, there is a great difference between Yama and desire: though unwelcome, Yama does what is beneficial for a person; desire, though pleasant, causes harm.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yamasya kāmasya ca tāratamyaṃ
vicāryamāṇe mahad asti loke|
hitaṃ karotyasya yamo’priyaḥ san
kāmas tvanarthaṃ kurute priyaḥ san||
units.editionTranslation: If he should exercise right judgement, he will see how vast is the difference between Yama, the god of death, and lust, which is the death of life. Even though Yama is forbidding in appearance, he is beneficent; but lust lures man and destroys him utterly.

units.label: Verse 56
units.deva:
यमोऽसताम् एव करोत्यनर्थं
सतां तु सौख्यं कुरुते हितः सन्।
कामः सताम् एव गतिं निरुन्धन्
करोत्यनर्थं ह्यसतां नु का कथा॥
units.translation: Yama harms only the wicked; being well-disposed, he brings happiness to the good. Desire, however, blocks the good person’s path and causes harm; what need is there to speak of the wicked?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yamo’satām eva karotyanarthaṃ
satāṃ tu saukhyaṃ kurute hitaḥ san|
kāmaḥ satām eva gatiṃ nirundhan
karotyanarthaṃ hyasatāṃ nu kā kathā||
units.editionTranslation: Therefore only the wicked are afraid of Yama. In reality he is the well wisher of the virtuous people, for he grants bliss to them. But lust blocks the path even for the wise. and it is obvious how the wicked fare.

units.label: Verse 57
units.deva:
विश्वस्य वृद्धिं स्वयम् एव काङ्क्षन्
प्रवर्तकं कामि-जनं ससर्ज।
तेनैव लोकः परिमुह्यमानः
प्रवर्धते चन्द्रमसेव चाब्धिः॥
units.translation: Desiring the growth of the world, the creator himself created desire-driven people as its agents. Deluded by this, the world grows, like the ocean under the moon.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
viśvasya vṛddhiṃ svayam eva kāṅkṣan
pravartakaṃ kāmi-janaṃ sasarja|
tenaiva lokaḥ parimuhyamānaḥ
pravardhate candramaseva cābdhiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Lust is but Nature’s contraption for the perpetuation of the race. Human beings are drawn by the power of lust, just as the tide is urged forward when the moon is full.

units.label: Verse 58
units.deva:
कामो नाम महाञ् जगद्-भ्रमयिता स्थित्वान्तरङ्गे स्वयं
स्त्री-पुंसाव् इतरेतराङ्गकगुणैर् हासैश्च भावैः स्फुटम्।
अन्योन्यं परिमोह्य नैज-तमसा प्रेमानुबन्धेन तौ
बद्ध्वा भ्रामयति प्रपञ्च-रचनां संवर्धयन् ब्रह्महा॥
units.translation: Desire is a great deluder of the world, dwelling within. Through the qualities of one another’s bodies, smiles, and expressions it deludes woman and man, binds them with its own darkness and bonds of love, and drives the world’s creation forward, obscuring knowledge of Brahman.

gloss.en: by the qualities of each other’s bodies

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kāmo nāma mahāñ jagad-bhramayitā sthitvāntaraṅge svayaṃ
strī-puṃsāv itaretarāṅgakaguṇair hāsaiśca bhāvaiḥ sphuṭam|
anyonyaṃ parimohya naija-tamasā premānubandhena tau
baddhvā bhrāmayati prapañca-racanāṃ saṃvardhayan brahmahā||
units.editionTranslation: But there is nothing more delusive than lust. It has its abode in the human heart, and there, by means of physical attraction, smiles and emotional allurement it brings about the union of man and woman in order that the world of creation might go on. Lust is real destroyer of Brahman, for it deludes man by the bonds of love.

units.label: Verse 59
units.deva:
अतोऽन्तरङ्ग-स्थित-काम-वेगाद्
भोग्ये प्रवृत्तिः स्वत एव सिद्धा।
सर्वस्य जन्तोर् ध्रुवम् अन्यथा चेद्
अबोधितार्थेषु कथं प्रवृत्तिः॥
units.translation: Therefore, the impulse toward objects of enjoyment arises naturally from the force of desire dwelling within. If not, how could any living being be drawn toward things it has not known?

gloss.en: from the force of desire dwelling within

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ato’ntaraṅga-sthita-kāma-vegād
bhogye pravṛttiḥ svata eva siddhā|
sarvasya jantor dhruvam anyathā ced
abodhitārtheṣu kathaṃ pravṛttiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: It is only because lust has its abode within oneself, that people go in quest of the various objects of enjoyment. If it were otherwise, would anyone go in quest of that which he knows not?

units.label: Verse 60
units.deva:
तेनैव सर्व-जन्तूनां कामना बलवत्-तरा।
जीर्यत्यपि च देहेऽस्मिन् कामना नैव जीर्यते॥
units.translation: For this reason desire in all creatures is stronger: even as this body grows old, desire does not grow old.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tenaiva sarva-jantūnāṃ kāmanā balavat-tarā|
jīryatyapi ca dehe’smin kāmanā naiva jīryate||
units.editionTranslation: The physical body might decay with the advance of old-age, but lust decays not. Impetuous indeed are the passions.

units.label: Verse 61
units.deva:
अवेक्ष्य विषये दोषं बुद्धि-युक्तो विचक्षणः।
काम-पाशेन यो मुक्तः स मुक्तेः पथि गोचरः॥
units.translation: A discerning person who sees the defect in sense objects and is free from desire’s noose is fit to tread the path of liberation.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
avekṣya viṣaye doṣaṃ buddhi-yukto vicakṣaṇaḥ|
kāma-pāśena yo muktaḥ sa mukteḥ pathi gocaraḥ||
units.editionTranslation: But that person who is intelligent and wise, and who knows what defects lie hidden in the objects of enjoyment knows how to free himself from the bonds of desire. Only such a person is fit to tread the path that leads to liberation.

units.label: Verse 62
units.deva:
कामस्य विजयोपायं सूक्ष्मं वक्ष्याम्यहं सताम्।
सङ्कल्पस्य परित्याग उपायः सुलभो मतः॥
units.translation: I will explain to the good the subtle means of conquering desire: giving up the conception [that an object is desirable] is considered an easy method.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kāmasya vijayopāyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vakṣyāmyahaṃ satām|
saṅkalpasya parityāga upāyaḥ sulabho mataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The means of conquering desire Let me tell you what that subtle path is by means of which all those who are virtuous might conquer desire. The simplest means of conquering desire is to give up the idea that a particular object is attractive, and not to think of it at all.

units.label: Verse 63
units.deva:
श्रुते दृष्टेऽपि वा भोग्ये यस्मिन् कस्मिंश्च वस्तुनि।
समीचीनत्व-धी-त्यागात् कामो नोदेति कर्हिचित्॥
units.translation: Even when any object of enjoyment is heard of or seen, desire never arises once the thought that it is desirable has been given up.

gloss.en: from giving up the thought that it is desirable

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śrute dṛṣṭe’pi vā bhogye yasmin kasmiṃśca vastuni|
samīcīnatva-dhī-tyāgāt kāmo nodeti karhicit||
units.editionTranslation: Even when one hears of a particular object or sees it, no one ever desires to possess it, unless first of all there arises the idea that it is a desirable object.

units.label: Verse 64
units.deva:
कामस्य बीजं सङ्कल्पः सङ्कल्पाद् एव जायते।
बीजे नष्टेऽङ्कुर इव तस्मिन् नष्टे विनश्यति॥
units.translation: A conception is the seed of desire; desire arises from conception alone. When that seed is destroyed, desire perishes, just as a sprout cannot remain when its seed is destroyed.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kāmasya bījaṃ saṅkalpaḥ saṅkalpād eva jāyate|
bīje naṣṭe’ṅkura iva tasmin naṣṭe vinaśyati||
units.editionTranslation: That mental concept that a particular object is attractive is the source of all desires. Where no such thought arises, there can be no desire. For if the seed should be destroyed, how can it sprout?

units.label: Verse 65
units.deva:
न कोऽपि सम्यक्त्व-धिया विनैव
भोग्यं नरः कामयितुं समर्थः।
यतस् ततः काम-जयेच्छुर् एतां
सम्यक्त्व-बुद्धिं विषये निहन्यात्॥
units.translation: No one can desire an object of enjoyment without first judging it desirable. Therefore, one who wishes to conquer desire should remove this sense of desirability from the object.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
na ko’pi samyaktva-dhiyā vinaiva
bhogyaṃ naraḥ kāmayituṃ samarthaḥ|
yatas tataḥ kāma-jayecchur etāṃ
samyaktva-buddhiṃ viṣaye nihanyāt||
units.editionTranslation: No one ever covets any object of enjoyment unless one thinks that it is desirable. Let him who is intent upon the conquest of desire first of all erase from his mind all ideas as to the desirability of any given object.

units.label: Verse 66
units.deva:
भोग्ये नरः काम-जयेच्छुर् एतां
सुखत्व-बुद्धिं विषये निहन्यात्।
यावत् सुखत्व-भ्रम-धीः पदार्थे
तावन् न जेतुं प्रभवेद्धि कामम्॥
units.translation: One who wishes to conquer desire should remove from an object the notion that it is pleasant. As long as the deluded idea that an object brings pleasure remains, one cannot conquer desire.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
bhogye naraḥ kāma-jayecchur etāṃ
sukhatva-buddhiṃ viṣaye nihanyāt|
yāvat sukhatva-bhrama-dhīḥ padārthe
tāvan na jetuṃ prabhaveddhi kāmam||
units.editionTranslation: And let him who is intent upon the conquest of desire give up the feeling of pleasureableness which is associated with such objects for where there is the feeling of pleasureableness, lust cannot be conquered.

units.label: Verse 67
units.deva:
सङ्कल्पानुदये हेतुर् यथा-भूतार्थ-दर्शनम्।
अनर्थ-चिन्तनं चाभ्यां नावकाशोऽस्य विद्यते॥
units.translation: Seeing things as they are and reflecting on their harm prevent the thought of wanting them from arising; these two leave it no opening.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
saṅkalpānudaye hetur yathā-bhūtārtha-darśanam|
anartha-cintanaṃ cābhyāṃ nāvakāśo’sya vidyate||
units.editionTranslation: But where, as a result of right knowledge in relation to things and as a result of reflection, one becomes aware of the harm that results, there does not arise the idea that a given object is attractive. Where both these factors are present, the very idea of attractiveness withers away for lack of opportunity.

units.label: Verse 68
units.deva:
रत्ने यदि शिला-बुद्धिर् जायते वा भयं ततः।
समीचीनत्व-धीर् नैति नोपादेयत्व-धीर् अपि॥
units.translation: If a jewel is thought to be only a stone, or if it causes fear, the thought that it is desirable does not arise, nor does the thought that it should be acquired.

gloss.en: the thought that it is a stone
the thought that it is desirable
the thought that it should be acquired

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ratne yadi śilā-buddhir jāyate vā bhayaṃ tataḥ|
samīcīnatva-dhīr naiti nopādeyatva-dhīr api||
units.editionTranslation: Thus when one knows that a precious stone is only a piece of stone, or feels a sense of fear towards it, one would not wish to possess it or feel that it is worth having.

units.label: Verse 69
units.deva:
यथार्थ-दर्शनं वस्तुन्यनर्थस्यापि चिन्तनम्।
सङ्कल्पस्यापि कामस्य तद् वधोपाय इष्यते॥
units.translation: Seeing an object as it is and reflecting on its harm are held to be the means of destroying both the conception and desire.

gloss.en: seeing an object as it is

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yathārtha-darśanaṃ vastunyanarthasyāpi cintanam|
saṅkalpasyāpi kāmasya tad vadhopāya iṣyate||
units.editionTranslation: Therefore the conquest of desire becomes possible only when one becomes aware of the evil consequences that flow from the objects of desire as a result of right knowledge.

units.label: Verse 70
units.deva:
धनं भय-निबन्धनं सतत-दुःख-संवर्धनं
प्रचण्डतरकर्दनं स्फुटित-बन्धु-संवर्धनम्।
विशिष्ट-गुण-बाधनं कृपण-धी-समाराधनं
न मुक्ति-गति-साधनं भवति नापि हृच्-छोधनम्॥
units.translation: Wealth is a source of fear, steadily increases sorrow, causes severe distress, increases ruptures among relatives, hinders noble qualities, and is worshipped by the miserly mind. It is neither a means to liberation nor a purifier of the heart.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
dhanaṃ bhaya-nibandhanaṃ satata-duḥkha-saṃvardhanaṃ
pracaṇḍatarakardanaṃ sphuṭita-bandhu-saṃvardhanam|
viśiṣṭa-guṇa-bādhanaṃ kṛpaṇa-dhī-samārādhanaṃ
na mukti-gati-sādhanaṃ bhavati nāpi hṛc-chodhanam||
units.editionTranslation: Non-covetousness Fear, ever-increasing sorrow, self-glorification, discord among friends – all these are the evil consequences that flow from wealth. It is also a hindrance to the practice of virtue. Although the miser worships wealth, it is not conducive either to salvation or to self-purification.

units.label: Verse 71
units.deva:
राज्ञो भयं चोर-भयं प्रमादाद्
भयं तथा ज्ञाति-भयं च वस्तुतः।
धनं भय-ग्रस्तम् अनर्थ-मूलं
यतः सतां नैव सुखाय कल्पते॥
units.translation: Wealth brings fear of kings and thieves, fear through carelessness, and fear of one’s own kin. It is beset by fear and is the root of harm; therefore it does not bring happiness even to the good.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
rājño bhayaṃ cora-bhayaṃ pramādād
bhayaṃ tathā jñāti-bhayaṃ ca vastutaḥ|
dhanaṃ bhaya-grastam anartha-mūlaṃ
yataḥ satāṃ naiva sukhāya kalpate||
units.editionTranslation: Wealth makes a person feel afraid of kings and thieves. It makes one suspicious of one’s own kinsmen also. It makes one suspect oneself also, lest one should be careless. Inasmuch as wealth is ever attended with fear, it is always a source of discord. The virtuous never hope to find any happiness in it.

units.label: Verse 72
units.deva:
आर्जने रक्षणे दाने व्यये वापि च वस्तुतः।
दुःखम् एव सदा नॄणां न धनं सुख-साधनम्॥
units.translation: In earning, protecting, giving, or spending, wealth is always a source of sorrow for people; it is not a means of happiness.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ārjane rakṣaṇe dāne vyaye vāpi ca vastutaḥ|
duḥkham eva sadā nṝṇāṃ na dhanaṃ sukha-sādhanam||
units.editionTranslation: Wealth is ever a source of grief, both when it is being earned, and when it is preserved; it is also a source of grief, whether it is spent or given as a gift. None has ever found it to be a source of bliss.

units.label: Verse 73
units.deva:
सताम् अपि पदार्थस्य लाभाल् लोभः प्रवर्धते।
विवेको लुप्यते लोभात् तस्मिंल् लुप्ते विनश्यति॥
units.translation: Even good people grow greedy when they gain possessions. Greed erases discernment; when discernment is lost, a person perishes.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
satām api padārthasya lābhāl lobhaḥ pravardhate|
viveko lupyate lobhāt tasmiṃl lupte vinaśyati||
units.editionTranslation: Even the virtuous become greedy when they begin to acquire wealth. One who is greedy becomes incapable of discriminating between good and evil, and one who lacks discrimination is destroyed.

units.label: Verse 74
units.deva:
दहत्य् अलाभे निःस्वत्वं लाभे लोभो दहत्य् अमुम्।
तस्मात् सन्तापकं वित्तं कस्य सौख्यं प्रयच्छति॥
units.translation: Poverty burns a person when wealth is absent; when wealth is gained, greed burns that person. Therefore, to whom does wealth bring happiness when it causes distress?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
dahaty alābhe niḥsvatvaṃ lābhe lobho dahaty amum|
tasmāt santāpakaṃ vittaṃ kasya saukhyaṃ prayacchati||
units.editionTranslation: The person who is not rich is victimised by poverty; but the rich is victimised by greed. In either case, as no one ever feels happy with it, wealth is always a source of sorrow.

units.label: Verse 75
units.deva:
भोगेन मत्तता जन्तोर् दानेन पुनर्-उद्भवः।
वृथैवोभयथा वित्तं नास्त्येव गतिर् अन्यथा॥
units.translation: Through enjoyment, a person becomes intoxicated; through giving, there is birth again. Either way, wealth is futile; there is no other escape.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
bhogena mattatā jantor dānena punar-udbhavaḥ|
vṛthaivobhayathā vittaṃ nāstyeva gatir anyathā||
units.editionTranslation: There are some who become intoxicated with the possession of wealth. Even if wealth should be given in charity, it is the cause of people being reborn. Therefore, there is no escape from pain.

units.label: Verse 76
units.deva:
धनेन मद-वृद्धिः स्यान् मदेन स्मृति-नाशनम्।
स्मृति-नाशाद् बुद्धि-नाशो बुद्धि-नाशात् प्रणश्यति॥
units.translation: Wealth increases pride; pride destroys memory. From the loss of memory comes loss of discernment, and from the loss of discernment a person perishes.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
dhanena mada-vṛddhiḥ syān madena smṛti-nāśanam|
smṛti-nāśād buddhi-nāśo buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati||
units.editionTranslation: With the growth of wealth pride increases; and the proud man forgets all that he has learnt. When a man forgets what he has learnt, his intellect decays; and finally the man himself perishes.

units.label: Verse 77
units.deva:
सुखयति धनम् एवेत्यन्तर्-आशा-पिशाच्या
दृढतरम् उपगूढो मूढ-लोको जडात्मा।
निवसति तद्-उपान्ते सन्ततं प्रेक्षमाणो
व्रजति तदपि पश्चात् प्राणम् एतस्य हृत्वा॥
units.translation: Believing “wealth alone makes me happy,” the dull-minded man is firmly embraced by the inner demon of hope and stays beside it, watching it constantly. Later wealth too departs, taking his life with it.

gloss.en: by the inner demon of hope

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sukhayati dhanam evetyantar-āśā-piśācyā
dṛḍhataram upagūḍho mūḍha-loko jaḍātmā|
nivasati tad-upānte santataṃ prekṣamāṇo
vrajati tadapi paścāt prāṇam etasya hṛtvā||
units.editionTranslation: As for the deluded man who is lured by the demon of greed from within he firmly persuades himself that wealth is ever a source of happiness. Lapped in wealth, he falls into deeper delusion. Finally after it is all spent, wealth departs, taking with it the man’s life.

units.label: Verse 78
units.deva:
सम्पन्नोऽन्धवद् एव किञ्चिद् अपरं नो वीक्षते चक्षुषा
सद्भिर् वर्जित-मार्ग एव चरति प्रोत्सारितो बालिशैः।
तस्मिन्न् एव मुहुः स्खलन् प्रतिपदं गत्वान्ध-कूपे पतति
अस्यान्धत्व-निवर्तकौषधम् इदं दारिद्र्यम् एवाञ्जनम्॥
units.translation: The wealthy person sees nothing else, like a blind man, and, urged on by fools, follows a road the wise have abandoned. Stumbling at every step, he falls into a blind pit. Poverty alone is the eye-salve that cures this blindness.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sampanno’ndhavad eva kiñcid aparaṃ no vīkṣate cakṣuṣā
sadbhir varjita-mārga eva carati protsārito bāliśaiḥ|
tasminn eva muhuḥ skhalan pratipadaṃ gatvāndha-kūpe patati
asyāndhatva-nivartakauṣadham idaṃ dāridryam evāñjanam||
units.editionTranslation: Wealth tends to narrow one’s vision. As he is surrounded by flatterers, the rich man traverses a path which the wise have abandoned; and at every step he stumbles into hidden pitfalls. Where the vision becomes blurred, there is no remedy other than poverty.

units.label: Verse 79
units.deva:
लोभः क्रोधश्च डम्भश्च मदो मत्सर एव च। (दम्भश्च)
वर्धते वित्त-सम्प्राप्त्या कथं तच् चित्त-शोधनम्॥
units.translation: With the acquisition of wealth, greed, anger, conceit, arrogance, and envy all grow. How could wealth then purify the mind?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
lobhaḥ krodhaśca ḍambhaśca mado matsara eva ca| (dambhaśca)
vardhate vitta-samprāptyā kathaṃ tac citta-śodhanam||
units.editionTranslation: Greed, anger, pride, conceit and jealousy grow ever more with the acquisition of wealth. Can it ever become a means of attaining purity of mind?

units.label: Verse 80
units.deva:
अलाभाद् द्वि-गुणं दुःखं वित्तस्य व्यय-सम्भवे।
ततोऽपि त्रि-गुणं दुःखं दुर्व्यये विदुषाम् अपि॥
units.translation: Not gaining wealth brings sorrow; when wealth is spent, sorrow is twice as great; when it is badly spent, sorrow is threefold even for the wise.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
alābhād dvi-guṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ vittasya vyaya-sambhave|
tato’pi tri-guṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ durvyaye viduṣām api||
units.editionTranslation: Not to earn wealth is a source of sorrow; but when money is spent the sorrow that is felt is twice as great. When it is ill-spent, the sorrow felt by the wise is thrice as great.

units.label: Verse 81
units.deva:
नित्याहितेन वित्तेन
भय-चिन्तानपायिना।
चित्त-स्वास्थ्यं कुतो जन्तोर्
गृह-स्थेनाहिना यथा॥
units.translation: With wealth as a constant harm, and fear and worry never leaving, how could a person have peace of mind? It is like a snake living in the house.

gloss.en: with fear and worry that do not leave

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
nityāhitena vittena
bhaya-cintānapāyinā|
citta-svāsthyaṃ kuto jantor
gṛha-sthenāhinā yathā||
units.editionTranslation: In as much as fear and anxiety ever wait upon wealth, and as wealth is as harmful as a snake in one’s home, how can any one ever feel at ease in its presence?
units.sourceNote: Restored the missing first pāda नित्याहितेन वित्तेन from the cited edition.

units.label: Verse 82
units.deva:
कान्तारे विजने वने जन-पदे सेतौ निरीतौ च वा
चोरैर् वापि तथेतरैर् नरवरैर् युक्तो वियुक्तोऽपि वा।
निःस्वः स्वस्थतया सुखेन वसति ह्याद्रीयमाणो जनैः
क्लिश्नात्य् एव धनी सदाकुल-मतिर् भीतश्च पुत्राद् अपि॥
units.translation: A person without wealth lives happily and at ease, respected by people, whether alone or accompanied, in wilderness, forest, town, village, on a bridge, or in a safe place—even among thieves and rulers. The wealthy person alone suffers, always troubled and afraid even of his son.

gloss.en: in a place free from danger

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kāntāre vijane vane jana-pade setau nirītau ca vā
corair vāpi tathetarair naravarair yukto viyukto’pi vā|
niḥsvaḥ svasthatayā sukhena vasati hyādrīyamāṇo janaiḥ
kliśnāty eva dhanī sadākula-matir bhītaśca putrād api||
units.editionTranslation: He who has no wealth leads a happy life and is respected by the people, whether he lives alone or in company. He may live in the midst of thieves, ill-natured people, or kings. He lives a care-free life, whether it is in a lonely forest, or in a town, or in a village, or under a bridge, or in any other place that is free from trouble. But the rich are subject to nervous agitation, and are afraid of even their own children, and they meet with nothing except misery.

units.label: Verse 83
units.deva:
तस्माद् अनर्थस्य निदानम् अर्थः
पुमर्थ-सिद्धिर् न भवत्यनेन।
ततो वनान्ते निवसन्ति सन्तः
संन्यस्य सर्वं प्रतिकूलम् अर्थम्॥
units.translation: Wealth is therefore the cause of harm; it does not bring fulfillment of human aims. The wise live in the forest, renouncing all wealth that stands in their way.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tasmād anarthasya nidānam arthaḥ
pumartha-siddhir na bhavatyanena|
tato vanānte nivasanti santaḥ
saṃnyasya sarvaṃ pratikūlam artham||
units.editionTranslation: Wealth is ever attended with grief. None may attain by means of wealth the highest reward of life. The wise flee the world, and they give up the love of wealth; for it is an obstacle in the path. Thus they resort to a life of seclusion in a forest.

units.label: Verse 84
units.deva:
श्रद्धा-भक्तिमतीं सतीं गुणवतीं पुत्राञ् श्रुतान् सम्मतान्
अक्षय्यं वसुधानु-भोग-विभवैः श्रीसुन्दरं मन्दिरम्।
सर्वं नश्वरम् इत्य् अवेत्य कवयः श्रुत्युक्तिभिर् युक्तिभिः
संन्यस्यन्त्य् अपरे तु तत् सुखम् इति भ्राम्यन्ति दुःखार्णवे॥
units.translation: Knowing through scripture and reasoning that everything is perishable—the faithful, devoted, virtuous wife; learned, respected sons; abundant wealth and its enjoyments; and a beautiful home—the wise renounce it all. Others, however, mistake it for happiness and wander in an ocean of sorrow.

gloss.en: with wealth and abundant means of enjoyment

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śraddhā-bhaktimatīṃ satīṃ guṇavatīṃ putrāñ śrutān sammatān
akṣayyaṃ vasudhānu-bhoga-vibhavaiḥ śrīsundaraṃ mandiram|
sarvaṃ naśvaram ity avetya kavayaḥ śrutyuktibhir yuktibhiḥ
saṃnyasyanty apare tu tat sukham iti bhrāmyanti duḥkhārṇave||
units.editionTranslation: From what the Śruti says, and from what reason points out, the wise realize that all that they own, such as a good and devoted wife, learned and agreeable children, abundant wealth and home made resplendent with it, and all other means of enjoyment are transient. The wise renounce them; but those who are not wise imagine that they lead to happiness and wander about in the ocean of misery.

units.label: Verse 85
units.deva:
सुखम् इति मल-राशौ ये रमन्तेऽत्र गेहे
कृमय इव कलत्र-क्षेत्र-पुत्रानुषक्त्या।
सुर-पद इव तेषां नैव मोक्ष-प्रसङ्गस्
त्वपि तु निरय-गर्भावास-दुःख-प्रवाहः॥
units.translation: Those who, attached to wife, land, and sons, delight in the home as if it were a god’s abode are like worms rejoicing in a heap of filth. They have no prospect of liberation; instead, they face a stream of suffering in hell and the womb.

gloss.en: a stream of suffering in hell and the womb

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sukham iti mala-rāśau ye ramante’tra gehe
kṛmaya iva kalatra-kṣetra-putrānuṣaktyā|
sura-pada iva teṣāṃ naiva mokṣa-prasaṅgas
tvapi tu niraya-garbhāvāsa-duḥkha-pravāhaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Those who rejoice in the possession of wife, home and children, as if they were heaven, are like unto worms that rejoice in filth. Such seek not the path of salvation; and their lot is hell, the cycle of rebirth, and trouble unending.

units.label: Verse 86
units.deva:
येषाम् आशा निराशा स्याद्
दारापत्य-धनादिषु।
तेषां सिध्यति नान्येषां
मोक्षाशाभिमुखी गतिः॥
units.translation: For those whose longing for wife, children, wealth, and the like has ended, the path toward liberation succeeds; it succeeds for no others.

gloss.en: for wife, children, wealth, and the like
turned toward the hope of liberation

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yeṣām āśā nirāśā syād
dārāpatya-dhanādiṣu|
teṣāṃ sidhyati nānyeṣāṃ
mokṣāśābhimukhī gatiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Only those who have their passions stilled, and who crave not for wife, children or wealth, proceed onward on the path of liberation. None else may achieve it.

units.label: Verse 87
units.deva:
सत्-कर्म-क्षय-पाप्मनां श्रुतिमतां सिद्धात्मनां धीमतां
नित्यानित्य-पदार्थ-शोधनम् इदं युक्त्या मुहुः कुर्वताम्।
तस्माद् उत्थ-महाविरक्त्य्-असिमतां मोक्षैक-काङ्क्षावतां
धन्यानां सुलभं स्त्रियादि-विषयेष्व् आशालताच्छेदनम्॥
units.translation: For the blessed—whose sins are exhausted by good actions, who are versed in scripture and steadfast in Self-knowledge, who repeatedly discern the eternal from the transient through reasoning, who bear the sword of great dispassion born of that inquiry, and whose only desire is liberation—it is easy to cut the creeper of longing for women and other sense objects.

gloss.en: whose sins are exhausted by good actions
discrimination between the eternal and the transient
bearing the sword of great dispassion
toward women and other sense objects

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sat-karma-kṣaya-pāpmanāṃ śrutimatāṃ siddhātmanāṃ dhīmatāṃ
nityānitya-padārtha-śodhanam idaṃ yuktyā muhuḥ kurvatām|
tasmād uttha-mahāvirakty-asimatāṃ mokṣaika-kāṅkṣāvatāṃ
dhanyānāṃ sulabhaṃ striyādi-viṣayeṣv āśālatācchedanam||
units.editionTranslation: To those blessed ones whose meritorious deeds have destroyed all sins, who study the Śruti, who make use of the power of reason to discriminate again and again between the eternal and the transient, who are endowed with detachment of a high order as a result of such discrimination, and who are ever intent upon liberation, to those who are self-possessed, and enlightened; it becomes easy to cut off with one stroke of dispassion all the bonds of life.

units.label: Verse 88
units.deva:
संसार-मृत्योर् बलिनः प्रवेष्टुं
द्वाराणि तु त्रीणि महान्ति लोके।
कान्ता च जिह्वा कनकं च तानि
रुणद्धि यस् तस्य भयं न मृत्योः॥
units.translation: The great gates to the mighty death of saṃsāra are three: woman, the tongue, and gold. Whoever restrains them has no fear of death.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
saṃsāra-mṛtyor balinaḥ praveṣṭuṃ
dvārāṇi tu trīṇi mahānti loke|
kāntā ca jihvā kanakaṃ ca tāni
ruṇaddhi yas tasya bhayaṃ na mṛtyoḥ||
units.editionTranslation: There are three big gateways which lead to the mighty city of saṃsāra. They are lust, greed, and the palate; and all of them lead to death. But he who is not lured by them fears no death.

units.label: Verse 89
units.deva:
मुक्ति-श्री-नगरस्य दुर्जयतरं द्वारं यद् अस्त्य् आदिमं
तस्य द्वे अररे धनं च युवती ताभ्यां पिनद्धं दृढम्।
कामाख्यार्गल-दारुणा बलवता द्वारं तद् एतत् त्रयं
धीरो यस् तु भिनत्ति सोऽर्हति सुखं भोक्तुं विमुक्ति-श्रियः॥
units.translation: The first and hardest-to-conquer gate of the city of liberation’s glory has two leaves, wealth and a young woman, firmly fastened together. A terrible, powerful bolt called desire bars that gate. The steadfast person who breaks through this threefold barrier is worthy to enjoy the bliss of liberation.

gloss.en: of the city of liberation’s glory

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
mukti-śrī-nagarasya durjayataraṃ dvāraṃ yad asty ādimaṃ
tasya dve arare dhanaṃ ca yuvatī tābhyāṃ pinaddhaṃ dṛḍham|
kāmākhyārgala-dāruṇā balavatā dvāraṃ tad etat trayaṃ
dhīro yas tu bhinatti so’rhati sukhaṃ bhoktuṃ vimukti-śriyaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: But there is another city, the sacred city of freedom absolute. The entrance to that city is closed by a mighty gateway; woman and wealth constitute the two panels of its doors; while lust is like a mighty crossbar which closes it from within. But the hero fights his way through them. He alone is fit to enjoy the bliss of ultimate liberation.

units.label: Verse 90
units.deva:
आरूढस्य विवेकाश्वं तीव्र-वैराग्य-खड्गिनः।
तितिक्षा-वर्म-युक्तस्य प्रतियोगी न दृश्यते॥
units.translation: For one who rides the horse of discernment, bears the sword of intense dispassion, and wears the armor of endurance, no opponent is seen.

gloss.en: bearing the sword of intense dispassion
equipped with the armor of endurance

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ārūḍhasya vivekāśvaṃ tīvra-vairāgya-khaḍginaḥ|
titikṣā-varma-yuktasya pratiyogī na dṛśyate||
units.editionTranslation: To such a hero, the wise person, discrimination is the steed, dispassion the sword, and fortitude an armour of proof; and he fears no enemy.

units.label: Verses 91–92
units.deva:
विवेक-जां तीव्र-विरक्तिम् एव
मुक्तेर् निदानं निगदन्ति सन्तः।
तस्माद् विवेकी विरतिं मुमुक्षुः
सम्पादयेत् तां प्रथमं प्रयत्नात्॥
पुमान् अजात-निर्वेदो देह-बन्धं जिहासितुम्।
न हि शक्नोति निर्वेदो बन्ध-भेदो महान् असौ॥
units.translation: The wise declare that intense dispassion born of discernment is the root of liberation. Therefore, a discerning seeker of liberation should first strive to cultivate it. A person in whom dispassion has not arisen cannot abandon bondage to the body; dispassion is the great breaker of bondage.

gloss.en: in whom dispassion has not arisen

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
viveka-jāṃ tīvra-viraktim eva
mukter nidānaṃ nigadanti santaḥ|
tasmād vivekī viratiṃ mumukṣuḥ
sampādayet tāṃ prathamaṃ prayatnāt||
pumān ajāta-nirvedo deha-bandhaṃ jihāsitum|
na hi śaknoti nirvedo bandha-bhedo mahān asau||
units.editionTranslation: Out of discrimination comes dispassionateness and the wise say that dispassion is the root of liberation. The discriminating person who desires liberation should put forth all effort, and acquire dispassion first of all.

units.label: Verse 93
units.deva:
वैराग्य-रहिता एव यमालय इवालये।
क्लिश्नन्ति त्रिविधैस् तापैर् मोहिता अपि पण्डिताः॥
units.translation: Without dispassion, the home is like Yama’s abode; even learned people, deluded, suffer there from the threefold afflictions.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
vairāgya-rahitā eva yamālaya ivālaye|
kliśnanti trividhais tāpair mohitā api paṇḍitāḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Where there is no dispassion home becomes a hell; it does not exempt even the learned from the threefold ills of life.

units.label: Verse 94
units.deva:
शमो दमस् तितिक्षोपरतिः श्रद्धा ततः परम्।
समाधानम् इति प्रोक्तं षड् एवैते शमादयः॥
units.translation: Tranquillity, sense-restraint, forbearance, withdrawal, faith, and collectedness are said to be these six, beginning with śama.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śamo damas titikṣoparatiḥ śraddhā tataḥ param|
samādhānam iti proktaṃ ṣaḍ evaite śamādayaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Śama, etc. Hence it is that tranquillity, the control of the senses, fortitude, renunciation, faith, and concentration of mind are regarded as the six cardinal virtues of life.

units.label: Verse 95
units.deva:
एक-वृत्त्यैव मनसः स्व-लक्ष्ये नियत-स्थितिः।
शम इत्युच्यते सद्भिः शम-लक्षण-वेदिभिः॥
units.translation: The wise who know the definition of śama call it the mind’s steady fixing on its own aim through a single current of thought.

gloss.en: with a single current of thought

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
eka-vṛttyaiva manasaḥ sva-lakṣye niyata-sthitiḥ|
śama ityucyate sadbhiḥ śama-lakṣaṇa-vedibhiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Tranquility The wise, who are entitled to speak of it, say that tranquility (śama) comes as a result of the mind being one-pointed, and being constantly directed to the object of meditation.

units.label: Verse 96
units.deva:
उत्तमो मध्यमश्चैव जघन्य इति च त्रिधा।
निरूपितो विपश्चिद्भिः तत्तल्-लक्षण-वेदिभिः॥
units.translation: The wise who know the marks of each kind describe tranquillity as threefold: highest, middle, and lowest.

gloss.en: by those who know each one’s mark

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
uttamo madhyamaścaiva jaghanya iti ca tridhā|
nirūpito vipaścidbhiḥ tattal-lakṣaṇa-vedibhiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Those who are entitled to speak of it say that there are three kinds of tranquility. They classify it into three categories: the best, that which is middling, and that which is of poor quality.

units.label: Verse 97
units.deva:
स्व-विकारं परित्यज्य वस्तुमात्रतया स्थितिः।
मनसः सोत्तमा शान्तिर् ब्रह्म-निर्वाण-लक्षणा॥
units.translation: When the mind abandons its own modifications and abides as mere reality, that is the highest tranquillity, marked by liberation in Brahman.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sva-vikāraṃ parityajya vastumātratayā sthitiḥ|
manasaḥ sottamā śāntir brahma-nirvāṇa-lakṣaṇā||
