units.editionTranslation: That state of mind which enjoys the nature of the supreme Reality, and which lies beyond the mind and its modifications, is regarded as the highest form of tranquility. It partakes of the nature of the bliss of Brahman.

units.label: Verse 98
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्-प्रत्यय-सन्तान-प्रवाह-करणं धियः।
यद् एषा मध्यमा शान्तिः शुद्ध-सत्त्वैक-लक्षणा॥
units.translation: The continuous flow of inward-directed thoughts in the mind is the middle tranquillity, marked solely by pure sattva.

gloss.en: producing a continuous flow of inward-directed thoughts

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
pratyak-pratyaya-santāna-pravāha-karaṇaṃ dhiyaḥ|
yad eṣā madhyamā śāntiḥ śuddha-sattvaika-lakṣaṇā||
units.editionTranslation: The continuous series of the modifications of the mind, directed in spite of distractions towards the pure consciousness of the Absolute is regarded as tranquility of the middling order.

units.label: Verse 99
units.deva:
विषय-व्यापृतिं त्यक्त्वा श्रवणैक-मन-स्थितिः।
मनसश्चेतरा शान्तिर् मिश्र-सत्त्वैक-लक्षणा॥
units.translation: Giving up engagement with sense objects and fixing the mind solely on listening to scripture is another tranquillity, marked by mixed sattva.

gloss.en: the mind fixed solely on listening

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
viṣaya-vyāpṛtiṃ tyaktvā śravaṇaika-mana-sthitiḥ|
manasaścetarā śāntir miśra-sattvaika-lakṣaṇā||
units.editionTranslation: To the lowest category belongs that aspect of tranquility, which consists of sattva which is some what mixed with the other qualities. At that stage, the mind’s inclination towards the objects of the senses is given up, and the mind is devoted to the learning of the Śruti.

units.label: Verse 100
units.deva:
प्राच्योदीच्याङ्ग-सद्-भावे शमः सिध्यति नान्यथा।
तीव्रा विरक्तिः प्राच्याङ्गम् उदीच्याङ्गं दमादयः॥
units.translation: Tranquillity is attained only when its prior and later supports are present. Intense dispassion is the prior support; sense-restraint and the like are the later supports.

gloss.en: when the prior and later supports are present

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
prācyodīcyāṅga-sad-bhāve śamaḥ sidhyati nānyathā|
tīvrā viraktiḥ prācyāṅgam udīcyāṅgaṃ damādayaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Tranquility may be realized only when its auxiliaries are present. Its prior auxiliary is intense dispassion. Its posterior auxiliary consists in the control of the senses and the like. In the absence of these, tranquility cannot be realized.

units.label: Verse 101
units.deva:
कामः क्रोधश्च लोभश्च मदो मोहश्च मत्सरः।
न जिताः षडिमे येन तस्य शान्तिर् न सिध्यति॥
units.translation: For one who has not conquered these six—desire, anger, greed, pride, delusion, and envy—peace is not attained.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kāmaḥ krodhaśca lobhaśca mado mohaśca matsaraḥ|
na jitāḥ ṣaḍime yena tasya śāntir na sidhyati||
units.editionTranslation: Unless one conquers the six passions, such as lust, wrath, greed, pride, delusion and jealousy none can attain peace.

units.label: Verse 102
units.deva:
शब्दादि-विषयेभ्यो यो विषवन् न निवर्तते।
तीव्र-मोक्षेच्छया भिक्षोस् तस्य शान्तिर् न सिध्यति॥
units.translation: A mendicant who does not turn away from sense objects beginning with sound as though they were poison does not attain peace, even with an intense desire for liberation.

gloss.en: from sense objects beginning with sound

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śabdādi-viṣayebhyo yo viṣavan na nivartate|
tīvra-mokṣecchayā bhikṣos tasya śāntir na sidhyati||
units.editionTranslation: Unless one shuns like poison the pleasures of the senses, none can attain peace. It is not enough if there is merely an ardent desire for peace.

units.label: Verse 103
units.deva:
येन नाराधितो देवो यस्य नो गुर्वनुग्रहः।
न वश्यं हृदयं यस्य तस्य शान्तिर् न सिध्यति॥
units.translation: One who has not worshipped the Lord, has no guru’s grace, and whose heart is not controlled does not attain peace.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yena nārādhito devo yasya no gurvanugrahaḥ|
na vaśyaṃ hṛdayaṃ yasya tasya śāntir na sidhyati||
units.editionTranslation: One who does not participate in divine service, who does not have the grace of the Guru, and whose feelings are not under restraint, cannot attain peace.

units.label: Verse 104
units.deva:
मनः-प्रसाद-सिद्ध्यर्थं साधनं श्रूयतां बुधैः।
मनः-प्रसादो यत्-सत्त्वे यद-भावे न सिध्यति॥
units.translation: Wise people, listen to the means for attaining serenity of mind: when these are present, serenity arises; without them, it is not attained.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
manaḥ-prasāda-siddhyarthaṃ sādhanaṃ śrūyatāṃ budhaiḥ|
manaḥ-prasādo yat-sattve yada-bhāve na sidhyati||
units.editionTranslation: Serenity Let him who is wise listen and understand what factors are essential in order to attain serenity (prasāda) of mind; how serenity is attained when these factors are present and how in their absence it is not attained.

units.label: Verse 105
units.deva:
ब्रह्म-चर्यम् अहिंसा च दया भूतेष्ववक्रता।
विषयेष्वतिवैतृष्ण्यं शौचं दम्भ-विवर्जनम्॥
units.translation: Brahmacarya, nonviolence, compassion toward living beings, straightforwardness, freedom from craving for sense objects, purity, and absence of pretence [are the means].
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
brahma-caryam ahiṃsā ca dayā bhūteṣvavakratā|
viṣayeṣvativaitṛṣṇyaṃ śaucaṃ dambha-vivarjanam||
units.editionTranslation: It is by the practice of Brahma-carya, non-injury (ahiṃsā), sympathy (dayā), guilelessness (avikratā), intense dispassion (vaitṛṣṇya) towards all the objects of sense-pleasure, and by the practice of purity (śauca) and humility (dambha-vivarjana) that serenity is attained.

units.label: Verse 106
units.deva:
सत्यं निर्ममता स्थैर्यम् अभिमान-विसर्जनम्।
ईश्वर-ध्यान-परता ब्रह्मविद्भिः सह स्थितिः॥
units.translation: Truthfulness, freedom from possessiveness, steadiness, relinquishing conceit, devotion to contemplation of the Lord, and association with knowers of Brahman [are also means to serenity].

gloss.en: devotion to contemplation of the Lord

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
satyaṃ nirmamatā sthairyam abhimāna-visarjanam|
īśvara-dhyāna-paratā brahmavidbhiḥ saha sthitiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Truthfulness (satya), non-attachment (nirmamatā), the cultivation of the steadiness (sthairya) of mind which is born as a result of conviction in the Śāstras, the absence of egoism (abhimāna-visarjana), faith in divine contemplation (dhyāna), and the love (sthiti) of holy company are also essential.

units.label: Verse 107
units.deva:
ज्ञान-शास्त्रैक-परता समता सुख-दुःखयोः।
मानानासक्तिर् एकान्त-शीलता च मुमुक्षुता॥
units.translation: Exclusive devotion to the texts of knowledge, evenness in pleasure and pain, freedom from attachment to honor, a habit of solitude, and longing for liberation [are also means].

gloss.en: exclusive devotion to the texts of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
jñāna-śāstraika-paratā samatā sukha-duḥkhayoḥ|
mānānāsaktir ekānta-śīlatā ca mumukṣutā||
units.editionTranslation: Add to it a devout study (eka-paratā) of the Jñāna Śāstras, the attitude of looking upon prosperity and adversity with equanimity (samatā), the absence of the hankering after public honour (māna-anāsakti), the love of solitude (ekānta-śīlatā), and the intense desire for liberation (mumukṣutā).

units.label: Verse 108
units.deva:
यस्यैतद् विद्यते सर्वं तस्य चित्तं प्रसीदति।
न त्वेतद् धर्म-शून्यस्य प्रकारान्तर-कोटिभिः॥
units.translation: For one who has all these, the mind becomes serene. But for one lacking these qualities, [serenity] is not attained even through crores of other means.

gloss.en: even through crores of other kinds

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yasyaitad vidyate sarvaṃ tasya cittaṃ prasīdati|
na tvetad dharma-śūnyasya prakārāntara-koṭibhiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: One who is endowed in full measure with all these noble qualities attains peace. But where these essential qualities are lacking, even millions of other qualities are of little value.

units.label: Verses 109–110
units.deva:
स्मरणं दर्शनं स्त्रीणां गुण-कर्मानुकीर्तनम्।
समीचीनत्व-धीस् तासु प्रीतिः सम्भाषणं मिथः॥
सह-वासश्च संसर्गोऽष्टधा मैथुनं विदुः।
एतद्-विलक्षणं ब्रह्म-चर्यं चित्त-प्रसादकम्॥
units.translation: Remembering women, seeing them, praising their qualities and actions, thinking them desirable, affection for them, private conversation, living together, and close association—these are known as eightfold sexual involvement. Brahmacarya, distinct from these, brings clarity to the mind.

gloss.en: the idea that they are desirable

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
smaraṇaṃ darśanaṃ strīṇāṃ guṇa-karmānukīrtanam|
samīcīnatva-dhīs tāsu prītiḥ sambhāṣaṇaṃ mithaḥ||
saha-vāsaśca saṃsargo’ṣṭadhā maithunaṃ viduḥ|
etad-vilakṣaṇaṃ brahma-caryaṃ citta-prasādakam||
units.editionTranslation: Brahma-carya At first a man begins to think of women. He then sees them, praises their qualities and deeds. He fancies them beautiful, loves them and talks to them in private. Thus he comes to live and move with them. In this way a man longes for himself the eightfold fetters of life. But it is only by shunning all this that Brahma-carya may be attained. It is only by this means that it is possible to attain tranquility of mind.

units.label: Verse 111
units.deva:
अहिंसा वाङ्मनःकायैः प्राणिमात्रा-प्रपीडनम्।
स्वात्मवत् सर्व-भूतेषु कायेन मनसा गिरा॥
units.translation: Non-injury is [refraining from] harming any living being through speech, mind, or body, and regarding all beings as one's own self through body, mind, and speech.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ahiṃsā vāṅmanaḥkāyaiḥ prāṇimātrā-prapīḍanam|
svātmavat sarva-bhūteṣu kāyena manasā girā||
units.editionTranslation: Non-injury Next comes the quality of non-injury. It does not mean merely abstaining from inflicting pain upon other living beings, either in thought, expression or action; it also includes regarding all beings as oneself in thought, word, and deed.

units.label: Verse 112
units.deva:
अनुकम्पा दया सैव प्रोक्ता वेदान्त-वेदिभिः।
करण-त्रितयेष्वेक-रूपतावक्रता मता॥
units.translation: Compassion is the kindness named by knowers of Vedānta. Straightforwardness is considered consistency among the three instruments: body, speech, and mind.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
anukampā dayā saiva proktā vedānta-vedibhiḥ|
karaṇa-tritayeṣveka-rūpatāvakratā matā||
units.editionTranslation: Compassion and guilelessness Compassion means kindness, so say the knowers of Vedānta. Similarly the quality of straightforwardness implies the co-ordination of thought, expression, and action, as revealed in one’s day to day conduct.

units.label: Verse 113
units.deva:
ब्रह्मादि-स्थावरान्तेषु वैराग्यं विषयेष्व् अनु।
यथैव काकविष्ठायां वैराग्यं तद्धि निर्मलम्॥
units.translation: Dispassion toward objects ranging from Brahmā to immovable things, like one's dispassion toward crow dung—that indeed is pure dispassion.

gloss.en: among objects ranging from Brahmā to immovable things

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
brahmādi-sthāvarānteṣu vairāgyaṃ viṣayeṣv anu|
yathaiva kākaviṣṭhāyāṃ vairāgyaṃ taddhi nirmalam||
units.editionTranslation: Dispassion Dispassion means the total absence of desire towards all the objects of enjoyment. Where there is dispassion, even the office of Hiraṇya-garbha is considered to be of little worth.

units.label: Verses 114–115
units.deva:
बाह्यम् आभ्यन्तरं चेति द्विविधं शौचम् उच्यते।
मृज्-जलाभ्यां कृतं शौचं बाह्यं शारीरकं स्मृतम्॥
अज्ञान-दूरी-करणं मानसं शौचम् आन्तरम्।
अन्तः-शौचे स्थिते सम्यग् बाह्यं नावश्यकं नृणाम्॥
units.translation: Purity is said to be twofold: external and internal. Cleanliness performed with earth and water is regarded as external, bodily cleanliness.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ ceti dvividhaṃ śaucam ucyate|
mṛj-jalābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ śaucaṃ bāhyaṃ śārīrakaṃ smṛtam||
ajñāna-dūrī-karaṇaṃ mānasaṃ śaucam āntaram|
antaḥ-śauce sthite samyag bāhyaṃ nāvaśyakaṃ nṛṇām||
units.editionTranslation: Cleanliness Cleanliness is of two kinds, external and internal. External cleanliness is attained by the use of earth and water. Internal cleanliness or purity is attained only by means of the removal of ignorance. Where there is inner purity, mere external cleanliness becomes less significant.

units.label: Verse 116
units.deva:
ध्यान-पूजादिकं लोके द्रष्टर्य् एव करोति यः।
पारमार्थिक-धी-हीनः स दम्भाचार उच्यते॥
units.translation: Whoever performs meditation, worship, and the like in public before onlookers, while lacking insight into ultimate reality, is called one whose conduct is pretentious.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
dhyāna-pūjādikaṃ loke draṣṭary eva karoti yaḥ|
pāramārthika-dhī-hīnaḥ sa dambhācāra ucyate||
units.editionTranslation: Humility To pray too much in public place, or to indulge in elaborate ritualistic worship where many are gathered, with out having true knowledge, is mere vanity and ostentation.

units.label: Verse 117
units.deva:
पुंसस् तथानाचरणम् अदम्भित्वं विदुर् बुधाः।
यत् स्वेन दृष्टं सम्यक् च श्रुतं तस्यैव भाषणम्॥
units.translation: The wise call a person's not acting in that way freedom from pretence. Truthfulness is saying only what one has clearly seen and correctly heard.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
puṃsas tathānācaraṇam adambhitvaṃ vidur budhāḥ|
yat svena dṛṣṭaṃ samyak ca śrutaṃ tasyaiva bhāṣaṇam||
units.editionTranslation: The wise distinguish the absence of this to be humility. Truthfulness As for truthfulness, it implies nothing more than saying what has been clearly seen or correctly heard by oneself.
units.sourceNote: The missing opening pāda has been restored from the cited A.K. Aruna edition.

units.label: Verse 118
units.deva:
सत्यम् इत्युच्यते ब्रह्म सत्यम् इत्यभिभाषणम्।
देहादिषु स्वकीयत्व-दृढ-बुद्धि-विसर्जनम्॥
units.translation: Saying “Brahman is real” is called speaking truth. Relinquishing the firm notion of ownership regarding the body and the like [is non-attachment].

gloss.en: in the body and the like
relinquishing the firm notion of ownership

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
satyam ity ucyate brahma satyam ity abhibhāṣaṇam|
dehādiṣu svakīyatva-dṛḍha-buddhi-visarjanam||
units.editionTranslation: To say that Brahman is real is an example of truth speaking. Non-attachment Next, one should give up the idea of ‘I and mine’ in relation to one’s physical body and the like, for, that is the essence of non-attachment.
units.sourceNote: The missing opening pāda has been restored from the cited A.K. Aruna edition.

units.label: Verse 119
units.deva:
निर्ममत्वं स्मृतं येन कैवल्यं लभते बुधः।
गुरु-वेदान्त-वचनैर् निश्चितार्थे दृढ-स्थितिः॥
units.translation: Freedom from possessiveness, by which the wise person attains liberation, is so called. Steadiness is firm abiding in the meaning ascertained through the teacher's and Vedānta's words.

gloss.en: through the words of the teacher and Vedānta

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
nirmamatvaṃ smṛtaṃ yena kaivalyaṃ labhate budhaḥ|
guru-vedānta-vacanair niścitārthe dṛḍha-sthitiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: That is why the wise regard non-attachment as a means to liberation. Steadiness As to what it is that constitutes steadiness, it is said that it implies an unswerving devotion to what the Guru says and what the Vedānta teaches.
units.sourceNote: The missing opening pāda has been restored from the cited A.K. Aruna edition.

units.label: Verse 120
units.deva:
तद्-एक-वृत्त्या तत् स्थैर्यं नैश्चल्यं न तु वर्ष्मणः।
विद्यैश्वर्य-तपो-रूप-कुल-वर्णाश्रमादिभिः॥
units.translation: Steadiness is abiding in that single mental mode; it is not bodily immobility. [Conceit may arise] through learning, wealth, austerity, appearance, family, social class, life stage, and the like.

gloss.en: through learning, wealth, austerity, appearance, family, social class, life stage, and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tad-eka-vṛttyā tat sthairyaṃ naiścalyaṃ na tu varṣmaṇaḥ|
vidyaiśvarya-tapo-rūpa-kula-varṇāśramādibhiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: It is the one-pointedness of the mind that is called steadiness: it does not mean remaining motionless physically. Absence of egoism The next quality is that one should give up all self-conceit. Whether it be due to one’s book learning, wealth, the practice of spiritual austerity or having good looks, a noble lineage and a high station in life…
units.sourceNote: The missing opening pāda has been restored from the cited A.K. Aruna edition.

units.label: Verse 121
units.deva:
सञ्जाताहङ्कृति-त्यागस् त्वभिमान-विसर्जनम्।
त्रिभिश्च करणैः सम्यग् हित्वा वैषयिकीं क्रियाम्॥
units.translation: Giving up the conceit arising from these is relinquishing pride. Having properly abandoned sense-directed activity through the three instruments [body, speech, and mind]…

gloss.en: giving up the conceit that has arisen

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sañjātāhaṅkṛti-tyāgas tv abhimāna-visarjanam|
tribhiśca karaṇaiḥ samyag hitvā vaiṣayikīṃ kriyām||
units.editionTranslation: The absence of egoism means the giving up of all pride. Contemplation on the Lord After abandoning all such egoism which is born of extraneous factors with the senses restrained from the pursuit of external objects, one should unify the faculties of body, mind and intellect.
units.sourceNote: The missing opening pāda has been restored from the cited A.K. Aruna edition.

units.label: Verse 122
units.deva:
स्वात्मैक-चिन्तनं यत् तद् ईश्वर-ध्यानम् ईरितम्।
छायेव सर्वदा वासो ब्रह्मविद्भिः सह स्थितिः॥
units.translation: What is contemplation solely on one's own Self is called contemplation of the Lord. Remaining always with knowers of Brahman, like a shadow, is association with them.

gloss.en: contemplation solely on one's own Self

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
svātmaika-cintanaṃ yat tad īśvara-dhyānam īritam|
chāyeva sarvadā vāso brahmavidbhiḥ saha sthitiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: To direct one’s co-ordinated faculties to the contemplation of the Ātman, the Self within, is to contemplate on the Lord. Seeking the society of the knowers of Brahman To seek the society of the knowers of Brahman, and to follow them constantly as a shadow is to seek the company of the holy.
units.sourceNote: The missing opening pāda has been restored from the cited A.K. Aruna edition.

units.label: Verse 123
units.deva:
यद् यद् उक्तं ज्ञान-शास्त्रे श्रवणादि-कमेषु यः।
निरतः कर्म-धी-हीनः ज्ञान-निष्ठः स एव हि॥
units.translation: Whoever is devoted to whatever the knowledge-text teaches about listening and the other practices, and is free from the notion of being an agent, is indeed established in knowledge.

gloss.en: in listening and the other practices
free from the notion of being an agent

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yad yad uktaṃ jñāna-śāstre śravaṇādi-kameṣu yaḥ|
nirataḥ karma-dhī-hīnaḥ jñāna-niṣṭhaḥ sa eva hi||
units.editionTranslation: Devotion to the knowledge To give up the idea that one is oneself the doer, and to be ever engaged in pursuing the teaching of the jñāna-śāstras is known as devotion to the knowledge of Brahman.

units.label: Verse 124
units.deva:
धन-कान्ता-ज्वरादीनां प्राप्त-काले सुखादिभिः।
विकार-हीनतैव स्यात् सुख-दुःख-समानता॥
units.translation: When wealth, a beloved woman, fever, and the like occur, remaining unaltered through pleasure and the like is equanimity toward pleasure and pain.

gloss.en: of wealth, a beloved woman, fever, and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
dhana-kāntā-jvarādīnāṃ prāpta-kāle sukhādibhiḥ|
vikāra-hīnataiva syāt sukha-duḥkha-samānatā||
units.editionTranslation: Equanimity Not to rejoice at acquiring wealth or woman and not to grieve when ill-health such as fever afflicts a person, but to be ever constant and un-affected in mind is known as equanimity.

units.label: Verse 125
units.deva:
श्रेष्ठं पूज्यं विदित्वा मां मानयन्तु जना भुवि।
इत्यासक्त्या विहीनत्वं मानानासक्तिर् उच्यते॥
units.translation: Not being attached to the thought, “May people on earth honor me, knowing me to be excellent and worthy of reverence,” is called freedom from attachment to honor.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śreṣṭhaṃ pūjyaṃ viditvā māṃ mānayantu janā bhuvi|
ityāsaktyā vihīnatvaṃ mānānāsaktir ucyate||
units.editionTranslation: Absence of self-glorification To regard public opinion with indifference, and not to think too highly of oneself, either on account of one’s birth, social status or public honour, is regarded as the absence of self-glorification.

units.label: Verse 126
units.deva:
सच्-चिन्तनस्य सम्बाधो विघ्नोऽयं निर्जने ततः।
स्थेयम् इत्येक एवास्ति चेत् सैवैकान्त-शीलता॥
units.translation: This crowding obstructs contemplation of reality; therefore one should remain in a secluded place. If one recognizes, “I should stay alone,” that indeed is the habit of solitude.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sac-cintanasya sambādho vighno’yaṃ nirjane tataḥ|
stheyam ityeka evāsti cet saivaikānta-śīlatā||
units.editionTranslation: Love of solitude After having realized that a crowded place is the least conducive to the practice of contemplation, to resort to a sequestered place, in order to meditate upon the Lord is known as the love of solitude.

units.label: Verse 127
units.deva:
संसार-बन्ध-निर्मुक्तिः कदा झटिति मे भवेत्।
इति या सुदृढा बुद्धिर् ईरिता सा मुमुक्षुता॥
units.translation: “When will I be quickly freed from the bond of saṃsāra?”—this firm thought is declared to be the desire for liberation.

gloss.en: release from the bond of saṃsāra

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
saṃsāra-bandha-nirmuktiḥ kadā jhaṭiti me bhavet|
iti yā sudṛḍhā buddhir īritā sā mumukṣutā||
units.editionTranslation: Desirous of liberation The strong feeling to end as early as possible one’s bondage to the world is the characteristic feature of one who desires liberation.

units.label: Verse 128
units.deva:
ब्रह्म-चर्यादिभिर् धर्मैर् बुद्धेर् दोष-निवृत्तये।
दण्डनं दम इत्याहुर् दम-शब्दार्थ-कोविदाः॥
units.translation: The knowers of the meaning of the word dama call the disciplining of the intellect, to remove its faults through brahmacarya and other disciplines, “dama” (restraint).

gloss.en: those skilled in the meaning of the word dama

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
brahma-caryādibhir dharmair buddher doṣa-nivṛttaye|
daṇḍanaṃ dama ityāhur dama-śabdārtha-kovidāḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Restraint of the senses It is by the practice of continence and other virtues that the intellect becomes purified. That is why the wise say that ‘dama’ or the restraint of the senses is like a rod to check erring.

units.label: Verse 129
units.deva:
तत्तद्-वृत्ति-निरोधेन बाह्येन्द्रिय-विनिग्रहः।
योगिनो दम इत्याहुर् मनसः शान्ति-साधनम्॥
units.translation: Yogis call the restraint of the external senses, by stopping their respective activities, “dama”; it is a means for the mind’s peace.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tattad-vṛtti-nirodhena bāhyendriya-vinigrahaḥ|
yogino dama ityāhur manasaḥ śānti-sādhanam||
units.editionTranslation: The yogīs say that ‘dama’ or the restraint of the senses is a means to the control of the mind. They consider that it is conducive to the attainment of tranquility.

units.label: Verse 130
units.deva:
इन्द्रियेष्विन्द्रियार्थेषु प्रवृत्तेषु यदृच्छया।
अनुधावति तान्येव मनो वायुम् इवानलः॥
units.translation: When the senses happen to be engaged with their objects, the mind pursues those very objects, like fire driven by wind.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
indriyeṣvindriyārtheṣu pravṛtteṣu yadṛcchayā|
anudhāvati tānyeva mano vāyum ivānalaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: When the senses pursue the objects of desire however unintentionally, that pursuit acts upon the mind like a wind that fans a flame.

units.label: Verse 131
units.deva:
इन्द्रियेषु निरुद्धेषु त्यक्त्वा वेगं मनः स्वयम्।
सत्त्व-भावम् उपादत्ते प्रसादस् तेन जायते॥
units.translation: When the senses are restrained, the mind itself gives up its impulses and takes on a lucid quality; from that, serenity arises.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
indriyeṣu niruddheṣu tyaktvā vegaṃ manaḥ svayam|
sattva-bhāvam upādatte prasādas tena jāyate||
units.editionTranslation: But where the senses are held under restraint, the mind ceases to be agitated. The mind then regains its pure nature and attains tranquility. It is only when the mind is serene that liberation may be attained. It cannot be attained otherwise.

units.label: Verse 132
units.deva:
प्रसन्ने सति चित्तेऽस्य मुक्तिः सिध्यति नान्यथा।
मनः-प्रसादस्य निदानम् एव
निरोधनं यत् सकलेन्द्रियाणाम्।
बाह्येन्द्रिये साधु निरुध्यमाने
बाह्यार्थ-भोगो मनसो वियुज्यते॥
units.translation: When the mind is clear, liberation is attained; it is not attained otherwise. The restraint of all the senses is indeed the cause of mental serenity. When the external senses are properly restrained, enjoyment of external objects is separated from the mind.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
prasanne sati citte’sya muktiḥ sidhyati nānyathā|
manaḥ-prasādasya nidānam eva
nirodhanaṃ yat sakalendriyāṇām|
bāhyendriye sādhu nirudhyamāne
bāhyārtha-bhogo manaso viyujyate||
units.editionTranslation: Serenity comes only as a result of the control of the senses. Where self-control is firm-based, the desire for the objects of enjoyment does not arise.

units.label: Verse 133
units.deva:
तेन स्व-दौष्ट्यं परिमुच्य चित्तं
शनैः शनैः शान्तिम् उपाददाति।
चित्तस्य बाह्यार्थ-विमोक्षम् एव
मोक्षं विदुर् मोक्षण-लक्षण-ज्ञाः॥
units.translation: By that, the mind, giving up its own faults, gradually attains peace. Those who know the mark of liberation call precisely the mind’s release from external objects “liberation.”

gloss.en: those who know the nature of liberation

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tena sva-dauṣṭyaṃ parimucya cittaṃ
śanaiḥ śanaiḥ śāntim upādadāti|
cittasya bāhyārtha-vimokṣam eva
mokṣaṃ vidur mokṣaṇa-lakṣaṇa-jñāḥ||
units.editionTranslation: In this way, the purified mind freed from all inherent defects attains step by step the peace supreme. Those who are entitled to speak of it say that mokṣa or liberation is nothing more than freeing the mind from all that sullies it.

units.label: Verse 134
units.deva:
दमं विना साधु मनः-प्रसाद-
हेतुं न विद्मः सुकरं मुमुक्षोः।
दमेन चित्तं निज-दोष-जातं
विसृज्य शान्तिं समुपैति शीघ्रम्॥
units.translation: We know of no easy, proper means for a seeker’s mental serenity without restraint. Through restraint, the mind gives up its own faults and soon attains peace.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
damaṃ vinā sādhu manaḥ-prasāda-
hetuṃ na vidmaḥ sukaraṃ mumukṣoḥ|
damena cittaṃ nija-doṣa-jātaṃ
visṛjya śāntiṃ samupaiti śīghram||
units.editionTranslation: By no other means may the seeker after liberation attain peace of mind. When all the defects of the mind have been overcome by the practice of self-restraint, peace follows before long.

units.label: Verse 135
units.deva:
प्राणायामाद् भवति मनसो निश्चलत्वं प्रसादो
यस्याप्यस्य प्रतिनियत-दिग्-देश-कालाद्यवेक्ष्य।
सम्यग्-दृष्ट्या क्वचिद् अपि तया नो दमो हन्यते तत्
कुर्याद् धीमान् दमम् अनलसश् चित्त-शान्त्यै प्रयत्नात्॥
units.translation: Through breath control, steadiness and clarity of mind arise for one who attends to fixed direction, place, time, and the like. Such practice does not undermine right discernment or restraint. The wise should diligently practise restraint to quiet the mind.

gloss.en: fixed direction, place, time, and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
prāṇāyāmād bhavati manaso niścalatvaṃ prasādo
yasyāpyasya pratiniyata-dig-deśa-kālādyavekṣya|
samyag-dṛṣṭyā kvacid api tayā no damo hanyate tat
kuryād dhīmān damam analasaś citta-śāntyai prayatnāt||
units.editionTranslation: This peace of mind is also attained by the practice of prāṇāyāma. But it should be practised in conformity with the Śāstras, and subject to time, place and causality. By means of it, not only are the senses held under restraint, but true insight is also attained. Under no circumstances is such insight destroyed. Let the wise practice self-restraint untiringly and with zeal, in order to attain peace.

units.label: Verse 136
units.deva:
सर्वेन्द्रियाणां गति-निग्रहेण
भोग्येषु दोषाद्यवमर्शनेन।
ईश-प्रसादाच् च गुरोः प्रसादाच्
शान्तिं समायात्य् अचिरेण चित्तम्॥
units.translation: By restraining the movement of all the senses, reflecting on the faults and the like in objects of enjoyment, and through the grace of the Lord and the guru, the mind soon attains peace.

gloss.en: by reflecting on faults and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sarvendriyāṇāṃ gati-nigraheṇa
bhogyeṣu doṣādyavamarśanena|
īśa-prasādāc ca guroḥ prasādāc
śāntiṃ samāyāty acireṇa cittam||
units.editionTranslation: By checking the flow of the senses, by knowing the inherent defects in the objects of enjoyment, by the grace of Īśvara and the guru, the mind attains serenity before long.

units.label: Verse 137
units.deva:
आध्यात्मिकादि यद् दुःखं प्राप्तं प्रारब्ध-वेगतः।
अचिन्तया तत्-सहनं तितिक्षेति निगद्यते॥
units.translation: Whatever suffering of the adhyātmika kind and the like comes through the force of prārabdha, enduring it without brooding is called fortitude.

gloss.en: of the adhyātmika kind and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ādhyātmikādi yad duḥkhaṃ prāptaṃ prārabdha-vegataḥ|
acintayā tat-sahanaṃ titikṣeti nigadyate||
units.editionTranslation: Fortitude It is the result of one’s past actions now bearing fruit that one is called upon to suffer the threefold ills of life. To endure them uncomplainingly and without taking them to heart is indeed fortitude.

units.label: Verse 138
units.deva:
रक्षा तितिक्षा-सदृशी मुमुक्षोर्
न विद्यतेऽसौ पविना न भिद्यते।
याम् एव धीराः कवचीव विघ्नान्
सर्वांस् तृणी-कृत्य जयन्ति मायाम्॥
units.translation: For a seeker of liberation, no protection like fortitude exists; it is not split by a thunderbolt. Wearing it like armor, the wise overcome every obstacle and conquer māyā, treating them as straw.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
rakṣā titikṣā-sadṛśī mumukṣor
na vidyate’sau pavinā na bhidyate|
yām eva dhīrāḥ kavacīva vighnān
sarvāṃs tṛṇī-kṛtya jayanti māyām||
units.editionTranslation: To the seeker after liberation there is no armour stronger than fortitude. No thunderbolt can cleave it. Like a well-armed hero who overcomes all obstacles, he who is protected by fortitude overcomes Māyā, the veil that hides reality.

units.label: Verse 139
units.deva:
क्षमावताम् एव हि योग-सिद्धिः
स्वाराज्य-लक्ष्मी-सुख-भोग-सिद्धिः।
क्षमा-विहीना निपतन्ति विघ्नैर्
वातैर् हताः पर्णचया इव द्रुमात्॥
units.translation: For those who have forbearance alone come success in yoga and attainment of the joy of self-sovereignty. Those without forbearance fall through obstacles like heaps of leaves struck by winds from a tree.

gloss.en: attainment of the joy of self-sovereignty

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kṣamāvatām eva hi yoga-siddhiḥ
svārājya-lakṣmī-sukha-bhoga-siddhiḥ|
kṣamā-vihīnā nipatanti vighnair
vātair hatāḥ parṇacayā iva drumāt||
units.editionTranslation: Only those who are endowed with fortitude may attain the goal of yoga. They alone enjoy the freedom and joy of Self-realization. Others who lack fortitude are overpowered by obstacles; they drift about like withered leaves before the wind. ((ChanU.7.25.2) (Chāndogya Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 140
units.deva:
तितिक्षया तपो दानं यज्ञस् तीर्थं व्रतं श्रुतम्।
भूतिः स्वर्गोऽपवर्गश्च प्राप्यते तत्-तदर्थिभिः॥
units.translation: Through fortitude, those who seek each respective goal attain austerity, giving, sacrifice, pilgrimage, vows, sacred learning, prosperity, heaven, and liberation.

gloss.en: by those seeking each respective goal

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
titikṣayā tapo dānaṃ yajñas tīrthaṃ vrataṃ śrutam|
bhūtiḥ svargo’pavargaśca prāpyate tat-tadarthibhiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Whether it be the practice of tapasya, the offering of gifts, the performance of sacrifices, or going on pilgrimages to holy places and sacred streams, or the attainment of wealth, well-being and spiritual liberation, all that may be attained only by means of fortitude.

units.label: Verse 141
units.deva:
ब्रह्म-चर्यम् अहिंसा च साधूनाम् अप्यगर्हणम्। (अपि चार्हणम्)
पराक्षे-पादि-सहनं तितिक्षोर् एव सिध्यति॥
units.translation: Only a person of fortitude succeeds in brahmacarya and non-injury, in not disparaging the virtuous (or, by an alternate reading, honoring them), and in enduring insults and the like.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
brahma-caryam ahiṃsā ca sādhūnām apyagarhaṇam| (api cārhaṇam)
parākṣe-pādi-sahanaṃ titikṣor eva sidhyati||
units.editionTranslation: Only that person who is endowed with fortitude can be successful in the practice of brahma-carya and ahiṃsā. He alone knows how to honour those who are worthy of reverence, and he alone knows how to endure the reproach of the others.

units.label: Verse 142
units.deva:
साधनेष्वपि सर्वेषु तितिक्षोत्तम-साधनम्।
यत्र विघ्नाः पलायन्ते दैविका अपि भौतिकाः॥
units.translation: Among all disciplines, fortitude is the highest means, through which even divine and earthly obstacles flee.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sādhaneṣvapi sarveṣu titikṣottama-sādhanam|
yatra vighnāḥ palāyante daivikā api bhautikāḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Of all the means available for spiritual liberation fortitude is the noblest. Where there is fortitude, all the obstacles both terrestrial and super-terrestrial vanish before it.

units.label: Verse 143
units.deva:
तितिक्षोर् एव विघ्नेभ्यस् त्वनिवर्तित-चेतसः।
सिध्यन्ति सिद्धयः सर्वा अणिमाद्याः समृद्धयः॥
units.translation: All attainments and powers, beginning with aṇimā, arise for the person of fortitude whose mind does not turn back from obstacles.

gloss.en: whose mind does not turn back

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
titikṣor eva vighnebhyas tvanivartita-cetasaḥ|
sidhyanti siddhayaḥ sarvā aṇimādyāḥ samṛddhayaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: It is only he who is endowed with fortitude and who does not turn away from life’s supreme goal of liberation, whatever obstacles may intervene, that attains all the super natural powers such as aṇimā and the like.

units.label: Verse 144
units.deva:
तस्मान् मुमुक्षोर् अधिका तितिक्षा
सम्पादनीयेप्सित-कार्य-सिद्ध्यै।
तीव्रा मुमुक्षा च महत्य् उपेक्षा
चोभे तितिक्षा-सहकारि-कारणम्॥
units.translation: Therefore, for the seeker of liberation, great fortitude should be cultivated to accomplish the desired aim. Intense longing for liberation and great dispassion are both supports for fortitude.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tasmān mumukṣor adhikā titikṣā
sampādanīyepsita-kārya-siddhyai|
tīvrā mumukṣā ca mahaty upekṣā
cobhe titikṣā-sahakāri-kāraṇam||
units.editionTranslation: Therefore the aspirant after liberation should attain fortitude in full measure. This attainment is facilitated by the earnest desire for liberation and by intense dispassion.

units.label: Verse 145
units.deva:
तत्तत्-काल-समागतामयततेः शान्त्यै प्रवृत्तो यदि
स्यात् तत्तत्-परिहारकौषध-रतस् तच्-चिन्तने तत्-परः।
तद् भिक्षुः श्रवणादि-धर्म-रहितो भूत्वा मृतश् चेत्ततः
किं सिद्धं फलम् आप्नुयाद् उभयथा भ्रष्टो भवेत् स्वार्थतः॥
units.translation: If a mendicant becomes intent on relief from the mass of ailments arriving at their respective times, devoted to medicines that remove each one and absorbed in thinking about them, then—if he dies after becoming devoid of disciplines such as listening—what result has he gained? In either case, he has fallen away from his own aim.

gloss.en: of the mass of ailments arriving at their respective times
devoted to medicines for removing each
devoid of disciplines beginning with listening

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tattat-kāla-samāgatāmayatateḥ śāntyai pravṛtto yadi
syāt tattat-parihārakauṣadha-ratas tac-cintane tat-paraḥ|
tad bhikṣuḥ śravaṇādi-dharma-rahito bhūtvā mṛtaś cettataḥ
kiṃ siddhaṃ phalam āpnuyād ubhayathā bhraṣṭo bhavet svārthataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Of what avail is it if a sannyāsin should abandon his sva-dharma, that of harkening to the Vedas, and waste his time in worrying himself over the various ailments to which his body may be subject, and in gathering medicines to cure them? Such a person loses both here and hereafter.

units.label: Verse 146
units.deva:
योगम् अभ्यस्यतो भिक्षोर् योगाच्चलित-चेतसः।
प्राप्य पुण्य-कृतांल् लोकान् इत्यादि प्राह केशवः॥
units.translation: Keśava says, “The mendicant who practises yoga, whose mind has slipped from yoga, after reaching the worlds of the meritorious…” and so on.

gloss.en: of those who have done merit

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yogam abhyasyato bhikṣor yogāccalita-cetasaḥ|
prāpya puṇya-kṛtāṃl lokān ityādi prāha keśavaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: But the sannyāsin who strives after communion with Brahman, even if he should deviate from his resolve attains the regions of the blessed, as the Lord Keśava proclaims.

units.label: Verse 147
units.deva:
न तु कृत्वैव संन्यासं तूष्णीम् एव मृतस्य हि।
पुण्य-लोक-गतिं ब्रूते भगवान् न्यास-मात्रतः॥
units.translation: But the Blessed Lord does not say that one who has merely taken renunciation and then died quietly obtains a world of merit through renunciation alone.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
na tu kṛtvaiva saṃnyāsaṃ tūṣṇīm eva mṛtasya hi|
puṇya-loka-gatiṃ brūte bhagavān nyāsa-mātrataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: But the Lord does not say that merely by virtue of one’s formal sannyāsa, any one who does nothing else might attain after his death those happy regions that are reserved for the blessed. ((BhG.6.37) (Bhagavad Gītā), (.41) (Bhagavad Gītā))

units.label: Verse 148
units.deva:
न च संन्यसनाद् एव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति।
इत्यनुष्ठेय-सन्त्यागात् सिद्ध्यभावम् उवाच च॥
units.translation: He also said, “One does not attain success through renunciation alone,” thereby stating that success does not come from abandoning the duties that must be performed.

gloss.en: from abandoning what should be performed

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
na ca saṃnyasanād eva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati|
ityanuṣṭheya-santyāgāt siddhyabhāvam uvāca ca||
units.editionTranslation: In fact the Lord says, “By mere sannyāsa he does not (completely) attain the goal (of sannyāsa)” implying thereby that by abandoning one’s duties, one misses the goal. ((BhG.3.4) (Bhagavad Gītā))

units.label: Verse 149
units.deva:
तस्मात् तितिक्षया सोढ्वा तत्तद्-दुःखम् उपागतम्।
कुर्याच् छक्त्यनुरूपेण श्रवणादि शनैः शनैः॥
units.translation: Therefore, having endured through fortitude whatever particular suffering has come, one should gradually undertake listening and the other practices, according to one’s capacity.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tasmāt titikṣayā soḍhvā tattad-duḥkham upāgatam|
kuryāc chaktyanurūpeṇa śravaṇādi śanaiḥ śanaiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: It is therefore imperative that by the practice of fortitude one should conquer such sorrow as falls to one’s lot. One should then step by step direct one’s attention to such disciplines as listening to the Śruti according to the measure of one’s ability.

units.label: Verse 150
units.deva:
प्रयोजनं तितिक्षायाः साधितायाः प्रयत्नतः।
प्राप्त-दुःखासहिष्णुत्वे न किञ्चिदपि दृश्यते॥
units.translation: If one cannot endure the suffering that has come, no purpose at all is seen in the fortitude cultivated through effort.

gloss.en: when unable to endure suffering that has come

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
prayojanaṃ titikṣāyāḥ sādhitāyāḥ prayatnataḥ|
prāpta-duḥkhāsahiṣṇutve na kiñcidapi dṛśyate||
units.editionTranslation: What is the use of acquiring fortitude with great effort, if one could not endure such affliction as falls to one’s lot?

units.label: Verse 151
units.deva:
साधनत्वेन दृष्टानां सर्वेषाम् अपि कर्मणाम्।
विधिना यः परित्यागः स संन्यासः सतां मतः॥
units.translation: The wise regard as renunciation the prescribed relinquishment of all actions that are regarded as means.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sādhanatvena dṛṣṭānāṃ sarveṣām api karmaṇām|
vidhinā yaḥ parityāgaḥ sa saṃnyāsaḥ satāṃ mataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Renunciation In the opinion of the wise, renunciation means the abandonment in proper form of all actions, which are enjoined as means to earthly and heavenly happiness.

units.label: Verse 152
units.deva:
उपरमयति कर्माणीत्युपरति-शब्देन कथ्यते न्यासः।
न्यासेन हि सर्वेषां श्रुत्या प्रोक्तो विकर्मणां त्यागः॥
units.translation: The word “withdrawal” (uparati) means causing actions to cease; through renunciation, scripture indeed teaches the relinquishment of all forbidden actions.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
uparamayati karmāṇītyuparati-śabdena kathyate nyāsaḥ|
nyāsena hi sarveṣāṃ śrutyā prokto vikarmaṇāṃ tyāgaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The word ‘uparati’ means cessation of action. It signifies renunciation. By implication, this includes the renunciation of evil actions also, according to the Śruti.

units.label: Verse 153
units.deva:
कर्मणा साध्यमानस्यानित्यत्वं श्रूयते यतः।
कर्मणानेन किं नित्य-फलेप्सोः परमार्थिनः॥
units.translation: Because impermanence is heard of what is accomplished by action, what use is this action to a seeker of the highest truth who desires an eternal result?

gloss.en: for one seeking an eternal result
for a seeker of the highest truth

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
karmaṇā sādhyamānasyānityatvaṃ śrūyate yataḥ|
karmaṇānena kiṃ nitya-phalepsoḥ paramārthinaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The Śruti points out that all things that are achieved by means of action are transitory. Such being the case, of what avail are actions to one who is devoted to the highest truth, and who seeks the eternal good? ((MunU.1.2.11) (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 154
units.deva:
उत्पाद्यम् आप्यं संस्कार्यं विकार्यं परिगण्यते।
चतुर्विधं कर्म-साध्यं फलं नान्यद् इतः परम्॥
units.translation: A result produced by action is counted as fourfold: something to be produced, attained, purified, or transformed. There is nothing beyond these kinds.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
utpādyam āpyaṃ saṃskāryaṃ vikāryaṃ parigaṇyate|
caturvidhaṃ karma-sādhyaṃ phalaṃ nānyad itaḥ param||
units.editionTranslation: By means of action one might produce something new, (make) perfect something already existing, change the shape of things, or reach a goal. There is nothing else that is possible.

units.label: Verse 155
units.deva:
नैतद्-अन्यतरं ब्रह्म कदा भवितुम् अर्हति।
स्वतः-सिद्धं सर्वदाप्तं शुद्धं निर्मलम् अक्रियम्॥
units.translation: Brahman can never be any one of these [four results of action], because it is self-established, always attained, pure, stainless, and actionless.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
naitad-anyataraṃ brahma kadā bhavitum arhati|
svataḥ-siddhaṃ sarvadāptaṃ śuddhaṃ nirmalam akriyam||
units.editionTranslation: As for Brahman, it is self-existent. It is ever attained, eternally pure, devoid of taint, and subject to no modification. That is why Brahman cannot be realized by means of action.

units.label: Verse 156
units.deva:
न चास्य कश्चिज् जनितेत्य् आगमेन निषिध्यते।
कारणं ब्रह्म तत् तस्माद् ब्रह्म नोत्पाद्यम् इष्यते॥
units.translation: Scripture denies that Brahman has any originator. Brahman is the cause; therefore Brahman is not regarded as something produced.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
na cāsya kaścij janitety āgamena niṣidhyate|
kāraṇaṃ brahma tat tasmād brahma notpādyam iṣyate||
units.editionTranslation: The Āgama-Śāstras say that Brahman is self-existent. ‘It has no origin’. It is not caused by anything else; and therefore it cannot be the product of any kind of activity. ((SvetU.1.9) (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 157
units.deva:
आप्त्राप्ययोस् तु भेदश् चेद् आप्त्रा चाप्यम् अवाप्यते।
आप्तृ-स्वरूपम् एवैतद् ब्रह्म नाप्यं कदाचन॥
units.translation: If the attainer and what is attained were different, the attainer could attain the object. But this Brahman is the very nature of the attainer; it is never something to be attained.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
āptrāpyayos tu bhedaś ced āptrā cāpyam avāpyate|
āptṛ-svarūpam evaitad brahma nāpyaṃ kadācana||
units.editionTranslation: We may reach a goal only when the goal is outside us, and is other than ourselves. But Brahman is not other than ourselves. It is our inmost Self. Therefore Brahman is not something to be attained afresh.

units.label: Verse 158
units.deva:
मलिनस्यैव संस्कारो दर्पणादेर् इहेष्यते।
व्योमवन् नित्य-शुद्धस्य ब्रह्मणो नैव संस्क्रिया॥
units.translation: Here, purification is intended only for something impure, such as a mirror. No purification applies to Brahman, which is eternally pure like space.

gloss.en: of a mirror and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
malinasyaiva saṃskāro darpaṇāder iheṣyate|
vyomavan nitya-śuddhasya brahmaṇo naiva saṃskriyā||
units.editionTranslation: An external object, such as a dust-laden mirror, lends itself to being cleansed. But Brahman is as pure as the sky. How can that which is perfect be made more perfect?

units.label: Verse 159
units.deva:
केन दुष्टेन युज्येत वस्तु निर्मलम् अक्रियम्।
यद्-योगाद् आगतं दोषं संस्कारो विनिवर्तयेत्॥
units.translation: How could a stainless, actionless reality be joined to any impurity, so that purification might remove a defect that came from that connection?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kena duṣṭena yujyeta vastu nirmalam akriyam|
yad-yogād āgataṃ doṣaṃ saṃskāro vinivartayet||
units.editionTranslation: Brahman is devoid of stain, and participates in no kind of activity. By what means can it come into contact with evil, be tainted by it, or become subject to purification by means of action?

units.label: Verse 160
units.deva:
निर्गुणस्य गुणाधानम् अपि नैवोपपद्यते।
केवलो निर्गुणश् चेति नैर्गुण्यं श्रूयते यतः॥
units.translation: Because scripture repeatedly teaches that Brahman is alone and without qualities, it is not reasonable to add qualities to what is qualityless.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
nirguṇasya guṇādhānam api naivopapadyate|
kevalo nirguṇaś ceti nairguṇyaṃ śrūyate yataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: In the words of the Śruti, Brahman is devoid of attributes: ‘Kevalo nirguṇaśca.’ Such being the case, it is not possible to confer upon it any new attributes. ((SvetU.6.11) (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 161
units.deva:
सावयवस्य क्षीरादेर् वस्तुनः परिणामिनः।
येन केन विकारित्वं स्यान् नो निष्कर्म-वस्तुनः॥
units.translation: A composite, changeable object such as milk can be altered by one thing or another; the actionless reality cannot.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sāvayavasya kṣīrāder vastunaḥ pariṇāminaḥ|
yena kena vikāritvaṃ syān no niṣkarma-vastunaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: All objects which are compounds, such as milk for instance, may be acted upon by other objects and are liable to change. But Brahman is not a compound of parts and action affects it not. What external object can modify its nature?

units.label: Verse 162
units.deva:
निष्कलं निष्क्रियं शान्तं निरवद्यं निरञ्जनम्।
इत्येव वस्तुनस् तत्त्वं श्रुति-युक्ति-व्यवस्थितम्॥
units.translation: “Without parts, actionless, peaceful, faultless, stainless”—this indeed is the nature of reality, established by scripture and reasoning.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
niṣkalaṃ niṣkriyaṃ śāntaṃ niravadyaṃ nirañjanam|
ityeva vastunas tattvaṃ śruti-yukti-vyavasthitam||
units.editionTranslation: Brahman is ever tranquil, faultless, free from impurity, devoid of parts, and actionless. The Śruti proclaims that such is the nature of the ultimate Reality, and reason approves it.

units.label: Verse 163
units.deva:
तस्मान् न कर्म-साध्यत्वं ब्रह्मणोऽस्ति कुतश्चन।
कर्म-साध्यं त्वनित्यं हि ब्रह्म नित्यं सना-तनम्॥
units.translation: Therefore Brahman is in no way something produced by action. What is produced by action is impermanent, whereas Brahman is eternal and everlasting.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tasmān na karma-sādhyatvaṃ brahmaṇo’sti kutaścana|
karma-sādhyaṃ tvanityaṃ hi brahma nityaṃ sanā-tanam||
units.editionTranslation: It therefore follows that we cannot gain Brahman as product of any kind of activity. Moreover, what is gained by action lasts only for a while, whereas Brahman is eternal and is self-existent.

units.label: Verse 164
units.deva:
देहादिः क्षीयते लोको यथैवं कर्मणा चितः।
तथैवामुष्मिको लोकः सञ्चितः पुण्य-कर्मणा॥
units.translation: As the world of the body and the like, formed through action, perishes, so too the otherworldly realm accumulated through meritorious action perishes.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
dehādiḥ kṣīyate loko yathaivaṃ karmaṇā citaḥ|
tathaivāmuṣmiko lokaḥ sañcitaḥ puṇya-karmaṇā||
units.editionTranslation: Our physical bodies as well as the various objects of enjoyment are the outcome of whatever action we have performed in our previous lives; and the body falls according to the law of causation. Similarly in the world to come also, whatever may be achieved by means of meritorious action must necessarily come to an end.

units.label: Verse 165
units.deva:
कृतकत्वम् अनित्यत्वे हेतुर् जागर्ति सर्वदा।
तस्माद् अनित्ये स्वर्गादौ पण्डितः को नु मुह्यति॥
units.translation: The fact of being made is always an evident reason for impermanence. So what wise person would be deluded by heaven and the like, which are impermanent?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kṛtakatvam anityatve hetur jāgarti sarvadā|
tasmād anitye svargādau paṇḍitaḥ ko nu muhyati||
units.editionTranslation: That which is achieved by means of action cannot be eternal, for such is the law. Therefore even the happiness of svarga (heaven) can last only for a while. Would any wise person covet it?

units.label: Verse 166
units.deva:
जगद्-धेतोस् तु नित्यत्वं सर्वेषाम् अपि सम्मतम्।
जगद्धेतुत्वम् अस्यैव वावदीति श्रुतिर् मुहुः॥
units.translation: All agree that the cause of the universe is eternal; scripture repeatedly declares that Brahman alone is the cause of the universe.

gloss.en: of the cause of the universe
being the cause of the universe

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
jagad-dhetos tu nityatvaṃ sarveṣām api sammatam|
jagaddhetutvam asyaiva vāvadīti śrutir muhuḥ||
units.editionTranslation: But that which is the cause of the universe must needs be eternal; upon that all are agreed. And it is reiterated in the Śruti that Brahman is the cause of the universe.

units.label: Verse 167
units.deva:
ऐतदात्म्यम् इदं सर्वं तत् सत्यम् इति च श्रुतिः।
अस्यैव नित्यतां ब्रूते जगद्धेतोः सतः स्फुटम्॥
units.translation: Scripture says, “All this has That as its Self; That is real.” It clearly teaches the eternality of this Being, the cause of the universe.

gloss.en: of the cause of the universe

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ tat satyam iti ca śrutiḥ|
asyaiva nityatāṃ brūte jagaddhetoḥ sataḥ sphuṭam||
units.editionTranslation: The Śruti says, “All this is ensouled by Being. Being alone is real.” The Śruti thus explicitly asserts that this ultimate Being, the cause of the universe is eternal. ((ChanU.6.8.7) (Chāndogya Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 168
units.deva:
न कर्मणा न प्रजया धनेनेति स्वयं श्रुतिः।
कर्मणो मोक्ष-हेतुत्वं साक्षाद् एव निषेधति॥
units.translation: Scripture itself directly denies that action is a cause of liberation when it says, “Not by action, not by offspring, not by wealth.”
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
na karmaṇā na prajayā dhaneneti svayaṃ śrutiḥ|
karmaṇo mokṣa-hetutvaṃ sākṣād eva niṣedhati||
units.editionTranslation: Consequently when the Śruti declares, ‘nor by action, nor by begetting children, nor by acquiring wealth’ may Brahman be attained, it explicitly refutes the view that liberation may be attained by means of action.

units.label: Verse 169
units.deva:
प्रत्यग्-ब्रह्म-विचार-पूर्वम् उभयोर् एकत्व-बोधाद् विना
कैवल्यं पुरुषस्य सिध्यति पर-ब्रह्मात्मता-लक्षणम्।
न स्नानैर् अपि कीर्तनैर् अपि जपैर् नो कृच्छ्र-चान्द्रायणैर्
नो वाप्य् अध्वर-यज्ञ-दान-निगमैर् नो मन्त्र-तन्त्रैर् अपि॥
units.translation: A person’s liberation, whose nature is identity with supreme Brahman, is attained only through understanding the unity of the inward Self and Brahman, preceded by inquiry into both—not through baths, hymns, recitations, severe vows such as kṛcchra and cāndrāyaṇa, sacrifices, offerings, Vedic texts, mantras, or ritual manuals.

gloss.en: preceded by inquiry into the inward Self and Brahman
characterized by identity with supreme Brahman
by sacrifices, offerings, and Vedic texts

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
pratyag-brahma-vicāra-pūrvam ubhayor ekatva-bodhād vinā
kaivalyaṃ puruṣasya sidhyati para-brahmātmatā-lakṣaṇam|
na snānair api kīrtanair api japair no kṛcchra-cāndrāyaṇair
no vāpy adhvara-yajña-dāna-nigamair no mantra-tantrair api||
units.editionTranslation: Liberation, consisting of the utter identity with Brahman, is unattainable except through the comprehension of the unity of the Ātman and Brahman, through a process of rational enquiry into the two. It is not to be attained by bathing in sacred streams, chanting holy hymns, reciting sacred formulas or by means of hard penances such as kṛccra and cāndrāyaṇa, or by means of sacrifices, charity, scriptures and sacred syllables, and other approved actions.

units.label: Verse 170
units.deva:
ज्ञानाद् एव तु कैवल्यम् इति श्रुत्या निगद्यते।
ज्ञानस्य मुक्ति-हेतुत्वम् अन्य-व्यावृत्ति-पूर्वकम्॥
units.translation: Scripture says, “Liberation is attained by knowledge alone,” and declares knowledge to be the cause of freedom after excluding all other means.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
jñānād eva tu kaivalyam iti śrutyā nigadyate|
jñānasya mukti-hetutvam anya-vyāvṛtti-pūrvakam||
units.editionTranslation: This is why the Śruti says, ‘By knowledge alone doth one attain liberation.’ By proclaiming the unique nature of knowledge the Śruti negates all other means.

units.label: Verse 171
units.deva:
विवेकिनो विरक्तस्य ब्रह्म-नित्यत्व-वेदिनः।
तद्-भावेच्छोर् अनित्यार्थे तत्-सामग्र्ये कुतोऽरतिः॥
units.translation: How could there be disinterest in impermanent aims and the means for them for a discerning, dispassionate person who knows Brahman’s eternality and wishes to become that?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
vivekino viraktasya brahma-nityatva-vedinaḥ|
tad-bhāvecchor anityārthe tat-sāmagrye kuto’ratiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Is it ever possible that a man of discrimination who knows that Brahman is eternal, who desires to be Brahman, and is indifferent to all else, would have any longing for perishable objects or seek the means to acquire them?

units.label: Verse 172
units.deva:
तस्माद् अनित्ये स्वर्गादौ साधनत्वेन चोदितम्।
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं चापि सर्वं कर्म ससाधनम्॥
units.translation: Therefore all action—daily and occasional, with its means—is prescribed as a means toward impermanent heaven and the like.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tasmād anitye svargādau sādhanatvena coditam|
nityaṃ naimittikaṃ cāpi sarvaṃ karma sasādhanam||
units.editionTranslation: A seeker after liberation who is desirous of being Brahman must needs give up all rituals, both those that should be observed daily, and those that are performed on special occasions, as well as those that are performed in order to attain reward in heaven.

units.label: Verse 173
units.deva:
मुमुक्षुणा परित्याज्यं ब्रह्म-भावम् अभीप्सुना।
मुमुक्षोर् अपि कर्मास्तु श्रवणं चापि साधनम्॥
units.translation: For the seeker who longs for the state of Brahman, [action is] to be relinquished; yet let action and listening also be means for the seeker of liberation.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
mumukṣuṇā parityājyaṃ brahma-bhāvam abhīpsunā|
mumukṣor api karmāstu śravaṇaṃ cāpi sādhanam||
units.editionTranslation: There are some who opine that the earnest aspirant after liberation should continue the performance of action, and observe the prescribed rituals, while pursuing one’s quest after Brahman as taught in the Vedas.

units.label: Verse 174
units.deva:
हस्तवद् द्वयम् एतस्य स्वकार्यं साधयिष्यति।
यथा विजृम्भते दीपो ऋजू-करण-कर्मणा॥
units.translation: The two [action and knowledge] will accomplish this person’s purpose, like a lamp shines when its wick is straightened.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
hastavad dvayam etasya svakāryaṃ sādhayiṣyati|
yathā vijṛmbhate dīpo ṛjū-karaṇa-karmaṇā||
units.editionTranslation: Such combination is compared to the complementary function of the two hands which are essential for action. They say that by such conjunction knowledge shines the brighter, like a (oil) lamp that has been trimmed.

units.label: Verse 175
units.deva:
तथा श्रवण-जो बोधः पुंसो विहित-कर्मणा।
अतः सापेक्षितं ज्ञानम् अथवापि समुच्चयम्॥
units.translation: Likewise, [they argue,] insight born from listening in a person depends on prescribed action. Therefore knowledge is dependent [on action], or [knowledge and action] are combined.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tathā śravaṇa-jo bodhaḥ puṃso vihita-karmaṇā|
ataḥ sāpekṣitaṃ jñānam athavāpi samuccayam||
units.editionTranslation: Some of the knowers of Brahman say that knowledge forms an aspect of the performance of rituals; there are others who put them on a par and who consider that the combination of knowledge and action constitutes the most efficacious means of attaining liberation.

units.label: Verse 176
units.deva:
मोक्षस्य साधनम् इति वदन्ति ब्रह्म-वादिनः।
मुमुक्षोर् युज्यते त्यागः कथं विहित-कर्मणः॥
units.translation: The proponents of Brahman say, “Action is a means to liberation.” How, then, is relinquishing prescribed action fitting for a seeker of liberation?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
mokṣasya sādhanam iti vadanti brahma-vādinaḥ|
mumukṣor yujyate tyāgaḥ kathaṃ vihita-karmaṇaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Such Brahma-vādins therefore ask the question: “How is it possible for an aspirant after liberation to abandon the prescribed rituals?”

units.label: Verse 177
units.deva:
इति शङ्का न कर्तव्या मूढवत् पण्डितोत्तमैः।
कर्मणः फलम् अन्यत् तु श्रवणस्य फलं पृथक्॥
units.translation: The best of the wise should not raise such a doubt as fools do. The result of action is one thing, but the result of listening is distinct.

gloss.en: by the best of the wise

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
iti śaṅkā na kartavyā mūḍhavat paṇḍitottamaiḥ|
karmaṇaḥ phalam anyat tu śravaṇasya phalaṃ pṛthak||
units.editionTranslation: Let not the wise entertain any such unwise doubts. The benefit to be gained by the performance of rituals is one thing; the benefit to be attained by the study of Vedānta is altogether different.

units.label: Verse 178
units.deva:
वैलक्षण्यं च सामग्र्योश् चोभयत्राधिकारिणोः।
कामी कर्मण्यधिकृतो निष्कामी श्रवणे मतः॥
units.translation: The qualifications and required means differ in the two cases: the desirous person is qualified for action, while the desireless person is considered qualified for listening.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
vailakṣaṇyaṃ ca sāmagryoś cobhayatrādhikāriṇoḥ|
kāmī karmaṇyadhikṛto niṣkāmī śravaṇe mataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Both as regards the aim, and means to be employed, there is considerable difference between them. One who has desires performs the prescribed rituals; but one who has no desires studies Vedānta.

units.label: Verse 179
units.deva:
अर्थी समर्थ इत्यादि लक्षणं कर्मिणो मतम्।
परीक्ष्य लोकान् इत्यादि लक्षणं मोक्ष-काङ्क्षिणः॥
units.translation: A person who desires results, is capable, and so on is considered qualified for action. “Having examined the worlds,” and so on, describes the one who longs for liberation.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
arthī samartha ityādi lakṣaṇaṃ karmiṇo matam|
parīkṣya lokān ityādi lakṣaṇaṃ mokṣa-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: A man who has the requisite qualification, such as physical strength and the desire for reward in heaven is free to perform the prescribed rituals. But he who is solely intent upon the pursuit of liberation gets disgusted after examining the benefits to be derived by the performance of rituals.

units.label: Verse 180
units.deva:
मोक्षाधिकारी संन्यासी गृहस्थः किल कर्मणि।
कर्मणः साधनं भार्या स्रुक्-स्रुवादि-परिग्रहः॥
units.translation: The renunciant is qualified for liberation; the householder, indeed, for action. A wife and the possession of ladles, spoons, and the like are means for action.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
mokṣādhikārī saṃnyāsī gṛhasthaḥ kila karmaṇi|
karmaṇaḥ sādhanaṃ bhāryā sruk-sruvādi-parigrahaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: It is the all-renouncing monk who seeks liberation. It is the householder with a wife and the requisite utensils for sacrifice that performs rituals. ((MunU.1.2.12) (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 181
units.deva:
नैवान्य-साधनापेक्षा शुश्रूषोस् तु गुरुं विना।
उपर्य् उपर्य् अहङ्कारो वर्धते कर्मणा भृशम्॥
units.translation: For one eager to learn, no other means is needed apart from the guru. Through action, ego grows stronger and stronger.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
naivānya-sādhanāpekṣā śuśrūṣos tu guruṃ vinā|
upary upary ahaṅkāro vardhate karmaṇā bhṛśam||
units.editionTranslation: The only sādhana that the sannyāsī performs is that of service to the guru; for, the sannyāsī knows that the more rituals one performs the greater is one’s sense of egoism.

units.label: Verse 182
units.deva:
अहङ्कारस्य विच्छित्तिः श्रवणेन प्रतिक्षणम्।
प्रवर्तकं कर्म-शास्त्रं ज्ञान-शास्त्रं निवर्तकम्॥
units.translation: Listening cuts away ego at every moment. The text on action impels [one to act]; the text on knowledge turns [one away from action].
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ahaṅkārasya vicchittiḥ śravaṇena pratikṣaṇam|
pravartakaṃ karma-śāstraṃ jñāna-śāstraṃ nivartakam||
units.editionTranslation: But egoism is utterly effaced by harkening again and again to the Śruti. The Śāstras which enjoin rituals bind a man to the world; but the Śāstras which impart knowledge lead to one’s release from the world.

units.label: Verse 183
units.deva:
इत्यादि वैपरीत्यं तत्-साधने चाधिकारिणोः।
द्वयोः परस्-परापेक्षा विद्यते न कदाचन॥
units.translation: This and the like shows opposition in the means and in the qualified persons. The two never depend on each other.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ityādi vaiparītyaṃ tat-sādhane cādhikāriṇoḥ|
dvayoḥ paras-parāpekṣā vidyate na kadācana||
units.editionTranslation: Therefore knowledge and rituals stand to each other in mutual opposition both as regards the means to be employed, and the agents entitled to them. At no time either of the two requires the support of the other. ((AtB.3) (Ātma Bodha))

units.label: Verse 184
units.deva:
सामग्र्योश् चोभयोस् तद्वद् उभयत्राधिकारिणोः।
ऊर्ध्वं नयति विज्ञानम् अधः प्रापयति क्रिया॥
units.translation: The means and the qualified persons are opposed in both cases: knowledge leads upward; action carries [one] downward.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sāmagryoś cobhayos tadvad ubhayatrādhikāriṇoḥ|
ūrdhvaṃ nayati vijñānam adhaḥ prāpayati kriyā||
units.editionTranslation: They are incompatible both as regards the agent who performs them and the means to be employed. Knowledge leads one upward to Brahman; but rituals drag one downward, to the Earth.

units.label: Verse 185
units.deva:
कथम् अन्योन्य-सापेक्षा कथं वापि समुच्चयः।
यथाग्नेस् तृण-कूटस्य तेजसस् तिमिरस्य च॥
units.translation: How could there be mutual dependence or combination, as between fire and a heap of straw, or between light and darkness?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
katham anyonya-sāpekṣā kathaṃ vāpi samuccayaḥ|
yathāgnes tṛṇa-kūṭasya tejasas timirasya ca||
units.editionTranslation: What relation can there be between knowledge and rituals, other than that which is to be formed between a bundle of straw and a lighted match?

units.label: Verse 186
units.deva:
सह-योगो न घटते तथैव ज्ञान-कर्मणोः।
किमूपकुर्याज् ज्ञानस्य कर्म स्व-प्रतियोगिनः।
यस्य संनिधिमात्रेण स्वयं न स्फूर्तिम् ऋच्छति॥
units.translation: Association of knowledge and action does not fit. What help could action offer knowledge, its opposite, when through knowledge’s mere presence action itself no longer shines forth?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
saha-yogo na ghaṭate tathaiva jñāna-karmaṇoḥ|
kimūpakuryāj jñānasya karma sva-pratiyoginaḥ|
yasya saṃnidhimātreṇa svayaṃ na sphūrtim ṛcchati||
units.editionTranslation: Knowledge and rituals are as incompatible as light and darkness. Knowledge, therefore, cannot be combined with action. How can action aid knowledge, when one is opposed to the other? It destroys action by its very proximity to it.

units.label: Verse 187
units.deva:
कोटीन्धनाद्रिज्वलितोऽपि वह्निर्
अर्कस्य नार्हत्य् उपकर्तुम् ईषत्।
यथा तथा कर्म-सहस्र-कोटिर्
ज्ञानस्य किं नु स्वयम् एव लीयते॥
units.translation: Even a fire blazing from a mountain of countless logs cannot help the sun in the least. Likewise, what can countless actions do for knowledge? They themselves simply dissolve.

gloss.en: blazing from a mountain of countless fuel

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
koṭīndhanādrijvalito’pi vahnir
arkasya nārhaty upakartum īṣat|
yathā tathā karma-sahasra-koṭir
jñānasya kiṃ nu svayam eva līyate||
units.editionTranslation: Logs of wood may be heaped mountain high, and be ignited. The resulting fire cannot contribute to the light of the Sun. It is the same with rituals also; in the proximity of knowledge, even a thousand crores of rituals would be of no avail.

units.label: Verse 188
units.deva:
एक-कर्त्राश्रयौ हस्तौ कर्मण्यधिकृताव् उभौ।
सह-योगस् तयोर् युक्तो न तथा ज्ञान-कर्मणोः॥
units.translation: Both hands depend on one doer and are equipped for action; their working together is fitting. Knowledge and action are not so.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
eka-kartrāśrayau hastau karmaṇyadhikṛtāv ubhau|
saha-yogas tayor yukto na tathā jñāna-karmaṇoḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Inasmuch as the two hands obey the will of a single master, it is possible to co-ordinate them; but such is not the case as between knowledge and action.

units.label: Verse 189
units.deva:
कर्त्रा कर्तुम् अकर्तुं वाप्य् अन्यथा कर्म शक्यते।
न तथा वस्तुनो ज्ञानं कर्तृ-तन्त्रं कदाचन॥
units.translation: An agent can perform an action, refrain from it, or perform it differently. Knowledge of a thing, however, is never governed by the agent.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kartrā kartum akartuṃ vāpy anyathā karma śakyate|
na tathā vastuno jñānaṃ kartṛ-tantraṃ kadācana||
units.editionTranslation: As for rituals, one is free to perform them in a given manner, to alter the manner of performance, or to abstain from performing them; but knowledge depends upon what it is in itself, and it does not depend upon human agency.

units.label: Verse 190
units.deva:
यथा वस्तु तथा ज्ञानं प्रमाणेन विजायते।
नापेक्षते च यत् किञ्चित् कर्म वा युक्ति-कौशलम्॥
units.translation: Knowledge arises according to the thing as it is, through a valid means of knowing. It depends on no action or skill in reasoning whatsoever.

gloss.en: through a valid means of knowing

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yathā vastu tathā jñānaṃ pramāṇena vijāyate|
nāpekṣate ca yat kiñcit karma vā yukti-kauśalam||
units.editionTranslation: Knowledge is the awareness of what a thing is in itself, it is gained by the help of the valid means of knowledge. Neither logical acumen, nor ritualistic observances are of avail in acquiring knowledge.

units.label: Verse 191
units.deva:
ज्ञानस्य वस्तु-तन्त्रत्वे संशयाद्य्-उदयः कथम्।
अतो न वास्तवं ज्ञानम् इति नो शङ्क्यतां बुधैः॥
units.translation: “If knowledge depends on the object, how can doubts and the like arise? So do not doubt, wise ones, that knowledge is therefore unreal.”

gloss.en: the arising of doubt and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
jñānasya vastu-tantratve saṃśayādy-udayaḥ katham|
ato na vāstavaṃ jñānam iti no śaṅkyatāṃ budhaiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: “If knowledge should depend upon the thing in itself, how can doubt arise? Because doubts arise, knowledge is not real.” Let not the wise raise this objection.

units.label: Verse 192
units.deva:
प्रमाणासौष्ठव-वृतं संशयादि न वास्तवम्।
श्रुतिप्रमाणसुष्ठुत्वे ज्ञानं भवति वास्तवम्॥
units.translation: Doubt and the like, arising from defects in the means of knowing, are not real. When the means of scripture are sound, knowledge is real.

gloss.en: arising from defects in a means of knowing
when the scriptural means of knowing is sound

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
pramāṇāsauṣṭhava-vṛtaṃ saṃśayādi na vāstavam|
śrutipramāṇasuṣṭhutve jñānaṃ bhavati vāstavam||
units.editionTranslation: Doubts etc. are not real, for they are due to the imperfection of the way of knowing. As our knowledge of the Real is well-based upon the Śruti, it is self-validated.

units.label: Verse 193
units.deva:
वस्तु तावत् परं ब्रह्म नित्यं सत्यं ध्रुवं विभु।
श्रुति-प्रमाणे तज्-ज्ञानं स्याद् एव निरपेक्षकम्॥
units.translation: The supreme reality is indeed Brahman: eternal, true, firm, and all-pervading. When scripture is the means of knowing, knowledge of That is indeed independent.

gloss.en: when scripture is the means of knowing

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
vastu tāvat paraṃ brahma nityaṃ satyaṃ dhruvaṃ vibhu|
śruti-pramāṇe taj-jñānaṃ syād eva nirapekṣakam||
units.editionTranslation: Śruti declares that Brahman is eternal, true, and real. Brahman is not subject to any kind of change; and Śruti is the proof of it. Therefore the knowledge of Brahman does not depend upon anything else.

units.label: Verse 194
units.deva:
रूप-ज्ञानं यथा सम्यग्-दृष्टौ सत्यां भवेत् तथा।
श्रुति-प्रमाणे सत्येव ज्ञानं भवति वास्तवम्॥
units.translation: Just as knowledge of form arises when vision is sound, so knowledge is real when scripture is present as a valid means of knowing.

gloss.en: when scripture is a valid means of knowing

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
rūpa-jñānaṃ yathā samyag-dṛṣṭau satyāṃ bhavet tathā|
śruti-pramāṇe satyeva jñānaṃ bhavati vāstavam||
units.editionTranslation: Just as the eye that is devoid of defects comprehends the shape of things in their totality, so also the Śruti, in as much as it is free from defects, comprehends the whole of Brahman. Therefore the Śruti is our means of knowledge.

units.label: Verse 195
units.deva:
न कर्म यत् किञ्चिद् अपेक्षते हि
रूपोपलब्धौ पुरुषस्य चक्षुः।
ज्ञानं तथैव श्रवणादि-जन्यं
वस्तु-प्रकाशे निरपेक्षम् एव॥
units.translation: A person’s eye needs no action to perceive form. Likewise, knowledge born from listening and the other practices is entirely independent in revealing reality.

gloss.en: born from listening and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
na karma yat kiñcid apekṣate hi
rūpopalabdhau puruṣasya cakṣuḥ|
jñānaṃ tathaiva śravaṇādi-janyaṃ
vastu-prakāśe nirapekṣam eva||
units.editionTranslation: Just as the eye sees of its own accord the colour and form of things, and wants no compulsion, so also the light of knowledge which the Śāstras give us shines of its own accord. It does not depend upon any external activity.

units.label: Verse 196
units.deva:
कर्तृ-तन्त्रं भवेत् कर्म कर्म-तन्त्रं शुभाशुभम्।
प्रमाण-तन्त्रं विज्ञानं माया-तन्त्रम् इदं जगत्॥
units.translation: Action is governed by the doer; good and evil are governed by action; knowledge is governed by a valid means of knowing; this world is governed by Māyā.

gloss.en: governed by a valid means of knowing

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kartṛ-tantraṃ bhavet karma karma-tantraṃ śubhāśubham|
pramāṇa-tantraṃ vijñānaṃ māyā-tantram idaṃ jagat||
units.editionTranslation: Action depends upon the doer; happiness and misery depend upon one’s action; knowledge depends upon proof; and the world depends upon Māyā the illusion of reality.

units.label: Verse 197
units.deva:
विद्यां चाविद्यां चेति सहोक्तिर् इयम् उपकृता सद्भिः।
सत्-कर्मोपासनयोर् न त्वात्म-ज्ञान-कर्मणोः क्वापि॥
units.translation: The wise apply the statement “knowledge and non-knowledge” together to right action and worship, never to Self-knowledge and action.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
vidyāṃ cāvidyāṃ ceti sahoktir iyam upakṛtā sadbhiḥ|
sat-karmopāsanayor na tvātma-jñāna-karmaṇoḥ kvāpi||
units.editionTranslation: When the Śruti speaks of ‘the combination of knowledge and action’ the wise should understand that it refers to the knowledge of the devas, and action as a means of gaining their favour. Here the Śruti does not refer to the knowledge of the Ātman to be attained by means of action.

units.label: Verse 198
units.deva:
नित्यानित्य-पदार्थ-बोध-रहितो यश् चोभयत्र स्रगाद्य्-
अर्थानाम् अनुभूति-लग्न-हृदयो निर्विण्ण-बुद्धिर् जनः।
तस्यैवास्य जडस्य कर्म विहितं श्रुत्या विरज्याभितो
मोक्षेच्छोर् न विधीयते तु परमानन्दार्थिनो धीमतः॥
units.translation: Scripture prescribes ritual action for the dull person who cannot distinguish the eternal from the non-eternal, whose heart is attached to enjoying objects such as garlands here and hereafter. It is not prescribed for the wise seeker of liberation who has become dispassionate and seeks supreme bliss.

gloss.en: lacking discernment of eternal and non-eternal things
whose heart is attached to experiencing

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
nityānitya-padārtha-bodha-rahito yaś cobhayatra sragādy-
arthānām anubhūti-lagna-hṛdayo nirviṇṇa-buddhir janaḥ|
tasyaivāsya jaḍasya karma vihitaṃ śrutyā virajyābhito
mokṣecchor na vidhīyate tu paramānandārthino dhīmataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Rituals are for those who cannot distinguish between what is eternal and what is not eternal, who seek pleasure, either here or hereafter, and who are attached to the fruit of action. They are not meant for those who have conquered passion, who can analyse things wisely, who are intent upon liberation, and who are eager to attain the supreme bliss.

units.label: Verse 199
units.deva:
मोक्षेच्छया यद् अहर् एव विरज्यतेऽसौ
न्यासस् तदैव विहितो विदुषो मुमुक्षोः।
श्रुत्या तयैव परया च ततः सुधीभिः
प्रामाणिकोऽयम् इति चेतसि निश्चितव्यः॥
units.translation: On the very day a wise seeker of liberation becomes dispassionate through the desire for liberation, renunciation is prescribed for that person. The wise should settle in their hearts that this is authoritative, on the strength of that very supreme Śruti.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
mokṣecchayā yad ahar eva virajyate’sau
nyāsas tadaiva vihito viduṣo mumukṣoḥ|
śrutyā tayaiva parayā ca tataḥ sudhībhiḥ
prāmāṇiko’yam iti cetasi niścitavyaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: When as a result of the intense desire for liberation, one feels no interest whatever in worldly things, that very day the intelligent aspirant becomes fit for renunciation. To him Śruti is the only means of valid knowledge for attaining the Absolute.

units.label: Verse 200
units.deva:
स्वापरोक्षस्य वेदादेः साधनत्वं निषेधति।
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसेत्यादिना भगवानपि॥
units.translation: The Lord too denies that the Vedas and the like are a means for direct realization of the Self, with the words, “Not by the Vedas, nor by austerity…”

gloss.en: of direct realization of the Self
of the Vedas and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
svāparokṣasya vedādeḥ sādhanatvaṃ niṣedhati|
nāhaṃ vedairna tapasetyādinā bhagavānapi||
units.editionTranslation: The Lord says, ‘I cannot be known by the Vedas, by austere penance’. Therefore the view that the study of the Vedas and the observance of religious formalities would help a person to realize the innermost Ātman stands refuted. ((BhG.11.53) (Bhagavad Gītā))

units.label: Verse 201
units.deva:
प्रवृत्तिश्च निवृत्तिश्च द्वे एते श्रुति-गोचरे।
प्रवृत्त्या बध्यते जन्तुर् निवृत्त्या तु विमुच्यते॥
units.translation: There are two paths within the scope of scripture: engagement and withdrawal. Through engagement a person is bound; through withdrawal, liberated.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
pravṛttiśca nivṛttiśca dve ete śruti-gocare|
