pravṛttyā badhyate jantur nivṛttyā tu vimucyate||
units.editionTranslation: There are two paths, both of them Śruti-ordained. The one is the path of acquisition (pravṛtti) and the other is the path of renunciation (nivṛtti). The former binds; the latter liberates.

units.label: Verse 202
units.deva:
यन् न स्वबन्धोऽभिमतो मूढस्यापि क्वचित् ततः।
निवृत्तिः कर्म-संन्यासः कर्तव्यो मोक्ष-काङ्क्षिभिः॥
units.translation: Since no one, even a foolish person, ever approves of being bound, those who long for liberation should undertake withdrawal through renunciation of action.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yan na svabandho’bhimato mūḍhasyāpi kvacit tataḥ|
nivṛttiḥ karma-saṃnyāsaḥ kartavyo mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: As no one desires to be bound, however dull one may be, it is befitting that the lover of liberation should renounce his all and resort to sannyāsa.

units.label: Verse 203
units.deva:
न ज्ञान-कर्मणोर् यस्मात् सह-योगस् तु युज्यते।
तस्मात् त्याज्यं प्रयत्नेन कर्म ज्ञानेच्छुना ध्रुवम्॥
units.translation: Because knowledge and action cannot properly be joined, the seeker of knowledge should certainly relinquish action with effort.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
na jñāna-karmaṇor yasmāt saha-yogas tu yujyate|
tasmāt tyājyaṃ prayatnena karma jñānecchunā dhruvam||
units.editionTranslation: Along these opposite paths of karma and jñāna no one may travel simultaneously. It is therefore essential that the seeker after liberation should renounce his all and resort to sannyāsa.

units.label: Verse 204
units.deva:
इष्ट-साधनता-बुद्ध्या गृहीतस्यापि वस्तुनः।
विज्ञाय फल्गुतां पश्चात् कः पुनस् तत् प्रतीक्षते॥
units.translation: After discovering the worthlessness of something taken to be a means to the desired goal, who would continue to seek it?

gloss.en: with the belief that it is a means to the desired goal
of what has been taken up

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
iṣṭa-sādhanatā-buddhyā gṛhītasyāpi vastunaḥ|
vijñāya phalgutāṃ paścāt kaḥ punas tat pratīkṣate||
units.editionTranslation: Who is there who would consciously seek that which seems apparently to lead to that which is good, but which on examination is found to be of no value?

units.label: Verse 205
units.deva:
उपरति-शब्दार्थो ह्युपरमणं पूर्व-दृष्ट-वृत्तिभ्यः।
सोऽयं मुख्यो गौणश् चेति च वृत्त्या द्वि-रूपतां धत्ते॥
units.translation: The meaning of the word uparati is cessation from previously experienced activities. By common usage, this has two forms: primary and secondary.

gloss.en: the meaning of the word uparati

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
uparati-śabdārtho hyuparamaṇaṃ pūrva-dṛṣṭa-vṛttibhyaḥ|
so’yaṃ mukhyo gauṇaś ceti ca vṛttyā dvi-rūpatāṃ dhatte||
units.editionTranslation: The term ‘renunciation (uparati)’ implies the giving up of all those actions which one had previously imagined to be a source of happiness. The term ‘renunciation’ is to be understood in a twofold sense, the one direct and the other indirect.

units.label: Verse 206
units.deva:
वृत्तेर् दृश्य-परित्यागो मुख्यार्थ इति कथ्यते।
गौणार्थः कर्म-संन्यासः श्रुतेर् अङ्गतया मतः॥
units.translation: Giving up the objects seen by the mind is called the primary meaning [of uparati]. Renunciation of action is considered its secondary meaning, as a limb of scripture.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
vṛtter dṛśya-parityāgo mukhyārtha iti kathyate|
gauṇārthaḥ karma-saṃnyāsaḥ śruter aṅgatayā mataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: In its primary meaning renunciation implies the giving up of the objects which influence the mind. According to the Śruti its secondary meaning is the giving up of action such as rituals.

units.label: Verse 207
units.deva:
पुंसः प्रधान-सिद्ध्यर्थम् अङ्गस्याश्रयणं ध्रुवम्।
कर्तव्यम् अङ्ग-हीनं चेत् प्रधानं नैव सिध्यति॥
units.translation: To accomplish the principal goal, one must certainly rely on its supporting means. If it lacks its supporting limb, the principal goal cannot be accomplished.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
puṃsaḥ pradhāna-siddhyartham aṅgasyāśrayaṇaṃ dhruvam|
kartavyam aṅga-hīnaṃ cet pradhānaṃ naiva sidhyati||
units.editionTranslation: It is essential that in order to attain the main objective one should make use of the requisite means to it, for in absence of the means, the goal cannot be achieved.

units.label: Verse 208
units.deva:
संन्यसेत् सुविरक्तः सन्न् इहामुत्रार्थतः सुखात्।
अविरक्तस्य संन्यासो निष्फलोऽयाज्य-यागवत्॥
units.translation: One who is thoroughly dispassionate should renounce happiness sought here and hereafter. Renunciation by one without dispassion is fruitless, like a sacrifice performed by someone not entitled to perform it.

gloss.en: like a sacrifice by one not entitled to perform it

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
saṃnyaset suviraktaḥ sann ihāmutrārthataḥ sukhāt|
aviraktasya saṃnyāso niṣphalo’yājya-yāgavat||
units.editionTranslation: The sannyāsī should be completely indifferent to the good things of life both here and hereafter, and renounce all Vedic rituals. Renunciation without dispassion is of no avail. It may be compared to a sacrifice by one who is not entitled to perform it.

units.label: Verse 209
units.deva:
संन्यस्य तु यतिः कुर्यान् न पूर्व-विषय-स्मृतिम्।
तां तां तत्-स्मरणे तस्य जुगुप्सा जायते यतः॥
units.translation: After renouncing, an ascetic should not bring back each memory of former sense objects, because recalling them gives rise to disgust.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
saṃnyasya tu yatiḥ kuryān na pūrva-viṣaya-smṛtim|
tāṃ tāṃ tat-smaraṇe tasya jugupsā jāyate yataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Hence too the injunction that a sannyāsī should no even recall to his mind his past association with the world of sense-objects. To the true sannyāsī even the memory of the past would evoke a sense of disgust.

units.label: Verse 210
units.deva:
गुरु-वेदान्त-वाक्येषु बुद्धिर् या निश्चयात्मिका।
सत्यम् इत्येव सा श्रद्धा निदानं मुक्ति-सिद्धये॥
units.translation: A firm conviction that the guru’s and Vedānta’s words are true is śraddhā (faith); it is the cause of attaining liberation.

gloss.en: in the words of the guru and Vedānta

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
guru-vedānta-vākyeṣu buddhir yā niścayātmikā|
satyam ityeva sā śraddhā nidānaṃ mukti-siddhaye||
units.editionTranslation: Faith The aspirant after liberation ought to have absolute faith in what the guru says and what the Vedānta teaches. Such faith is known as śraddhā. It is by means of such faith that one attains liberation.

units.label: Verse 211
units.deva:
श्रद्धावताम् एव सतां पुम्-अर्थः
समीरितः सिध्यति नेतरेषाम्।
उक्तं सुसूक्ष्मं परमार्थ-तत्त्वं
श्रद्धत्स्व सोम्येति च वक्ति वेदः॥
units.translation: The declared human aim is attained only by people who have faith and are virtuous, not by others. The Veda too says, “Trust, dear one, the very subtle ultimate reality that has been spoken of.”
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śraddhāvatām eva satāṃ pum-arthaḥ
samīritaḥ sidhyati netareṣām|
uktaṃ susūkṣmaṃ paramārtha-tattvaṃ
śraddhatsva somyeti ca vakti vedaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The Śāstras speak of liberation as the ultimate goal of life. Only those who have faith in the guru and in the Vedānta may attain it. It is not for the others. That is why the Śruti says, “Subtle is the path; have faith, and listen earnestly to what is taught”.

units.label: Verse 212
units.deva:
श्रद्धा-विहीनस्य तु न प्रवृत्तिः
प्रवृत्ति-शून्यस्य न साध्य-सिद्धिः।
अश्रद्धयैवाभिहताश्च सर्वे
मज्जन्ति संसार-महा-समुद्रे॥
units.translation: One without faith has no initiative; one without initiative does not attain the goal. Struck by faithlessness alone, all sink in the great ocean of saṃsāra.

gloss.en: in the great ocean of saṃsāra

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śraddhā-vihīnasya tu na pravṛttiḥ
pravṛtti-śūnyasya na sādhya-siddhiḥ|
aśraddhayaivābhihatāśca sarve
majjanti saṃsāra-mahā-samudre||
units.editionTranslation: Without faith there is no exertion, and without exertion there is no achievement Hence it is that those who are devoid of faith become lost in the ocean of saṃsāra.

units.label: Verse 213
units.deva:
दैवे च वेदे च गुरौ च मन्त्रे
तीर्थे महात्मन्यपि भेषजे च।
श्रद्धा भवत्यस्य यथा यथान्तस्
तथा तथा सिद्धिर् उदेति पुंसाम्॥
units.translation: As much inward faith as a person has in the deity, the Veda, a guru, a mantra, a sacred place, a great soul, and medicine, so much success arises for people.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
daive ca vede ca gurau ca mantre
tīrthe mahātmanyapi bheṣaje ca|
śraddhā bhavatyasya yathā yathāntas
tathā tathā siddhir udeti puṃsām||
units.editionTranslation: Whether it be the gaining of divine grace, Vedic insight, knowledge of the mantras (mantras), communion with holy men, or association with holy places, or deriving benefit from medical treatment, all that may be achieved only in proportion to one’s faith.

units.label: Verse 214
units.deva:
अस्तीत्य् एवोपलब्धव्यं वस्तु सद्-भाव-निश्चयात्।
सद्-भाव-निश्चयस् तस्य श्रद्धया शास्त्र-सिद्धया॥
units.translation: The reality must be recognized as “it exists,” through certainty of its existence. That certainty of existence comes through faith established by scripture.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
astīty evopalabdhavyaṃ vastu sad-bhāva-niścayāt|
sad-bhāva-niścayas tasya śraddhayā śāstra-siddhayā||
units.editionTranslation: Brahman is That which is (sad-bhāva). One should ascertain the nature of Brahman by ascertaining the nature of existence. To ascertain Brahman requires faith in the Śāstras. ((KathU.1.2.3) (Kaṭha Upaniṣad), (.12) (Kaṭha Upaniṣad))

units.label: Verse 215
units.deva:
तस्माच् छ्रद्धा सुसम्पाद्या गुरु-वेदान्त-वाक्ययोः।
मुमुक्षोः श्रद्दधानस्य फलं सिध्यति नान्यथा॥
units.translation: Therefore, faith in the words of the guru and Vedānta should be carefully cultivated. For a liberation-seeker who has faith, the result is attained; otherwise, it is not.

gloss.en: in the words of the guru and Vedānta

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tasmāc chraddhā susampādyā guru-vedānta-vākyayoḥ|
mumukṣoḥ śraddadhānasya phalaṃ sidhyati nānyathā||
units.editionTranslation: One should therefore cultivate supreme faith in the guru, and in what the Vedānta says. It is by faith (śraddhā, trust in them as the pramāṇa) alone and by no other means that the earnest seeker attains liberation.

units.label: Verse 216
units.deva:
यथार्थ-वादिता पुंसां श्रद्धा-जनन-कारणम्।
वेदस्येश्वर-वाक्यत्वाद् यथार्थत्वे न संशयः॥
units.translation: Truthful speech is the cause of faith arising among people. Because the Veda is the Lord’s word, there is no doubt about its truth.

gloss.en: because it is the Lord’s word

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yathārtha-vāditā puṃsāṃ śraddhā-janana-kāraṇam|
vedasyeśvara-vākyatvād yathārthatve na saṃśayaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: To the extent to which one speaks the truth, one inspires faith. The Vedas are to be trusted because they constitute the word of God.

units.label: Verse 217
units.deva:
मुक्तस्येश्वर-रूपत्वाद् गुरोर् वाग् अपि तादृशी।
तस्मात् तद्-वाक्ययोः श्रद्धा सतां सिध्यति धीमताम्॥
units.translation: Because a liberated person is of the nature of the Lord, the guru’s speech too is like that. Therefore, the wise and virtuous have faith in the words of both.

gloss.en: because of having the nature of the Lord
in the words of those two

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
muktasyeśvara-rūpatvād guror vāg api tādṛśī|
tasmāt tad-vākyayoḥ śraddhā satāṃ sidhyati dhīmatām||
units.editionTranslation: Inasmuch as a liberated soul is one with God, the word of such a guru is also true. Hence it is that the wise should have faith in the words of both.

units.label: Verse 218
units.deva:
श्रुत्युक्तार्थावगाहाय विदुषा ज्ञेय-वस्तुनि।
चित्तस्य सम्यगाधानं समाधानम् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: To penetrate the meaning stated in Śruti, the wise call the mind’s proper placement on the object to be known “concentration” (samādhāna).

gloss.en: on the object to be known

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śrutyuktārthāvagāhāya viduṣā jñeya-vastuni|
cittasya samyagādhānaṃ samādhānam itīryate||
units.editionTranslation: Concentration One should dive deep into what the Śruti says. One should be completely absorbed in it, in order to attain the knowledge of the ultimate Reality. It is such total absorption that is called concentration (samādhāna).

units.label: Verse 219
units.deva:
चित्तस्य साध्यैक-परत्वम् एव
पुमर्थ-सिद्धेर् नियमेन कारणम्।
नैवान्यथा सिध्यति साध्यम् ईषन्
मनः-प्रमादे विफलः प्रयत्नः॥
units.translation: The mind’s exclusive focus on the goal is indeed the invariable cause of attaining the human aim. Otherwise, the goal is not attained; with even slight inattention of mind, effort is fruitless.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
cittasya sādhyaika-paratvam eva
pumartha-siddher niyamena kāraṇam|
naivānyathā sidhyati sādhyam īṣan
manaḥ-pramāde viphalaḥ prayatnaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: It is only by virtue of concentration that it becomes possible for one to attain one’s goal. Where the mind is distracted by wayward impulses, one’s efforts are all in vain.

units.label: Verse 220
units.deva:
चित्तं च दृष्टिं करणं तथान्यद्
एकत्र बघ्नाति हि लक्ष्य-भेत्ता।
किञ्चित् प्रमादे सति लक्ष्य-भेत्तुर्
बाण-प्रयोगो विफलो यथा तथा॥
units.translation: An archer indeed fixes the mind, gaze, and another instrument together on one point. When there is even slight carelessness on the archer’s part, the arrow-shot is fruitless; so it is here too.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
cittaṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ karaṇaṃ tathānyad
ekatra baghnāti hi lakṣya-bhettā|
kiñcit pramāde sati lakṣya-bhettur
bāṇa-prayogo viphalo yathā tathā||
units.editionTranslation: Like a marksman shooting at the bull’s eye, by directing his mind and eye, as well as his hand towards it, the spiritual aspirant should concentrate on his object. Even if there should be the slightest deviation, the marksman’s shooting would be in vain.

units.label: Verse 221
units.deva:
सिद्धेश् चित्त-समाधानम् असाधारण-कारणम्।
यतस् ततो मुमुक्षूणां भवितव्यं सदामुना॥
units.translation: Concentration of mind is the unique cause of attainment; therefore, seekers of liberation must always have it.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
siddheś citta-samādhānam asādhāraṇa-kāraṇam|
yatas tato mumukṣūṇāṃ bhavitavyaṃ sadāmunā||
units.editionTranslation: As an aid to the attainment of the supreme peace, concentration stands unexcelled among the sādhanas. At no time could the aspirant after liberation afford to dispense with it.

units.label: Verse 222
units.deva:
अत्यन्त-तीव्र-वैराग्यं फल-लिप्सा महत्तरा।
तद् एतद् उभयं विद्यात् समाधानस्य कारणम्॥
units.translation: Extremely intense dispassion and a very great desire for the result—one should know both of these as causes of concentration.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
atyanta-tīvra-vairāgyaṃ phala-lipsā mahattarā|
tad etad ubhayaṃ vidyāt samādhānasya kāraṇam||
units.editionTranslation: Where there is the most intense form of dispassion, and where there is the supreme love of liberation, it is by virtue of their combined influence that one attains concentration of mind.

units.label: Verse 223
units.deva:
बहिर्-अङ्गं श्रुतिः प्राह ब्रह्म-चर्यादि-मुक्तये।
शमादि-षट्कम् एवैतद् अन्तर्-अङ्गं विदुर् बुधाः॥
units.translation: Śruti calls brahmacarya and related practices external aids to liberation. The wise know this sixfold group beginning with śama as an internal aid.

gloss.en: the sixfold group beginning with śama

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
bahir-aṅgaṃ śrutiḥ prāha brahma-caryādi-muktaye|
śamādi-ṣaṭkam evaitad antar-aṅgaṃ vidur budhāḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The Śruti declares that Brahma-carya etc. are in the nature of external aids to liberation. The wise know that the six cardinal virtues such as self-restraint (śama) etc. are in the nature of internal aids to liberation.

units.label: Verse 224
units.deva:
अन्तरङ्गं हि बलवद् बहिरङ्गाद् यतस् ततः।
शमादि-षट्कं जिज्ञासोर् अवश्यं भाव्यम् आन्तरम्॥
units.translation: Because an internal aid is indeed stronger than an external one, the sixfold group beginning with śama must necessarily be developed inwardly by the seeker of knowledge.

gloss.en: the sixfold group beginning with śama

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
antaraṅgaṃ hi balavad bahiraṅgād yatas tataḥ|
śamādi-ṣaṭkaṃ jijñāsor avaśyaṃ bhāvyam āntaram||
units.editionTranslation: The internal qualities surpass the external ones in value. The six noble qualities beginning with self-restraint are therefore indispensable aids for the seeker after liberation.

units.label: Verse 225
units.deva:
अन्तरङ्ग-विहीनस्य कृत-श्रवण-कोटयः।
न फलन्ति यथा योद्धुर् अधीरस्यास्त्र-सम्पदः॥
units.translation: For one lacking inner qualifications, countless acts of listening do not bear fruit, just as a store of weapons is useless to an unsteady warrior.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
antaraṅga-vihīnasya kṛta-śravaṇa-koṭayaḥ|
na phalanti yathā yoddhur adhīrasyāstra-sampadaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: In the absence of these aids from within, no amount of formal listening to the Śāstras would be of any avail. To one who is devoid of courage, a well furnished armoury is of no use.

units.label: Verse 226
units.deva:
ब्रह्मात्मैकत्व-विज्ञानाद् यद् विद्वान् मोक्तुम् इच्छति।
संसार-पाश-बन्धं तन् मुमुक्षुत्वं निगद्यते॥
units.translation: The wish of a wise person to free [themself] from the fetter of saṃsāra through knowledge of the oneness of Brahman and the Self is called mumukṣutva, the desire for liberation.

gloss.en: through knowledge of the oneness of Brahman and the Self

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
brahmātmaikatva-vijñānād yad vidvān moktum icchati|
saṃsāra-pāśa-bandhaṃ tan mumukṣutvaṃ nigadyate||
units.editionTranslation: The desire for liberation When one desires to snap in twain the fetters of life, through a realization of the oneness of Brahman and Ātman, that state is called the desire for liberation (mumukṣutvam).

units.label: Verse 227
units.deva:
साधनानां तु सर्वेषां मुमुक्षा मूल-कारणम्।
अनिच्छोर् अप्रवृत्तस्य क्व श्रुतिः क्व नु तत्-फलम्॥
units.translation: The desire for liberation is the root cause of all means. For one who has no desire and makes no effort, what use is scripture, and where is its result?

gloss.en: of one who does not act

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sādhanānāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ mumukṣā mūla-kāraṇam|
anicchor apravṛttasya kva śrutiḥ kva nu tat-phalam||
units.editionTranslation: Unless one has an intense love of liberation, and unless one makes the necessary effort to realize it, of what use is the study of the Śāstras? The love of liberation lies at the root of realization.

units.label: Verse 228
units.deva:
तीव्र-मध्यम-मन्दातिमन्दभेदाश् चतुर्विधाः।
मुमुक्षा तत्-प्रकारोऽपि कीर्त्यते श्रूयतां बुधैः॥
units.translation: Desire for liberation is fourfold: intense, moderate, dull, and very dull. These types are declared; let the wise hear them.

gloss.en: distinctions of intense, moderate, dull, and very dull

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tīvra-madhyama-mandātimandabhedāś caturvidhāḥ|
mumukṣā tat-prakāro’pi kīrtyate śrūyatāṃ budhaiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: There are four classes of aspirants. They may be classified as the very eager (tīvra), the moderately eager, the lukewarm, and the indifferent.

units.label: Verse 229
units.deva:
तापैस् त्रिभिर् नित्यम् अनेक-रूपैः
सन्तप्यमानः क्षुभितान्तरात्मा।
परिग्रहं सर्वम् अनर्थ-बुद्ध्या
जहाति सा तीव्रतरा मुमुक्षा॥
units.translation: One constantly tormented by the threefold afflictions in their many forms, with an agitated inner being, abandons all possessions, seeing them as harmful. This is the most intense desire for liberation.

gloss.en: with the view that they are harmful

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tāpais tribhir nityam aneka-rūpaiḥ
santapyamānaḥ kṣubhitāntarātmā|
parigrahaṃ sarvam anartha-buddhyā
jahāti sā tīvratarā mumukṣā||
units.editionTranslation: The feeling which impels one to go through the travail of the world here, and willingly renounce everything, be it pleasure or pain, is the characteristic feature of the most ardent type of the love of liberation.

units.label: Verse 230
units.deva:
ताप-त्रयं तीव्रम् अवेक्ष्य वस्तु
दृष्ट्वा कलत्रं तनयान् विहातुम्।
मध्ये द्वयोर् लोडनम् आत्मनो यत्
सैषा मता माध्यमिकी मुमुक्षा॥
units.translation: Having seen the threefold affliction as severe and real, yet seeing one’s wife and children and wanting to leave them, one wavers between the two. This is considered a middling desire for liberation.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tāpa-trayaṃ tīvram avekṣya vastu
dṛṣṭvā kalatraṃ tanayān vihātum|
madhye dvayor loḍanam ātmano yat
saiṣā matā mādhyamikī mumukṣā||
units.editionTranslation: Where there is a conflict of emotions arising out of a keen perception of the three-fold ills of life, and where there is an indirect knowledge of Brahman on the one hand, and on the other hand there is a desire to give up one’s wife and children, that is deemed to be the characteristic feature of the second order of the love of liberation.

units.label: Verse 231
units.deva:
मोक्षस्य कालोऽस्ति किम् अद्य मे त्वरा
भुक्त्वैव भोगान् कृत-सर्व-कार्यः।
मुक्त्यै यतिष्येऽहम् अथेति बुद्धिर्
एषैव मन्दा कथिता मुमुक्षा॥
units.translation: The thought “Is there a time for liberation? Why should I hurry today? Having enjoyed the pleasures and completed all tasks, then I will strive for liberation” is called a dull desire for liberation.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
mokṣasya kālo’sti kim adya me tvarā
bhuktvaiva bhogān kṛta-sarva-kāryaḥ|
muktyai yatiṣye’ham atheti buddhir
eṣaiva mandā kathitā mumukṣā||
units.editionTranslation: ‘There is a time for liberation. What is the use of being in a hurry? I shalt think of liberation at leisure, sometime in the distant future, after I have finished all my duties, and have had my fill of enjoyment’. Such an attitude of mind shows but a dull desire for liberation and belongs to the third category.

units.label: Verse 232
units.deva:
मार्गे प्रयातुर् मणि-लाभवन् मे
लभेत मोक्षो यदि तर्हि धन्यः।
इत्याशया मूढ-धियां मतिर् या
सैषातिमन्दाभिमता मुमुक्षा॥
units.translation: “If liberation came to me like a traveler finding a jewel on the road, then I would be fortunate”—such a thought of foolish people is considered an extremely dull desire for liberation.

gloss.en: like the finding of a jewel

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
mārge prayātur maṇi-lābhavan me
labheta mokṣo yadi tarhi dhanyaḥ|
ityāśayā mūḍha-dhiyāṃ matir yā
saiṣātimandābhimatā mumukṣā||
units.editionTranslation: ‘Just as a lucky wayfarer might hit by chance upon a precious stone, if I can have liberation by a lucky accident, I shall feel happy’. Such is the attitude of mind of the dullest of aspirants, and that is classified as belonging to the fourth category.

units.label: Verse 233
units.deva:
जन्मानेक-सहस्रेषु तपसाराधितेश्वरः।
तेन निःशेष-निर्धूत-हृदय-स्थित-कल्मषः॥
units.translation: One who has worshipped the Lord through austerity in many thousands of births has, through that, completely swept away the impurity residing in the heart.

gloss.en: one who has worshipped the Lord

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
janmāneka-sahasreṣu tapasārādhiteśvaraḥ|
tena niḥśeṣa-nirdhūta-hṛdaya-sthita-kalmaṣaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The fact is that it is only by prolonged austerity and by worshipping the Lord in life after life that one is at last established in perfect purity of heart.

units.label: Verse 234
units.deva:
शास्त्रविद् गुण-दोष-ज्ञो भोग्यमात्रे विनिस्पृहः।
नित्यानित्य-पदार्थ-ज्ञो मुक्ति-कामो दृढ-व्रतः॥
units.translation: Such a person knows scripture and virtue and fault, is free from longing for all objects of enjoyment, knows what is eternal and non-eternal, seeks liberation, and is firm in resolve.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śāstravid guṇa-doṣa-jño bhogyamātre vinispṛhaḥ|
nityānitya-padārtha-jño mukti-kāmo dṛḍha-vrataḥ||
units.editionTranslation: One who is pure of heart becomes well versed in the Śāstras, and capable of discriminating between right and wrong. Such a person is devoid of the craving after sense-pleasures is aware of the difference between what is eternal and what is not, and is ever intent upon final liberation.

units.label: Verse 235
units.deva:
निष्टप्तम् अग्निना पात्रम् उद्वास्य त्वरया यथा। (उधृत्य)
जहाति गेहं तद्वच् च तीव्र-मोक्षेच्छया द्विजः॥
units.translation: As one quickly removes a vessel heated by fire, so a twice-born person leaves home with an intense desire for liberation.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
niṣṭaptam agninā pātram udvāsya tvarayā yathā| (udhṛtya)
jahāti gehaṃ tadvac ca tīvra-mokṣecchayā dvijaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The twice-born abandons home firm in his resolve to attain liberation. Such a person may be compared to one who drops from one’s hand a vessel that has become too hot to hold.

units.label: Verse 236
units.deva:
स एव सद्यस् तरति संसृतिं गुर्वनुग्रहात्।
यस्तु तीव्र-मुमुक्षुः स्यात् स जीवन्न् एव मुच्यते॥
units.translation: That very person immediately crosses saṃsāra through the guru’s grace. Whoever has intense desire for liberation is indeed freed while still living.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
sa eva sadyas tarati saṃsṛtiṃ gurvanugrahāt|
yastu tīvra-mumukṣuḥ syāt sa jīvann eva mucyate||
units.editionTranslation: Thanks to the guru’s grace, one transcends the cycle of birth and death, the wheel of saṃsāra. One who is endowed with this passion for liberation is indeed liberated even when alive.

units.label: Verse 237
units.deva:
जन्मान्तरे मध्यमस् तु तद्-अन्यस् तु युगान्तरे।
चतुर्थः कल्प-कोट्यां वा नैव बन्धाद् विमुच्यते॥
units.translation: The moderate one [is freed] in another birth, and the one next after that in another age. The fourth is not freed from bondage, even after crores of kalpas.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
janmāntare madhyamas tu tad-anyas tu yugāntare|
caturthaḥ kalpa-koṭyāṃ vā naiva bandhād vimucyate||
units.editionTranslation: But not the others. The aspirant of the second order might have to be reborn before he could realize his aim. The aspirant of the third order might have to wait for ages; as for the aspirant of the fourth order, he might be reborn any number of times, and yet fail to reach the goal.

units.label: Verse 238
units.deva:
नृजन्म जन्तोर् अतिदुर्लभं विदुस्
ततोऽपि पुंस्त्वं च ततो विवेकः।
लब्ध्वा तद् एतत् त्रितयं महात्मा
यतेत मुक्त्यै सहसा विरक्तः॥
units.translation: Human birth is extremely rare for a living being, they say; manhood is rarer still, and discernment rarer than that. Having gained these three, a noble and dispassionate person should quickly strive for liberation.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
nṛjanma jantor atidurlabhaṃ vidus
tato’pi puṃstvaṃ ca tato vivekaḥ|
labdhvā tad etat tritayaṃ mahātmā
yateta muktyai sahasā viraktaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: It is a rare privilege to be born a human being. Even more rare is it to be born a man. Rarest of all is it that one is born endowed with discrimination. That great man, who is born with these three qualifications must strive after liberation in a spirit of complete dispassionateness.

units.label: Verse 239
units.deva:
पुत्र-मित्र-कलत्रादि-सुखं जन्मनि जन्मनि।
मर्त्यत्वं पुरुषत्वं च विवेकश्च न लभ्यते॥
units.translation: The happiness of sons, friends, a spouse, and the like is found in birth after birth; human birth, manhood, and discernment are not attained.

gloss.en: the happiness of sons, friends, a spouse, and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
putra-mitra-kalatrādi-sukhaṃ janmani janmani|
martyatvaṃ puruṣatvaṃ ca vivekaśca na labhyate||
units.editionTranslation: It is possible that one might have friends, wife, sons and daughters in birth after birth. But to be born a human being, a man, and a wise one, is indeed hard of attainment.

units.label: Verse 240
units.deva:
लब्ध्वा सुदुर्लभतरं नर-जन्म जन्तुस्
तत्रापि पौरुषम् अतः सदसद्-विवेकम्।
सम्प्राप्य चैहिक-सुखाभि-रतो यदि स्याद्
धिक् तस्य जन्म कुमतेः पुरुषाधमस्य॥
units.translation: Having gained a human birth, so exceedingly difficult to obtain, and then manhood and discernment between the real and unreal, if a person remains absorbed in worldly pleasure, shame on the birth of that foolish person, the lowest among men.

gloss.en: discernment between the real and unreal

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
labdhvā sudurlabhataraṃ nara-janma jantus
tatrāpi pauruṣam ataḥ sadasad-vivekam|
samprāpya caihika-sukhābhi-rato yadi syād
dhik tasya janma kumateḥ puruṣādhamasya||
units.editionTranslation: He who is endowed with all these gifts, and who yet fails to avail himself of the opportunity to attain liberation must be deemed to be the most unfortunate. Such a person is lured by worldly pleasures, and by being addicted to evil ways, becomes the most degraded of mankind.

units.label: Verse 241
units.deva:
खादते मोदते नित्यं शुनकः सूकरः खरः।
तेषाम् एषां विशेषः को वृत्तिर् येषां तु तैः समा॥
units.translation: A dog, pig, and donkey continually eat and enjoy. What distinction is there for people whose way of life is the same as theirs?
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
khādate modate nityaṃ śunakaḥ sūkaraḥ kharaḥ|
teṣām eṣāṃ viśeṣaḥ ko vṛttir yeṣāṃ tu taiḥ samā||
units.editionTranslation: Even the lower animals such dogs, pigs and mules, eat and enjoy the pleasures of the senses. Unless a man differs from them by his pre-eminence he is no better than the lower animals.

units.label: Verses 242–243
units.deva:
यावन् नाश्रयते रोगो यावन् नाक्रमते जरा।
यावन् न धीर् विपर्येति यावन् मृत्युं न पश्यति॥
तावद् एव नरः स्वस्थः सार-ग्रहण-तत्परः।
विवेकी प्रयतेताशु भव-बन्ध-विमुक्तये॥
units.translation: As long as illness has not taken hold, old age has not overtaken one, the mind has not become impaired, and death has not been seen, a healthy, discerning person intent on grasping the essence should promptly strive for release from the bondage of worldly existence.

gloss.en: for release from the bondage of worldly existence

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
yāvan nāśrayate rogo yāvan nākramate jarā|
yāvan na dhīr viparyeti yāvan mṛtyuṃ na paśyati||
tāvad eva naraḥ svasthaḥ sāra-grahaṇa-tatparaḥ|
vivekī prayatetāśu bhava-bandha-vimuktaye||
units.editionTranslation: Therefore before one is afflicted by ill-health, before one becomes weak with advanced age, before the mind becomes clouded and before death comes, that is the time for earnest striving. When a man is in good health, he who is bent upon what is essential and who is discriminating should exert himself in time, and strive after liberation.

units.label: Verse 244
units.deva:
देवर्षि-पितृ-मर्त्य-ऋण-बन्ध-मुक्तास् तु कोटिशः।
भव-बन्ध-विमुक्तस् तु यः कश्चिद् ब्रह्म-वित्तमः॥
units.translation: Countless people are freed from the bonds of debt to gods, sages, ancestors, and humans; but whoever is freed from the bondage of worldly existence is a supreme knower of Brahman.

gloss.en: freed from bonds of debt to gods, sages, ancestors, and humans
freed from the bondage of worldly existence

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
devarṣi-pitṛ-martya-ṛṇa-bandha-muktās tu koṭiśaḥ|
bhava-bandha-vimuktas tu yaḥ kaścid brahma-vittamaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: There is no known limit to the number of those who have fulfilled their obligation in life to the gods, to the spirits of the departed, to the seers of truth, and to their fellow mortals. But very few have known Brahman and gained mukti.

units.label: Verse 245
units.deva:
अन्तर्बन्धेन बद्धस्य किं बहिर्बन्ध-मोचनैः।
तद् अन्तर्बन्ध-मुक्त्यर्थं क्रियतां कृतिभिः कृतिः॥
units.translation: What use is release from outer bonds for someone bound by inner bondage? Therefore, capable people should make an effort to free themselves from inner bondage.

gloss.en: for the purpose of release from inner bondage

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
antarbandhena baddhasya kiṃ bahirbandha-mocanaiḥ|
tad antarbandha-muktyarthaṃ kriyatāṃ kṛtibhiḥ kṛtiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: In the absence of inner freedom, what is the good of being released from external bonds? It is therefore essential that one should try repeatedly until one frees oneself from within.

units.label: Verse 246
units.deva:
कृति-पर्यवसानैव मता तीव्र-मुमुक्षुता।
अन्या तु रञ्जनामात्रा यत्र नो दृश्यते कृतिः॥
units.translation: Intense desire for liberation is considered to culminate in action. Another kind is merely for pleasing [others], where no action is seen.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kṛti-paryavasānaiva matā tīvra-mumukṣutā|
anyā tu rañjanāmātrā yatra no dṛśyate kṛtiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: An intense love of liberation is the culmination of all spiritual discipline. The discipline that we often note in those lacking it, is merely for pleasing the public.

units.label: Verse 247
units.deva:
गेहादि सर्वम् अपहाय लघुत्व-बुद्ध्या
सौख्येच्छया स्वपतिनानलम् आविविक्षोः।
कान्ता-जनस्य नियता सुदृढा त्वरा या
सैषा फलान्त-गमने करणं मुमुक्षोः॥
units.translation: After abandoning her home and everything else as unimportant, a wife who wishes to enter the fire with her husband, out of desire for happiness, has steady and very firm urgency; this is a means for a liberation-seeker to reach the goal.

gloss.en: with the view that they are unimportant

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
gehādi sarvam apahāya laghutva-buddhyā
saukhyecchayā svapatinānalam āvivikṣoḥ|
kāntā-janasya niyatā sudṛḍhā tvarā yā
saiṣā phalānta-gamane karaṇaṃ mumukṣoḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Just as a woman who is intent upon committing satī abandons with a light heart her home and all the good things of life, the seeker after liberation should be intent upon Self-realization, and should hold in light esteem all the good things of this world and of the next.

units.label: Verse 248
units.deva:
नित्यानित्य-विवेकश्च देह-क्षणिकता-मतिः।
मृत्योर् भीतिश्च तापश्च मुमुक्षा-वृद्धि-कारणम्॥
units.translation: Discrimination between the eternal and non-eternal, conviction that the body is transient, fear of death, and awareness of suffering are causes for the growth of desire for liberation.

gloss.en: discrimination between the eternal and non-eternal
conviction that the body is transient
a cause for the growth of desire for liberation

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
nityānitya-vivekaśca deha-kṣaṇikatā-matiḥ|
mṛtyor bhītiśca tāpaśca mumukṣā-vṛddhi-kāraṇam||
units.editionTranslation: The desire for liberation grows in growing measure with discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal, with the awareness of the transient nature of life, and with the fear of death, as well as with a knowledge of the ills of life.

units.label: Verses 249–250
units.deva:
शिरो विवेकस् त्वत्यन्तं वैराग्यं वपुर् उच्यते।
शमादयः षडङ्गानि मोक्षेच्छा प्राण इष्यते॥
ईदृशाङ्ग-समायुक्तो जिज्ञासुर् युक्ति-कोविदः।
शूरो मृत्युं निहन्त्येव सम्यग्-ज्ञानासिना ध्रुवम्॥
units.translation: Discrimination is said to be the head, intense dispassion the body; the six qualities beginning with śama are the limbs, and desire for liberation is held to be the life-breath. A seeker endowed with these limbs, skilled in reasoning and heroic, certainly destroys death with the sword of right knowledge.

gloss.en: with the sword of right knowledge

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śiro vivekas tvatyantaṃ vairāgyaṃ vapur ucyate|
śamādayaḥ ṣaḍaṅgāni mokṣecchā prāṇa iṣyate||
īdṛśāṅga-samāyukto jijñāsur yukti-kovidaḥ|
śūro mṛtyuṃ nihantyeva samyag-jñānāsinā dhruvam||
units.editionTranslation: Let us imagine a being whose head is discrimination; whose body is intense dispassion; whose limbs are the six cardinal virtues such as self-restraint and the like; and whose life-breath is the love of liberation. Such is the ideal aspirant. If he should also be wise, and be endowed with a keen power of reasoning, he would be deemed a hero. With one stroke of knowledge, as with a sword, he would free himself from the bonds of death.

units.label: Verse 251
units.deva:
उक्त-साधन-सम्पन्नो जिज्ञासुर् यतिर् आत्मनः।
जिज्ञासायै गुरुं गच्छेत् समित्-पाणिर् नयोज्ज्वलः॥
units.translation: A renunciate seeker, equipped with the stated means and distinguished in conduct, should go to a guru for inquiry into the Self, carrying kindling sticks in hand.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
ukta-sādhana-sampanno jijñāsur yatir ātmanaḥ|
jijñāsāyai guruṃ gacchet samit-pāṇir nayojjvalaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The ideal aspirant after liberation, who is virtuous and has taken the vow of sannyāsa, who is equipped with all the requisite means, and who shines with spiritual lustre should approach a guru, samidh (kindling) in hand, and in all humility seek to be instructed upon the nature of the Ātman.

units.label: Verse 252
units.deva:
श्रोत्रियो ब्रह्म-निष्ठो यः प्रशान्तः समदर्शनः।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारो निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः॥
units.translation: The guru should be learned in scripture and established in Brahman, calm, equal-seeing, free from possessiveness and ego, free from the pairs of opposites, and without possessions.

gloss.en: free from the pairs of opposites

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śrotriyo brahma-niṣṭho yaḥ praśāntaḥ samadarśanaḥ|
nirmamo nirahaṅkāro nirdvandvo niṣparigrahaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The Guru should be one who is well-versed in the Śāstras, and is intent upon the knowledge of Brahman. He should be calm of mind, equable, non-attached, devoid of egoism, beyond the pairs of opposites, and free from the craving after worldly possessions.

units.label: Verse 253
units.deva:
अनपेक्षः शुचिर् दक्षः करुणामृत-सागरः।
एवं-लक्षण-सम्पन्नः स गुरुर् ब्रह्म-वित्तमः।
उपासाद्यः प्रयत्नेन जिज्ञासोः स्वार्थ-सिद्धये॥
units.translation: A guru who is free from dependence, pure, capable, and an ocean of compassion, endowed with these qualities and supreme in knowledge of Brahman, should be diligently approached by a seeker for the attainment of their own goal.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
anapekṣaḥ śucir dakṣaḥ karuṇāmṛta-sāgaraḥ|
evaṃ-lakṣaṇa-sampannaḥ sa gurur brahma-vittamaḥ|
upāsādyaḥ prayatnena jijñāsoḥ svārtha-siddhaye||
units.editionTranslation: He should be one who is not in need of anything from others. He should be pure of mind, skilful in action, and filled with boundless compassion, as wide as the ocean. He who is endowed in full with all these qualities is the ideal guru. Let him, who seeks liberation, approach such a guru with due humility, and seek enlightenment, so that he might attain his goal.

units.label: Verse 254
units.deva:
जन्मानेक-शतैः सदादरयुजा भक्त्या समाराधितो
भक्तैर् वैदिक-लक्षणेन विधिना सन्तुष्ट ईशः स्वयम्।
साक्षाच् छ्रीगुरु-रूपम् एत्य कृपया दृग्-गोचरः सन् प्रभुः
तत्त्वं साधु विबोध्य तारयति तान् संसार-दुःखार्णवात्॥
units.translation: Worshipped by devotees with reverent devotion and Vedic rites through many hundreds of births, the Lord becomes pleased; through grace, the Lord himself comes visibly in the form of Śrī Guru, teaches them reality clearly, and ferries them across the ocean of saṃsāra’s sorrow.

gloss.en: from the ocean of saṃsāra’s sorrow

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
janmāneka-śataiḥ sadādarayujā bhaktyā samārādhito
bhaktair vaidika-lakṣaṇena vidhinā santuṣṭa īśaḥ svayam|
sākṣāc chrīguru-rūpam etya kṛpayā dṛg-gocaraḥ san prabhuḥ
tattvaṃ sādhu vibodhya tārayati tān saṃsāra-duḥkhārṇavāt||
units.editionTranslation: When the Lord is pleased with the continuous devotion and worship, as prescribed in the Vedas, He assumes the form of the guru. He is mercy incarnate, and He imparts the knowledge of reality, and takes the aspirant across a sea of trouble.

units.label: Verse 255
units.deva:
अविद्या-हृदय-ग्रन्थि-विमोक्षोऽपि भवेद् यतः।
तम् एव गुरुर् इत्याहुर् गुरु-शब्दार्थ-वेदिनः॥
units.translation: Because the heart-knot of ignorance is released through him, those who know the meaning of the word guru call that person the guru alone.

gloss.en: release of the heart-knot of ignorance
those who know the meaning of the word guru

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
avidyā-hṛdaya-granthi-vimokṣo’pi bhaved yataḥ|
tam eva gurur ityāhur guru-śabdārtha-vedinaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Only such a person who liberates the aspirant from the bonds of desire, when one is still ignorant and knows not the Ātman, should be deemed, in the opinion of the wise, the guru.

units.label: Verse 256
units.deva:
शिव एव गुरुः साक्षात् गुरुर् एव शिवः स्वयम्।
उभयोर् अन्तरं किञ्चिन् न द्रष्टव्यं मुमुक्षुभिः॥
units.translation: Śiva himself is the guru; the guru himself is Śiva. A seeker of liberation should see no difference between the two.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śiva eva guruḥ sākṣāt gurur eva śivaḥ svayam|
ubhayor antaraṃ kiñcin na draṣṭavyaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Śiva himself takes the form of the guru. The guru is Śiva incarnate. Therefore the seeker afer liberation should not make any distinction between the two.

units.label: Verse 257
units.deva:
बन्ध-मुक्तं ब्रह्म-निष्ठं कृत-कृत्यं भजेद् गुरुम्।
यस्य प्रसादात् संसार-सागरो गोष्-पदायते॥
units.translation: One should serve a guru who is free from bondage, established in Brahman, and has accomplished what must be accomplished; by whose grace the ocean of saṃsāra becomes as small as a cow’s hoofprint.

gloss.en: having accomplished what must be accomplished
becomes the size of a cow’s hoofprint

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
bandha-muktaṃ brahma-niṣṭhaṃ kṛta-kṛtyaṃ bhajed gurum|
yasya prasādāt saṃsāra-sāgaro goṣ-padāyate||
units.editionTranslation: By meditating upon the guru who is free from bondage, who is ever absorbed in Brahman, who has achieved all that has to be achieved, the aspirant should gain the grace of the guru. Thanks to his grace, the vast ocean of misery shrinks to the size of a puddle that has been formed by the hoof-mark of a cow.

units.label: Verse 258
units.deva:
शुश्रूषया सदा भक्त्या प्रणामैर् विनयोक्तिभिः।
प्रसन्नं गुरुम् आसाद्य प्रष्टव्यं ज्ञेयम् आत्मनः॥
units.translation: Having approached a pleased guru through service, constant devotion, prostrations, and humble words, one should ask what is to be known about the Self.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
śuśrūṣayā sadā bhaktyā praṇāmair vinayoktibhiḥ|
prasannaṃ gurum āsādya praṣṭavyaṃ jñeyam ātmanaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: He who desires the grace of the guru should render devoted service, with reverence, offer personal homage, speak with humility and seek to be enlightened.

units.label: Verse 259
units.deva:
भगवन् करुणा-सिन्धो भव-सिन्धोर् भवांस् तरिः।
याम् आश्रित्याश्रमेणैव परं पारं गता बुधाः॥
units.translation: O Bhagavan, ocean of compassion, you are the ferry across the ocean of worldly existence. By taking refuge in you, the wise have reached the far shore through effort.

gloss.en: of the ocean of worldly existence

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
bhagavan karuṇā-sindho bhava-sindhor bhavāṃs tariḥ|
yām āśrityāśrameṇaiva paraṃ pāraṃ gatā budhāḥ||
units.editionTranslation: (On approaching his preceptor, the disciple says:) Bhagavan, you are the embodiment of grace. Have mercy upon me. Please ferry me across the ocean of misery, even as you have helped the many wise people who have sought shelter with you.

units.label: Verse 260
units.deva:
जन्मान्तर-कृतानन्त-पुण्य-कर्म-फलोदयः।
अद्य संनिहितो यस्मात् त्वत्-कृपा-पात्रम् अस्म्य् अहम्॥
units.translation: Because the fruit of countless meritorious deeds performed in previous births has ripened today, I am a recipient of your grace.

gloss.en: the arising of the fruit of countless meritorious deeds done in previous births

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
janmāntara-kṛtānanta-puṇya-karma-phalodayaḥ|
adya saṃnihito yasmāt tvat-kṛpā-pātram asmy aham||
units.editionTranslation: It is only as the result of the fruition of meritorious deeds performed in previous lives that one becomes worthy as I have become today, of receiving your grace.

units.label: Verse 261
units.deva:
सम्प्रीतिम् अक्ष्णोर् वदन-प्रसादम्
आनन्दम् अन्तः-करणस्य सद्यः।
विलोकनं ब्रह्म-विदस् तनोति
छिनत्ति मोहं सुगतिं व्यनक्ति॥
units.translation: The sight of a knower of Brahman immediately spreads delight in the eyes, serenity to the face, and joy in the heart; it cuts through delusion and reveals the good path.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
samprītim akṣṇor vadana-prasādam
ānandam antaḥ-karaṇasya sadyaḥ|
vilokanaṃ brahma-vidas tanoti
chinatti mohaṃ sugatiṃ vyanakti||
units.editionTranslation: A single kind look from a knower of Brahman is sufficient to flood the eye with tears, illumine the face with serenity, and fill the heart with bliss. It removes all delusion and is a harbinger of well-being.

units.label: Verse 262
units.deva:
हुताशनानां शशिनाम् इनानाम्
अप्य् अर्बुदं वापि न यन् निहन्तुम्।
शक्नोति तद् ध्वान्तम् अनन्तम् आन्तरं
हन्त्यात्म-वेत्ता सकृद् ईक्षणेन॥
units.translation: Even an immense number of fires, moons, and suns cannot destroy the boundless inner darkness; the knower of the Self destroys it with a single glance.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
hutāśanānāṃ śaśinām inānām
apy arbudaṃ vāpi na yan nihantum|
śaknoti tad dhvāntam anantam āntaraṃ
hantyātma-vettā sakṛd īkṣaṇena||
units.editionTranslation: The knower of Ātman destroys at a glance all the abysmal darkness within, which neither a hundred million fires, nor as many suns and moons could ever destroy.

units.label: Verse 263
units.deva:
दुष्पारे भव-सागरे जनि-मृत-व्याध्यादि-दुःखोत्कटे
घोरे पुत्र-कलत्र-मित्र-बहुल-ग्राहा-करे भी-करे।
कर्मोत्तुङ्ग-तरङ्ग-भङ्ग-निकरैर् आकृष्यमाणो मुहुः
यातायात-गति-भ्रमेण शरणं किञ्चिन् न पश्याम्यहम्॥
units.translation: I see no refuge at all. I am repeatedly dragged by heaps of towering waves of karma, confused by the cycle of coming and going, in this terrible, hard-to-cross ocean of worldly existence, fierce with the sorrows of birth, death, illness, and the like, and filled with many sharks—sons, spouse, and friends.

gloss.en: in the ocean of worldly existence
birth, death, illness, and the like
filled with many sharks—sons, spouse, and friends
by heaps of towering waves of karma
by confusion over the cycle of coming and going

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
duṣpāre bhava-sāgare jani-mṛta-vyādhyādi-duḥkhotkaṭe
ghore putra-kalatra-mitra-bahula-grāhā-kare bhī-kare|
karmottuṅga-taraṅga-bhaṅga-nikarair ākṛṣyamāṇo muhuḥ
yātāyāta-gati-bhrameṇa śaraṇaṃ kiñcin na paśyāmyaham||
units.editionTranslation: I am one who suffers in the sea of misery that is miscalled life. Birth and death come and go, alternating like the crest and the trough of the waves. Ill-health comes regular1y like the tides. Friends and relations are like the sharks at sea. I am utterly lost, and do not know how to save myself.

units.label: Verse 264
units.deva:
केन वा पुण्य-शेषेण तव पादाम्बुज-द्वयम्।
दृष्टवान् अस्मि माम् आर्तं मृत्योस् त्राहि दया-दृशा॥
units.translation: By what remaining merit have I seen your pair of lotus feet? I am distressed; save me from death with a compassionate glance.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
kena vā puṇya-śeṣeṇa tava pādāmbuja-dvayam|
dṛṣṭavān asmi mām ārtaṃ mṛtyos trāhi dayā-dṛśā||
units.editionTranslation: I do not know what meritorious deeds I have performed in my previous lives, that I should now be brought to your lotus feet. Save me from death, and be gracious unto me.

units.label: Verse 265
units.deva:
वदन्तम् एवं तं शिष्यं दृष्ट्यैव दयया गुरुः।
दद्याद् अभयम् एतस्मै मा भैष्टेति मुहुर् मुहुः॥
units.translation: The guru, looking compassionately at the disciple who speaks thus, should give him fearlessness, saying repeatedly, “Do not fear.”
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
vadantam evaṃ taṃ śiṣyaṃ dṛṣṭyaiva dayayā guruḥ|
dadyād abhayam etasmai mā bhaiṣṭeti muhur muhuḥ||
units.editionTranslation: With his eyes overflowing with mercy, the guru looks kindly upon the disciple, and says to him, ‘Fear not’. In this way the guru holds out the assurance of protection.

units.label: Verse 266
units.deva:
विद्वन् मृत्यु-भयं जहीहि भवतो नास्त्येव मृत्युः क्वचिन्
नित्यस्य द्वय-वर्जितस्य परमानन्दात्मनो ब्रह्मणः।
भ्रान्त्या किञ्चिद् अवेक्ष्य भीत-मनसा मिथ्या त्वया कथ्यते
मां त्राहीति हि सुप्तवत् प्रलपनं शून्यात्मकं ते मृषा॥
units.translation: “O wise one, give up the fear of death; death does not exist for you at all. Brahman is eternal, free from duality, and of the nature of supreme bliss. Seeing something through delusion, you falsely say with a frightened mind, ‘Protect me!’ Like someone asleep, your babbling is hollow and untrue.”
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
vidvan mṛtyu-bhayaṃ jahīhi bhavato nāstyeva mṛtyuḥ kvacin
nityasya dvaya-varjitasya paramānandātmano brahmaṇaḥ|
bhrāntyā kiñcid avekṣya bhīta-manasā mithyā tvayā kathyate
māṃ trāhīti hi suptavat pralapanaṃ śūnyātmakaṃ te mṛṣā||
units.editionTranslation: (The guru says:) You are wise, give up this fear of death; for there is no such thing. You are the eternal Brahman; the one without a second. You are of the nature of bliss. When you say that you are lost, you are merely talking out of delusion, as in a dream; and therefore it is not true.

units.label: Verse 267
units.deva:
निद्रा-गाढ-तमो-वृतः किल जनः स्वप्ने भुजङ्गादिना
ग्रस्तं स्वं समवेक्ष्य यत् प्रलपति त्रासाद् धतोऽस्मीत्यलम्।
आप्तेन प्रतिबोधितः कर-तलेनाताड्य पृष्टः स्वयं
किञ्चिन् नेति वदत्यमुष्य वचनं स्यात् तत् किमर्थं वद॥
units.translation: A person wrapped in the deep darkness of sleep sees himself in a dream seized by a snake or the like and babbles in fear, “I am surely killed!” If a trusted person wakes him by tapping him with a palm and asks him, he himself says, “Nothing.” Tell me, what can that statement of his mean?

gloss.en: wrapped in the deep darkness of sleep
by a snake or the like
with the palm of the hand

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
nidrā-gāḍha-tamo-vṛtaḥ kila janaḥ svapne bhujaṅgādinā
grastaṃ svaṃ samavekṣya yat pralapati trāsād dhato’smītyalam|
āptena pratibodhitaḥ kara-talenātāḍya pṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃ
kiñcin neti vadatyamuṣya vacanaṃ syāt tat kimarthaṃ vada||
units.editionTranslation: Lost in dull sleep, a man dreams that he has been bitten by a snake; and he then cries out incoherently through fear and says, ‘Oh! I am lost’. But if a friendly hand should shake him, and wake him and ask him what he meant, he merely replies, ‘Oh! It is nothing.’ How would you explain it?

units.label: Verse 268
units.deva:
रज्जोस् तु तत्त्वम् अनवेक्ष्य गृहीत-सर्प-
भावः पुमान् अयम् अहिर् वसतीति मोहात्।
आक्रोशति प्रतिबिभेति च कम्पते तन्
मिथ्यैव नात्र भुजगोऽस्ति विचार्यमाणे॥
units.translation: Failing to discern the true nature of a rope, this person, taking it to be a snake and thinking “a snake lives here,” cries out, becomes afraid, and trembles. When examined, that is indeed false: no snake exists here.

gloss.en: having taken on the idea of a snake

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
rajjos tu tattvam anavekṣya gṛhīta-sarpa-
bhāvaḥ pumān ayam ahir vasatīti mohāt|
ākrośati pratibibheti ca kampate tan
mithyaiva nātra bhujago’sti vicāryamāṇe||
units.editionTranslation: When one is not aware that a way-side rope is only rope one might imagine it to be a snake, feel fear, and tremble all over. All that is out of delusion; for on examination it is found that there is no snake at all.

units.label: Verse 269
units.deva:
तद्वत् त्वयाप्यात्मन उक्तम् एतज्
जन्माप्यय-व्याधि-जरादि-दुःखम्।
मृषैव सर्वं भ्रम-कल्पितं ते
सम्यग् विचार्यात्मनि मुञ्च भीतिम्॥
units.translation: Likewise, you have said this of the Self: the sorrow of birth, death, illness, old age, and the like. All of it is false, imagined by delusion. Examine the Self carefully and give up fear.

gloss.en: the sorrow of birth, death, illness, old age, and the like

units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
tadvat tvayāpyātmana uktam etaj
janmāpyaya-vyādhi-jarādi-duḥkham|
mṛṣaiva sarvaṃ bhrama-kalpitaṃ te
samyag vicāryātmani muñca bhītim||
units.editionTranslation: You say that you are subject to birth and death, sorrow and suffering, ill-health and old age. But really speaking, they are not inherent in your nature. They are but the figments of the mind. Seek your real nature as Ātman and give up this delusion.

units.label: Verse 270
units.deva:
भवान् अनात्मनो धर्मान् आत्मन्यारोप्य शोचति।
तद् अज्ञान-कृतं सर्वं भयं त्यक्त्वा सुखी भव॥
units.translation: You grieve by superimposing the qualities of the non-Self on the Self. Abandon all that fear caused by ignorance and be happy.
units.sectionTitle: The Topic of this Study and the Successful Student
units.iast:
bhavān anātmano dharmān ātmanyāropya śocati|
tad ajñāna-kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ bhayaṃ tyaktvā sukhī bhava||
units.editionTranslation: What you have superimposed upon the Ātman. are not in reality the attributes of the Ātman. All your grief is in vain; for it is the product of fear. Give up this error and become calm of mind.

units.label: Verse 271
units.deva:
श्रीमद्भिर् उक्तं सकलं मृषेति
दृष्टान्त एव ह्युपपद्यते तत्।
दार्ष्टान्तिके नैव भवादि-दुःखं
प्रत्यक्षतः सर्व-जन-प्रसिद्धम्॥
units.translation: “All that the revered one said is false”—that fits only the example. In the case being illustrated, suffering from worldly existence and the like is directly known to everyone.

gloss.en: suffering from worldly existence and the like

units.iast:
śrīmadbhir uktaṃ sakalaṃ mṛṣeti
dṛṣṭānta eva hyupapadyate tat|
dārṣṭāntike naiva bhavādi-duḥkhaṃ
pratyakṣataḥ sarva-jana-prasiddham||
units.editionTranslation: The disciple says: Revered Sir, you say that all grief is in vain. It may hold good as far as the analogy is concerned, but it does not enlighten me, for sorrow is at once real and universal. There is the evidence of the senses to prove it.

units.label: Verse 272
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्षेणानुभूतार्थः कथं मिथ्यात्वम् अर्हति।
चक्षुषो विषयं कुम्भं कथं मिथ्या करोम्यहम्॥
units.translation: How can an object experienced through direct perception be unreal? How can I regard the pot, an object of sight, as unreal?
units.iast:
pratyakṣeṇānubhūtārthaḥ kathaṃ mithyātvam arhati|
cakṣuṣo viṣayaṃ kumbhaṃ kathaṃ mithyā karomyaham||
units.editionTranslation: How can anyone say that what is based upon the testimony of the senses is unreal? If I should see this jar before me, how can I maintain that it is all unreal?

units.label: Verse 273
units.deva:
विद्यमानस्य मिथ्यात्वं कथं नु घटते प्रभो।
प्रत्यक्षं खलु सर्वेषां प्रमाणं प्रस्फुटार्थकम्॥
units.translation: O Lord, how can unreality be possible for what exists? Direct perception is indeed a means of knowledge for everyone, making its object clear.
units.iast:
vidyamānasya mithyātvaṃ kathaṃ nu ghaṭate prabho|
pratyakṣaṃ khalu sarveṣāṃ pramāṇaṃ prasphuṭārthakam||
units.editionTranslation: Revered Sir, how can we deny that which exists, and which the senses prove to be real. Is not sense perception one of the valid means of knowledge?

units.label: Verse 274
units.deva:
मर्त्यस्य मम जन्मादि-दुःख-भाजोऽल्प-जीविनः।
ब्रह्मत्वम् अपि नित्यत्वं परमानन्दता कथम्॥
units.translation: How can I, a mortal who bears the suffering beginning with birth and lives only briefly, be Brahman, eternal, and of supreme bliss?

gloss.en: sharing in suffering beginning with birth

units.iast:
martyasya mama janmādi-duḥkha-bhājo’lpa-jīvinaḥ|
brahmatvam api nityatvaṃ paramānandatā katham||
units.editionTranslation: Mortal that I am, and subject to the ills of life, how can I say that I am the absolute eternal existence and bliss supreme?

units.label: Verse 275
units.deva:
क आत्मा कस् त्वनात्मा च किमु लक्षणम् एतयोः।
आत्मन्यनात्म-धर्माणाम् आरोपः क्रियते कथम्॥
units.translation: What is the Self, and what is the non-Self? What are their characteristics, and how are the attributes of the non-Self superimposed on the Self?
units.iast:
ka ātmā kas tvanātmā ca kimu lakṣaṇam etayoḥ|
ātmanyanātma-dharmāṇām āropaḥ kriyate katham||
units.editionTranslation: What is the Ātman; and what is that which is other than the Ātman; and how do we distinguish between the two; and how does one superimpose upon the Ātman all those attributes which are not inherent in the Ātman?

units.label: Verse 276
units.deva:
किम् अज्ञानं तद्-उत्पन्न-भय-त्यागोऽपि वा कथम्।
किमु ज्ञानं तद्-उत्पन्न-सुख-प्राप्तिश्च वा कथम्॥
units.translation: What is ignorance, and how is the fear arising from it relinquished? What is knowledge, and how is the happiness arising from it attained?

gloss.en: giving up the fear produced by it
attaining the happiness produced by it

units.iast:
kim ajñānaṃ tad-utpanna-bhaya-tyāgo’pi vā katham|
kimu jñānaṃ tad-utpanna-sukha-prāptiśca vā katham||
units.editionTranslation: What is the nature of ignorance, and how do we overcome the fear arising from it? What is knowledge, and how does it help us to attain bliss eternal?

units.label: Verse 277
units.deva:
सर्वम् एतद् यथा-पूर्वं करामलकवत् स्फुटम्।
प्रतिपादय मे स्वामिन् श्री-गुरो करुणा-निधे॥
units.translation: O Master, revered Guru, treasure of compassion, explain all this clearly to me, as plainly as an āmalaka fruit in the palm of one’s hand.

gloss.en: like an āmalaka fruit in the palm

units.iast:
sarvam etad yathā-pūrvaṃ karāmalakavat sphuṭam|
pratipādaya me svāmin śrī-guro karuṇā-nidhe||
units.editionTranslation: I request you Revered Sir, out of your abounding mercy, to make all this as clear to me as the proverbial myrobalan in one’s hand.

units.label: Verse 278
units.deva:
धन्यः कृतार्थस् त्वम् अहो विवेकः
शिव-प्रसादस् तव विद्यते महान्।
विसृज्य तु प्राकृत-लोक-मार्गं
ब्रह्मावगन्तुं यतसे यतस् त्वम्॥
units.translation: Blessed and fulfilled are you! Great discernment and Śiva’s grace are present in you, because you have abandoned the ordinary people’s path and strive to know Brahman.
units.iast:
dhanyaḥ kṛtārthas tvam aho vivekaḥ
śiva-prasādas tava vidyate mahān|
visṛjya tu prākṛta-loka-mārgaṃ
brahmāvagantuṃ yatase yatas tvam||
units.editionTranslation: The guru says: Blessed you are. You have realised the object of life’s quest. By the grace of the Lord, you have given up the path trodden by the common people. You are in quest of Brahman, the absolute.

units.label: Verse 279
units.deva:
शिव-प्रसादेन विना न सिद्धिः
शिव-प्रसादेन विना न बुद्धिः।
शिव-प्रसादेन विना न युक्तिः
शिव-प्रसादेन विना न मुक्तिः॥
units.translation: Without Śiva’s grace there is no success; without Śiva’s grace there is no understanding, no reasoning, and no liberation.
units.iast:
śiva-prasādena vinā na siddhiḥ
śiva-prasādena vinā na buddhiḥ|
śiva-prasādena vinā na yuktiḥ
śiva-prasādena vinā na muktiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Unless the gracious Śiva is pleased, there is no success. Without the grace of Śiva, there is neither knowledge nor reasoning: and without the grace of Śiva, there is no liberation.

units.label: Verse 280
units.deva:
यस्य प्रसादेन विमुक्त-सङ्गाः
शुकादयः संसृति-बन्ध-मुक्ताः।
तस्य प्रसादो बहु-जन्म-लभ्यो
भक्त्यैक-गम्यो भव-मुक्ति-हेतुः॥
units.translation: By whose grace Śuka and others, freed from attachment, became free from the bonds of saṃsāra; that grace is attained after many births, reached by devotion alone, and is the cause of liberation from worldly existence.

gloss.en: freed from the bonds of saṃsāra
a cause of liberation from worldly existence

units.iast:
yasya prasādena vimukta-saṅgāḥ
śukādayaḥ saṃsṛti-bandha-muktāḥ|
tasya prasādo bahu-janma-labhyo
bhaktyaika-gamyo bhava-mukti-hetuḥ||
units.editionTranslation: It is by the grace of Śiva that Śuka and others have attained liberation from the bonds of saṃsāra. At the end of many lives, by his abounding grace, He grants freedom from bondage.

units.label: Verse 281
units.deva:
विवेको जन्तूनां प्रभवति जनिष्वेव बहुषु
प्रसादाद् एवैशाद् बहु-सुकृत-पाकोदय-वशात्।
यतस् तस्माद् एव त्वम् अपि परमार्थावगमने
कृतारम्भः पुंसाम् इदम् इह विवेकस्य तु फलं॥
units.translation: Discernment arises among beings only after many births, by the Lord’s grace and through the ripening of many meritorious deeds. Therefore, you too have undertaken to know the highest reality; this indeed is the fruit of discernment in a person.

gloss.en: through the ripening of many meritorious deeds

units.iast:
viveko jantūnāṃ prabhavati janiṣveva bahuṣu
prasādād evaiśād bahu-sukṛta-pākodaya-vaśāt|
yatas tasmād eva tvam api paramārthāvagamane
kṛtārambhaḥ puṃsām idam iha vivekasya tu phalaṃ||
units.editionTranslation: By the grace of God, those who have performed meritorious deeds in their previous lives become capable of distinguishing between the real and the unreal. It is as the result of such acquired merit that you are now exerting yourself, for it is only those who are worthy that are endowed with discrimination.

units.label: Verse 282
units.deva:
मर्त्यत्व-सिद्धेर् अपि पुंस्त्व-सिद्धेर्
विप्रत्व-सिद्धेश्च विवेक-सिद्धेः।
वदन्ति मुख्यं फलम् एव मोक्षं
व्यर्थं समस्तं यदि चेन् न मोक्षः॥
units.translation: They say the chief fruit of attaining human birth, manhood, brahminhood, and discernment is liberation alone. If there is no liberation, everything is in vain.
units.iast:
martyatva-siddher api puṃstva-siddher
vipratva-siddheśca viveka-siddheḥ|
vadanti mukhyaṃ phalam eva mokṣaṃ
vyarthaṃ samastaṃ yadi cen na mokṣaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The learned say that the principal benefit to be derived by having a human body, by being born as a brahmin and by being endowed with discrimination is that one might attain liberation. If one should be endowed with all these; and yet fail to attain liberation, all that would be in vain.

units.label: Verse 283
units.deva:
प्रश्नः समीचीनतरस् तवायं
यद् आत्म-तत्त्वावगमे प्रवृत्तिः।
ततस् तवैतत् सकलं समूलं
निवेदयिष्यामि मुदा शृणुष्व॥
units.translation: Your question is especially apt, because you are engaged in knowing the truth of the Self. Therefore I shall gladly explain all this to you, down to its roots. Listen.

gloss.en: in knowing the truth of the Self

units.iast:
praśnaḥ samīcīnataras tavāyaṃ
yad ātma-tattvāvagame pravṛttiḥ|
tatas tavaitat sakalaṃ samūlaṃ
nivedayiṣyāmi mudā śṛṇuṣva||
units.editionTranslation: You have raised a number of pertinent questions. I find that you are striving to know the truth of the Ātman. I shall therefore explain to you in detail all that you have asked. Listen to me with an equable mind.

units.label: Verse 284
units.deva:
मर्त्यत्वं त्वयि कल्पितं भ्रम-वशात् तेनैव जन्मादयः
तत्-सम्भावितम् एव दुःखम् अपि ते नो वस्तुतस् तन् मृषा।
निद्रा-मोह-वशाद् उपागत-सुखं दुःखं च किं नु त्वया
सत्यत्वेन विलोकितं क्वचिद् अपि ब्रूहि प्रबोधागमे॥
units.translation: Mortality has been imagined in you through delusion; from that very delusion come birth and the like, and the suffering they bring. These are not truly yours; they are false. Tell me: after waking, have you ever regarded dream pleasure or pain as real?
units.iast:
martyatvaṃ tvayi kalpitaṃ bhrama-vaśāt tenaiva janmādayaḥ
tat-sambhāvitam eva duḥkham api te no vastutas tan mṛṣā|
nidrā-moha-vaśād upāgata-sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca kiṃ nu tvayā
satyatvena vilokitaṃ kvacid api brūhi prabodhāgame||
units.editionTranslation: You have superimposed the idea of death upon the Ātman; and out of delusion you imagine that you are subject to birth and death. But grieve not, for they are not natural to you. They are unreal. Would anyone deem the pleasures and pains of the dream world to be real at the waking moment?

units.label: Verse 285
units.deva:
नाशेष-लोकैर् अनुभूयमानः
प्रत्यक्षतोऽयं सकल-प्रपञ्चः।
कथं मृषा स्याद् इति शङ्कनीयं
विचार-शून्येन विमुह्यता त्वया॥
units.translation: You, confused and devoid of reflection, should not question how this entire universe—directly experienced by everyone—could be false.
units.iast:
nāśeṣa-lokair anubhūyamānaḥ
pratyakṣato’yaṃ sakala-prapañcaḥ|
kathaṃ mṛṣā syād iti śaṅkanīyaṃ
vicāra-śūnyena vimuhyatā tvayā||
units.editionTranslation: Having been overcome by delusion, you have lost your power of reflection. That is why you are asking how can that which all people consider to be real upon the basis of sense perception be deemed unreal.

units.label: Verse 286
units.deva:
दिवान्ध-दृष्टेस् तु दिवान्धकारः
प्रत्यक्ष-सिद्धोऽपि स किं यथार्थः।
तद्वद् भ्रमेणावगतः पदार्थो
भ्रान्तस्य सत्यः सुमतेर् मृषैव॥
units.translation: To a person blind in daylight, darkness is directly perceived; but is it truly real? Likewise, an object perceived through delusion is real to the deluded person, but false to the wise.

gloss.en: to the sight of a person blind in daylight

units.iast:
divāndha-dṛṣṭes tu divāndhakāraḥ
pratyakṣa-siddho’pi sa kiṃ yathārthaḥ|
tadvad bhrameṇāvagataḥ padārtho
bhrāntasya satyaḥ sumater mṛṣaiva||
units.editionTranslation: To a blind man the day seems dark. Would you say that his senses reveal the truth to him? In the same manner, whatever is perceived in a state of delusion is real only as long as the delusion lasts.

units.label: Verse 287
units.deva:
घटोऽयम् इत्यत्र घटाभिधानः
प्रत्यक्षतः कश्चिद् उदेति दृष्टेः।
विचार्यमाणे स तु नास्ति तत्र
मृद् अस्ति तद्भाव-विलक्षणा सा॥
units.translation: When one sees an object and says, “This is a jar,” the idea of a jar arises from direct perception. But on examination, that jar does not exist there; clay exists, distinct from the jar-form.
units.iast:
ghaṭo’yam ityatra ghaṭābhidhānaḥ
pratyakṣataḥ kaścid udeti dṛṣṭeḥ|
vicāryamāṇe sa tu nāsti tatra
mṛd asti tadbhāva-vilakṣaṇā sā||
units.editionTranslation: Upon the evidence of visual perception, people say, ‘This is a jar’. But when we examine it, we find that there is no jar at all. There has been only clay; the jar is a form of it, it is not different from clay.

units.label: Verse 288
units.deva:
प्रादेशमात्रः परिदृश्यतेऽर्कः
शास्त्रेण सन्दर्शित-लक्ष-योजनः।
मानान्तरेण क्वचिद् एति बाधां
प्रत्यक्षम् अप्यत्र हि न व्यवस्था॥
units.translation: The sun appears to be only a span, while scripture describes it as a hundred thousand yojanas in size. By another means of measurement, direct perception is contradicted; therefore it is not a settled measure here.
units.iast:
prādeśamātraḥ paridṛśyate’rkaḥ
śāstreṇa sandarśita-lakṣa-yojanaḥ|
mānāntareṇa kvacid eti bādhāṃ
pratyakṣam apyatra hi na vyavasthā||
units.editionTranslation: By enclosing the forefinger and the thumb one says that it represents the dimension of the sun, but the Śāstras say that the dimension of the sun is of the order of a hundred thousand yojanas or miles. Thus what the senses perceive stands negated by a different kind of evidence. Consequently, what is perceived by the senses cannot be said to be final.

units.label: Verse 289
units.deva:
तस्मात् त्वयीदं भ्रमतः प्रतीतं
मृषैव नो सत्यम् अवेहि साक्षात्।
ब्रह्म त्वम् एवासि सुख-स्वरूपं
त्वत्तो न भिन्नं विचिनुष्व बुद्धौ॥
units.translation: Therefore know directly that this appearance in you, while deluded, is false, not true. You yourself are Brahman, whose nature is bliss; discern in your understanding that Brahman is not different from you.
units.iast:
tasmāt tvayīdaṃ bhramataḥ pratītaṃ
mṛṣaiva no satyam avehi sākṣāt|
brahma tvam evāsi sukha-svarūpaṃ
tvatto na bhinnaṃ vicinuṣva buddhau||
units.editionTranslation: In the same way, all that which you have said in a state of delusion is also unreal. It has no bearing, really speaking. You are none other than Brahman, and Brahman is of the nature of bliss. The wise know that they are in no way other than Brahman.

units.label: Verse 290
units.deva:
लोकान्तरे वात्र गुहान्तरे वा
तीर्थान्तरे कर्म-परम्परान्तरे।
शास्त्रान्तरे नास्त्यनुपश्यताम् इह
स्वयं परं ब्रह्म विचार्यमाणे॥
units.translation: Upon inquiry, those who seek see that the supreme Brahman is not in another world, cave, sacred place, chain of rituals, or scripture; it is here itself.
units.iast:
lokāntare vātra guhāntare vā
tīrthāntare karma-paramparāntare|
śāstrāntare nāstyanupaśyatām iha
svayaṃ paraṃ brahma vicāryamāṇe||
units.editionTranslation: The wise do not seek Brahman in some far off region, either here or in some future world. They do not seek Brahman in some cavern, or on the bank of some sacred stream, or in rituals or in the Śāstras. They seek Brahman and realize Him as the Ātman within.

units.label: Verse 291
units.deva:
तत्त्वम् आत्मस्थम् अज्ञात्वा मूढः शास्त्रेषु पश्यति।
गोपः कक्ष-गतं छागं यथा कूपेषु दुर्मतिः॥
units.translation: Not knowing the reality that abides in oneself, a fool looks for it in the scriptures, like a foolish herdsman searching wells for a goat tucked under his arm.
units.iast:
tattvam ātmastham ajñātvā mūḍhaḥ śāstreṣu paśyati|
gopaḥ kakṣa-gataṃ chāgaṃ yathā kūpeṣu durmatiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: As for those who are not wise, they fail to realize Him, and seek Him in the Śāstras, like the foolish goat-herd who in a fit of absent-mindedness, sought the goat that he carried in his arms, in the reflection cast by it in a well.

units.label: Verse 292
units.deva:
स्वम् आत्मानं परं मत्वा परमात्मानम् अन्यथा।
विमृग्यते पुनः स्वात्मा बहिः कोशेषु पण्डितैः॥
units.translation: Having thought one’s own Self to be one thing and the Supreme Self another, even the learned search again for their own Self outside, in the sheaths.
units.iast:
svam ātmānaṃ paraṃ matvā paramātmānam anyathā|
vimṛgyate punaḥ svātmā bahiḥ kośeṣu paṇḍitaiḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The so-called wise think that the Ātman is something other than themselves, and that the Paramātman is something other than the Ātman; and they go in quest of the Ātman in the external sheaths.

units.label: Verse 293
units.deva:
विस्मृत्य वस्तुनस् तत्त्वम् अध्यारोप्य च वस्तुनि।
अवस्तुतां च तद्-धर्मान् मुधा शोचति नान्यथा॥
units.translation: Having forgotten the truth of reality and superimposed unreality and its attributes on reality, one grieves in vain—and for no other reason.
units.iast:
vismṛtya vastunas tattvam adhyāropya ca vastuni|
avastutāṃ ca tad-dharmān mudhā śocati nānyathā||
units.editionTranslation: They forget the nature of that which is real. They superimpose upon the Ātman all those attributes which are not natural to the Ātman. That is why they grieve in vain; though, really, there is no cause for grief.

units.label: Verse 294
units.deva:
आत्मानात्म-विवेकं ते वक्ष्यामि शृणु सादरम्।
यस्य श्रवणमात्रेण मुच्यतेऽनात्म-बन्धनात्॥
units.translation: I shall explain to you the discernment of the Self and non-Self; listen attentively. By merely hearing it, one is freed from bondage to the non-Self.

gloss.en: discernment of the Self and non-Self

units.iast:
ātmānātma-vivekaṃ te vakṣyāmi śṛṇu sādaram|
yasya śravaṇamātreṇa mucyate’nātma-bandhanāt||
units.editionTranslation: Distinguishing between the Ātman and what the Ātman is not Listen earnestly, and I shall tell you how to distinguish between what the Ātman is and what the Ātman is not. By listening to it attentively, one would be liberated from bondage.

units.label: Verses 295–296
units.deva:
इत्युक्त्वाभिमुखी-कृत्य शिष्यं करुणया गुरुः।
अध्यारोपाप-वादाभ्यां निष्प्रपञ्चं प्रपञ्चयन्॥
सम्यक् प्राबोधयत् तत्त्वं शास्त्र-दृष्टेन वर्त्मना।
सर्वेषाम् उपकाराय तत्-प्रकारोऽत्र दर्श्यते॥
units.translation: Having said this, the guru compassionately turns the student toward him. Through superimposition and negation he expounds the non-manifold [reality] and properly teaches the truth by the method found in scripture. For everyone’s benefit, that method is shown here.
units.iast:
ityuktvābhimukhī-kṛtya śiṣyaṃ karuṇayā guruḥ|
adhyāropāpa-vādābhyāṃ niṣprapañcaṃ prapañcayan||
samyak prābodhayat tattvaṃ śāstra-dṛṣṭena vartmanā|
sarveṣām upakārāya tat-prakāro’tra darśyate||
units.editionTranslation: Thus, out of his abounding grace, the guru explained to his disciple the nature of Reality. He taught how Brahman is not tainted by contact with the world; how people superimpose the unreal upon the real, and how it should be negated. What he thus taught is in accordance with the known method of the Śāstras. It is now given exactly in the same order for the benefit of all.

units.label: Verse 297
units.deva:
वस्तुन्य् अवस्त्वारोपो यः सोऽध्यारोप इतीर्यते।
असर्प-भूते रज्ज्वादौ सर्पत्वारोपणं यथा॥
units.translation: The imposition of something unreal onto the real is called adhyāropa, superimposition; for example, attributing snakehood to a rope that is not a snake.

gloss.en: in what is not a snake
in a rope and the like

units.iast:
vastuny avastvāropo yaḥ so’dhyāropa itīryate|
asarpa-bhūte rajjvādau sarpatvāropaṇaṃ yathā||
units.editionTranslation: Superimposition To attribute to that which is real the nature or the properties of unreal objects is known as superimposition (adhyāropa). It is as though one imagines that a wayside rope is a snake.

units.label: Verse 298
units.deva:
वस्तु तावत् परं ब्रह्म सत्य-ज्ञानादि-लक्षणम्।
इदम् आरोपितं यत्र भाति खे नीलतादिवत्॥
units.translation: The real is supreme Brahman, characterized by truth, knowledge, and the like. This [world] appears superimposed upon it, like blueness in the sky.

gloss.en: characterized by truth, knowledge, and the like

units.iast:
vastu tāvat paraṃ brahma satya-jñānādi-lakṣaṇam|
idam āropitaṃ yatra bhāti khe nīlatādivat||
units.editionTranslation: The Supreme Brahman is characterised by truth, knowledge, and bliss; and that is the only Reality. The universe is perceived to be real, because it is superimposed upon Brahman, just as the blue colour is superimposed upon the sky (kha, space).

units.label: Verse 299
units.deva:
तत् कारणं यद् अज्ञानं सकार्यं सद्-विलक्षणम्।
अवस्त्व् इत्युच्यते सद्भिर् यस्य बाधा प्रदृश्यते॥
units.translation: That cause, ignorance, together with its effect and distinct from Being, is called unreal by the wise, because its sublation is observed.
units.iast:
tat kāraṇaṃ yad ajñānaṃ sakāryaṃ sad-vilakṣaṇam|
avastv ityucyate sadbhir yasya bādhā pradṛśyate||
units.editionTranslation: Ignorance Ignorance (ajñāna) is the cause of the world seeming to be real. But ignorance is something other than Reality. As both ignorance and its effect are unreal, they are negated on the evidence of Vedānta. It is in this way that the wise eliminate both ignorance which is the cause and the world which is the effect.

units.label: Verse 300
units.deva:
अवस्तु तत् प्रमाणैर् यद् बाध्यते शुक्ति-रौप्यवत्।
न बाध्यते यत् तद् वस्तु त्रिषु कालेषु शुक्तिवत्॥
units.translation: That which is sublated by valid means of knowledge, like silver in nacre, is unreal. That which is not sublated in the three times, like nacre, is real.
units.iast:
avastu tat pramāṇair yad bādhyate śukti-raupyavat|
na bādhyate yat tad vastu triṣu kāleṣu śuktivat||
units.editionTranslation: Whatever is negated by means of proof, such as the seeming idea of silver upon the mother-of-pearl must needs be unreal. But what is not so disproved as for instance the mother-of-pearl itself, must needs be real, if it is true at all times.

units.label: Verse 301
units.deva:
शुक्तेर् बाधा न खल्वस्ति रजतस्य यथा तथा।
अवस्तु-संज्ञितं यत् तज् जगद्-अध्यास-कारणम्॥
units.translation: Just as the falsity of silver does not negate the nacre itself, so what is called unreal is the cause of the world’s superimposition.

gloss.en: the cause of the world’s superimposition

units.iast:
śukter bādhā na khalvasti rajatasya yathā tathā|
avastu-saṃjñitaṃ yat taj jagad-adhyāsa-kāraṇam||
units.editionTranslation: Although the presence of silver in the mother-of-pearl is unreal, the mother-of-pearl as such is real. Ignorance, therefore, is the cause of all such unreal superimpositions; and that is why the universe seems to be real.

units.label: Verse 302
units.deva:
सदसद्भ्याम् अनिर्वाच्यम् अज्ञानं त्रि-गुणात्मकम्।
वस्तु तत्त्वावबोधैक-बाध्यं तद्-भाव-लक्षणम्॥
units.translation: Ignorance is indescribable as either existent or nonexistent, and is made of three guṇas. It is an entity negated only by knowledge of reality; this is its defining mark.

gloss.en: negated only by knowledge of reality

units.iast:
sadasadbhyām anirvācyam ajñānaṃ tri-guṇātmakam|
vastu tattvāvabodhaika-bādhyaṃ tad-bhāva-lakṣaṇam||
units.editionTranslation: As ignorance is the product of the triune qualities, it is indescribable; and we cannot say of it that it either is, or is not. But such is its peculiar characteristic that it is negated in the light of the knowledge of the ultimate Reality, Brahman.

units.label: Verse 303
units.deva:
मिथ्या-सम्बन्धतस् तत्र ब्रह्मण्याश्रित्य तिष्ठति।
मणौ शक्तिर् यथा तद्वन् नैतद् आश्रय-दूषकम्॥
units.translation: It abides there in Brahman, resting on it through a false relation, as a power abides in a gem; yet this does not taint its support.
units.iast:
mithyā-sambandhatas tatra brahmaṇyāśritya tiṣṭhati|
maṇau śaktir yathā tadvan naitad āśraya-dūṣakam||
units.editionTranslation: Although it is unreal in itself, it has Brahman for its basis, and abides in Brahman. But Brahman is not tainted by contact with it; for Brahman is like a gem which nothing can defile.

units.label: Verse 304
units.deva:
सद्-भावे लिङ्गम् एतस्य कार्यम् एतच् चराचरम्।
मानं श्रुतिः स्मृतिश् चाज्ञोऽहम् इत्यनुभवोऽपि च॥
units.translation: This moving and unmoving world, its effect, is a sign of Brahman’s existence. Śruti and Smṛti, and even the experience “I am ignorant,” are means of knowing Brahman.
units.iast:
sad-bhāve liṅgam etasya kāryam etac carācaram|
mānaṃ śrutiḥ smṛtiś cājño’ham ityanubhavo’pi ca||
units.editionTranslation: The animate and the inanimate, and all that are produced out of them, prove the existence of Brahman. Śruti and Smṛti are the measure of it. Thus when one says, ‘I do not know Brahman’ even that should be taken as a proof of the existence of Brahman.

units.label: Verse 305
units.deva:
