अज्ञानं प्रकृतिः शक्तिर् अविद्येति निगद्यते।
तद् एतत् सन् न भवति नासद् वा शुक्ति-रौप्यवत्॥
units.translation: Ignorance is called prakṛti, power, and avidyā. Like silver in nacre, this is neither existent nor nonexistent.
units.iast:
ajñānaṃ prakṛtiḥ śaktir avidyeti nigadyate|
tad etat san na bhavati nāsad vā śukti-raupyavat||
units.editionTranslation: One may call it by various names, such as ajñāna or ignorance, prakṛti or the material cause, sakti or the power that animates, and avidyā or the absence of knowledge. By whatever name it is called, all that may be said of it is that like the proverbial silver in the mother-of-pearl, it neither is nor is not.

units.label: Verse 306
units.deva:
सतो भिन्नम् अभिन्नं वा न दीपस्य प्रभा यथा।
न सावयवम् अन्यद् वा बीजस्याङ्कुरवत् क्वचित्॥
units.translation: Like a lamp’s light, it cannot be defined as either different from or non-different from Being. Nor is it made of parts or something entirely separate, as a sprout is [from] a seed.
units.iast:
sato bhinnam abhinnaṃ vā na dīpasya prabhā yathā|
na sāvayavam anyad vā bījasyāṅkuravat kvacit||
units.editionTranslation: It is neither one with Brahman, nor even entirely other than Brahman. Like a lamp and its light, it is in Brahman; but it is not itself Brahman. Like a sprout and the seed which gives birth to it, it is neither a part of Brahman, nor apart from it.

units.label: Verse 307
units.deva:
अत एतद् अनिर्वाच्यम् इत्येव कवयो विदुः।
समष्टि-व्यष्टि-रूपेण द्विधाज्ञानं निगद्यते॥
units.translation: Therefore the wise know this to be indescribable. Ignorance is said to be twofold, in its collective and individual forms.
units.iast:
ata etad anirvācyam ityeva kavayo viduḥ|
samaṣṭi-vyaṣṭi-rūpeṇa dvidhājñānaṃ nigadyate||
units.editionTranslation: The wise say that the nature of ajñāna is inexplicable. Yet they distinguish two aspects of it – the one, its aggregate, characterised by collective pervasion; and the other, its aspect in relation to the individual.

units.label: Verse 308
units.deva:
नानात्वेन प्रतीतानाम् अज्ञानानाम् अभेदतः।
एकत्वेन समष्टिः स्याद् भू-रुहाणां वनं यथा॥
units.translation: Like a forest formed from many trees, the ignorances that appear as many may be one collective whole through their non-difference.
units.iast:
nānātvena pratītānām ajñānānām abhedataḥ|
ekatvena samaṣṭiḥ syād bhū-ruhāṇāṃ vanaṃ yathā||
units.editionTranslation: Thus, like a forest and the trees of which it is composed, it has at once a collective and an individual aspect. The collective aspect is something more than the sum total of the units. It has a distinctive peculiarity.

units.label: Verse 309
units.deva:
इयं समष्टिर् उत्कृष्टा सत्त्वांशोत्कर्षतः पुरा।
मायेति कथ्यते तज्-ज्ञैः शुद्ध-सत्त्वैक-लक्षणा॥
units.translation: This elevated collective, due to the predominance of the sattva component, is called Māyā by those who know it, characterized by pure sattva alone.

gloss.en: due to the predominance of the sattva component

units.iast:
iyaṃ samaṣṭir utkṛṣṭā sattvāṃśotkarṣataḥ purā|
māyeti kathyate taj-jñaiḥ śuddha-sattvaika-lakṣaṇā||
units.editionTranslation: In its collective aspect, it is dominated by the quality of sattva or purity. It is then known as Māyā, the cosmic illusion, the veil that hides Reality.

units.label: Verse 310
units.deva:
मायोपहित-चैतन्यं साभासं सत्त्व-बृंहितम्।
सर्व-ज्ञत्वादि-गुणकं सृष्टि-स्थित्यन्त-कारणम्॥
units.translation: Consciousness conditioned by Māyā, accompanied by appearance, enriched with sattva, and endowed with qualities such as omniscience, is the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution.

gloss.en: endowed with qualities such as omniscience
the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution

units.iast:
māyopahita-caitanyaṃ sābhāsaṃ sattva-bṛṃhitam|
sarva-jñatvādi-guṇakaṃ sṛṣṭi-sthityanta-kāraṇam||
units.editionTranslation: The Lord Pure consciousness has Māyā for its adjunct and is reflected in and through it. It is then endowed with the quality of all-knowingness and with an abundance of sattva. It is that which is the cause of the creation, preservation, and dissolution of the universe.

units.label: Verse 311
units.deva:
अव्याकृतं तद् अव्यक्तम् ईश इत्यपि गीयते।
सर्व-शक्ति-गुणोपेतः सर्व-ज्ञानावभासकः॥
units.translation: That is called the unmanifest, the unmanifested, and Īśa. It is endowed with all powers and qualities, and illuminates all knowledge.

gloss.en: endowed with all powers and qualities

units.iast:
avyākṛtaṃ tad avyaktam īśa ityapi gīyate|
sarva-śakti-guṇopetaḥ sarva-jñānāvabhāsakaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: It is then known as the Unmanifested, as the primordial element, and as Īśvara. The Lord is then endowed with the quality of all-knowingness, and is regarded as the illuminator of knowledge.

units.label: Verse 312
units.deva:
स्व-तन्त्रः सत्य-सङ्कल्पः सत्य-कामः स ईश्वरः।
तस्यैतस्य महा-विष्णोर् महा-शक्तेर् महीयसः॥
units.translation: He is independent, of true resolve and true desire; that is Īśvara, this great and mighty Mahāviṣṇu.
units.iast:
sva-tantraḥ satya-saṅkalpaḥ satya-kāmaḥ sa īśvaraḥ|
tasyaitasya mahā-viṣṇor mahā-śakter mahīyasaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Only the Supreme Lord, Īśvara, is independent. His will alone is realised. His desire alone is fulfilled and he alone is all-pervading, omnipotent, omniscient.

units.label: Verse 313
units.deva:
सर्व-ज्ञत्वेश्वरत्वादि-कारणत्वान् मनीषिणः।
कारणं वपुर् इत्याहुः समष्टिं सत्त्व-बृंहितम्॥
units.translation: The wise call the sattva-enriched collective the causal body, because it is the cause of omniscience, lordship, and the like.

gloss.en: because it is the cause of omniscience, lordship, and the like

units.iast:
sarva-jñatveśvaratvādi-kāraṇatvān manīṣiṇaḥ|
kāraṇaṃ vapur ityāhuḥ samaṣṭiṃ sattva-bṛṃhitam||
units.editionTranslation: On account of the dominance of sattva in it, the sages regard avidyā in its aggregate aspect as the causal body of Īśvara. Hence it is that Īśvara, the first cause of all is regarded as the omniscient Lord.

units.label: Verse 314
units.deva:
आनन्द-प्रचुरत्वेन साधकत्वेन कोशवत्।
सैषानन्दमयः कोश इतीशस्य निगद्यते॥
units.translation: Because of its supporting function and abundance of bliss, this is called the blissful sheath of Īśvara, like a sheath.
units.iast:
ānanda-pracuratvena sādhakatvena kośavat|
saiṣānandamayaḥ kośa itīśasya nigadyate||
units.editionTranslation: Like a cocoon that wraps a silk worm round and round, this superabundance of bliss that is in the Lord envelops this world, and marks itself manifest in and through the world. That is why the world is known, in its aggregate aspect, as the sheath of Īśvara.

units.label: Verse 315
units.deva:
सर्वोपरम-हेतुत्वात् सुषुप्ति-स्थानम् इष्यते।
प्राकृतः प्रलयो यत्र श्राव्यते श्रुतिभिर् मुहुः॥
units.translation: Because it is the cause of all things coming to rest, it is regarded as the state of deep sleep, where the natural dissolution is repeatedly taught in the Śrutis.

gloss.en: because it causes everything to come to rest

units.iast:
sarvoparama-hetutvāt suṣupti-sthānam iṣyate|
prākṛtaḥ pralayo yatra śrāvyate śrutibhir muhuḥ||
units.editionTranslation: In as much as in the stage of deep sleep everything merges in its original cause, that stage is regarded as the dwelling place of it. As the Śruti tells us repeatedly, in the same manner everything merges in Īśvara, the original cause, at the time of the final dissolution.

units.label: Verse 316
units.deva:
अज्ञानं व्यष्ट्यभिप्रायाद् अनेकत्वेन भिद्यते।
अज्ञान-वृत्तयो नाना तत्तद्-गुण-विलक्षणाः॥
units.translation: From the individual standpoint, ignorance is divided into many forms. Its forms are numerous and distinct according to their respective qualities.

gloss.en: distinct according to their respective qualities

units.iast:
ajñānaṃ vyaṣṭyabhiprāyād anekatvena bhidyate|
ajñāna-vṛttayo nānā tattad-guṇa-vilakṣaṇāḥ||
units.editionTranslation: Ajñāna however takes diverse forms in its individual aspect. The reason for it is that individuals are constituted diversely out of the three guṇas, or qualities.

units.label: Verse 317
units.deva:
वनस्य व्यष्ट्यभिप्रायाद् भू-रुहा इत्यनेकता।
यथा तथैवाज्ञानस्य व्यष्टितः स्याद् अनेकता॥
units.translation: Just as a forest is many trees when viewed individually, ignorance likewise has many forms from the individual standpoint.
units.iast:
vanasya vyaṣṭyabhiprāyād bhū-ruhā ityanekatā|
yathā tathaivājñānasya vyaṣṭitaḥ syād anekatā||
units.editionTranslation: The forest is one, but the trees are many. In the same way, from the point of view of distributive pervasion, ajñāna takes diverse forms.

units.label: Verse 318
units.deva:
व्यष्टिर् मलिन-सत्त्वैषा रजसा तमसा युता।
ततो निकृष्टा भवति योपाधिः प्रत्यग्-आत्मनः॥
units.translation: This individual aspect has a tainted sattva and is joined with rajas and tamas. Therefore, the adjunct of the inner Self is inferior.
units.iast:
vyaṣṭir malina-sattvaiṣā rajasā tamasā yutā|
tato nikṛṣṭā bhavati yopādhiḥ pratyag-ātmanaḥ||
units.editionTranslation: The individual On account of the predominance of rajas and tamas in the individual, the power of sattva becomes weakened. Thus, within the individual, pure consciousness become stained by contact with the adjuncts. That is why the individual aspect of ajñāna is inferior to the collective aspect.

units.label: Verses 319–320
units.deva:
चैतन्यं व्यष्ट्यवच्छिन्नं प्रत्यग्-आत्मेति गीयते।
साभासं व्यष्ट्युपहितं सत्-तादात्म्येन तद्-गुणैः॥
अभिभूतः स एवात्मा जीव इत्यभिधीयते।
किञ्चिज् ज्ञत्वानीश्वरत्व-संसारित्वादि-धर्मवान्॥
units.translation: Consciousness delimited by the individual is called the inner Self. Reflected and conditioned by the individual, it is identified with the individual qualities as real; that same Self, overcome by them and marked by limited knowledge, lack of lordship, and transmigration, is called the jīva.

gloss.en: having qualities such as limited knowledge, lack of lordship, and transmigration

units.iast:
caitanyaṃ vyaṣṭyavacchinnaṃ pratyag-ātmeti gīyate|
sābhāsaṃ vyaṣṭyupahitaṃ sat-tādātmyena tad-guṇaiḥ||
abhibhūtaḥ sa evātmā jīva ityabhidhīyate|
kiñcij jñatvānīśvaratva-saṃsāritvādi-dharmavān||
units.editionTranslation: When pure consciousness is revealed in and through the individual, in conjunction with avidyā as its adjunct, it becomes particularised, and is known as the inner Self. When the innermost Self identifies itself with the individual aspect of avidyā, and becomes overpowered by the triune guṇas or qualities, it feels as though its knowledge is circumscribed, that it is powerless, and subject to the law of transmigration. It is then that the inner self is known as the jīva.

units.label: Verse 321
units.deva:
अस्य व्यष्टिर् अहङ्कार-कारणत्वेन कारणम्।
वपुस् तत्राभिमान्यात्मा प्राज्ञ इत्युच्यते बुधैः॥
units.translation: Its individual aspect is the cause of ego. The Self that identifies with that causal body is called Prājña by the wise.
units.iast:
asya vyaṣṭir ahaṅkāra-kāraṇatvena kāraṇam|
vapus tatrābhimānyātmā prājña ityucyate budhaiḥ||

units.label: Verse 322
units.deva:
प्राज्ञत्वम् अस्यैकाज्ञान-भासकत्वेन सम्मतम्।
व्यष्टेर् निकृष्टत्वेनास्य नानेकाज्ञान-भासकम्॥
units.translation: It is accepted as Prājña because it illumines one ignorance. Since the individual aspect is limited, it does not illumine many ignorances.
units.iast:
prājñatvam asyaikājñāna-bhāsakatvena sammatam|
vyaṣṭer nikṛṣṭatvenāsya nānekājñāna-bhāsakam||

units.label: Verse 323
units.deva:
स्व-रूपाच्छादकत्वेनाप्यानन्द-प्रचुरत्वतः।
कारणं वपुर् आनन्दमयः कोश इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: Because it conceals its own nature and is abundant in bliss, the causal body is called the blissful sheath.

gloss.en: because it conceals its own nature

units.iast:
sva-rūpācchādakatvenāpyānanda-pracuratvataḥ|
kāraṇaṃ vapur ānandamayaḥ kośa itīryate||

units.label: Verse 324
units.deva:
अस्यावस्था सुषुप्तिः स्याद् यत्रानन्दः प्रकृष्यते।
एषोऽहं सुखम् अस्वाप्सं न तु किञ्चिद् अवेदिषम्॥
units.translation: Its state is deep sleep, in which bliss is prominent. [One recalls:] “I slept happily; I knew nothing.”
units.iast:
asyāvasthā suṣuptiḥ syād yatrānandaḥ prakṛṣyate|
eṣo’haṃ sukham asvāpsaṃ na tu kiñcid avediṣam||

units.label: Verses 325–326
units.deva:
इत्यानन्द-समुत्कर्षः प्रबुद्धेषु प्रदृश्यते।
समष्टेर् अपि च व्यष्टेर् उभयोर् वन-वृक्षवत्॥
अभेद एव नो भेदो जात्येकत्वेन वस्तुतः।
अभेद एव ज्ञातव्यस् तथेश-प्राज्ञयोर् अपि॥
units.translation: Thus the fullness of bliss is seen in those who awaken. The collective and individual aspects are both like a forest and its trees. In reality, because they are of one kind, there is no difference; likewise, Īśvara and Prājña are to be understood as non-different.

gloss.en: like a forest and its trees

units.iast:
ityānanda-samutkarṣaḥ prabuddheṣu pradṛśyate|
samaṣṭer api ca vyaṣṭer ubhayor vana-vṛkṣavat||
abheda eva no bhedo jātyekatvena vastutaḥ|
abheda eva jñātavyas tatheśa-prājñayor api||

units.label: Verse 327
units.deva:
सत्युपाध्योर् अभिन्नत्वे क्व भेदस् तद्-विशिष्टयोः।
एकी-भावे तरङ्गाब्ध्योः को भेदः प्रतिबिम्बयोः॥
units.translation: When the two adjuncts are non-different, what difference is there between the two things qualified by them? When waves and the ocean are one, what difference is there between their reflections?
units.iast:
satyupādhyor abhinnatve kva bhedas tad-viśiṣṭayoḥ|
ekī-bhāve taraṅgābdhyoḥ ko bhedaḥ pratibimbayoḥ||

units.label: Verse 328
units.deva:
अज्ञान-तद्-अवच्छिन्नाभासयोर् उभयोर् अपि।
आधारं शुद्ध-चैतन्यं यत् तत् तुर्यम् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: That pure consciousness which is the basis of both ignorance and the reflection delimited by it is called the Fourth (turya).

gloss.en: of the reflection delimited by it

units.iast:
ajñāna-tad-avacchinnābhāsayor ubhayor api|
ādhāraṃ śuddha-caitanyaṃ yat tat turyam itīryate||

units.label: Verse 329
units.deva:
एतद् एवाविविक्तं सद् उपाधिभ्यां च तद्-गुणैः।
महा-वाक्यस्य वाच्यार्थो विविक्तं लक्ष्य इष्यते॥
units.translation: This same Reality, when undifferentiated from the two adjuncts and their qualities, is the direct meaning of the great statement. When distinguished from them, it is understood as the implied meaning.
units.iast:
etad evāviviktaṃ sad upādhibhyāṃ ca tad-guṇaiḥ|
mahā-vākyasya vācyārtho viviktaṃ lakṣya iṣyate||

units.label: Verse 330
units.deva:
अनन्त-शक्ति-सम्पन्नो मायोपाधिक ईश्वरः।
ईक्षा-मात्रेण सृजति विश्वम् एतच् चराचरम्॥
units.translation: Īśvara, endowed with limitless power and having Māyā as his adjunct, creates this moving and unmoving universe by mere seeing.
units.iast:
ananta-śakti-sampanno māyopādhika īśvaraḥ|
īkṣā-mātreṇa sṛjati viśvam etac carācaram||

units.label: Verse 331
units.deva:
अद्वितीय-स्वमात्रोऽसौ निरुपादान ईश्वरः।
स्वयम् एव कथं सर्वं सृजतीति न शङ्क्यताम्॥
units.translation: Do not doubt how this nondual Lord, who is only himself and has no separate material cause, creates everything by himself.
units.iast:
advitīya-svamātro’sau nirupādāna īśvaraḥ|
svayam eva kathaṃ sarvaṃ sṛjatīti na śaṅkyatām||

units.label: Verse 332
units.deva:
निमित्तम् अप्युपादानं स्वयम् एव भवन् प्रभुः।
चराचरात्मकं विश्वं सृजत्य् अवति लुम्पति॥
units.translation: Being both the efficient cause and the material cause, the Lord himself creates, sustains, and dissolves the universe consisting of the moving and the unmoving.

gloss.en: consisting of the moving and the unmoving

units.iast:
nimittam apyupādānaṃ svayam eva bhavan prabhuḥ|
carācarātmakaṃ viśvaṃ sṛjaty avati lumpati||

units.label: Verse 333
units.deva:
स्व-प्राधान्येन जगतो निमित्तम् अपि कारणम्।
उपादानं तथोपाधि-प्राधान्येन भवत्ययम्॥
units.translation: When his own nature predominates, he is the efficient cause of the world; when the adjunct predominates, he becomes its material cause.
units.iast:
sva-prādhānyena jagato nimittam api kāraṇam|
upādānaṃ tathopādhi-prādhānyena bhavatyayam||

units.label: Verse 334
units.deva:
यथा लूता निमित्तं च स्व-प्रधानतया भवेत्।
स्व-शरीर-प्रधानत्वेनोपादानं तथेश्वरः॥
units.translation: As a spider is the efficient cause through itself and the material cause through its own body, so is Īśvara.

gloss.en: through the predominance of its own body

units.iast:
yathā lūtā nimittaṃ ca sva-pradhānatayā bhavet|
sva-śarīra-pradhānatvenopādānaṃ tatheśvaraḥ||

units.label: Verse 335
units.deva:
तमः-प्रधान-प्रकृति-विशिष्टात् परमात्मनः।
अभूत् सकाशाद् आकाशम् आकाशाद् वायुर् उच्यते॥
units.translation: From the Supreme Self, qualified by primordial nature in which tamas predominates, space arose; from space, air is said to arise.

gloss.en: from that qualified by primordial nature in which tamas predominates

units.iast:
tamaḥ-pradhāna-prakṛti-viśiṣṭāt paramātmanaḥ|
abhūt sakāśād ākāśam ākāśād vāyur ucyate||

units.label: Verses 336–337
units.deva:
वायोर् अग्निस् तथैवाग्नेर् आपोऽद्भ्यः पृथिवी क्रमात्।
शक्तेस् तमः-प्रधानत्वं तत्-कार्ये जाड्य-दर्शनात्॥
आरभन्ते कार्य-गुणान्ये कारण-गुणा हि ते।
एतानि सूक्ष्म-भूतानि भूत-मात्रा अपि क्रमात्॥
units.translation: Fire arises from air, likewise water from fire, and earth from water, in sequence. The predominance of tamas in the power is inferred from the insentience seen in its effect. The qualities of the cause indeed bring forth the qualities of the effect. These subtle elements are also called elemental essences, in sequence.
units.iast:
vāyor agnis tathaivāgner āpo’dbhyaḥ pṛthivī kramāt|
śaktes tamaḥ-pradhānatvaṃ tat-kārye jāḍya-darśanāt||
ārabhante kārya-guṇān ye kāraṇa-guṇā hi te|
etāni sūkṣma-bhūtāni bhūta-mātrā api kramāt||

units.label: Verse 338
units.deva:
एतेभ्यः सूक्ष्म-भूतेभ्यः सूक्ष्म-देहा भवन्त्यपि।
स्थूलान्यपि च भूतानि चान्योन्यांश-विमेलनात्॥
units.translation: Subtle bodies also arise from these subtle elements; gross elements arise from the mixing of parts with one another.

gloss.en: from mixing parts with one another

units.iast:
etebhyaḥ sūkṣma-bhūtebhyaḥ sūkṣma-dehā bhavantyapi|
sthūlānyapi ca bhūtāni cānyonyāṃśa-vimelanāt||

units.label: Verse 339
units.deva:
अपञ्ची-कृत-भूतेभ्यो जातं सप्त-दशाङ्गकम्।
संसार-कारणं लिङ्गम् आत्मनो भोग-साधनम्॥
units.translation: The subtle body, born from the elements before their fivefold combination, has seventeen parts. It causes transmigration and serves as the means for the Self’s experience.
units.iast:
apañcī-kṛta-bhūtebhyo jātaṃ sapta-daśāṅgakam|
saṃsāra-kāraṇaṃ liṅgam ātmano bhoga-sādhanam||

units.label: Verse 340
units.deva:
श्रोत्रादि-पञ्चकं चैव वाग्-आदीनां च पञ्चकम्।
प्राणादि-पञ्चकं बुद्धि-मनसी लिङ्गम् उच्यते॥
units.translation: The five beginning with hearing, the five beginning with speech, the five beginning with breath, the intellect, and the mind are called the subtle body.

gloss.en: the group of five beginning with hearing
the group of five beginning with breath

units.iast:
śrotrādi-pañcakaṃ caiva vāg-ādīnāṃ ca pañcakam|
prāṇādi-pañcakaṃ buddhi-manasī liṅgam ucyate||

units.label: Verse 341
units.deva:
श्रोत्र-त्वक्-चक्षुर्-जिह्वा-घ्राणानि पञ्च जातानि।
आकाशादीनां सत्त्वांशेभ्यो धीन्द्रियाण्यनुक्रमतः॥
units.translation: The five senses—hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell—arise in order from the sattva portions of space and the other elements.

gloss.en: of space and the other elements

units.iast:
śrotra-tvak-cakṣur-jihvā-ghrāṇāni pañca jātāni|
ākāśādīnāṃ sattvāṃśebhyo dhīndriyāṇyanukramataḥ||

units.label: Verse 342
units.deva:
आकाशादि-गताः पञ्च सात्त्विकांशाः परस्-परम्।
मिलित्वैवान्तःकरणम् अभवत् सर्व-कारणम्॥
units.translation: The five sattva portions present in space and the other elements, joining with one another, became the internal organ, the cause of all.

gloss.en: present in space and the other elements

units.iast:
ākāśādi-gatāḥ pañca sāttvikāṃśāḥ paras-param|
militvaivāntaḥkaraṇam abhavat sarva-kāraṇam||

units.label: Verse 343
units.deva:
प्रकाशकत्वाद् एतेषां सात्त्विकांशत्वम् इष्यते।
प्रकाशकत्वं सत्त्वस्य स्वच्छत्वेन यतस् ततः॥
units.translation: Because these [portions] illuminate, they are regarded as sattvic portions; for sattva’s illuminating quality comes from its clarity.

gloss.en: the condition of being sattva portions

units.iast:
prakāśakatvād eteṣāṃ sāttvikāṃśatvam iṣyate|
prakāśakatvaṃ sattvasya svacchatvena yatas tataḥ||

units.label: Verse 344
units.deva:
तद् अन्तः-करणं वृत्ति-भेदेन स्याच् चतुर्विधम्।
मनो बुद्धिर् अहङ्कारश् चित्तं चेति तद् उच्यते॥
units.translation: That internal organ is fourfold according to its functions; it is called mind, intellect, ego, and memory.
units.iast:
tad antaḥ-karaṇaṃ vṛtti-bhedena syāc caturvidham|
mano buddhir ahaṅkāraś cittaṃ ceti tad ucyate||

units.label: Verse 345
units.deva:
सङ्कल्पान् मन इत्याहुर् बुद्धिर् अर्थस्य निश्चयात्।
अभिमानाद् अहङ्कारश् चित्तम् अर्थस्य चिन्तनात्॥
units.translation: They call it mind because of intentions; intellect because it determines an object; ego because of identification; and memory because of thinking about an object.
units.iast:
saṅkalpān mana ityāhur buddhir arthasya niścayāt|
abhimānād ahaṅkāraś cittam arthasya cintanāt||

units.label: Verse 346
units.deva:
मनस्यपि च बुद्धौ च चित्ताहङ्कारयोः क्रमात्।
अन्तर्-भावोऽत्र बोद्धव्यो लिङ्ग-लक्षण-सिद्धये॥
units.translation: Here, the inclusion of memory in the mind and of ego in the intellect, respectively, should be understood to establish the definition of the subtle body.

gloss.en: to establish the definition of the subtle body

units.iast:
manasyapi ca buddhau ca cittāhaṅkārayoḥ kramāt|
antar-bhāvo’tra boddhavyo liṅga-lakṣaṇa-siddhaye||

units.label: Verse 347
units.deva:
चिन्तनं च मनो-धर्मः सङ्कल्पादिर् यथा तथा।
अन्तर्-भावो मनस्येव सम्यक् चित्तस्य सिध्यति॥
units.translation: Just as thinking, like intention and the rest, is a function of the mind, so the inclusion of memory in the mind is properly established.
units.iast:
cintanaṃ ca mano-dharmaḥ saṅkalpādir yathā tathā|
antar-bhāvo manasyeva samyak cittasya sidhyati||

units.label: Verse 348
units.deva:
देहादाव् अहम् इत्येव भावो दृढतरो धियः।
दृश्यतेऽहङ्-कृतेस् तस्माद् अन्तर्-भावोऽत्र युज्यते॥
units.translation: A very firm notion “I am this” about the body and the like is seen in the intellect; therefore, including ego in it is fitting.

gloss.en: in the body and the like

units.iast:
dehādāv aham ityeva bhāvo dṛḍhataro dhiyaḥ|
dṛśyate’haṅ-kṛtes tasmād antar-bhāvo’tra yujyate||

units.label: Verse 349
units.deva:
तस्माद् एव तु बुद्धेः कर्तृत्वं तद्-इतरस्य करणत्वम्।
सिद्ध्यत्यात्मन उभयं विद्यात् संसार-कारणं मोहात्॥
units.translation: Therefore, agency belongs to the intellect and instrumentality to the other [faculty]. Know that, through delusion, both are causes of the Self’s transmigration.
units.iast:
tasmād eva tu buddheḥ kartṛtvaṃ tad-itarasya karaṇatvam|
siddhyatyātmana ubhayaṃ vidyāt saṃsāra-kāraṇaṃ mohāt||

units.label: Verse 350
units.deva:
विज्ञानमय-कोशः स्यात् बुद्धिर् ज्ञानेन्द्रियैः सह।
विज्ञान-प्रचुरत्वेनाप्य् आच्छादकतयात्मनः॥
units.translation: The intellect together with the organs of knowledge is the sheath of knowledge, because knowledge is abundant in it and it also covers the Self.
units.iast:
vijñānamaya-kośaḥ syāt buddhir jñānendriyaiḥ saha|
vijñāna-pracuratvenāpy ācchādakatayātmanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 351
units.deva:
विज्ञानमय-कोशोऽयम् इति विद्वद्भिर् उच्यते।
अयं महान् अहङ्कार-वृत्तिमान् कर्तृ-लक्षणः॥
units.translation: This is called the sheath of knowledge by the wise. This great principle, endowed with the function of ego, is characterized by agency.

gloss.en: endowed with the function of ego

units.iast:
vijñānamaya-kośo’yam iti vidvadbhir ucyate|
ayaṃ mahān ahaṅkāra-vṛttimān kartṛ-lakṣaṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 352
units.deva:
अहं ममेत्येव सदाभिमानं
देहेन्द्रियादौ कुरुते गृहादौ।
जीवाभिमानः पुरुषोऽयम् एव
कर्ता च भोक्ता च सुखी च दुःखी॥
units.translation: This person, identified as a jīva, always thinks “I” and “mine” of the body, senses, and the like, and of the home and the like. He alone is the doer and experiencer, happy and unhappy.

gloss.en: in the body, senses, and the like
in the home and the like

units.iast:
ahaṃ mametyeva sadābhimānaṃ
dehendriyādau kurute gṛhādau|
jīvābhimānaḥ puruṣo’yam eva
kartā ca bhoktā ca sukhī ca duḥkhī||

units.label: Verse 353
units.deva:
स्व-वासना-प्रेरित एव नित्यं
करोति कर्मोभय-लक्षणं च।
भुङ्क्ते तद्-उत्पन्न-फलं विशिष्टं
सुखं च दुःखं च परत्र चात्र॥
units.translation: Always impelled by his own latent tendencies, he performs both kinds of action and experiences their particular results, pleasure and pain, here and elsewhere.

gloss.en: impelled by his own latent tendencies

units.iast:
sva-vāsanā-prerita eva nityaṃ
karoti karmobhaya-lakṣaṇaṃ ca|
bhuṅkte tad-utpanna-phalaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ
sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca paratra cātra||

units.label: Verse 354
units.deva:
नाना-योनि-सहस्रेषु जायमानो मुहुर् मुहुः।
म्रियमाणो भ्रमत्येष जीवः संसार-मण्डले॥
units.translation: Born and dying again and again among thousands of different wombs, this jīva wanders in the round of saṃsāra.
units.iast:
nānā-yoni-sahasreṣu jāyamāno muhur muhuḥ|
mriyamāṇo bhramatyeṣa jīvaḥ saṃsāra-maṇḍale||

units.label: Verse 355
units.deva:
मनो मनोमयः कोशो भवेज् ज्ञानेन्द्रियैः सह।
प्राचुर्यं मनसो यत्र दृश्यतेऽसौ मनोमयः॥
units.translation: The mind together with the organs of knowledge forms the sheath of mind; where the mind predominates, that is called the manomaya sheath.
units.iast:
mano manomayaḥ kośo bhavej jñānendriyaiḥ saha|
prācuryaṃ manaso yatra dṛśyate’sau manomayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 356
units.deva:
चिन्ता-विषाद-हर्षाद्याः कामाद्याः अस्य वृत्तयः।
मनुते मनसैव एषः फलं कामयते बहिः।
यतते कुरुते भुङ्क्ते तन् मनः सर्व-कारणम्॥
units.translation: Worry, grief, joy, desire, and the like are its functions. This person thinks about a result with the mind, desires outwardly, strives, acts, and experiences; thus the mind is the cause of all these.
units.iast:
cintā-viṣāda-harṣādyāḥ kāmādyā asya vṛttayaḥ|
manute manasaiva eṣaḥ phalaṃ kāmayate bahiḥ|
yatate kurute bhuṅkte tan manaḥ sarva-kāraṇam||

units.label: Verse 357
units.deva:
मनो ह्यमुष्य प्रवणस्य हेतुर्
अन्तर् बहिश् चार्थम् अनेन वेत्ति।
शृणोति जिघ्रत्य् अमुनैव चेक्षते
वक्ति स्पृशत्य् अत्ति करोति सर्वम्॥
units.translation: The mind is indeed the cause of this person’s inclinations. Through it one knows objects within and without; through it alone one hears, smells, sees, speaks, touches, eats, and does everything.
units.iast:
mano hyamuṣya pravaṇasya hetur
antar bahiś cārtham anena vetti|
śṛṇoti jighraty amunaiva cekṣate
vakti spṛśaty atti karoti sarvam||

units.label: Verse 358
units.deva:
बन्धश्च मोक्षो मनसैव पुंसाम्
अर्थोऽप्यनर्थोऽप्यमुनैव सिध्यति।
शुद्धेन मोक्षो मलिनेन बन्धो
विवेकतोऽर्थोऽप्यविवेकतोऽन्यः॥
units.translation: For people, bondage and liberation, and benefit and harm, are brought about by the mind alone. Through a pure mind comes liberation; through a tainted one, bondage. Through discernment comes what is worthwhile; without discernment, the opposite.
units.iast:
bandhaśca mokṣo manasaiva puṃsām
artho’pyanartho’pyamunaiva sidhyati|
śuddhena mokṣo malinena bandho
vivekato’rtho’pyavivekato’nyaḥ||

units.label: Verse 359
units.deva:
रजस्-तमोभ्यां मलिनं त्वशुद्धम्
अज्ञान-जं सत्त्व-गुणेन रिक्तम्।
मनस् तमो-दोष-समन्वितत्वाज्
जडत्व-मोहालसता-प्रमादैः।
तिरस्-कृतं सन् न तु वेत्ति वास्तवं
पदार्थ-तत्त्वं ह्युपलभ्यमानम्॥
units.translation: Impure, born of ignorance, stained by rajas and tamas, and lacking sattva, the mind, overpowered by tamas’s faults—dullness, delusion, laziness, and heedlessness—does not know the actual truth of an object even when it is perceived.

gloss.en: because it is endowed with tamas’s faults

units.iast:
rajas-tamobhyāṃ malinaṃ tvaśuddham
ajñāna-jaṃ sattva-guṇena riktam|
manas tamo-doṣa-samanvitatvāj
jaḍatva-mohālasatā-pramādaiḥ|
tiras-kṛtaṃ san na tu vetti vāstavaṃ
padārtha-tattvaṃ hyupalabhyamānam||

units.label: Verse 360
units.deva:
रजो-दोषैर् युक्तं यदि भवति विक्षेपक-गुणैः
प्रतीपैः कामाद्यैर् अनिशम् अभिभूतं व्यथयति।
कथञ्चित् सूक्ष्मार्थावगतिमद् अपि भ्राम्यति
भृशं मनो दीपो यद्वत् प्रबल-मरुता ध्वस्त-महिमा॥
units.translation: If joined with the faults of rajas and constantly overcome by opposing, distracting qualities such as desire, the mind causes distress. Even if it somehow grasps subtle things, it wanders greatly, like a lamp whose brightness is ruined by a strong wind.
units.iast:
rajo-doṣair yuktaṃ yadi bhavati vikṣepaka-guṇaiḥ
pratīpaiḥ kāmādyair aniśam abhibhūtaṃ vyathayati|
kathañcit sūkṣmārthāvagatimad api bhrāmyati
bhṛśaṃ mano dīpo yadvat prabala-marutā dhvasta-mahimā||

units.label: Verse 361
units.deva:
ततो मुमुक्षुर् भव-बन्ध-मुक्त्यै
रजस्-तमोभ्यां च तदीय-कार्यैः।
वियोज्य चित्तं परिशुद्ध-सत्त्वं
प्रियं प्रयत्नेन सदैव कुर्यात्॥
units.translation: Therefore, one seeking release from worldly bondage should free the mind from rajas, tamas, and their effects, and should always work to make it purely sattvic and pleasing.
units.iast:
tato mumukṣur bhava-bandha-muktyai
rajas-tamobhyāṃ ca tadīya-kāryaiḥ|
viyojya cittaṃ pariśuddha-sattvaṃ
priyaṃ prayatnena sadaiva kuryāt||

units.label: Verse 362
units.deva:
गर्भ-वास-जनि-प्रणाशन-जरा-व्याध्यादिषु प्राणिनां यद्
दुःखं परिदृश्यते च नरके तच् चिन्तयित्वा मुहुः।
दोषान् एव विलोक्य सर्व-विषयेष्वाशां विमुच्याभितः
चित्त-ग्रन्थि-विमोचनाय सुमतिः सत्त्वं समालम्बताम्॥
units.translation: Having repeatedly contemplated the suffering of beings in the womb, at birth, in death, old age, disease, and the like, and in hell, and having seen the faults of all objects, the wise person should give up desire for them and take to sattva to loosen the knot of the mind.

gloss.en: to loosen the knot of the mind

units.iast:
garbha-vāsa-jani-praṇāśana-jarā-vyādhyādiṣu prāṇināṃ yad
duḥkhaṃ paridṛśyate ca narake tac cintayitvā muhuḥ|
doṣān eva vilokya sarva-viṣayeṣvāśāṃ vimucyābhitaḥ
citta-granthi-vimocanāya sumatiḥ sattvaṃ samālambatām||

units.label: Verse 363
units.deva:
यमेषु निरतो यस् तु नियमेषु च यत्नतः।
विवेकिनस् तस्य चित्तं प्रसादम् अधिगच्छति॥
units.translation: The mind of the discerning person who is devoted to the yamas and diligently observes the niyamas attains clarity.
units.iast:
yameṣu nirato yas tu niyameṣu ca yatnataḥ|
vivekinas tasya cittaṃ prasādam adhigacchati||

units.label: Verse 364
units.deva:
आसुरीं सम्पदं त्यक्त्वा भजेद् यो दैव-सम्पदम्।
मोक्षैक-काङ्क्षया नित्यं तस्य चित्तं प्रसीदति॥
units.translation: The mind of one who abandons demonic qualities, cultivates divine qualities, and always longs only for liberation becomes clear.

gloss.en: with liberation as the sole desire

units.iast:
āsurīṃ sampadaṃ tyaktvā bhajed yo daiva-sampadam|
mokṣaika-kāṅkṣayā nityaṃ tasya cittaṃ prasīdati||

units.label: Verse 365
units.deva:
पर-द्रव्य-पर-द्रोह-पर-निन्दा-पर-स्त्रियः।
नालम्बते मनो यस्य तस्य चित्तं प्रसीदति॥
units.translation: The mind of one who does not dwell on others’ property, harm to others, slander of others, or other men’s wives becomes clear.
units.iast:
para-dravya-para-droha-para-nindā-para-striyaḥ|
nālambate mano yasya tasya cittaṃ prasīdati||

units.label: Verse 366
units.deva:
आत्मवत् सर्व-भूतेषु यः समत्वेन पश्यति।
सुखं दुःखं विवेकेन तस्य चित्तं प्रसीदति॥
units.translation: The mind of one who, with discernment, sees the happiness and suffering of all beings as their own becomes clear.
units.iast:
ātmavat sarva-bhūteṣu yaḥ samatvena paśyati|
sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vivekena tasya cittaṃ prasīdati||

units.label: Verse 367
units.deva:
अत्यन्तं श्रद्धया भक्त्या गुरुम् ईश्वरम् आत्मनि।
यो भजत्य् अनिशं क्षान्तस् तस्य चित्तं प्रसीदति॥
units.translation: The mind of the patient person who constantly worships the teacher and Īśvara within, with great faith and devotion, becomes clear.
units.iast:
atyantaṃ śraddhayā bhaktyā gurum īśvaram ātmani|
yo bhajaty aniśaṃ kṣāntas tasya cittaṃ prasīdati||

units.label: Verse 368
units.deva:
शिष्टान्नम् ईश्-आर्चनम् आर्य-सेवां
तीर्थाटनं स्वाश्रम-धर्म-निष्ठाम्।
यमानुषक्तिं नियमानुवृत्तिं
चित्त-प्रसादाय वदन्ति तज्-ज्ञाः॥
units.translation: The wise say that leftover food, worship of Īśvara, service to the noble, pilgrimage, steadfastness in the duties of one’s stage of life, commitment to the restraints, and observance of the disciplines bring clarity to the mind.
units.iast:
śiṣṭānnam īś-ārcanam ārya-sevāṃ
tīrthāṭanaṃ svāśrama-dharma-niṣṭhām|
yamānuṣaktiṃ niyamānuvṛttiṃ
citta-prasādāya vadanti taj-jñāḥ||

units.label: Verse 369
units.deva:
कट्वाम्ल-लवणात्युष्ण-
तीक्ष्ण-रूक्ष-विधायिनाम्।
त्यागः सत्त्वाय कल्पते॥
units.translation: Avoiding what is bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot, pungent, and dry supports sattva.
units.iast:
kaṭvāmla-lavaṇātyuṣṇa-
tīkṣṇa-rūkṣa-vidhāyinām|
tyāgaḥ sattvāya kalpate||

units.label: Verse 370
units.deva:
श्रुत्या सत्त्व-पुराणानां
सेवया सत्त्व-वस्तुनः।
अनुवृत्त्या च साधूनां
सत्त्व-वृत्तिः प्रजायते॥
units.translation: By hearing the sattvic Purāṇas, associating with sattvic things, and following good people, a sattvic disposition arises.
units.iast:
śrutyā sattva-purāṇānāṃ
sevayā sattva-vastunaḥ|
anuvṛttyā ca sādhūnāṃ
sattva-vṛttiḥ prajāyate||

units.label: Verse 371
units.deva:
यस्य चित्तं निर्विषयं
हृदयं यस्य शीतलम्।
तस्य मित्रं जगत् सर्वं
तस्य मुक्तिः कर-स्थिता॥
units.translation: For one whose mind is free of sense objects and whose heart is calm, the whole world is a friend, and liberation is within reach.
units.iast:
yasya cittaṃ nirviṣayaṃ
hṛdayaṃ yasya śītalam|
tasya mitraṃ jagat sarvaṃ
tasya muktiḥ kara-sthitā||

units.label: Verse 372
units.deva:
हित-परिमित-भोजी नित्यम् एकान्त-सेवी
सकृद्-उचित-हितोक्तिः स्वल्प-निद्रा-विहारः।
अनुनियमन-शीलो यो भजत्य् उक्त-काले
स लभत इति शीघ्रं साधु चित्त-प्रसादम्॥
units.translation: He who eats wholesome food in measured quantity, seeks solitude, speaks aptly and beneficially, sleeps and recreates little, follows self-discipline, and worships at the appointed time soon gains a clear mind.

gloss.en: one who eats wholesome food in moderation
one whose speech is timely, apt, and beneficial

units.iast:
hita-parimita-bhojī nityam ekānta-sevī
sakṛd-ucita-hitoktiḥ svalpa-nidrā-vihāraḥ|
anuniyamana-śīlo yo bhajaty ukta-kāle
sa labhata iti śīghraṃ sādhu citta-prasādam||

units.label: Verse 373
units.deva:
चित्त-प्रसादेन विनावगन्तुं
बन्धं न शक्नोति परात्म-तत्त्वम्।
तत्त्वावगत्या तु विना विमुक्तिर्
न सिध्यति ब्रह्म-सहस्र-कोटिषु॥
units.translation: Without clarity of mind, one cannot understand bondage or the truth of the Supreme Self. Without realization of the truth, liberation is not attained even through countless cosmic cycles.

gloss.en: the truth of the Supreme Self
among thousands of crores of Brahmās

units.iast:
citta-prasādena vināvagantuṃ
bandhaṃ na śaknoti parātma-tattvam|
tattvāvagatyā tu vinā vimuktir
na sidhyati brahma-sahasra-koṭiṣu||

units.label: Verse 374
units.deva:
मनोऽप्रसादः पुरुषस्य बन्धो
मनः-प्रसादो भव-बन्ध-मुक्तिः।
मनः-प्रसादाधिगमाय तस्मान्
मनो-निरासं विदधीत विद्वान्॥
units.translation: A person’s unrest of mind is bondage; clarity of mind is release from worldly bondage. Therefore, the wise person should restrain the mind to attain clarity.
units.iast:
mano’prasādaḥ puruṣasya bandho
manaḥ-prasādo bhava-bandha-muktiḥ|
manaḥ-prasādādhigamāya tasmān
mano-nirāsaṃ vidadhīta vidvān||

units.label: Verse 375
units.deva:
पञ्चानाम् एव भूतानां रजोंशेभ्योऽभवन् क्रमात्।
वाक्-पाणि-पाद-पायूपस्थानि कर्मेन्द्रियाण्यनु॥
units.translation: From the rajas portions of the five elements arise, in order, the organs of action: speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals.
units.iast:
pañcānām eva bhūtānāṃ rajoṃśebhyo’bhavan kramāt|
vāk-pāṇi-pāda-pāyūpasthāni karmendriyāṇyanu||

units.label: Verse 376
units.deva:
समस्तेभ्यो रजोंशेभ्यो व्योमादीनां क्रियात्मकाः।
प्राणादयः समुत्पन्नाः पञ्चाप्य् आन्तर-वायवः॥
units.translation: The five inner winds, beginning with prāṇa and characterized by activity, arise from the rajas portions of all the elements, beginning with space.

gloss.en: of space and the other elements

units.iast:
samastebhyo rajoṃśebhyo vyomādīnāṃ kriyātmakāḥ|
prāṇādayaḥ samutpannāḥ pañcāpy āntara-vāyavaḥ||

units.label: Verses 377–378
units.deva:
प्राणः प्राग्-गमनेन स्याद् अपानोऽवाग्-गमनेन च।
व्यानस् तु विष्वग्-गमनाद् उत्क्रान्त्योदान इष्यते॥
अशितान्न-रसादीनां समी-करण-धर्मतः।
समान इत्यभिप्रेतो वायुर् यस् तेषु पञ्चमः॥
units.translation: Prāṇa moves forward, apāna downward, and vyāna in all directions; udāna is understood as moving upward at departure. The fifth wind is samāna; it is so called because it equalizes eaten food, its juices, and the like.

gloss.en: because it moves in all directions
of eaten food, its juices, and the like
because of the function of equalizing

units.iast:
prāṇaḥ prāg-gamanena syād apāno’vāg-gamanena ca|
vyānas tu viṣvag-gamanād utkrāntyodāna iṣyate||
aśitānna-rasādīnāṃ samī-karaṇa-dharmataḥ|
samāna ityabhipreto vāyur yas teṣu pañcamaḥ||

units.label: Verse 379
units.deva:
क्रियैव दिश्यते प्रायः प्राण-कर्मेन्द्रियेष्व् अलम्।
ततस् तेषां रजोंऽशेभ्यो जनिर् अङ्गी-कृता बुधैः॥
units.translation: Activity is chiefly associated with the vital winds and organs of action; therefore, the wise accept that they arise from the rajas portions.

gloss.en: in the vital winds and organs of action

units.iast:
kriyaiva diśyate prāyaḥ prāṇa-karmendriyeṣv alam|
tatas teṣāṃ rajoṃ’śebhyo janir aṅgī-kṛtā budhaiḥ||

units.label: Verse 380
units.deva:
राजसीं तु क्रिया-शक्तिं तमः-शक्तिं जडात्मिकाम्।
प्रकाश-रूपिणीं सत्त्व-शक्तिं प्राहुर् महर्षयः॥
units.translation: The great sages call the power of action rajasic, the power of tamas inert in nature, and the power of sattva luminous in form.
units.iast:
rājasīṃ tu kriyā-śaktiṃ tamaḥ-śaktiṃ jaḍātmikām|
prakāśa-rūpiṇīṃ sattva-śaktiṃ prāhur maharṣayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 381
units.deva:
एते प्राणादयः पञ्च पञ्च-कर्मेन्द्रियैः सह।
भवेत् प्राणमयः कोशः स्थूलो येनैव चेष्टते॥
units.translation: These five vital winds together with the five organs of action form the prāṇamaya sheath; through it alone the gross body acts.

gloss.en: with the five organs of action

units.iast:
ete prāṇādayaḥ pañca pañca-karmendriyaiḥ saha|
bhavet prāṇamayaḥ kośaḥ sthūlo yenaiva ceṣṭate||

units.label: Verse 382
units.deva:
यद् यन् निष्पाद्यते कर्म पुण्यं वा पापम् एव वा।
वाग्-आदिभिश्च वपुषा तत् प्राणमय-कर्तृकम्॥
units.translation: Whatever action is carried out, whether meritorious or sinful, through speech and the other organs and through the body, is done by the prāṇamaya sheath.
units.iast:
yad yan niṣpādyate karma puṇyaṃ vā pāpam eva vā|
vāg-ādibhiśca vapuṣā tat prāṇamaya-kartṛkam||

units.label: Verse 383
units.deva:
वायुनोच्चालितो वृक्षो नाना-रूपेण चेष्टते।
तस्मिन् विनिश्चले सोऽपि निश्चलः स्याद् यथा तथा॥
units.translation: As a tree set in motion by the wind moves in many ways, and becomes still when the wind becomes still, so does the body.
units.iast:
vāyunoccālito vṛkṣo nānā-rūpeṇa ceṣṭate|
tasmin viniścale so’pi niścalaḥ syād yathā tathā||

units.label: Verse 384
units.deva:
प्राण-कर्मेन्द्रियैर् देहः प्रेर्यमाणः प्रवर्तते।
नाना-क्रियासु सर्वत्र विहिताविहितादिषु॥
units.translation: Impelled by the vital winds and organs of action, the body functions in many activities, including those that are prescribed and prohibited.

gloss.en: by the vital winds and organs of action

units.iast:
prāṇa-karmendriyair dehaḥ preryamāṇaḥ pravartate|
nānā-kriyāsu sarvatra vihitāvihitādiṣu||

units.label: Verse 385
units.deva:
कोश-त्रयं मिलित्वैतद् वपुः स्यात् सूक्ष्मम् आत्मनः।
अतिसूक्ष्मतया लीनस्यात्मनो गमकत्वतः॥
units.translation: The three sheaths together form this subtle body of the Self; because the Self is extremely subtle and concealed, this body serves as its indicator.
units.iast:
kośa-trayaṃ militvaitad vapuḥ syāt sūkṣmam ātmanaḥ|
atisūkṣmatayā līnasyātmano gamakatvataḥ||

units.label: Verses 386–388
units.deva:
लिङ्गम् इत्युच्यते स्थूलापेक्षया सूक्ष्मम् इष्यते।
सर्वं लिङ्ग-वपुर्-जातम् एक-धी-विषयत्वतः॥
समष्टिः स्यात् तरु-गणः सामान्येन वनं यथा।
एतत् समष्ट्युपहितं चैतन्यं स-फलं जगुः॥
हिरण्य-गर्भः सूत्रात्मा प्राण इत्यपि पण्डिताः।
हिरण्मये बुद्धि-गर्भे प्रचकास्ति हिरण्यवत्॥
units.translation: The liṅga is considered subtle in relation to the gross body. The totality of subtle bodies is one object of cognition. Just as a collection of trees is generally called a forest, their totality is called the collective. The wise say that consciousness conditioned by this collective is accompanied by its effects. They call it Hiraṇyagarbha, Sūtrātman, and Prāṇa; it shines like gold in the golden interior of the intellect.

gloss.en: because it is one object of cognition
in the interior of the intellect

units.iast:
liṅgam ityucyate sthūlāpekṣayā sūkṣmam iṣyate|
sarvaṃ liṅga-vapur-jātam eka-dhī-viṣayatvataḥ||
samaṣṭiḥ syāt taru-gaṇaḥ sāmānyena vanaṃ yathā|
etat samaṣṭyupahitaṃ caitanyaṃ sa-phalaṃ jaguḥ||
hiraṇya-garbhaḥ sūtrātmā prāṇa ityapi paṇḍitāḥ|
hiraṇmaye buddhi-garbhe pracakāsti hiraṇyavat||

units.label: Verse 389
units.deva:
हिरण्य-गर्भ इत्यस्य व्यपदेशस् ततो मतः।
समस्त-लिङ्ग-देहेषु सूत्रवन् मणि-पङ्क्तिषु।
व्याप्य स्थितत्वात् सूत्रात्मा प्राणनात् प्राण उच्यते॥
units.translation: It is therefore called Hiraṇyagarbha. Because it pervades and abides in all subtle bodies like a thread through a row of gems, it is Sūtrātman; because it breathes, it is called Prāṇa.
units.iast:
hiraṇya-garbha ityasya vyapadeśas tato mataḥ|
samasta-liṅga-deheṣu sūtravan maṇi-paṅktiṣu|
vyāpya sthitatvāt sūtrātmā prāṇanāt prāṇa ucyate||

units.label: Verses 390–391
units.deva:
नैक-धी-विषयत्वेन लिङ्गं व्यष्टिर् भवत्यथ।
य एतद् व्यष्ट्युपहितं चिद्-आभास-समन्वितम्॥
चैतन्यं तैजस इति निगदन्ति मनीषिणः।
तेजोमयान्तःकरणोपाधित्वेनैष तैजसः॥
units.translation: Because it is not the object of a single cognition, the subtle body becomes individual. The wise call the consciousness conditioned by this individual aspect and joined with reflected consciousness Taijasa. Because its adjunct is an inner organ made of tejas, it is Taijasa.

gloss.en: because its adjunct is an inner organ made of tejas

units.iast:
naika-dhī-viṣayatvena liṅgaṃ vyaṣṭir bhavatyatha|
ya etad vyaṣṭyupahitaṃ cid-ābhāsa-samanvitam||
caitanyaṃ taijasa iti nigadanti manīṣiṇaḥ|
tejomayāntaḥkaraṇopādhitvenaiṣa taijasaḥ||

units.label: Verse 392
units.deva:
स्थूलात् सूक्ष्मतया व्यष्टिर् अस्य सूक्ष्म-वपुर् मतम्।
अस्य जागर-संस्कारमयत्वाद् वपुर् उच्यते॥
units.translation: Compared with the gross body, the individual’s body is regarded as subtle because of its subtlety. It is called a body because it is made of impressions of the waking state.

gloss.en: because it consists of waking-state impressions

units.iast:
sthūlāt sūkṣmatayā vyaṣṭir asya sūkṣma-vapur matam|
asya jāgara-saṃskāramayatvād vapur ucyate||

units.label: Verse 393
units.deva:
स्वप्ने जागर-कालीन-वासना-परिकल्पितान्।
तैजसो विषयान् भुङ्क्ते सूक्ष्मार्थान् सूक्ष्म-वृत्तिभिः॥
units.translation: In dreams, Taijasa experiences, through subtle mental functions, subtle objects fashioned from impressions of the waking state.
units.iast:
svapne jāgara-kālīna-vāsanā-parikalpitān|
taijaso viṣayān bhuṅkte sūkṣmārthān sūkṣma-vṛttibhiḥ||

units.label: Verse 394
units.deva:
समष्टेर् अपि च व्यष्टेः सामान्येनैव पूर्ववत्।
अभेद एव ज्ञातव्यो जात्येकत्वे कुतो भिदा॥
units.translation: As before, the collective and individual aspects are to be understood as non-different in general; when they are one in kind, where is the difference?
units.iast:
samaṣṭer api ca vyaṣṭeḥ sāmānyenaiva pūrvavat|
abheda eva jñātavyo jātyekatve kuto bhidā||

units.label: Verse 395
units.deva:
द्वयोर् उपाध्योर् एकत्वे तयोर् अप्यभिमानिनोः।
सूत्रात्मनस् तैजसस्याप्य् अभेदः पूर्ववन् मतः॥
units.translation: When the two adjuncts are one, those identified with them are also non-different; as before, Sūtrātman and Taijasa are considered non-different.
units.iast:
dvayor upādhyor ekatve tayor apyabhimāninoḥ|
sūtrātmanas taijasasyāpy abhedaḥ pūrvavan mataḥ||

units.label: Verse 396
units.deva: अथ स्थूल-प्रपञ्चस्य प्रकारः कथ्यते शृणु॥
units.translation: Now hear: the method of the gross universe is explained.
units.iast: atha sthūla-prapañcasya prakāraḥ kathyate śṛṇu||

units.label: Verse 397
units.deva:
तान्येव सूक्ष्म-भूतानि व्योमादीनि परस्-परम्।
पञ्ची-कृतानि स्थूलानि भवन्ति शृणु तत्-क्रमम्॥
units.translation: Those very subtle elements, beginning with space, become gross through quintuplication. Hear the sequence.
units.iast:
tānyeva sūkṣma-bhūtāni vyomādīni paras-param|
pañcī-kṛtāni sthūlāni bhavanti śṛṇu tat-kramam||

units.label: Verse 398
units.deva:
खादीनां भूतम् एकैकं समम् एव द्विधा द्विधा।
विभज्य भागं तत्राद्यं त्यक्त्वा भागं द्वितीयकम्॥
units.translation: Each element beginning with space is divided equally into two parts. Keeping the first part aside, one takes the second part.
units.iast:
khādīnāṃ bhūtam ekaikaṃ samam eva dvidhā dvidhā|
vibhajya bhāgaṃ tatrādyaṃ tyaktvā bhāgaṃ dvitīyakam||

units.label: Verse 399
units.deva:
चतुर्धा सुविभज्याथ तम् एकैकं विनिक्षिपेत्।
चतुर्णां प्रथमे भागे क्रमेण स्वार्धम् अन्तरा॥
units.translation: Then divide each [second part] well into four and place one part in turn among the four [other elements], with its own half in the middle.
units.iast:
caturdhā suvibhajyātha tam ekaikaṃ vinikṣipet|
caturṇāṃ prathame bhāge krameṇa svārdham antarā||

units.label: Verse 400
units.deva:
ततो व्योमादि-भूतानां भागाः पञ्च भवन्ति ते।
स्व-स्वार्ध-भागेनान्येभ्यः प्राप्तं भाग-चतुष्टयम्॥
units.translation: Thus the elements beginning with space each have five parts: their own half and the four quarter-parts received from the others.

gloss.en: of the elements beginning with space

units.iast:
tato vyomādi-bhūtānāṃ bhāgāḥ pañca bhavanti te|
sva-svārdha-bhāgenānyebhyaḥ prāptaṃ bhāga-catuṣṭayam||

units.label: Verse 401
units.deva:
संयोज्य स्थूलतां यान्ति व्योमादीनि यथा-क्रमम्।
अमुष्य पञ्ची-करणस्याप्रामाण्यं न शङ्क्यताम्॥
units.translation: Thus, combined in order, the elements beginning with space become gross. Do not doubt the validity of this quintuplication.
units.iast:
saṃyojya sthūlatāṃ yānti vyomādīni yathā-kramam|
amuṣya pañcī-karaṇasyāprāmāṇyaṃ na śaṅkyatām||

units.label: Verse 402
units.deva:
उपलक्षणम् अस्यापि तत्-त्रिवृत्-करण-श्रुतिः।
पञ्चानाम् अपि भूतानां श्रूयतेऽन्यत्र सम्भवः॥
units.translation: The Śruti teaching the threefold combination also serves as an illustration of this. Elsewhere, the creation of all five elements is taught.

gloss.en: the Śruti teaching that threefold combination

units.iast:
upalakṣaṇam asyāpi tat-trivṛt-karaṇa-śrutiḥ|
pañcānām api bhūtānāṃ śrūyate’nyatra sambhavaḥ||

units.label: Verse 403
units.deva:
ततः प्रामाणिकं पञ्ची-करणं मन्यतां बुधैः।
प्रत्यक्षादि-विरोधः स्याद् अन्यथा क्रियते यदि॥
units.translation: Therefore, the wise should accept quintuplication as authoritative. If it were done otherwise, there would be conflict with perception and the other means of knowledge.

gloss.en: conflict with perception and the rest

units.iast:
tataḥ prāmāṇikaṃ pañcī-karaṇaṃ manyatāṃ budhaiḥ|
pratyakṣādi-virodhaḥ syād anyathā kriyate yadi||

units.label: Verse 404
units.deva:
आकाश-वाय्वोर् धर्मस्तु वह्न्यादाव् उपलभ्यते।
यथा तथाकाश-वाय्वोर् नाग्न्यादेर् धर्म ईक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: The qualities of space and air are observed in fire and the rest; likewise, the qualities of fire and the rest are not observed in space and air.
units.iast:
ākāśa-vāyvor dharmastu vahnyādāv upalabhyate|
yathā tathākāśa-vāyvor nāgnyāder dharma īkṣyate||

units.label: Verse 405
units.deva:
अतोऽप्रामाणिकम् इति न किञ्चिद् अपि चिन्त्यताम्।
खांश-व्याप्तिश्च ख-व्याप्तिर् विद्यते पावकादिषु॥
units.translation: Therefore, do not consider this unsupported by valid knowledge: a portion of space, and space itself, pervade fire and the other elements.

gloss.en: pervasion by a portion of space

units.iast:
ato’prāmāṇikam iti na kiñcid api cintyatām|
khāṃśa-vyāptiśca kha-vyāptir vidyate pāvakādiṣu||

units.label: Verse 406
units.deva:
तेनोपलभ्यते शब्दः कारणस्यातिरेकतः।
तथा नभस्वतो धर्मोऽप्यग्न्यादाव् उपलभ्यते॥
units.translation: Through that [presence of space], sound is perceived because the cause extends into the effect. Likewise, the property of air is observed in fire and the rest.
units.iast:
tenopalabhyate śabdaḥ kāraṇasyātirekataḥ|
tathā nabhasvato dharmo’pyagnyādāv upalabhyate||

units.label: Verse 407
units.deva:
न तथा विद्यते व्याप्तिर् वह्न्यादेः ख-नभस्वतोः।
सूक्ष्मत्वाद् अंशक-व्याप्तेस् तद्-धर्मो नोपलभ्यते॥
units.translation: Fire and the other elements do not pervade space and air in the same way. Because their portions there are subtle and partial, their properties are not perceived.
units.iast:
na tathā vidyate vyāptir vahnyādeḥ kha-nabhasvatoḥ|
sūkṣmatvād aṃśaka-vyāptes tad-dharmo nopalabhyate||

units.label: Verse 408
units.deva:
कारणस्यानुरूपेण कार्यं सर्वत्र दृश्यते।
तस्मात् प्रामाण्यम् एष्टव्यं बुद्धैः पञ्ची-कृतेर् अपि॥
units.translation: Everywhere, an effect is seen to correspond to its cause. Therefore, the wise should accept the validity of quintuplication as well.
units.iast:
kāraṇasyānurūpeṇa kāryaṃ sarvatra dṛśyate|
tasmāt prāmāṇyam eṣṭavyaṃ buddhaiḥ pañcī-kṛter api||

units.label: Verse 409
units.deva:
अनेनोद्भूत-गुणकं भूतं वक्ष्येऽवधारय।
शब्दैक-गुणम् आकाशं शब्द-स्पर्श-गुणोऽनिलः॥
units.translation: I will explain the elements and their manifest qualities; listen carefully. Space has sound as its only quality, and air has sound and touch as its qualities.

gloss.en: having sound as its only quality
having sound and touch as qualities

units.iast:
anenodbhūta-guṇakaṃ bhūtaṃ vakṣye’vadhāraya|
śabdaika-guṇam ākāśaṃ śabda-sparśa-guṇo’nilaḥ||

units.label: Verse 410
units.deva:
तेजः शब्द-स्पर्श-रूपैर् गुणवत् कारणं क्रमात्।
आपश् चतुर्-गुणः शब्द-स्पर्श-रूप-रसैः क्रमात्॥
units.translation: Fire, in due order, has the qualities sound, touch, and form. Water has four qualities: sound, touch, form, and taste, in order.

gloss.en: with sound, touch, form, and taste

units.iast:
tejaḥ śabda-sparśa-rūpair guṇavat kāraṇaṃ kramāt|
āpaś catur-guṇaḥ śabda-sparśa-rūpa-rasaiḥ kramāt||

units.label: Verse 411
units.deva:
एतैश् चतुर्भिर् गन्धेन सह पञ्च-गुणा मही।
आकाशांशतया श्रोत्रं शब्दं गृह्णाति तद्-गुणम्॥
units.translation: Earth has five qualities: these four together with smell. The ear, being constituted by a portion of space, receives sound, the quality of space.

gloss.en: because of a portion of space

units.iast:
etaiś caturbhir gandhena saha pañca-guṇā mahī|
ākāśāṃśatayā śrotraṃ śabdaṃ gṛhṇāti tad-guṇam||

units.label: Verse 412
units.deva:
त्वङ् मारुतांशकतया स्पर्शं गृह्णाति तद्-गुणम्।
तेजोंशकतया चक्षू रूपं गृह्णाति तद्-गुणम्॥
units.translation: The skin, being constituted by a portion of air, receives touch, its quality. The eye, being constituted by a portion of fire, receives form, its quality.

gloss.en: because of a portion of air
because of a portion of fire

units.iast:
tvaṅ mārutāṃśakatayā sparśaṃ gṛhṇāti tad-guṇam|
tejoṃśakatayā cakṣū rūpaṃ gṛhṇāti tad-guṇam||

units.label: Verse 413
units.deva:
अपांशकतया जिह्वा रसं गृह्णाति तद्-गुणम्।
भूम्यंशकतया घ्राणं गन्धं गृह्णाति तद्-गुणम्॥
units.translation: The tongue, being constituted by a portion of water, receives taste, its quality. The nose, being constituted by a portion of earth, receives smell, its quality.

gloss.en: because of a portion of water
because of a portion of earth

units.iast:
apāṃśakatayā jihvā rasaṃ gṛhṇāti tad-guṇam|
bhūmyaṃśakatayā ghrāṇaṃ gandhaṃ gṛhṇāti tad-guṇam||

units.label: Verse 414
units.deva:
करोति खांशकतया वाक् शब्दोच्चारण-क्रियाम्।
वाय्वंशकतया पादौ गमनादि-क्रिया-परौ॥
units.translation: Because it is constituted by a portion of space, speech performs the action of pronouncing sounds. Because they are constituted by a portion of air, the feet are engaged in walking and related actions.

gloss.en: because of a portion of space
because of a portion of air
engaged in walking and related actions

units.iast:
karoti khāṃśakatayā vāk śabdoccāraṇa-kriyām|
vāyvaṃśakatayā pādau gamanādi-kriyā-parau||

units.label: Verse 415
units.deva:
तेजोंशकतया पाणी वह्न्याद्यर्चन-तत्-परौ।
जलांशकतयोपस्थो रेतो-मूत्र-विसर्ग-कृत्॥
units.translation: Because they are constituted by a portion of fire, the hands are devoted to worship of fire and the rest. Because it is constituted by a portion of water, the organ of generation releases semen and urine.

gloss.en: because of a portion of fire
devoted to worship of fire and the rest
because of a portion of water
causing the release of semen and urine

units.iast:
tejoṃśakatayā pāṇī vahnyādyarcana-tat-parau|
jalāṃśakatayopastho reto-mūtra-visarga-kṛt||

units.label: Verse 416
units.deva:
भूम्यंशकतया पायुः कठिनं मलम् उत्सृजेत्।
श्रोत्रस्य दैवतं दिक् स्यात् त्वचो वायुर् दृशो रविः॥
units.translation: Because it is constituted by a portion of earth, the anus expels solid waste. The presiding deity of the ear is a direction; that of the skin is Vāyu, and that of the eye is the Sun.

gloss.en: because of a portion of earth

units.iast:
bhūmyaṃśakatayā pāyuḥ kaṭhinaṃ malam utsṛjet|
śrotrasya daivataṃ dik syāt tvaco vāyur dṛśo raviḥ||

units.label: Verse 417
units.deva:
जिह्वाया वरुणो दैवं घ्राणस्य त्वश्विनाव् उभौ।
वाचोऽग्निर् हस्तयोर् इन्द्रः पादयोस् तु त्रि-विक्रमः॥
units.translation: Varuṇa is the deity of the tongue, and the two Aśvins of the nose. Agni presides over speech, Indra over the hands, and Trivikrama over the feet.
units.iast:
jihvāyā varuṇo daivaṃ ghrāṇasya tvaśvināv ubhau|
vāco’gnir hastayor indraḥ pādayos tu tri-vikramaḥ||

units.label: Verse 418
units.deva:
पायोर् मृत्युर् उपस्थस्य त्वधिदैवं प्रजा-पतिः।
मनसो दैवतं चन्द्रो बुद्धेर् दैवं बृहस्-पतिः॥
units.translation: Mṛtyu presides over the anus, and Prajāpati over the organ of generation. The Moon is the deity of the mind, and Bṛhaspati of the intellect.
units.iast:
pāyor mṛtyur upasthasya tvadhidaivaṃ prajā-patiḥ|
manaso daivataṃ candro buddher daivaṃ bṛhas-patiḥ||

units.label: Verse 419
units.deva:
रुद्रस् त्वहङ्-कृतेर् दैवं क्षेत्र-ज्ञश् चित्त-दैवतम्।
दिगाद्या देवताः सर्वाः खादि-सत्त्वांश-सम्भवाः॥
units.translation: Rudra is the deity of ego, and the knower of the field is the deity of memory. All deities beginning with the directions arise from the sattva portions of the elements beginning with space.

gloss.en: arising from sattva portions of the elements beginning with space

units.iast:
rudras tvahaṅ-kṛter daivaṃ kṣetra-jñaś citta-daivatam|
digādyā devatāḥ sarvāḥ khādi-sattvāṃśa-sambhavāḥ||

units.label: Verse 420
units.deva:
संमिता इन्द्रिय-स्थानेष्विन्द्रियाणां समन्ततः।
निगृह्णन्त्यनुगृह्णन्ति प्राणि-कर्मानुरूपतः॥
units.translation: Present at the locations of the senses, the deities restrain or assist the senses in accordance with the actions of living beings.

gloss.en: at the locations of the senses
in accordance with the actions of living beings

units.iast:
saṃmitā indriya-sthāneṣvindriyāṇāṃ samantataḥ|
nigṛhṇantyanugṛhṇanti prāṇi-karmānurūpataḥ||

units.label: Verse 421
units.deva:
शरीर-करण-ग्रामाप्राणाहम्-अधिदेवताः।
पञ्चैते हेतवः प्रोक्ता निष्पत्तौ सर्व-कर्मणाम्॥
units.translation: The body, group of instruments, vital breath, ego, and presiding deities are declared to be the five causes in the accomplishment of all actions.
units.iast:
śarīra-karaṇa-grāmāprāṇāham-adhidevatāḥ|
pañcaite hetavaḥ proktā niṣpattau sarva-karmaṇām||

units.label: Verse 422
units.deva:
कर्मानुरूपेण गुणोदयो भवेद्
गुणानुरूपेण मनः-प्रवृत्तिः।
मनोऽनुवृत्तैर् उभयात्मकेन्द्रियैर्
निर्वर्त्यते पुण्यम् अपुण्यम् अत्र॥
units.translation: Guṇas arise in accordance with action, and the mind acts in accordance with the guṇas. Here, the senses of both kinds, following the mind, produce merit and demerit.

gloss.en: by the senses of both kinds

units.iast:
karmānurūpeṇa guṇodayo bhaved
guṇānurūpeṇa manaḥ-pravṛttiḥ|
mano’nuvṛttair ubhayātmakendriyaiḥ
nirvartyate puṇyam apuṇyam atra||

units.label: Verse 423
units.deva:
करोति विज्ञानमयोऽभिमानं
कर्ताहम् एवेति तद्-आत्मना स्थितः।
आत्मा तु साक्षी न करोति किञ्चिन्
न कारयत्येव तटस्थवत् सदा॥
units.translation: The sheath of knowledge identifies itself, thinking, “I alone am the doer.” The Self, however, is a witness; it neither acts nor causes anything to act, and always remains detached.
units.iast:
karoti vijñānamayo’bhimānaṃ
kartāham eveti tad-ātmanā sthitaḥ|
ātmā tu sākṣī na karoti kiñcin
na kārayatyeva taṭasthavat sadā||

units.label: Verse 424
units.deva:
द्रष्टा श्रोता वक्ता कर्ता भोक्ता भवत्यहङ्कारः।
स्वयम् एतद्-विकृतीनां साक्षी निर्लेप एवात्मा॥
units.translation: The ego becomes the seer, hearer, speaker, doer, and experiencer. The Self itself is the unattached witness of these modifications.
units.iast:
draṣṭā śrotā vaktā kartā bhoktā bhavatyahaṅkāraḥ|
svayam etad-vikṛtīnāṃ sākṣī nirlepa evātmā||

units.label: Verse 425
units.deva:
आत्मनः साक्षिमात्रत्वं न कर्तृत्वं न भोक्तृता।
रविवत् प्राणिभिर् लोके क्रियमाणेषु कर्मसु॥
units.translation: The Self is merely a witness, neither an agent nor an experiencer, like the sun among actions performed by living beings in the world.

gloss.en: the state of being only a witness
the state of being an experiencer

units.iast:
ātmanaḥ sākṣimātratvaṃ na kartṛtvaṃ na bhoktṛtā|
ravivat prāṇibhir loke kriyamāṇeṣu karmasu||

units.label: Verse 426
units.deva:
न ह्यर्कः कुरुते कर्म न कारयति जन्तवः।
स्व-स्व-भावानुरोधेन वर्तन्ते स्व-स्व-कर्मसु॥
units.translation: The sun does not act, nor does it cause living beings to act. They engage in their own actions according to their own natures.
units.iast:
na hyarkaḥ kurute karma na kārayati jantavaḥ|
sva-sva-bhāvānurodhena vartante sva-sva-karmasu||

units.label: Verse 427
units.deva:
तथैव प्रत्यग्-आत्मापि रविवन् निष्क्रियात्मना।
उदासीनतयैवास्ते देहादीनां प्रवृत्तिषु॥
units.translation: Likewise, the inner Self, inactive in nature like the sun, remains impartial amid the activities of the body and the rest.

gloss.en: of the body and the rest

units.iast:
tathaiva pratyag-ātmāpi ravivan niṣkriyātmanā|
udāsīnatayaivāste dehādīnāṃ pravṛttiṣu||

units.label: Verse 428
units.deva:
अज्ञात्वैवं परं तत्त्वं माया-मोहित-चेतसः।
स्वात्मन्यारोपयन्त्येतत् कर्तृत्वाद्यन्य-गोचरम्॥
units.translation: Not knowing this supreme truth and their minds deluded by Māyā, people superimpose on the Self agency and the like, which belong to something else.

gloss.en: whose minds are deluded by Māyā

units.iast:
ajñātvaivaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ māyā-mohita-cetasaḥ|
svātmanyāropayantyetat kartṛtvādyanya-gocaram||

units.label: Verse 429
units.deva:
आत्म-स्वरूपम् अविचार्य विमूढ-बुद्धिर्
आरोपयत्य् अखिलम् एतद् अनात्म-कार्यम्।
स्वात्मन्य् असङ्ग-चिति-निष्क्रिय एव चन्द्रे
दूरस्थ-मेघ-कृत-धावनवद् भ्रमेण॥
units.translation: Without discerning the Self’s true nature, the deluded intellect superimposes all the activity of the not-Self on its own Self, which is unattached, conscious, and inactive—like the apparent motion of the moon caused by distant clouds.

gloss.en: like motion caused by distant clouds

units.iast:
ātma-svarūpam avicārya vimūḍha-buddhir
āropayaty akhilam etad anātma-kāryam|
svātmany asaṅga-citi-niṣkriya eva candre
dūrastha-megha-kṛta-dhāvanavad bhrameṇa||

units.label: Verse 430
units.deva:
आत्मानात्म-विवेकं स्फुटतरम् अग्रे निवेदयिष्यामः।
इमम् आकर्णय विद्वन् जगदुत्पत्ति-प्रकारम् आवृत्त्या॥
units.translation: We will explain the distinction between Self and not-Self more clearly later. For now, learned one, listen as I explain the process of the world’s creation in sequence.

gloss.en: the distinction between Self and not-Self
the process of the world’s creation

units.iast:
ātmānātma-vivekaṃ sphuṭataram agre nivedayiṣyāmaḥ|
imam ākarṇaya vidvan jagadutpatti-prakāram āvṛttyā||

units.label: Verse 431
units.deva:
पञ्ची-कृतेभ्यः खादिभ्यो भूतेभ्यस् त्वीक्षयेशितुः।
समुत्पन्नम् इदं स्थूलं ब्रह्माण्डं स-चराचरम्॥
units.translation: By the Lord’s seeing, this gross cosmic egg, including the moving and unmoving, arose from the fivefold-combined elements beginning with space.
units.iast:
pañcī-kṛtebhyaḥ khādibhyo bhūtebhyas tvīkṣayeśituḥ|
samutpannam idaṃ sthūlaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ sa-carācaram||

units.label: Verse 432
units.deva:
व्रीह्याद्योषधयः सर्वा वायु-तेजोम्बु-भूमयः।
सर्वेषाम् अप्यभूद् अन्नं चतुर्-विध-शरीरिणाम्॥
units.translation: All plants beginning with rice, along with air, fire, water, and earth, became food for beings with the four kinds of bodies.

gloss.en: for beings with four kinds of bodies

units.iast:
vrīhyādyoṣadhayaḥ sarvā vāyu-tejombu-bhūmayaḥ|
sarveṣām apyabhūd annaṃ catur-vidha-śarīriṇām||

units.label: Verse 433
units.deva:
केचिन् मारुत-भोजनाः खलु परे चन्द्रार्क-तेजोशनाः
केचित् तोय-कणाशिनोऽपरिमिताः केचित् तु मृद्-भक्षकाः।
केचित् पर्ण-शिला-तृणादन-पराः केचित्तु मांसाशिनः
केचिद् व्रीहि-यवान्न-भोजन-परा जीवन्त्य् अमी जन्तवः॥
units.translation: Some live on air; others on the light of the moon and sun. Some feed on drops of water, others on earth. Some live on leaves, stones, and grass; some on flesh; and some on rice, barley, and other grains.

gloss.en: feeding on the light of the moon and sun
devoted to eating leaves, stones, and grass
devoted to food of rice, barley, and grain

units.iast:
kecin māruta-bhojanāḥ khalu pare candrārka-tejośanāḥ
kecit toya-kaṇāśino’parimitāḥ kecit tu mṛd-bhakṣakāḥ|
kecit parṇa-śilā-tṛṇādana-parāḥ kecittu māṃsāśinaḥ
kecid vrīhi-yavānna-bhojana-parā jīvanty amī jantavaḥ||

units.label: Verse 434
units.deva:
जरायुजाण्डज-स्वेदजोद्भिज्जाद्याश् चतुर्विधाः।
स्व-स्व-कर्मानुरूपेण जातास् तिष्ठन्ति जन्तवः॥
units.translation: Beings are four kinds—womb-born, egg-born, sweat-born, and sprouting-born—and live according to their own actions.
units.iast:
jarāyujāṇḍaja-svedajodbhijjādyāś caturvidhāḥ|
sva-sva-karmānurūpeṇa jātās tiṣṭhanti jantavaḥ||

units.label: Verse 435
units.deva:
यत्र जाता जरायुभ्यस् ते नराद्या जरायु-जाः।
अण्ड-जास् ते स्युर् अण्डेभ्यो जाता ये विहगादयः॥
units.translation: Humans and the like, born from the womb, are womb-born. Birds and the like, born from eggs, are egg-born.
units.iast:
yatra jātā jarāyubhyas te narādyā jarāyu-jāḥ|
aṇḍa-jās te syur aṇḍebhyo jātā ye vihagādayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 436
units.deva:
स्वेदाज् जाताः स्वेद-जास् ते यूका लूक्षादयोऽपि च।
भूमिम् उद्भिद्य ये जाता उद्भिज्-जास् ते द्रुमादयः॥
units.translation: Lice and small insects are born from sweat. Trees and the like are sprouting-born, arising by breaking through the ground.
units.iast:
svedāj jātāḥ sveda-jās te yūkā lūkṣādayo’pi ca|
bhūmim udbhidya ye jātā udbhij-jās te drumādayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 437
units.deva:
इदं स्थूल-वपुर्-जातं भौतिकं च चतुर्-विधम्।
सामान्येन समष्टिः स्याद् एक-धी-विषयत्वतः॥
units.translation: This set of gross, material bodies is fourfold. Taken together, it is the collective because it is one object of cognition.

gloss.en: because it is one object of cognition

units.iast:
idaṃ sthūla-vapur-jātaṃ bhautikaṃ ca catur-vidham|
sāmānyena samaṣṭiḥ syād eka-dhī-viṣayatvataḥ||

units.label: Verse 438
units.deva:
एतत् समष्ट्यवच्छिन्नं चैतन्यं फल-संयुतम्।
प्राहुर् वैश्वानर इति विराड् इति च वैदिकाः॥
units.translation: The Vedic teachers call consciousness conditioned by this collective and joined with its effects Vaiśvānara and Virāṭ.
units.iast:
etat samaṣṭyavacchinnaṃ caitanyaṃ phala-saṃyutam|
prāhur vaiśvānara iti virāḍ iti ca vaidikāḥ||

units.label: Verse 439
units.deva:
वैश्वा-नरो विश्व-नरेष्वात्मत्वेनाभिमानतः।
विराट् स्याद् विविधत्वेन स्वयम् एव विराजनात्॥
units.translation: It is Vaiśvānara because it identifies with all beings as their Self; it is Virāṭ because it shines forth in diverse forms.
units.iast:
vaiśvā-naro viśva-nareṣvātmatvenābhimānataḥ|
virāṭ syād vividhatvena svayam eva virājanāt||

units.label: Verse 440
units.deva:
चतुर्-विधं भूत-जातं तत्-तज्-जाति-विशेषतः।
नैक-धी-विषयत्वेन पूर्ववद् व्यष्टिर् इष्यते॥
units.translation: Because the four kinds of beings are distinguished by their respective classes and are not one object of cognition, they are considered individual aggregates, as before.
units.iast:
catur-vidhaṃ bhūta-jātaṃ tat-taj-jāti-viśeṣataḥ|
naika-dhī-viṣayatvena pūrvavad vyaṣṭir iṣyate||

units.label: Verse 441
units.deva:
साभासं व्यष्ट्युपहितं तत्-तादात्म्यम् उपागतम्।
चैतन्यं विश्व इत्याहुर् वेदान्त-नय-कोविदाः॥
units.translation: The knowers of Vedānta call consciousness, associated with reflection, conditioned by the individual, and identified with it, Viśva.
units.iast:
sābhāsaṃ vyaṣṭyupahitaṃ tat-tādātmyam upāgatam|
caitanyaṃ viśva ityāhur vedānta-naya-kovidāḥ||

units.label: Verse 442
units.deva:
विश्वोऽस्मिन् स्थूल-देहेऽत्र स्वाभिमानेन तिष्ठति।
यतस् ततो विश्व इति नाम्ना सार्थो भवत्ययम्॥
units.translation: Viśva abides here in this gross body, identified with it as itself; therefore, the name Viśva is apt.
units.iast:
viśvo’smin sthūla-dehe’tra svābhimānena tiṣṭhati|
yatas tato viśva iti nāmnā sārtho bhavatyayam||

units.label: Verse 443
units.deva:
व्यष्टिर् एषास्य विश्वस्य भवति स्थूल-विग्रहः।
उच्यतेऽन्न-विकारित्वात् कोशोऽन्नमय इत्ययम्॥
units.translation: This individual gross form of Viśva is called the annamaya sheath because it is a modification of food.

gloss.en: because it is a modification of food

units.iast:
vyaṣṭir eṣāsya viśvasya bhavati sthūla-vigrahaḥ|
ucyate’nna-vikāritvāt kośo’nnamaya ityayam||

units.label: Verse 444
units.deva:
देहोऽयं पितृ-भुक्तान्न-विकाराच् छुक्ल-शोणितात्।
जातः प्रवर्धतेऽन्नेन तद्-अभावे विनश्यति॥
units.translation: This body is born from semen and blood, transformations of the food eaten by the parents; it grows through food and perishes when food is absent.

gloss.en: from the transformation of food eaten by the parents

units.iast:
deho’yaṃ pitṛ-bhuktānna-vikārāc chukla-śoṇitāt|
jātaḥ pravardhate’nnena tad-abhāve vinaśyati||

units.label: Verse 445
units.deva:
तस्माद् अन्न-विकारित्वेनायम् अन्नमयो मतः।
आच्छादकत्वाद् एतस्याप्य् असेः कोशवद् आत्मनः॥
units.translation: Therefore, this is considered made of food because it is a modification of food; it is called a sheath because it covers the Self like a sword’s sheath.

gloss.en: because it is a modification of food

units.iast:
tasmād anna-vikāritvenāyam annamayo mataḥ|
ācchādakatvād etasyāpy aseḥ kośavad ātmanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 446
units.deva:
आत्मनः स्थूल-भोगानाम्
एतद् आयतनं विदुः।
शब्दादि-विषयान् भुङ्क्ते
स्थूलान् स्थूलात्मनि स्थितः॥
units.translation: The gross body is known as the abode for the Self’s gross experiences. Situated in the gross body, the Self experiences gross objects, beginning with sound.
units.iast:
ātmanaḥ sthūla-bhogānām
etad āyatanaṃ viduḥ|
śabdādi-viṣayān bhuṅkte
sthūlān sthūlātmani sthitaḥ||

units.label: Verse 447
units.deva:
बहिर्-आत्मा ततः स्थूल-भोगायतनम् उच्यते।
इन्द्रियैर् उपनीतानां शब्दादीनाम् अयं स्वयम्।
देहेन्द्रिय-मनो-युक्तो भोक्तेत्याहुर् मनीषिणः॥
units.translation: Thus this outer self is called the abode of gross experiences. The wise call this embodied self, joined with body, senses, and mind, the experiencer of sound and the other objects brought by the senses.

gloss.en: joined with body, senses, and mind

units.iast:
bahir-ātmā tataḥ sthūla-bhogāyatanam ucyate|
indriyair upanītānāṃ śabdādīnām ayaṃ svayam|
dehendriya-mano-yukto bhoktetyāhur manīṣiṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 448
units.deva:
एकादश-द्वारवतीह देहे
सौधे महा-राज इवाक्ष-वर्गैः।
संसेव्यमानो विषयोपभोगान्
उपाधि-संस्थो बुभुजेऽयम् आत्मा॥
units.translation: Here, in the body-palace with eleven doors, this Self dwells in its adjunct and, attended by the senses like a great king, enjoys sense objects.
units.iast:
ekādaśa-dvāravatīha dehe
saudhe mahā-rāja ivākṣa-vargaiḥ|
saṃsevyamāno viṣayopabhogān
upādhi-saṃstho bubhuje’yam ātmā||

units.label: Verse 449
units.deva:
ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि निज-दैवत-चोदितानि
कर्मेन्द्रियाण्यपि तथा मन-आदिकानि।
स्व-स्व-प्रयोजन-विधौ नियतानि सन्ति
यत्नेन किङ्कर-जना इव तं भजन्ते॥
units.translation: Prompted by their presiding deities and each bound to its own function, the organs of knowledge, the organs of action, and the mind serve it diligently like attendants.

gloss.en: in the performance of their respective functions

units.iast:
jñānendriyāṇi nija-daivata-coditāni
karmendriyāṇyapi tathā mana-ādikāni|
sva-sva-prayojana-vidhau niyatāni santi
yatnena kiṅkara-janā iva taṃ bhajante||

units.label: Verse 450
units.deva:
यत्रोपभुङ्क्ते विषयान् स्थूलान् एष महा-मतिः।
अहं ममेति सैषास्यावस्था जाग्रद् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: When this great-minded person experiences gross objects and thinks “I” and “mine,” this state is called waking.
units.iast:
yatropabhuṅkte viṣayān sthūlān eṣa mahā-matiḥ|
ahaṃ mameti saiṣāsyāvasthā jāgrad itīryate||

units.label: Verse 451
units.deva:
एतत्-समष्टि-व्यष्ट्योश् चोभयोर् अप्यभिमानिनोः।
तद्-विश्व-वैश्वानरयोर् अभेदः पूर्ववन् मतः॥
units.translation: As before, no difference is held between the two identified with the collective and individual aspects—Vaiśvānara and Viśva.
units.iast:
etat-samaṣṭi-vyaṣṭyoś cobhayor apyabhimāninoḥ|
tad-viśva-vaiśvānarayor abhedaḥ pūrvavan mataḥ||

units.label: Verse 452
units.deva:
स्थूल-सूक्ष्म-कारणाख्याः प्रपञ्चा ये निरूपिताः।
ते सर्वेऽपि मिलित्वैकः प्रपञ्चोऽपि महान् भवेत्॥
units.translation: All the worlds described as gross, subtle, and causal, joining together, become one great universe.
units.iast:
sthūla-sūkṣma-kāraṇākhyāḥ prapañcā ye nirūpitāḥ|
te sarve’pi militvaikaḥ prapañco’pi mahān bhavet||

units.label: Verse 453
units.deva:
महा-प्रपञ्चावच्छिन्नं विश्व-प्राज्ञादि-लक्षणम्।
विराड्-आदीश-पर्यन्तं चैतन्यं चैकम् एव तत्॥
units.translation: That consciousness is one alone. Delimited by the great universe, it has the forms called Viśva, Prājña, and the rest, extending from Virāṭ to Īśa.

gloss.en: characterized by Viśva, Prājña, and the rest

units.iast:
mahā-prapañcāvacchinnaṃ viśva-prājñādi-lakṣaṇam|
virāḍ-ādīśa-paryantaṃ caitanyaṃ caikam eva tat||

units.label: Verse 454
units.deva:
यद् अनाद्यन्तम् अव्यक्तं चैतन्यम् अजम् अक्षरम्।
महा-प्रपञ्चेन सहाविविक्तं सद् अयोऽग्निवत्॥
units.translation: That consciousness is beginningless, endless, unmanifest, unborn, and imperishable. It exists undifferentiated from the great universe, like fire in iron.
units.iast:
yad anādyantam avyaktaṃ caitanyam ajam akṣaram|
mahā-prapañcena sahāviviktaṃ sad ayo’gnivat||

units.label: Verse 455
units.deva:
तत् सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्मेत्यस्य वाक्यस्य पण्डितैः।
वाच्यार्थ इति निर्णीतं विविक्तं लक्ष्य इत्यपि॥
units.translation: The wise understand the statement “All this is indeed Brahman” in its direct sense; when distinguished [from its adjuncts], its implied meaning is also understood.
units.iast:
tat sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahmetyasya vākyasya paṇḍitaiḥ|
vācyārtha iti nirṇītaṃ viviktaṃ lakṣya ityapi||

units.label: Verse 456
units.deva:
स्थूलाद्यज्ञान-पर्यन्तं कार्य-कारण-लक्षणम्।
दृश्यं सर्वम् अनात्मेति विजानीहि विचक्षण॥
units.translation: Understand, discerning one, that everything seen—from the gross [world] to ignorance, marked as effect and cause, is not-Self.
units.iast:
sthūlādyajñāna-paryantaṃ kārya-kāraṇa-lakṣaṇam|
dṛśyaṃ sarvam anātmeti vijānīhi vicakṣaṇa||

units.label: Verse 457
units.deva:
अन्तःकरण-तद्-वृत्ति-द्रष्टृ नित्यम् अविक्रियम्।
चैतन्यं यत् तद् आत्मेति बुद्ध्या बुध्यस्व सूक्ष्मया॥
units.translation: That consciousness which witnesses the inner organ and its modifications, and is eternal and changeless—that is the Self. Understand this with a subtle intellect.
units.iast:
antaḥkaraṇa-tad-vṛtti-draṣṭṛ nityam avikriyam|
caitanyaṃ yat tad ātmeti buddhyā budhyasva sūkṣmayā||

units.label: Verse 458
units.deva:
एष प्रत्यक् स्वप्रकाशो निरंशोऽसङ्गः शुद्धः सर्वदैक-स्वभावः।
नित्याखण्डानन्द-रूपो निरीहः
साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च॥
units.translation: The inner Self is self-luminous, partless, unattached, pure, always of one nature, eternally of undivided bliss, without desire, a witness and knower, alone and without qualities.

gloss.en: of the nature of undivided bliss

units.iast:
eṣa pratyak svaprakāśo niraṃśo’saṅgaḥ śuddhaḥ sarvadaika-svabhāvaḥ|
nityākhaṇḍānanda-rūpo nirīhaḥ
sākṣī cetā kevalo nirguṇaśca||

units.label: Verse 459
units.deva:
नैव प्रत्यग् जायते वर्धते नो
किञ्चिन् नापक्षीयते नैव नाशम्।
आत्मा नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो
नासौ हन्यो हन्यमाने शरीरे॥
units.translation: The inner Self is never born, does not grow or decline, and is not destroyed. This Self is eternal, everlasting, ancient; it is not killed when the body is killed.
units.iast:
naiva pratyag jāyate vardhate no
kiñcin nāpakṣīyate naiva nāśam|
ātmā nityaḥ śāśvato’yaṃ purāṇo
nāsau hanyo hanyamāne śarīre||

units.label: Verse 460
units.deva:
जन्मास्तित्व-विवृद्धयः परिणतिश् चापक्षतिर् नाशनं
दृश्यस्यैव भवन्ति षड्-विकृतयो नाना-विधा व्याधयः।
स्थूलत्वादि च नीलताद्यपि मितिर् वर्णाश्रमादि-प्रथा
दृश्यन्ते वपुषो न चात्मन इमे तद्-विक्रिया-साक्षिणः॥
units.translation: Birth, existence, growth, change, decline, and destruction are the six changes of what is seen; many diseases also belong to it. Grossness and the like, blueness and the like, size, and distinctions such as class and life-stage are seen in the body, not in the Self, which witnesses those changes.

gloss.en: customs such as class and life-stage

units.iast:
janmāstitva-vivṛddhayaḥ pariṇatiś cāpakṣatir nāśanaṃ
dṛśyasyaiva bhavanti ṣaḍ-vikṛtayo nānā-vidhā vyādhayaḥ|
sthūlatvādi ca nīlatādyapi mitir varṇāśramādi-prathā
dṛśyante vapuṣo na cātmana ime tad-vikriyā-sākṣiṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 461
units.deva:
अस्मिन्न् आत्मन्यनात्मत्वम् अनात्मन्यात्मतां पुनः।
विपरीततयाध्यस्य संसरन्ति विमोहतः॥
units.translation: Through delusion, people superimpose not-Selfhood on the Self and, conversely, Selfhood on the not-Self; thus they transmigrate.
units.iast:
asminn ātmanyanātmatvam anātmanyātmatāṃ punaḥ|
viparītatayādhyasya saṃsaranti vimohataḥ||

units.label: Verse 462
units.deva:
भ्रान्त्या मनुष्योऽहम् अहं द्वि-जोऽहम्
तज्-ज्ञोऽहम् अज्ञोऽहम् अतीव पापी।
भ्रष्टोऽस्मि शिष्टोऽस्मि सुखी च दुःखी इत्येवं
विमुह्यात्मनि कल्पयन्ति॥
units.translation: Through delusion, people imagine in the Self, “I am human; I am twice-born; I am learned; I am ignorant; I am very sinful; I am fallen; I am virtuous; I am happy and unhappy.”
units.iast:
bhrāntyā manuṣyo’ham ahaṃ dvi-jo’ham
taj-jño’ham ajño’ham atīva pāpī|
bhraṣṭo’smi śiṣṭo’smi sukhī ca duḥkhītyevaṃ
vimuhyātmani kalpayanti||

units.label: Verse 463
units.deva:
अनात्मनो जन्म-जरा-मृति-क्षुधा-
तृष्णासुख-क्लेश-भयादि-धर्मान्।
विपर्ययेण ह्यतथाविधेऽस्मिन्न्
आरोपयन्त्यात्मनि बुद्धि-दोषात्॥
units.translation: Through a defect of the intellect, they wrongly superimpose on the Self the qualities of the not-Self—birth, old age, death, hunger, thirst, pleasure, distress, fear, and the like—even though the Self is not of that kind.

gloss.en: because of a defect of the intellect

units.iast:
anātmano janma-jarā-mṛti-kṣudhā-
tṛṣṇāsukha-kleśa-bhayādi-dharmān|
viparyayeṇa hyatathāvidhe’sminn
āropayantyātmani buddhi-doṣāt||

units.label: Verse 464
units.deva:
भ्रान्त्या यत्र यद्-अध्यासस् तत्-कृतेन गुणेन वा।
दोषेणाप्यणु-मात्रेण स न सम्बध्यते क्वचित्॥
units.translation: Wherever something is superimposed through error, the underlying thing is never affected by the quality or fault attributed to it, even in the slightest.
units.iast:
bhrāntyā yatra yad-adhyāsas tat-kṛtena guṇena vā|
doṣeṇāpyaṇu-mātreṇa sa na sambadhyate kvacit||

units.label: Verse 465
units.deva:
किं मरुर् मृगतृष्णाम्बु-पूरेणार्द्रत्वम् ऋच्छति।
दृष्टि-संस्थित-पीतेन शङ्खः पीतायते किमु॥
units.translation: Does the desert become wet from a flood of mirage water? Does a conch turn yellow from the yellowness lodged in the eye?

gloss.en: from yellowness lodged in the eye

units.iast:
kiṃ marur mṛga-tṛṣṇāmbu-pūreṇārdra-tvam ṛcchati|
dṛṣṭi-saṃsthita-pītena śaṅkhaḥ pītāyate kimu||

units.label: Verse 466
units.deva:
वात-कल्पित-नैल्येन व्योम किं मलिनायते।
प्रत्यगात्मन्यविषयेऽनात्माध्यासः कथं प्रभो॥
units.translation: Does the sky become stained by blueness imagined by the wind? [The disciple asks:] How can not-Self be superimposed on the inner Self, which is not an object, O Lord?

gloss.en: by blueness imagined by the wind

units.iast:
vātakalpita-nailyena vyoma kiṃ malināyate|
pratyagātmany aviṣaye’nātmādhyāsaḥ kathaṃ prabho||

units.label: Verse 467
units.deva:
पुरो दृष्टे हि विषयेऽध्यस्यन्ति विषयान्तरम्।
तद् दृष्टं शुक्ति-रज्ज्वादौ सादृश्याद्यनुबन्धतः॥
units.translation: People superimpose one object on another seen before them; this is observed with mother-of-pearl or a rope, based on resemblance and the like.

gloss.en: in mother-of-pearl, a rope, and the rest
because of resemblance and the like

units.iast:
puro dṛṣṭe hi viṣaye’dhyasyanti viṣayāntaram|
tad dṛṣṭaṃ śukti-rajjvādau sādṛśyādyanubandhataḥ||

units.label: Verse 468
units.deva:
परत्र पूर्व-दृष्टस्यावभासः स्मृति-लक्षणः।
अध्यासः स कथं स्वामिन् भवेद् आत्मन्यगोचरे॥
units.translation: Superimposition is the appearance in another thing of what was seen before, and is characterized by memory. How can that occur in the Self, which is not an object, O Lord?
units.iast:
paratra pūrva-dṛṣṭasyāvabhāsaḥ smṛti-lakṣaṇaḥ|
adhyāsaḥ sa kathaṃ svāmin bhaved ātmanyagocare||

units.label: Verse 469
units.deva:
नानुभूतः कदाप्यात्माऽननुभूतस्य वस्तुनः।
सादृश्यं सिध्यति कथम् अनात्मनि विलक्षणे॥
units.translation: The Self has never been experienced as an object; how could resemblance to an unexperienced thing be established in the distinct not-Self?
units.iast:
nānubhūtaḥ kadāpyātmā’nanubhūtasya vastunaḥ|
sādṛśyaṃ sidhyati katham anātmani vilakṣaṇe||

units.label: Verse 470
units.deva:
अनात्मन्यात्मताध्यासः कथम् एष समागतः।
निवृत्तिः कथम् एतस्य केनोपायेन सिध्यति॥
units.translation: How did this superimposition of Selfhood on the not-Self arise? How can it cease, and by what means can that cessation be achieved?
units.iast:
anātmanyātmatādhyāsaḥ katham eṣa samāgataḥ|
nivṛttiḥ katham etasya kenopāyena sidhyati||

units.label: Verse 471
units.deva:
उपाधि-योग उभयोः सम एवेश-जीवयोः।
जीवस्यैव कथं बन्धो नेश्वरस्यास्ति तत् कथम्॥
units.translation: The association with adjuncts is the same for both Īśvara and the jīva. Why, then, is the jīva alone bound and not Īśvara?
units.iast:
upādhi-yoga ubhayoḥ sama eveśa-jīvayoḥ|
jīvasyaiva kathaṃ bandho neśvarasyāsti tat katham||

units.label: Verse 472
units.deva:
एतत् सर्वं दया-दृष्ट्या करामलकवत् स्फुटम्।
प्रतिपादय सर्वज्ञ श्रीगुरो करुणा-निधे॥
units.translation: O all-knowing revered teacher, ocean of compassion, explain all this clearly through your compassionate vision, as plainly as a myrobalan in the palm.

gloss.en: like a myrobalan in the palm

units.iast:
etat sarvaṃ dayā-dṛṣṭyā karāmalakavat sphuṭam|
pratipādaya sarvajña śrīguro karuṇā-nidhe||

units.label: Verse 473
units.deva:
न तावद् अयम् एकान्तेन आत्माविषय इष्यते।
अस्यास्मत्-प्रत्ययार्थत्वाद् अपरोक्षाच् च सर्वशः॥
units.translation: The Self is not held to be entirely unobjectifiable: it is directly evident in every way because it is the referent of the thought “I.”

gloss.en: because it is the meaning of the thought “I”

units.iast:
na tāvad ayam ekāntena ātmāviṣaya iṣyate|
asyāsmat-pratyayārthatvād aparokṣāc ca sarvaśaḥ||

units.label: Verse 474
units.deva:
प्रसिद्धिर् आत्मनोऽस्त्येव न कस्यापि च दृश्यते।
प्रत्ययो नाहम् अस्मीति न ह्यस्ति प्रत्यग्-आत्मनि॥
units.translation: The Self is manifestly evident; no one has the thought “I do not exist,” for such a thought does not arise in the inner Self.
units.iast:
prasiddhir ātmano’styeva na kasyāpi ca dṛśyate|
pratyayo nāham asmīti na hyasti pratyag-ātmani||

units.label: Verse 475
units.deva:
न कस्यापि स्व-सद्-भावे प्रमाणम् अभिकाङ्क्ष्यते।
प्रमाणानां च प्रामाण्यं यन्-मूलं किं नु बोधयेत्॥
units.translation: No one asks for proof of their own existence; what could establish the validity of the means of knowledge, whose very basis is the Self?
units.iast:
na kasyāpi sva-sad-bhāve pramāṇam abhikāṅkṣyate|
pramāṇānāṃ ca prāmāṇyaṃ yan-mūlaṃ kiṃ nu bodhayet||

units.label: Verse 476
units.deva:
माया-कार्यैस् तिरो-भूतो नैष आत्मानुभूयते।
मेघ-वृन्दैर् यथा भानुस् तथायम् अहम्-आदिभिः॥
units.translation: This Self is not recognized because it is concealed by the effects of Māyā, just as the sun is hidden by clusters of clouds and the Self by “I” and the like.
units.iast:
māyā-kāryais tiro-bhūto naiṣa ātmānubhūyate|
megha-vṛndair yathā bhānus tathāyam aham-ādibhiḥ||

units.label: Verse 477
units.deva:
पुरः-स्थ एव विषये वस्तुन्यध्यस्यताम् इति।
नियमो न कृतः सद्भिर् भ्रान्तिर् एवात्र कारणम्॥
units.translation: The wise set no rule that superimposition occurs only on an object standing directly before one; here, error alone is the cause.
units.iast:
puraḥ-stha eva viṣaye vastunyadhyasyatām iti|
niyamo na kṛtaḥ sadbhir bhrāntir evātra kāraṇam||

units.label: Verse 478
units.deva:
दृग्-आद्यविषये व्योम्नि नीलतादि यथाबुधाः।
अध्यस्यन्ति तथैवास्मिन्न् आत्मन्यपि मति-भ्रमात्॥
