units.translation: Just as ignorant people superimpose blueness and the like on the sky, which is not an object of sight and the rest, so too they superimpose [qualities] on this Self through error of mind.

gloss.en: not an object of sight and the rest

units.iast:
dṛg-ādyaviṣaye vyomni nīlatādi yathābudhāḥ|
adhyasyanti tathaivāsminn ātmanyapi mati-bhramāt||

units.label: Verse 479
units.deva:
अनात्मन्यात्मताध्यासे न सादृश्यम् अपेक्षते।
पीतोऽयं शङ्ख इत्यादौ सादृश्यं किम् अपेक्षितम्॥
units.translation: Superimposing Selfhood on the not-Self does not require resemblance. What resemblance is required when one says, “This conch is yellow”?
units.iast:
anātmanyātmatādhyāse na sādṛśyam apekṣate|
pīto’yaṃ śaṅkha ityādau sādṛśyaṃ kim apekṣitam||

units.label: Verse 480
units.deva:
निरुपाधि-भ्रमेष्वस्य नैवापेक्षा प्रदृश्यते।
सोपाधिष्वेव तद् दृष्टं रज्जु-सर्प-भ्रमादिषु॥
units.translation: In errors without a limiting adjunct, no need for similarity is seen. It is found only in errors with adjuncts, such as mistaking a rope for a snake.

gloss.en: in errors without a limiting adjunct
in errors such as mistaking a rope for a snake

units.iast:
nirupādhi-bhrameṣv asya naivāpekṣā pradṛśyate|
sopādhiṣv eva tad dṛṣṭaṃ rajju-sarpa-bhramādiṣu||

units.label: Verse 481
units.deva:
तथापि किञ्चिद् वक्ष्यामि सादृश्यं शृणु तत्-परः।
अत्यन्त-निर्मलः सूक्ष्म आत्मायम् अतिभास्वरः॥
units.translation: Even so, I will say something about the similarity; listen closely. This Self is utterly pure, subtle, and exceedingly luminous.
units.iast:
tathāpi kiñcid vakṣyāmi sādṛśyaṃ śṛṇu tat-paraḥ|
atyanta-nirmalaḥ sūkṣma ātmāyam atibhāsvaraḥ||

units.label: Verse 482
units.deva:
बुद्धिस् तथैव सत्त्वात्मा साभासा भास्वरामला।
सांनिध्याद् आत्मवद् भाति सूर्यवत् स्फटिको यथा॥
units.translation: The intellect too, with the nature of sattva, bears a reflection and is luminous and stainless. By the Self’s nearness it shines like the Self, as a crystal shines like the sun.
units.iast:
buddhis tathaiva sattvātmā sābhāsā bhāsvarāmalā|
sāṃnidhyād ātmavad bhāti sūryavat sphaṭiko yathā||

units.label: Verse 483
units.deva:
आत्माभासं ततो बुद्धिर् बुद्ध्याभासं ततो मनः।
अक्षाणि मन-आभासान्य् अक्षाभासम् इदं वपुः।
अत एवात्मता-बुद्धिर् देहाक्षादाव् अनात्मनि॥
units.translation: The intellect [has] the reflection of the Self; then the mind [has] the reflection of the intellect; the senses [have] reflections of the mind; and this body [has] the reflection of the senses. Hence the idea of being the Self arises in what is not the Self, such as the body and senses.

gloss.en: the idea of being the Self
in the body, senses, and so on
in what is not the Self

units.iast:
ātmābhāsaṃ tato buddhir buddhyābhāsaṃ tato manaḥ|
akṣāṇi mana-ābhāsāny akṣābhāsam idaṃ vapuḥ|
ata evātmatā-buddhir dehākṣādāv anātmani||

units.label: Verse 484
units.deva:
मूढानां प्रतिबिम्बादौ बालानाम् इव दृश्यते।
सादृश्यं विद्यते बुद्धावात्मनोऽध्यास-कारणम्॥
units.translation: For the deluded, similarity in a reflection and the like is seen as it is for children. A resemblance is present in the intellect, and it is the cause of superimposing the Self.

gloss.en: in a reflection and the like

units.iast:
mūḍhānāṃ pratibimbādau bālānām iva dṛśyate|
sādṛśyaṃ vidyate buddhāvātmano’dhyāsa-kāraṇam||

units.label: Verse 485
units.deva:
अनात्मन्यहम् इत्येव योऽयम् अध्यास ईरितः।
स्याद् उत्तरोत्तराध्यासे पूर्व-पूर्वस् तु कारणम्॥
units.translation: This superimposition, spoken of as “I” in what is not the Self, becomes the cause of each successive superimposition; each earlier one is its cause.

gloss.en: in what is not the Self

units.iast:
anātmanyaham ityeva yo’yam adhyāsa īritaḥ|
syād uttarottarādhyāse pūrva-pūrvas tu kāraṇam||

units.label: Verse 486
units.deva:
सुप्ति-मूर्छोत्थितेष्व् एव दृष्टः संसार-लक्षणः।
अनादिर् एषाविद्या तत्-संस्कारोऽपि च तादृशः॥
units.translation: The mark of saṃsāra is seen only in those who have awakened from sleep or fainting. This ignorance is beginningless, and its latent impression is likewise beginningless.

gloss.en: in those who have awakened from sleep or fainting

units.iast:
supti-mūrchotthiteṣv eva dṛṣṭaḥ saṃsāra-lakṣaṇaḥ|
anādir eṣāvidyā tat-saṃskāro’pi ca tādṛśaḥ||

units.label: Verse 487
units.deva:
अध्यास-बाधागमनस्य कारणं
शृणु प्रवक्ष्यामि समाहितात्मा।
यस्माद् इदं प्राप्तम् अनर्थ-जातं
जन्माप्यय-व्याधि-जरादि-दुःखम्॥
units.translation: Listen with a composed mind: I will explain the cause by which superimposition is brought to an end, from which this mass of misfortune has arisen—suffering from birth, death, disease, old age, and the like.

gloss.en: of attaining the sublation of superimposition
suffering from birth, death, disease, old age, and the like

units.iast:
adhyāsa-bādhāgamanasya kāraṇaṃ
śṛṇu pravakṣyāmi samāhitātmā|
yasmād idaṃ prāptam anartha-jātaṃ
janmāpyaya-vyādhi-jarādi-duḥkham||

units.label: Verse 488
units.deva:
आत्मोपाधेर् अविद्याया अस्ति शक्ति-द्वयं महत्।
विक्षेप आवृतिश् चेति याभ्यां संसार आत्मनः॥
units.translation: The ignorance that serves as the Self’s limiting adjunct has two great powers: projection and veiling. By these two, the Self has saṃsāra.
units.iast:
ātmopādher avidyāyā asti śakti-dvayaṃ mahat|
vikṣepa āvṛtiś ceti yābhyāṃ saṃsāra ātmanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 489
units.deva:
आवृतिस् तमसः शक्तिस् तद्ध्यावरण-कारणम्।
मूलाविद्येति सा प्रोक्ता यया संमोहितं जगत्॥
units.translation: Veiling is the power of tamas; it is the cause of covering. It is called root ignorance, by which the world is utterly deluded.
units.iast:
āvṛtis tamasaḥ śaktis taddhyāvaraṇa-kāraṇam|
mūlāvidyeti sā proktā yayā saṃmohitaṃ jagat||

units.label: Verse 490
units.deva:
विवेकवान् अप्यतियौक्तिकोऽपि
श्रुतात्म-तत्त्वोऽपि च पण्डितोऽपि।
शक्त्या यया संवृत-बोध-दृष्टिर्
आत्मानम् आत्म-स्थम् इमं न वेद॥
units.translation: Even a discriminating, highly skilled reasoner, learned in the truth of the Self and a scholar, does not know this Self abiding within, because that power has obscured his vision of awareness.

gloss.en: one who has learned the truth of the Self
whose vision of awareness is covered

units.iast:
vivekavān apyatiyauktiko’pi
śrutātma-tattvo’pi ca paṇḍito’pi|
śaktyā yayā saṃvṛta-bodha-dṛṣṭir
ātmānam ātma-stham imaṃ na veda||

units.label: Verse 491
units.deva:
विक्षेप-नाम्नी रजसस् तु शक्तिः
प्रवृत्ति-हेतुः पुरुषस्य नित्यम्।
स्थूलादि-लिङ्गान्तम् अशेषम् एतद्
यया सदात्मन्यसद् एव सूयते॥
units.translation: The power of rajas called projection is always a cause of activity for a person. By it, all this unreal—from the gross body through the subtle body—is produced in the real Self.
units.iast:
vikṣepa-nāmnī rajasas tu śaktiḥ
pravṛtti-hetuḥ puruṣasya nityam|
sthūlādi-liṅgāntam aśeṣam etad
yayā sadātmanyasad eva sūyate||

units.label: Verse 492
units.deva:
निद्रा यथा पुरुषम् अप्रमत्तं
समावृणोतीयम् अपि प्रतीचम्।
तथावृणोत्यावृति-शक्तिर् अन्तर्
विक्षेप-शक्तिं परिजृम्भयन्ती॥
units.translation: Just as sleep envelops an alert person, so the veiling power covers the inward Self, while making the projecting power expand.
units.iast:
nidrā yathā puruṣam apramattaṃ
samāvṛṇotīyam api pratīcam|
tathāvṛṇotyāvṛti-śaktir antar
vikṣepa-śaktiṃ parijṛmbhayantī||

units.label: Verse 493
units.deva:
शक्त्या महत्यावरणाभिधानया
समावृते सत्य् अमल-स्वरूपे।
पुमान् अनात्मन्यहम् एष एवे-
त्यात्मत्व-बुद्धिं विदधाति मोहात्॥
units.translation: When the stainless nature is covered by the great power called veiling, a person, out of delusion, forms the idea “I am this very non-Self.”

gloss.en: in what is not the Self
the idea of being the Self

units.iast:
śaktyā mahatyāvaraṇābhidhānayā
samāvṛte saty amala-svarūpe|
pumān anātmanyaham eṣa eve-
tyātmatva-buddhiṃ vidadhāti mohāt||

units.label: Verse 494
units.deva:
यथा प्रसुप्ति-प्रतिभास-देहे
स्वात्मत्व-धीर् एष तथा ह्यनात्मनः।
जन्माप्यय-क्षुद्-भय-तृट्छ्रमादीन्
आरोपयत्यात्मनि तस्य धर्मान्॥
units.translation: Just as this person takes the body appearing in sleep to be his own Self, so he superimposes on the Self the properties of what is not the Self: birth, death, hunger, fear, thirst, fatigue, and the like.

gloss.en: in the body appearing in sleep
the idea that it is one’s own Self
of what is not the Self

units.iast:
yathā prasupti-pratibhāsa-dehe
svātmatva-dhīr eṣa tathā hyanātmanaḥ|
janmāpyaya-kṣud-bhaya-tṛṭchramādīn
āropayatyātmani tasya dharmān||

units.label: Verse 495
units.deva:
विक्षेप-शक्त्या परिचोद्यमानः
करोति कर्माण्य् उभयात्मकानि।
भुञ्जान एतत्-फलम् अप्य् उपात्तं
परिभ्रमत्य् एष भवाम्बु-राशौ॥
units.translation: Impelled by the projecting power, this person performs actions of both kinds; experiencing their acquired fruits, he wanders in the ocean of becoming.
units.iast:
vikṣepa-śaktyā paricodyamānaḥ
karoti karmāṇy ubhayātmakāni|
bhuñjāna etat-phalam apy upāttaṃ
paribhramaty eṣa bhavāmbu-rāśau||

units.label: Verse 496
units.deva:
अध्यास-दोषात् समुपागतोऽयम्
संसार-बन्धः प्रबलः प्रतीचः।
यद्-योगतः क्लिश्यति गर्भ-वास-
जन्माप्यय-क्लेश-भयैर् अजस्रम्॥
units.translation: This powerful bondage of saṃsāra has arisen for the inward Self through the fault of superimposition. Through it, one suffers continually from the pains and fears of life in the womb, birth, death, and the like.
units.iast:
adhyāsa-doṣāt samupāgato’yam
saṃsāra-bandhaḥ prabalaḥ pratīcaḥ|
yad-yogataḥ kliśyati garbha-vāsa-
janmāpyaya-kleśa-bhayair ajasram||

units.label: Verse 497
units.deva:
अध्यासो नाम खल्वेष वस्तुनो योऽन्यथा-ग्रहः।
स्वाभाविक-भ्रान्ति-मूलं संसृतेर् आदि-कारणम्॥
units.translation: Superimposition is indeed this: taking a thing to be other than it is. It is the root of natural error and the first cause of transmigration.
units.iast:
adhyāso nāma khalveṣa vastuno yo’nyathā-grahaḥ|
svābhāvika-bhrānti-mūlaṃ saṃsṛter ādi-kāraṇam||

units.label: Verse 498
units.deva:
सर्वानर्थस्य तद् बीजं योऽन्यथा-ग्रह आत्मनः।
ततः संसार-सम्पातः सन्तत-क्लेश-लक्षणः॥
units.translation: That misapprehension of the Self is the seed of every misfortune; from it comes entry into saṃsāra, marked by unceasing distress.
units.iast:
sarvānarthasya tad bījaṃ yo’nyathā-graha ātmanaḥ|
tataḥ saṃsāra-sampātaḥ santata-kleśa-lakṣaṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 499
units.deva:
अध्यासाद् एव संसारो नष्टेऽध्यासे न दृश्यते।
तद् एतद् उभयं स्पष्टं पश्य त्वं बद्ध-मुक्तयोः॥
units.translation: Saṃsāra exists only because of superimposition; when superimposition is destroyed, it is no longer seen. See clearly this distinction between the bound and the liberated.
units.iast:
adhyāsād eva saṃsāro naṣṭe’dhyāse na dṛśyate|
tad etad ubhayaṃ spaṣṭaṃ paśya tvaṃ baddha-muktayoḥ||

units.label: Verse 500
units.deva:
बद्धं प्रवृत्तितो विद्धि मुक्तं विद्धि निवृत्तितः।
प्रवृत्तिर् एव संसारो निवृत्तिर् मुक्तिर् इष्यते॥
units.translation: Know the bound one by activity, and the liberated one by withdrawal. Activity itself is saṃsāra; withdrawal is held to be liberation.
units.iast:
baddhaṃ pravṛttito viddhi muktaṃ viddhi nivṛttitaḥ|
pravṛttir eva saṃsāro nivṛttir muktir iṣyate||

units.label: Verse 501
units.deva:
आत्मनः सोऽयम् अध्यासो मिथ्या-ज्ञान-पुरः-सरः।
असत्कल्पोऽपि संसारं तनुते रज्जु-सर्पवत्॥
units.translation: This superimposition on the Self is preceded by false knowledge. Though unreal, it spreads saṃsāra like the rope-snake.
units.iast:
ātmanaḥ so’yam adhyāso mithyā-jñāna-puraḥ-saraḥ|
asatkalpo’pi saṃsāraṃ tanute rajju-sarpavat||

units.label: Verse 502
units.deva:
उपाधि-योग-साम्येऽपि जीववत् परमात्मनः।
उपाधि-भेदान् नो बन्धस् तत्-कार्यम् अपि किञ्चन॥
units.translation: Even though the supreme Self’s association with adjuncts is like that of the jīva, the difference in adjuncts means there is no bondage or any effect of it.

gloss.en: in the similarity of association with adjuncts
because of the difference in adjuncts

units.iast:
upādhi-yoga-sāmye’pi jīvavat paramātmanaḥ|
upādhi-bhedān no bandhas tat-kāryam api kiñcana||

units.label: Verse 503
units.deva:
अस्योपाधिः शुद्ध-सत्त्व-प्रधाना
माया यत्र त्वस्य नास्त्यल्प-भावः।
सत्त्वस्यैवोत्कृष्टता तेन बन्धो
नो विक्षेपस् तत्-कृतो लेश-मात्रः॥
units.translation: His limiting adjunct is Māyā, predominantly pure sattva, in which there is no deficiency of sattva. Because sattva alone predominates, there is no bondage or even the slightest projection produced by it.
units.iast:
asyopādhiḥ śuddha-sattva-pradhānā
māyā yatra tvasya nāstyalpa-bhāvaḥ|
sattvasyaivotkṛṣṭatā tena bandho
no vikṣepas tat-kṛto leśa-mātraḥ||

units.label: Verse 504
units.deva:
सर्व-ज्ञोऽप्रतिबद्ध-बोध-विभवस् तेनैव देवः स्वयं
मायां स्वाम् अवलम्ब्य निश्चलतया स्व-च्छन्द-वृत्तिः प्रभुः।
सृष्टि-स्थित्यदन-प्रवेश-यमन-व्यापार-मात्रेच्छया
कुर्वन् क्रीडति तद् रजस् तम उभे संस्तभ्य शक्त्या स्वया॥
units.translation: The Lord is omniscient, with unobstructed awareness. Relying on his own Māyā, he remains steady and acts freely; by his own power he restrains both rajas and tamas and plays, acting solely by will through creation, maintenance, withdrawal, entry, and governance.

gloss.en: by the mere will for the processes of creation, maintenance, withdrawal, entry, and governance

units.iast:
sarva-jño’pratibaddha-bodha-vibhavas tenaiva devaḥ svayaṃ
māyāṃ svām avalambya niścalatayā sva-cchanda-vṛttiḥ prabhuḥ|
sṛṣṭi-sthityadana-praveśa-yamana-vyāpāra-mātrecchayā
kurvan krīḍati tad rajas tama ubhe saṃstabhya śaktyā svayā||

units.label: Verse 505
units.deva:
तस्माद् आवृति-विक्षेपौ किञ्चित् कर्तुं न शक्नुतः।
स्वयम् एव स्व-तन्त्रोऽसौ तत्-प्रवृत्ति-निरोधयोः॥
units.translation: Therefore veiling and projection cannot do anything. He himself is independent in their activity and cessation.
units.iast:
tasmād āvṛti-vikṣepau kiñcit kartuṃ na śaknutaḥ|
svayam eva sva-tantro’sau tat-pravṛtti-nirodhayoḥ||

units.label: Verse 506
units.deva:
तम् एव साधु-कर्मेति श्रुतिर् वक्ति महेशितुः।
निग्रहानुग्रहे शक्तिर् आवृति-क्षेपयोर् यतः॥
units.translation: The Śruti says of the Great Lord, “He alone makes [one perform] good action”; for the powers of restraint and favor lie in veiling and projection.
units.iast:
tam eva sādhukarmeti śrutir vakti maheśituḥ|
nigrahānugrahe śaktir āvṛti-kṣepayor yataḥ||

units.label: Verse 507
units.deva:
रजसस्तमसश्चैव प्राबल्यं सत्त्वहानतः।
जीवोपाधौ तथा जीवे तत्-कार्यं बलवत्-तरम्॥
units.translation: When sattva is diminished, rajas and tamas are strong in the jīva’s limiting adjunct and in the jīva; their effects are stronger there.

gloss.en: because of the loss of sattva

units.iast:
rajasastamasaścaiva prābalyaṃ sattvahānataḥ|
jīvopādhau tathā jīve tat-kāryaṃ balavat-taram||

units.label: Verse 508
units.deva:
तेन बन्धोऽस्य जीवस्य संसारोऽपि च तत्-कृतः।
सम्प्राप्तः सर्वदा यत्र दुःखं भूयः स ईक्षते॥
units.translation: By this, this jīva’s bondage and the saṃsāra produced by it have arisen; there the jīva continually encounters suffering again and again.
units.iast:
tena bandho’sya jīvasya saṃsāro’pi ca tat-kṛtaḥ|
samprāptaḥ sarvadā yatra duḥkhaṃ bhūyaḥ sa īkṣate||

units.label: Verse 509
units.deva:
एतस्य संसृतेर् हेतुर् अध्यासोऽर्थ-विपर्ययः।
अध्यास-मूलम् अज्ञानम् आहुर् आवृति-लक्षणम्॥
units.translation: Superimposition, a misapprehension of reality, is the cause of this transmigration. Ignorance is said to be the root of superimposition and to have veiling as its mark.
units.iast:
etasya saṃsṛter hetur adhyāso’rtha-viparyayaḥ|
adhyāsa-mūlam ajñānam āhur āvṛti-lakṣaṇam||

units.label: Verse 510
units.deva:
अज्ञानस्य निवृत्तिस् तु ज्ञानेनैव न कर्मणा।
अविरोधितया कर्म नैवाज्ञानस्य बाधकम्॥
units.translation: Ignorance ceases through knowledge alone, not through action. Since action does not oppose ignorance, it cannot remove it.
units.iast:
ajñānasya nivṛttis tu jñānenaiva na karmaṇā|
avirodhitayā karma naivājñānasya bādhakam||

units.label: Verse 511
units.deva:
कर्मणा जायते जन्तुः कर्मणैव प्रलीयते।
कर्मणः कार्यम् एवैषा जन्म-मृत्यु-परम्परा॥
units.translation: A being is born through action and is dissolved through action alone. This succession of birth and death is the effect of action.
units.iast:
karmaṇā jāyate jantuḥ karmaṇaiva pralīyate|
karmaṇaḥ kāryam evaiṣā janma-mṛtyu-paramparā||

units.label: Verse 512
units.deva:
नैतस्मात् कर्मणः कार्यम् अन्यद् अस्ति विलक्षणम्।
अज्ञान-कार्यं तत् कर्म यतोऽज्ञानेन वर्धते॥
units.translation: There is no other result of action that is distinct from it. That action is the effect of ignorance, since it grows through ignorance.
units.iast:
naitasmāt karmaṇaḥ kāryam anyad asti vilakṣaṇam|
ajñāna-kāryaṃ tat karma yato’jñānena vardhate||

units.label: Verse 513
units.deva:
यद् येन वर्धते तेन नाशस् तस्य न सिध्यति।
येन यस्य सहावस्था निरोधाय न कल्पते॥
units.translation: What grows through something is not destroyed by that very thing. What remains alongside something is not fit to bring about its cessation.
units.iast:
yad yena vardhate tena nāśas tasya na sidhyati|
yena yasya sahāvasthā nirodhāya na kalpate||

units.label: Verse 514
units.deva:
नाशकत्वं तद्-उभयोः को नु कल्पयितुं क्षमः।
सर्वं कर्माविरोध्य् एव यतोऽज्ञानस्य सर्वदा॥
units.translation: Who could suppose that either of the two has the power to destroy the other? All action is always indeed not opposed to ignorance.
units.iast:
nāśakatvaṃ tad-ubhayoḥ ko nu kalpayituṃ kṣamaḥ|
sarvaṃ karmāvirodhyeva yato’jñānasya sarvadā||

units.label: Verse 515
units.deva:
ततोऽज्ञानस्य विच्छित्तिः कर्मणा नैव सिध्यति।
यस्य प्रध्वंस-जनको यत्-संयोगोऽस्ति तत्-क्षणे॥
units.translation: Therefore, ignorance is not brought to an end by action. Its destruction occurs at the very moment of contact with that which causes its destruction.
units.iast:
tato’jñānasya vicchittiḥ karmaṇā naiva sidhyati|
yasya pradhvaṃsa-janako yat-saṃyogo’sti tat-kṣaṇe||

units.label: Verse 516
units.deva:
तयोर् एव विरोधित्वं युक्तं भिन्न-स्वभावयोः।
तमः-प्रकाशयोर् यद्वत् परस्-पर-विरोधिता॥
units.translation: Opposition between two things of distinct natures is reasonable, as in the mutual opposition of darkness and light.
units.iast:
tayor eva virodhitvaṃ yuktaṃ bhinna-svabhāvayoḥ|
tamaḥ-prakāśayor yadvat paraspara-virodhitā||

units.label: Verse 517
units.deva:
अज्ञान-ज्ञानयोस् तद्वद् उभयोर् एव दृश्यते।
न ज्ञानेन विनाऽज्ञान-नाशः केनापि सिध्यति॥
units.translation: Likewise, opposition between ignorance and knowledge is seen in both. Without knowledge, the destruction of ignorance cannot be achieved by anything.
units.iast:
ajñāna-jñānayos tadvad ubhayor eva dṛśyate|
na jñānena vinājñāna-nāśaḥ kenāpi sidhyati||

units.label: Verse 518
units.deva:
तस्माद् अज्ञान-विच्छित्त्यै ज्ञानं सम्पादयेत् सुधीः।
आत्मानात्म-विवेकेन ज्ञानं सिध्यति नान्यथा॥
units.translation: Therefore, the wise should bring about knowledge to end ignorance. Knowledge is established through discrimination between the Self and non-Self, and not otherwise.

gloss.en: through discrimination between Self and non-Self

units.iast:
tasmād ajñāna-vicchittyai jñānaṃ sampādayet sudhīḥ|
ātmānātma-vivekena jñānaṃ sidhyati nānyathā||

units.label: Verse 519
units.deva:
युक्त्यात्मानात्मनोस् तस्मात् करणीयं विवेचनम्।
अनात्मन्यात्मता-बुद्धि-ग्रन्थिर् येन विदीर्यते॥
units.translation: Therefore one should use reason to discriminate the Self and non-Self, by which the knot of the idea “Self” in what is not the Self is split.

gloss.en: in what is not the Self
the knot of the idea of being the Self

units.iast:
yuktyātmānātmanos tasmāt karaṇīyaṃ vivecanam|
anātmanyātmatā-buddhi-granthir yena vidīryate||

units.label: Verse 520
units.deva:
आत्मानात्म-विवेकार्थं विवादोऽयं निरूप्यते।
येनात्मानात्मनोस् तत्त्वं विविक्तं प्रस्फुटायते॥
units.translation: This discussion is set forth for the sake of discriminating the Self and non-Self; through it, their true nature becomes clearly distinguished.

gloss.en: for discriminating the Self and non-Self

units.iast:
ātmānātma-vivekārthaṃ vivādo’yaṃ nirūpyate|
yenātmānātmanos tattvaṃ viviktaṃ prasphuṭāyate||

units.label: Verse 521
units.deva:
मूढा अश्रुत-वेदान्ताः स्वयं पण्डित-मानिनः।
ईश-प्रसाद-रहिताः सद्-गुरोश्च बहिर्-मुखाः॥
units.translation: Fools who have not heard Vedānta, who regard themselves as learned, lack the Lord’s grace, and turn away from a true teacher.
units.iast:
mūḍhā aśruta-vedāntāḥ svayaṃ paṇḍita-māninaḥ|
īśa-prasāda-rahitāḥ sad-gurośca bahir-mukhāḥ||

units.label: Verse 522
units.deva:
विवदन्ति प्रकारं तं शृणु वक्ष्यामि सादरम्।
अत्यन्त-पामरः कश्चित् पुत्र आत्मेति मन्यते॥
units.translation: Listen respectfully as I explain the kinds of views they dispute: some utterly foolish person thinks that the son is the Self.
units.iast:
vivadanti prakāraṃ taṃ śṛṇu vakṣyāmi sādaram|
atyanta-pāmaraḥ kaścit putra ātmeti manyate||

units.label: Verse 523
units.deva:
आत्मनीव स्व-पुत्रेऽपि प्रबल-प्रीति-दर्शनात्।
पुत्रे तु पुष्टे पुष्टोऽहं नष्टे नष्टोऽहम् इत्यतः॥
units.translation: Seeing strong affection for one’s own son as for oneself, one says, “When my son thrives, I thrive; when he perishes, I perish.”
units.iast:
ātmanīva sva-putre’pi prabala-prīti-darśanāt|
putre tu puṣṭe puṣṭo’haṃ naṣṭe naṣṭo’ham ityataḥ||

units.label: Verse 524
units.deva:
अनुभूति-बलाच् चापि युक्तितोऽपि श्रुतेर् अपि।
आत्मा वै पुत्रनामासीत्येवं च वदति श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: They appeal to experience, reasoning, and scripture; Śruti too says, “The Self was indeed called ‘son.’”
units.iast:
anubhūti-balāc cāpi yuktito’pi śruter api|
ātmā vai putranāmāsītyevaṃ ca vadati śrutiḥ||

units.label: Verse 525
units.deva:
दीपाद् दीपो यथा तद्वत् पितुः पुत्रः प्रजायते।
पितुर् गुणानां तनये बीजाङ्कुरवद् ईक्षणात्॥
units.translation: Just as one lamp is born from another lamp, so a son is born from his father; the father’s qualities are seen in the child, as a seed [is seen] in a sprout.
units.iast:
dīpād dīpo yathā tadvat pituḥ putraḥ prajāyate|
pitur guṇānāṃ tanaye bījāṅkuravad īkṣaṇāt||

units.label: Verse 526
units.deva:
अतोऽयं पुत्र आत्मेति मन्यते भ्रान्तिमत्तमः।
तन्-मतं दूषयत्य् अन्यः पुत्र आत्मा कथं त्विति॥
units.translation: Thus a greatly deluded person thinks, “This son is the Self.” Another challenges that view: “How can the son be the Self?”
units.iast:
ato’yaṃ putra ātmeti manyate bhrāntimattamaḥ|
tan-mataṃ dūṣayaty anyaḥ putra ātmā kathaṃ tv iti||

units.label: Verse 527
units.deva:
प्रीति-मात्रात् कथं पुत्र आत्मा भवितुम् अर्हति।
अन्यत्रापीक्ष्यते प्रीतिः क्षेत्र-पात्र-धनादिषु॥
units.translation: How can the son be the Self merely because of affection? Affection is seen for other things too, such as fields, vessels, and wealth.

gloss.en: for fields, vessels, wealth, and the like

units.iast:
prīti-mātrāt kathaṃ putra ātmā bhavitum arhati|
anyatrāpīkṣyate prītiḥ kṣetra-pātra-dhanādiṣu||

units.label: Verse 528
units.deva:
पुत्राद् विशिष्टा देहेऽस्मिन् प्राणिनां प्रीतिर् इष्यते।
प्रदीप्ते भवने पुत्रं त्यक्त्वा जन्तुः पलायते॥
units.translation: People’s affection for this body is held to be greater than for a son. When a house is burning, a person runs away after abandoning his son.
units.iast:
putrād viśiṣṭā dehe’smin prāṇināṃ prītir iṣyate|
pradīpte bhavane putraṃ tyaktvā jantuḥ palāyate||

units.label: Verse 529
units.deva:
तं विक्रीणाति देहार्थं प्रतिकूलं निहन्ति च।
तस्माद् आत्मा तु तनयो न भवेच् च कदाचन॥
units.translation: One sells him for the sake of the body, and kills him if he is hostile. Therefore, a son can never be the Self.

gloss.en: for the sake of the body

units.iast:
taṃ vikrīṇāti dehārthaṃ pratikūlaṃ nihanti ca|
tasmād ātmā tu tanayo na bhavec ca kadācana||

units.label: Verse 530
units.deva:
गुण-रूपादि-सादृश्यं दीपवन् न सुते पितुः।
अव्यङ्गाज् जायते व्यङ्गः सु-गुणाद् अपि दुर्-गुणः॥
units.translation: A father and son are not alike in qualities, appearance, and the like as one lamp is like another. A deformed child may be born from an unblemished parent, and a wicked child even from a virtuous parent.

gloss.en: similarity in qualities, appearance, and the like

units.iast:
guṇa-rūpādi-sādṛśyaṃ dīpavan na sute pituḥ|
avyaṅgāj jāyate vyaṅgaḥ su-guṇād api dur-guṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 531
units.deva:
आभास-मात्रास् ताः सर्वा युक्तयोऽप्युक्तयोऽपि च।
पुत्रस्य पितृवद् गेहे सर्व-कार्येषु वस्तुषु॥
units.translation: All those arguments and statements are mere appearances: that a son is like his father in all the household tasks and things.
units.iast:
ābhāsa-mātrās tāḥ sarvā yuktayo’pyuktayo’pi ca|
putrasya pitṛvad gehe sarva-kāryeṣu vastuṣu||

units.label: Verse 532
units.deva:
स्वामित्व-द्योतनायास्मिन्न् आत्मत्वम् उपचर्यते।
श्रुत्या तु मुख्यया वृत्त्या पुत्र आत्मेति नोच्यते॥
units.translation: Selfhood is figuratively attributed to the son to indicate ownership; but Śruti does not say in its primary sense that the son is the Self.
units.iast:
svāmitva-dyotanāyāsminn ātmatvam upacaryate|
śrutyā tu mukhyayā vṛttyā putra ātmeti nocyate||

units.label: Verse 533
units.deva:
औपचारिकम् आत्मत्वं पुत्रे तस्मान् न मुख्यतः।
अहम्-पद-प्रत्ययार्थो देह एव न चेतरः॥
units.translation: Therefore, selfhood in the son is figurative, not primary. The referent of the word “I” is the body alone, and nothing else.
units.iast:
aupacārikam ātmatvaṃ putre tasmān na mukhyataḥ|
aham-pada-pratyayārtho deha eva na cetaraḥ||

units.label: Verse 534
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्षः सर्व-जन्तूनां देहोऽहम् इति निश्चयः।
एष पुरुषोऽन्न-रसमय इत्यपि च श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: For all living beings, the certainty “I am the body” is directly evident. Śruti also says, “This person is made of the essence of food.”

gloss.en: made of the essence of food

units.iast:
pratyakṣaḥ sarva-jantūnāṃ deho’ham iti niścayaḥ|
eṣa puruṣo’nna-rasamaya ityapi ca śrutiḥ||

units.label: Verse 535
units.deva:
पुरुषत्वं वदत्यस्य स्वात्मा हि पुरुषस् ततः।
आत्मायं देह एवेति चार्वाकेण विनिश्चितम्॥
units.translation: It calls this one a person; since the person is indeed one’s own self, the Cārvāka concludes that this Self is the body alone.
units.iast:
puruṣatvaṃ vadatyasya svātmā hi puruṣas tataḥ|
ātmāyaṃ deha eveti cārvākeṇa viniścitam||

units.label: Verse 536
units.deva:
तन्-मतं दूषयत्यन्योऽसहमानः पृथग्-जनः।
देह आत्मा कथं नु स्यात् पर-तन्त्रो ह्यचेतनः॥
units.translation: Another person, unwilling to accept that view, challenges it: “How could the body be the Self, since it is dependent on another and unconscious?”
units.iast:
tan-mataṃ dūṣayatyanyo’sahamānaḥ pṛthag-janaḥ|
deha ātmā kathaṃ nu syāt para-tantro hyacetanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 537
units.deva:
इन्द्रियैश् चाल्यमानोऽयं चेष्टते न स्वतः क्वचित्।
आश्रयश् चक्षुर्-आदीनां गृहवद् गृह-मेधिनाम्॥
units.translation: This body, moved by the senses, never acts by itself. It is a support for the eyes and other senses, as a house is for its residents.

gloss.en: for the eyes and the rest

units.iast:
indriyaiś cālyamāno’yaṃ ceṣṭate na svataḥ kvacit|
āśrayaś cakṣur-ādīnāṃ gṛhavad gṛha-medhinām||

units.label: Verse 538
units.deva:
बाल्यादि-नानावस्थावाञ् शुक्ल-शोणित-सम्भवः।
अतः कदापि देहस्य नात्मत्वम् उपपद्यते॥
units.translation: The body has many states beginning with childhood and arises from semen and blood. Therefore, the body’s being the Self is never reasonable.
units.iast:
bālyādi-nānāvasthāvāñ śukla-śoṇita-sambhavaḥ|
ataḥ kadāpi dehasya nātmatvam upapadyate||

units.label: Verse 539
units.deva:
बधिरोऽहं च काणोऽहं मूक इत्यनुभूतितः।
इन्द्रियाणि भवन्त्यात्मा येषाम् अस्त्यर्थ-वेदनम्॥
units.translation: The experience “I am deaf,” “I am blind,” and “I am mute” leads some to hold the senses to be the Self, since the senses register objects.
units.iast:
badhiro’haṃ ca kāṇo’haṃ mūka ityanubhūtitaḥ|
indriyāṇi bhavantyātmā yeṣām astyartha-vedanam||

units.label: Verse 540
units.deva:
इन्द्रियाणां चेतनत्वं देहे प्राणाः प्रजा-पतिम्।
एतम् एत्येत्य् ऊचुर् इति श्रुत्यैव प्रतिपाद्यते॥
units.translation: Śruti itself establishes the senses’ consciousness in the body, saying that the vital powers went to Prajāpati and, having approached him, spoke.
units.iast:
indriyāṇāṃ cetanatvaṃ dehe prāṇāḥ prajā-patim|
etam etyety ūcur iti śrutyaiva pratipādyate||

units.label: Verse 541
units.deva:
यतस् तस्माद् इन्द्रियाणां युक्तम् आत्मत्वम् इत्यमुम्।
निश्चयं दूषयत्यन्योऽसहमानः पृथग्-जनः॥
units.translation: Therefore another ordinary person, unwilling to accept the conclusion that selfhood in the senses is reasonable, refutes it.
units.iast:
yatas tasmād indriyāṇāṃ yuktam ātmatvam ityamum|
niścayaṃ dūṣayatyanyo’sahamānaḥ pṛthag-janaḥ||

units.label: Verse 542
units.deva:
इन्द्रियाणि कथं त्वात्मा करणानि कुठारवत्।
करणस्य कुठारादेश् चेतनत्वं न हीक्ष्यते॥
units.translation: How can the senses be the Self? They are instruments, like an axe; no one sees consciousness in an instrument such as an axe.

gloss.en: of an axe and the like

units.iast:
indriyāṇi kathaṃ tvātmā karaṇāni kuṭhāravat|
karaṇasya kuṭhārādeś cetanatvaṃ na hīkṣyate||

units.label: Verse 543
units.deva:
श्रुत्याधिदेवताम् एवेन्द्रियेषूपचर्यते।
न तु साक्षाद् इन्द्रियाणां चेतनत्वम् उदीर्यते॥
units.translation: Śruti figuratively assigns the presiding deities to the senses; it does not directly declare that the senses themselves are conscious.
units.iast:
śrutyādhidevatām evendriyeṣūpacaryate|
na tu sākṣād indriyāṇāṃ cetanatvam udīryate||

units.label: Verse 544
units.deva:
अचेतनस्य दीपादेर् अर्थाभासकता यथा।
तथैव चक्षुर्-आदीनां जडानाम् अपि सिध्यति॥
units.translation: Just as an insentient lamp and the like can make objects appear, the same is true of insentient eyes and the other senses.

gloss.en: the capacity to make objects appear
of the eyes and the rest

units.iast:
acetanasya dīpāder arthābhāsakatā yathā|
tathaiva cakṣur-ādīnāṃ jaḍānām api sidhyati||

units.label: Verse 545
units.deva:
इन्द्रियाणां चेष्टयिता प्राणोऽयं पञ्च-वृत्तिकः।
सर्वावस्थास्व् अवस्थावान् सोऽयम् आत्मत्वम् अर्हति।
अहं क्षुधावांस् तृष्णावान् इत्याद्यनुभवाद् अपि॥
units.translation: This fivefold prāṇa moves the senses and remains present in all states; it is fit to be called the Self. The experience “I am hungry, I am thirsty,” and the like also supports this.
units.iast:
indriyāṇāṃ ceṣṭayitā prāṇo’yaṃ pañca-vṛttikaḥ|
sarvāvasthāsv avasthāvān so’yam ātmatvam arhati|
ahaṃ kṣudhāvāṃs tṛṣṇāvān ityādyanubhavād api||

units.label: Verse 546
units.deva:
श्रुत्यान्योऽन्तर आत्मा प्राणमय इतीर्यते यस्मात्।
तस्मात् प्राणस्यात्मत्वं युक्तं नो करण-संज्ञानां क्वापि॥
units.translation: Since Śruti declares another inner Self to be made of prāṇa, it is reasonable to regard prāṇa as the Self, never the things called instruments.
units.iast:
śrutyānyo’ntara ātmā prāṇamaya itīryate yasmāt|
tasmāt prāṇasyātmatvaṃ yuktaṃ no karaṇa-saṃjñānāṃ kvāpi||

units.label: Verse 547
units.deva:
इति निश्चयम् एतस्य दूषयत्यपरो जडः।
भवत्यात्मा कथं प्राणो वायुर् एवैष आन्तरः॥
units.translation: Another dull disputant criticizes this conclusion: “How can prāṇa be the Self? This inner [breath] is only air.”
units.iast:
iti niścayam etasya dūṣayatyaparo jaḍaḥ|
bhavatyātmā kathaṃ prāṇo vāyur evaiṣa āntaraḥ||

units.label: Verse 548
units.deva:
बहिर् यात्य् अन्तर् आयाति भस्त्रिका-वायुवन् मुहुः।
न हितं वाऽहितं वा स्वम् अन्यद् वा वेद किञ्चन॥
units.translation: It repeatedly goes out and comes in like air in a bellows. It knows nothing at all—neither what is beneficial nor harmful, its own nor anything else.
units.iast:
bahir yāty antar āyāti bhastrikā-vāyuvan muhuḥ|
na hitaṃ vā’hitaṃ vā svam anyad vā veda kiñcana||

units.label: Verse 549
units.deva:
जड-स्वभावश् चपलः कर्म-युक्तश्च सर्वदा।
प्राणस्य भानं मनसि स्थिते सुप्ते न दृश्यते॥
units.translation: Prāṇa is inert by nature, restless, and always engaged in activity. When the mind is settled in sleep, the appearance of prāṇa is not seen.
units.iast:
jaḍa-svabhāvaś capalaḥ karma-yuktaśca sarvadā|
prāṇasya bhānaṃ manasi sthite supte na dṛśyate||

units.label: Verse 550
units.deva:
मनस् तु सर्वं जानाति सर्व-वेदन-कारणम्।
यत् तस्मान् मन एवात्मा प्राणस् तु न कदाचन॥
units.translation: The mind, however, knows everything and is the cause of all cognition. Therefore the mind alone is the Self; prāṇa is never the Self.
units.iast:
manas tu sarvaṃ jānāti sarva-vedana-kāraṇam|
yat tasmān mana evātmā prāṇas tu na kadācana||

units.label: Verse 551
units.deva:
सङ्कल्पवान् अहं चिन्तावान् अहं च विकल्पवान्।
इत्याद्यनुभवाद् अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा मनोमयः॥
units.translation: From experiences such as “I form intentions,” “I think,” and “I make distinctions,” [some infer] another inner Self, made of mind.
units.iast:
saṅkalpavān ahaṃ cintāvān ahaṃ ca vikalpavān|
ityādyanubhavād anyo’ntara ātmā manomayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 552
units.deva:
इत्यादि-श्रुति-सद्-भावाद् युक्ता मनस आत्मता।
इति निश्चयम् एतस्य दूषयत्यपरो जडः॥
units.translation: Because such statements occur in Śruti, it is reasonable to regard the mind as the Self. Another dull disputant refutes this conclusion.

gloss.en: because of their presence in Śruti

units.iast:
ityādi-śruti-sad-bhāvād yuktā manasa ātmatā|
iti niścayam etasya dūṣayatyaparo jaḍaḥ||

units.label: Verse 553
units.deva:
कथं मनस आत्मत्वं करणस्य दृग्-आदिवत्।
कर्तृ-प्रयोज्यं करणं न स्वयं तु प्रवर्तते॥
units.translation: How can the mind be the Self? Like sight and the other senses, it is an instrument. An instrument is set in motion by an agent; it does not act on its own.

gloss.en: set in motion by an agent

units.iast:
kathaṃ manasa ātmatvaṃ karaṇasya dṛg-ādivat|
kartṛ-prayojyaṃ karaṇaṃ na svayaṃ tu pravartate||

units.label: Verse 554
units.deva:
करण-प्रयोक्ता यः कर्ता तस्यैवात्मत्वम् अर्हति।
आत्मा स्व-तन्त्रः पुरुषो न प्रयोज्यः कदाचन॥
units.translation: The agent who employs an instrument alone deserves to be called the Self. The Self is an independent person, never something made to act by another.

gloss.en: to be made to act by another

units.iast:
karaṇa-prayoktā yaḥ kartā tasyaivātmatvam arhati|
ātmā sva-tantraḥ puruṣo na prayojyaḥ kadācana||

units.label: Verse 555
units.deva:
अहं कर्तास्म्यहं भोक्ता सुखीत्यनुभवाद् अपि।
बुद्धिर् आत्मा भवत्येव बुद्धि-धर्मो ह्यहङ्-कृतिः॥
units.translation: From the experience “I am the agent, I am the enjoyer, I am happy,” [some conclude] that the intellect itself is the Self, for the I-making function is a property of the intellect.
units.iast:
ahaṃ kartāsmyahaṃ bhoktā sukhītyanubhavād api|
buddhir ātmā bhavatyeva buddhi-dharmo hyahaṅ-kṛtiḥ||

units.label: Verse 556
units.deva:
अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा विज्ञानमय इति वदति निगमः।
मनसोऽपि च भिन्नं विज्ञानमयं कर्तृ-रूपम् आत्मानम्॥
units.translation: The Veda says, “Another inner Self is made of discernment.” It is a discernment-made, agent-shaped Self, distinct even from the mind.
units.iast:
anyo’ntara ātmā vijñānamaya iti vadati nigamaḥ|
manaso’pi ca bhinnaṃ vijñānamayaṃ kartṛ-rūpam ātmānam||

units.label: Verse 557
units.deva:
विज्ञानं यज्ञं तनुते कर्माणि तनुतेऽपि च।
इत्यस्य कर्तृता श्रुत्या मुखतः प्रतिपाद्यते।
तस्माद् युक्तात्मता बुद्धेर् इति बौद्धेन निश्चितम्॥
units.translation: It performs the sacrifice and performs actions too; Śruti explicitly presents its agency. Therefore, the Buddhist concludes, it is reasonable to regard the intellect as the Self.
units.iast:
vijñānaṃ yajñaṃ tanute karmāṇi tanute’pi ca|
ityasya kartṛtā śrutyā mukhataḥ pratipādyate|
tasmād yuktātmatā buddher iti bauddhena niścitam||

units.label: Verse 558
units.deva:
प्राभाकरस् तार्किकश्च ताव् उभाव् अप्य् अमर्षया।
तन्-निश्चयं दुषयतो बुद्धिर् आत्मा कथं त्विति॥
units.translation: Both a Prābhākara and a logician, dissatisfied, criticize that conclusion: “How can the intellect be the Self?”
units.iast:
prābhākaras tārkikaśca tāv ubhāv apy amarṣayā|
tan-niścayaṃ duṣayato buddhir ātmā kathaṃ tviti||

units.label: Verse 559
units.deva:
बुद्धेर् अज्ञान-कार्यत्वाद् विनाशित्वात् प्रतिक्षणम्।
बुद्ध्यादीनां च सर्वेषाम् अज्ञाने लय-दर्शनात्॥
units.translation: The intellect is a product of ignorance and perishes moment by moment; and all things beginning with the intellect are seen to dissolve into ignorance.

gloss.en: because it is a product of ignorance
of the intellect and the rest

units.iast:
buddher ajñāna-kāryatvād vināśitvāt pratikṣaṇam|
buddhyādīnāṃ ca sarveṣām ajñāne laya-darśanāt||

units.label: Verse 560
units.deva:
अज्ञोऽहम् इत्यनुभवाद् आ-स्त्री-बालादि-गोचरात्।
भवत्यज्ञानम् एवात्मा न तु बुद्धिः कदाचन॥
units.translation: From the common experience “I am ignorant,” even among women, children, and others, [some conclude] that ignorance itself is the Self, and never the intellect.

gloss.en: within the experience of women, children, and the like

units.iast:
ajño’ham ityanubhavād ā-strī-bālādi-gocarāt|
bhavatyajñānam evātmā na tu buddhiḥ kadācana||

units.label: Verse 561
units.deva:
विज्ञानमयाद् अन्यं त्वानन्दमयं परं तथात्मानम्।
अन्योऽन्तर आत्मानन्दमय इति वदति वेदोऽपि॥
units.translation: The Veda also says that another inner Self, distinct from the vijñānamaya, is the supreme Self made of bliss.
units.iast:
vijñānamayād anyaṃ tvānandamayaṃ paraṃ tathātmānam|
anyo’ntara ātmānandamaya iti vadati vedo’pi||

units.label: Verse 562
units.deva:
दुःख-प्रत्यय-शून्यत्वाद् आनन्दमयता मता।
अज्ञाने सकलं सुप्तौ बुद्ध्यादि प्रविलीयते॥
units.translation: Because the awareness of suffering is absent, it is considered made of bliss. In sleep, everything—intellect and the rest—dissolves into ignorance.

gloss.en: because awareness of suffering is absent
the state of being made of bliss

units.iast:
duḥkha-pratyaya-śūnyatvād ānandamayatā matā|
ajñāne sakalaṃ suptau buddhyādi pravilīyate||

units.label: Verse 563
units.deva:
दुःखिनोऽपि सुषुप्त्यादाव् आनन्दमयता ततः।
सुप्तौ किञ्चिन् न जानामीत्यनुभूतिश् च दृश्यते॥
units.translation: Therefore, even a suffering person has the nature of bliss in deep sleep and the like; the experience “I knew nothing in sleep” is also observed.

gloss.en: in deep sleep and the like

units.iast:
duḥkhino’pi suṣuptyādāv ānandamayatā tataḥ|
suptau kiñcin na jānāmītyanubhūtiś ca dṛśyate||

units.label: Verse 564
units.deva:
यत एवम् अतो युक्ता ह्यज्ञानस्यात्मता ध्रुवम्।
इति तन्-निश्चयं भाट्टा दूषयन्ति स्व-युक्तिभिः॥
units.translation: Since this is so, it would surely be reasonable to conclude that ignorance is the Self. The Bhāṭṭas refute that conclusion with their own reasoning.
units.iast:
yata evam ato yuktā hyajñānasyātmatā dhruvam|
iti tan-niścayaṃ bhāṭṭā dūṣayanti sva-yuktibhiḥ||

units.label: Verse 565
units.deva:
कथम् अज्ञानम् एवात्मा ज्ञानं चाप्युपलभ्यते।
ज्ञानाभावे कथं विद्युर् अज्ञोऽहम् इति चाज्ञताम्।
अस्वाप्सं सुखम् एवाहं न जानाम्यत्र किञ्चन॥
units.translation: How can ignorance itself be the Self, when knowledge is also perceived? Without knowledge, how would one know the state of ignorance by saying “I am ignorant”? One also says, “I slept happily; I knew nothing here.”
units.iast:
katham ajñānam evātmā jñānaṃ cāpyupalabhyate|
jñānābhāve kathaṃ vidyur ajño’ham iti cājñatām|
asvāpsaṃ sukham evāhaṃ na jānāmyatra kiñcana||

units.label: Verse 566
units.deva:
इत्यज्ञानम् अपि ज्ञानं प्रबुद्धेषु प्रदृश्यते।
प्रज्ञान-घन एवानन्दमय इत्यपि श्रुतिः॥
units.translation: Thus, even ignorance is perceived as knowledge by those who have awakened. Śruti also says, “The blissful Self is indeed a mass of consciousness.”
units.iast:
ityajñānam api jñānaṃ prabuddheṣu pradṛśyate|
prajñāna-ghana evānandamaya ityapi śrutiḥ||

units.label: Verse 567
units.deva:
प्रब्रवीत्य् उभयात्मत्वम् आत्मनः स्वयम् एव हि।
आत्मातश् चिज्-जड-तनुः खद्योत इव सम्मतः॥
units.translation: Śruti itself declares the Self’s twofold nature; therefore the Self is accepted as having a conscious and inert form, like a firefly.

gloss.en: having a conscious and inert form

units.iast:
prabravīty ubhayātmatvam ātmanaḥ svayam eva hi|
ātmā ataś cit-jaḍa-tanuḥ khadyota iva sammataḥ||

units.label: Verse 568
units.deva:
न केवलाज्ञानमयो घट-कुड्यादिवज् जडः।
इति निश्चयम् एतेषां दूषयत्यपरो जडः॥
units.translation: Another dull person challenges their conclusion: if the Self were merely ignorance, it would be inert like a pot, a wall, and the like.

gloss.en: like a pot, wall, and the rest

units.iast:
na kevalājñānamayo ghaṭa-kuḍyādivaj jaḍaḥ|
iti niścayam eteṣāṃ dūṣayatyaparo jaḍaḥ||

units.label: Verse 569
units.deva:
ज्ञानाज्ञानमयस् त्वात्मा कथं भवितुम् अर्हति।
परस्-पर-विरुद्धत्वात् तेजस्-तिमिरवत् तयोः॥
units.translation: How could the Self be made of both knowledge and ignorance, since the two are mutually opposed like light and darkness?
units.iast:
jñānājñānamayas tvātmā kathaṃ bhavitum arhati|
paras-para-viruddhatvāt tejas-timiravat tayoḥ||

units.label: Verse 570
units.deva:
सामानाधिकरण्यं वा संयोगो वा समाश्रयः।
तमः-प्रकाशवज् ज्ञानाज्ञानयोर् न हि सिध्यति॥
units.translation: A common substratum, conjunction, or shared support is not established for knowledge and ignorance, just as it is not for darkness and light.
units.iast:
sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ vā saṃyogo vā samāśrayaḥ|
tamaḥ-prakāśavaj jñānājñānayor na hi sidhyati||

units.label: Verse 571
units.deva:
अज्ञानम् अपि विज्ञानं बुद्धिर् वापि च तद्-गुणाः।
सुषुप्तौ नोपलभ्यन्ते यत् किञ्चिद् अपि वापरम्॥
units.translation: In deep sleep, ignorance, consciousness, intellect, its qualities, and anything else whatsoever are not perceived.
units.iast:
ajñānam api vijñānaṃ buddhir vāpi ca tad-guṇāḥ|
suṣuptau nopalabhyante yat kiñcid api vāparam||

units.label: Verse 572
units.deva:
मात्रादि-लक्षणं किं तु शून्यमेवोपलभ्यते।
सुषुप्तौ नान्यद् अस्त्येव नाहम् अप्यासम् इत्यनु॥
units.translation: But what is marked by the measures and the like? Only emptiness is perceived. In deep sleep nothing else exists at all; afterward one says, “I too was not.”

gloss.en: marked by measure and the like

units.iast:
mātrādi-lakṣaṇaṃ kiṃ tu śūnyam evopalabhyate|
suṣuptau nānyad astyeva nāham apy āsam ity anu||

units.label: Verse 573
units.deva:
सुप्तोत्थित-जनैः सर्वैः शून्यम् एवानुस्मर्यते।
यत् ततः शून्यम् एवात्मा न ज्ञानाज्ञान-लक्षणः॥
units.translation: Everyone who awakens from sleep remembers only emptiness. Therefore, they say, the Self is emptiness alone, not characterized by knowledge or ignorance.
units.iast:
suptotthita-janaiḥ sarvaiḥ śūnyam evānusmaryate|
yat tataḥ śūnyam evātmā na jñānājñāna-lakṣaṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 574
units.deva:
वेदेनाप्यसद् एवेदम् अग्र आसीद् इति स्फुटम्।
निरुच्यते यतस् तस्माच् छून्यस्यैवात्मता मता॥
units.translation: The Veda clearly says, “In the beginning, all this was non-being.” Therefore, they hold that selfhood belongs to emptiness alone.
units.iast:
vedenāpyasad evedam agra āsīd iti sphuṭam|
nirucyate yatas tasmāc chūnyasyaivātmatā matā||

units.label: Verse 575
units.deva:
असन्न् एव घटः पूर्वं जायमानः प्रदृश्यते।
न हि कुम्भः पुरैवान्तः स्थित्वोदेति बहिर्-मुखः॥
units.translation: A pot, when it comes into being, is seen as previously non-existent. For a pot does not rise outward after having already existed inside.
units.iast:
asann eva ghaṭaḥ pūrvaṃ jāyamānaḥ pradṛśyate|
na hi kumbhaḥ puraivāntaḥ sthitvodeti bahir-mukhaḥ||

units.label: Verse 576
units.deva:
यत् तस्माद् असतः सर्वं सद् इदं समजायत।
ततः सर्वात्मना शून्यस्यैवात्मत्वं समर्हति॥
units.translation: Since all this existent [world] arose from non-being, they conclude that selfhood must belong entirely to emptiness.
units.iast:
yat tasmād asataḥ sarvaṃ sad idaṃ samajāyata|
tataḥ sarvātmanā śūnyasyaivātmatvaṃ samarhati||

units.label: Verse 577
units.deva:
इत्येवं पण्डितं-मन्यैः परस्-पर-विरोधिभिः।
तत्-तन्-मतानुरूपाल्प-श्रुति-युक्त्यनुभूतिभिः॥
units.translation: Thus self-styled scholars, contradicting one another, rely on scant passages of scripture, reasoning, and experience that fit each particular doctrine.

gloss.en: by those who regard themselves as learned

units.iast:
ityevaṃ paṇḍitaṃ-manyaiḥ paras-para-virodhibhiḥ|
tat-tan-matānurūpālpa-śruti-yuktyanubhūtibhiḥ||

units.label: Verse 578
units.deva:
निर्णीत-मत-जातानि खण्डितान्येव पण्डितैः।
श्रुतिभिश् चाप्यनुभवैर् बाधकैः प्रतिवादिनाम्॥
units.translation: The doctrines that have been settled are indeed refuted by learned people, using Śruti and experiences that counter the disputants.
units.iast:
nirṇīta-mata-jātāni khaṇḍitānyeva paṇḍitaiḥ|
śrutibhiś cāpyanubhavair bādhakaiḥ prativādinām||

units.label: Verse 579
units.deva:
यतस् तस्मात् तु पुत्रादेः शून्यान्तस्य विशेषतः।
सुसाधितम् अनात्मत्वं श्रुति-युक्त्यनुभूतिभिः॥
units.translation: Therefore, the non-Selfhood of everything from the son and the like up to emptiness is well established by Śruti, reasoning, and experience.

gloss.en: of the son and the like

units.iast:
yatas tasmāt tu putrādeḥ śūnyāntasya viśeṣataḥ|
susādhitam anātmatvaṃ śruti-yuktyanubhūtibhiḥ||

units.label: Verse 580
units.deva:
न हि प्रमाणान्तर-बाधितस्य
याथार्थ्यम् अङ्गी-क्रियते महद्भिः।
पुत्रादि-शून्यान्तम् अनात्म-तत्त्वम्
इत्येव विस्पष्टम् अतः सुजातम्॥
units.translation: The learned do not accept as real what is contradicted by another means of valid knowledge. Thus it is clear that everything from the son through emptiness is the nature of non-Self.

gloss.en: of what is contradicted by another means of valid knowledge

units.iast:
na hi pramāṇāntara-bādhitasya
yāthārthyam aṅgī-kriyate mahadbhiḥ|
putrādi-śūnyāntam anātma-tattvam
ityeva vispaṣṭam ataḥ sujātam||

units.label: Verse 581
units.deva:
सुषुप्ति-काले सकले विलीने
शून्यं विना नान्यद् इहोपलभ्यते।
शून्यं त्वनात्मा न ततः परः को
ऽप्यात्माभिधानस् त्वनुभूयतेऽर्थः॥
units.translation: At the time of deep sleep, when everything has dissolved, nothing other than emptiness is experienced here. But emptiness is non-Self; beyond it, no entity called the Self is experienced.

gloss.en: at the time of deep sleep

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
suṣupti-kāle sakale vilīne
śūnyaṃ vinā nānyad ihopalabhyate|
śūnyaṃ tvanātmā na tataḥ paraḥ ko
’pyātmābhidhānas tvanubhūyate’rthaḥ||

units.label: Verse 582
units.deva:
यद्यस्ति चात्मा किमु नोपलभ्यते
सुप्तौ यथा तिष्ठति किं प्रमाणम्।
किं-लक्षणोऽसौ स कथं न बाध्यते
प्रबाध्यमानेष्वहम्-आदिषु स्वयम्॥
units.translation: If the Self exists, why is it not perceived? What proof shows how it remains in sleep? What is its characteristic, and how is it not negated when “I” and the rest are themselves negated?
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
yadyasti cātmā kimu nopalabhyate
suptau yathā tiṣṭhati kiṃ pramāṇam|
kiṃ-lakṣaṇo’sau sa kathaṃ na bādhyate
prabādhyamāneṣvaham-ādiṣu svayam||

units.label: Verse 583
units.deva:
एतत् संशय-जातं मे हृदय-ग्रन्थि-लक्षणम्।
छिन्धि युक्ति-महा-खड्ग-धारया कृपया गुरो॥
units.translation: Out of compassion, O teacher, cut this whole mass of doubts, which is like a knot in my heart, with the edge of the great sword of reasoning.

gloss.en: having the character of a knot in the heart
with the edge of the great sword of reasoning

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
etat saṃśaya-jātaṃ me hṛdaya-granthi-lakṣaṇam|
chindhi yukti-mahā-khaḍga-dhārayā kṛpayā guro||

units.label: Verse 584
units.deva:
अतिसूक्ष्मतरः प्रश्नस् तवायं सदृशो मतः।
सूक्ष्मार्थ-दर्शनं सूक्ष्म-बुद्धिष्वेव प्रदृश्यते॥
units.translation: Your question is considered exceedingly subtle and fitting. Insight into a subtle meaning is seen only in subtle intellects.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
atisūkṣmataraḥ praśnas tavāyaṃ sadṛśo mataḥ|
sūkṣmārtha-darśanaṃ sūkṣma-buddhiṣveva pradṛśyate||

units.label: Verse 585
units.deva:
शृणु वक्ष्यामि सकलं यद् यत् पृष्टं त्वयाधुना।
रहस्यं परमं सूक्ष्मं ज्ञातव्यं च मुमुक्षुभिः॥
units.translation: Listen: I will explain everything you have asked just now—the supreme, subtle secret that seekers of liberation should know.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
śṛṇu vakṣyāmi sakalaṃ yad yat pṛṣṭaṃ tvayādhunā|
rahasyaṃ paramaṃ sūkṣmaṃ jñātavyaṃ ca mumukṣubhiḥ||

units.label: Verse 586
units.deva:
बुद्ध्यादि सकलं सुप्ताव् अनुलीनं स्व-कारणे।
अव्यक्ते वटवद् बीजे तिष्ठत्यविकृतात्मना॥
units.translation: In sleep, everything beginning with the intellect dissolves into its own cause. It remains in the unmanifest, unchanged, like a banyan tree in a seed.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
buddhyādi sakalaṃ suptāv anulīnaṃ sva-kāraṇe|
avyakte vaṭavad bīje tiṣṭhatyavikṛtātmanā||

units.label: Verse 587
units.deva:
तिष्ठत्येव स्व-रूपेण न तु शून्यायते जगत्।
क्वचिद् अङ्कुर-रूपेण क्वचिद् बीजात्मना वटः।
कार्य-कारण-रूपेण यथा तिष्ठत्यदस् तथा॥
units.translation: The world remains in its own form; it does not become void. As a banyan exists sometimes in the form of a sprout and sometimes in the nature of a seed, so it remains in the forms of cause and effect.

gloss.en: in the form of a sprout
in the nature of a seed
in the forms of effect and cause

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
tiṣṭhatyeva sva-rūpeṇa na tu śūnyāyate jagat|
kvacid aṅkura-rūpeṇa kvacid bījātmanā vaṭaḥ|
kārya-kāraṇa-rūpeṇa yathā tiṣṭhatyadas tathā||

units.label: Verse 588
units.deva:
अव्याकृतात्मनावस्थां जगतो वदति श्रुतिः।
सुषुप्त्यादिषु तद्-भेदं तर्ह्यव्याकृतम् इत्यसौ॥
units.translation: Śruti describes the world as having an unmanifest state. In deep sleep and the like, its differentiation is then called unmanifest.

gloss.en: in deep sleep and the like

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
avyākṛtātmanāvasthāṃ jagato vadati śrutiḥ|
suṣuptyādiṣu tad-bhedaṃ tarhyavyākṛtam ityasau||

units.label: Verse 589
units.deva:
इमम् अर्थम् अविज्ञाय निर्णीतं श्रुति-युक्तिभिः।
जगतो दर्शनं शून्यम् इति प्राहुर् अतद्-विदः॥
units.translation: Not understanding this point, those who do not know the truth say that the world’s appearance—though determined by Śruti and reasoning—is emptiness.

gloss.en: those who do not know that truth

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
imam artham avijñāya nirṇītaṃ śruti-yuktibhiḥ|
jagato darśanaṃ śūnyam iti prāhur atad-vidaḥ||

units.label: Verse 590
units.deva:
नासतः सत उत्पत्तिः श्रूयते न च दृश्यते।
उदेति नर-शृङ्गात् किं ख-पुष्पात् किं भविष्यति॥
units.translation: The production of being from non-being is neither heard of nor seen. Does anything arise from a man’s horn? What could come from a sky-flower?
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
nāsataḥ sata utpattiḥ śrūyate na ca dṛśyate|
udeti nara-śṛṅgāt kiṃ kha-puṣpāt kiṃ bhaviṣyati||

units.label: Verse 591
units.deva:
प्रभवति न हि कुम्भोऽविद्यमानो मृदश्चेत्
प्रभवतु सिकताया वाथवा वारिणो वा।
न हि भवति च ताभ्यां सर्वथा क्वापि तस्माद्
यत उदयति योऽर्थोऽस्त्यत्र तस्य स्वभावः॥
units.translation: A pot that is absent from clay does not come into being; if it could, let it arise from sand or water. But it never arises from either. Therefore, an object has the nature of that from which it arises.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
prabhavati na hi kumbho’vidyamāno mṛdaścet
prabhavatu sikatāyā vāthavā vāriṇo vā|
na hi bhavati ca tābhyāṃ sarvathā kvāpi tasmād
yata udayati yo’rtho’styatra tasya svabhāvaḥ||

units.label: Verse 592
units.deva:
अन्यथा विपरीतं स्यात् कार्य-कारण-लक्षणम्।
नियतं सर्व-शास्त्रेषु सर्व-लोकेषु सर्वतः॥
units.translation: Otherwise the established nature of cause and effect, fixed in all scriptures and worlds everywhere, would be reversed.

gloss.en: the nature of cause and effect

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
anyathā viparītaṃ syāt kārya-kāraṇa-lakṣaṇam|
niyataṃ sarva-śāstreṣu sarva-lokeṣu sarvataḥ||

units.label: Verse 593
units.deva:
कथम् असतः सज् जायेतेति श्रुत्या निषिध्यते तस्मात्।
असतः सज्-जननं नो घटते मिथ्यैव शून्य-शब्दार्थः॥
units.translation: Śruti rejects this by asking, “How can being arise from non-being?” Therefore, being cannot be produced from non-being; the meaning of the word “void” is simply false.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
katham asataḥ saj jāyeteti śrutyā niṣidhyate tasmāt|
asataḥ saj-jananaṃ no ghaṭate mithyaiva śūnya-śabdārthaḥ||

units.label: Verse 594
units.deva:
अव्यक्त-शब्दिते प्राज्ञे सत्यात्मन्यत्र जाग्रति।
कथं सिध्यति शून्यत्वं तस्य भ्रान्ति-शिरो-मणे॥
units.translation: When the real Self, called the unmanifest Prājña, is present here, how can its being void be established, O crown jewel of delusion?
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
avyakta-śabdite prājñe satyātmanyatra jāgrati|
kathaṃ sidhyati śūnyatvaṃ tasya bhrānti-śiro-maṇe||

units.label: Verse 595
units.deva:
सुषुप्तौ शून्यम् एवेति केन पुंसा तवेरितम्।
हेतुनानुमितं केन कथं ज्ञातं त्वयोच्यताम्॥
units.translation: Who has said to you that only emptiness exists in deep sleep? By what reason was it inferred, and how was it known? Tell me.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
suṣuptau śūnyam eveti kena puṃsā taveritam|
hetunānumitaṃ kena kathaṃ jñātaṃ tvayocyatām||

units.label: Verse 596
units.deva:
इति पृष्टो मूढतमो वदिष्यति किम् उत्तरम्।
नैवानुरूपकं लिङ्गं वक्ता वा नास्ति कश्चन।
सुषुप्ति-स्थित-शून्यस्य बोद्धा कोन्वात्मनः परः॥
units.translation: When asked this, what answer could the most deluded person give? There is no fitting sign, nor is there anyone to speak. Who other than the Self knows the emptiness present in deep sleep?
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
iti pṛṣṭo mūḍhatamo vadiṣyati kim uttaram|
naivānurūpakaṃ liṅgaṃ vaktā vā nāsti kaścana|
suṣupti-sthita-śūnyasya boddhā konvātmanaḥ paraḥ||

units.label: Verse 597
units.deva:
स्वेनानुभूतं स्वयम् एव वक्ति
स्व-सुप्ति-काले स्थित-शून्य-भावम्।
तत्र स्व-सत्ताम् अनवेक्ष्य मूढः
स्वस्यापि शून्यत्वम् अयं ब्रवीति॥
units.translation: This deluded person reports what he experienced himself: the state of emptiness present during his sleep. Not seeing his own existence there, he says that even he himself was void.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
svenānubhūtaṃ svayam eva vakti
sva-supti-kāle sthita-śūnya-bhāvam|
tatra sva-sattām anavekṣya mūḍhaḥ
svasyāpi śūnyatvam ayaṃ bravīti||

units.label: Verse 598
units.deva:
अवेद्यमानः स्वयम् अन्य-लोकैः
सौषुप्तिकं धर्मम् अवैति साक्षात्।
बुद्ध्याद्यभावस्य च योऽत्र बोद्धा
स एष आत्मा खलु निर्विकारः॥
units.translation: Though not known by other people, he directly knows the state belonging to deep sleep. Whoever knows here the absence of intellect and the rest is indeed this changeless Self.

gloss.en: of the absence of intellect and the rest

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
avedyamānaḥ svayam anya-lokaiḥ
sauṣuptikaṃ dharmam avaiti sākṣāt|
buddhyādyabhāvasya ca yo’tra boddhā
sa eṣa ātmā khalu nirvikāraḥ||

units.label: Verse 599
units.deva:
यस्येदं सकलं विभाति महसा तस्य स्वयं-ज्योतिषः
सूर्यस्येव किम् अस्ति भासकम् इह प्रज्ञादि सर्वं जडम्।
न ह्यर्कस्य विभासकं क्षिति-तले दृष्टं तथैवात्मनो
नान्यः कोऽप्यनुभासकोऽनुभविता नातः परः कश्चन॥
units.translation: By whose power all this shines, what could illuminate that self-luminous Self, like the sun? The intellect and everything else are inert. No illuminator of the sun is seen on earth; likewise, no other illuminator or experiencer of the Self exists, nor anyone higher.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
yasyedaṃ sakalaṃ vibhāti mahasā tasya svayaṃ-jyotiṣaḥ
sūryasyeva kim asti bhāsakam iha prajñādi sarvaṃ jaḍam|
na hyarkasya vibhāsakaṃ kṣiti-tale dṛṣṭaṃ tathaivātmano
nānyaḥ ko’pyanubhāsako’nubhavitā nātaḥ paraḥ kaścana||

units.label: Verse 600
units.deva:
येनानुभूयते सर्वं जाग्रत्-स्वप्न-सुषुप्तिषु।
विज्ञातारम् इमं को नु कथं वेदितुम् अर्हति॥
units.translation: By whom everything is experienced in waking, dream, and deep sleep—who could know this knower, and how?

gloss.en: in waking, dream, and deep sleep

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
yenānubhūyate sarvaṃ jāgrat-svapna-suṣuptiṣu|
vijñātāram imaṃ ko nu kathaṃ veditum arhati||

units.label: Verse 601
units.deva:
सर्वस्य दाहको वह्निर् वह्नेर् नान्योऽस्ति दाहकः।
यथा तथात्मनो ज्ञातुर् ज्ञाता कोऽपि न दृश्यते॥
units.translation: Fire burns everything; there is no other burner of fire. Likewise, no knower of the knower—the Self—is seen.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
sarvasya dāhako vahnir vahner nānyo’sti dāhakaḥ|
yathā tathātmano jñātur jñātā ko’pi na dṛśyate||

units.label: Verse 602
units.deva:
उपलभ्येत केनायं ह्युपलब्धा स्वयं ततः।
उपलब्ध्यन्तराभावान् नायम् आत्मोपलभ्यते॥
units.translation: By whom could this be apprehended? It is itself the apprehender. Therefore, because there is no other cognition, the Self is not apprehended as an object.

gloss.en: because there is no other cognition

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
upalabhyeta kenāyaṃ hyupalabdhā svayaṃ tataḥ|
upalabdhyantarābhāvān nāyam ātmopalabhyate||

units.label: Verse 603
units.deva:
बुद्ध्यादि-वेद्य-विलयाद् अयम् एक एव
सुप्तौ न पश्यति शृणोति न वेत्ति किञ्चित्।
सौषुप्तिकस्य तमसः स्वयम् एव साक्षी
भूत्वात्र तिष्ठति सुखेन च निर्विकल्पः॥
units.translation: When objects known by the intellect and the rest dissolve, this one alone in sleep neither sees, hears, nor knows anything. Having become the witness of the darkness of deep sleep, it remains here happily, free of distinctions.

gloss.en: when objects known by the intellect and the rest dissolve

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
buddhyādi-vedya-vilayād ayam eka eva
suptau na paśyati śṛṇoti na vetti kiñcit|
sauṣuptikasya tamasaḥ svayam eva sākṣī
bhūtvātra tiṣṭhati sukhena ca nirvikalpaḥ||

units.label: Verse 604
units.deva:
सुषुप्तावात्म-सद्-भावे प्रमाणं पण्डितोत्तमाः।
विदुः स्व-प्रत्यभिज्ञानम् आ-बाल-वृद्ध-सम्मतम्॥
units.translation: The foremost wise know self-recognition, accepted by everyone from child to elder, as evidence for the Self’s existence in deep sleep.

gloss.en: for the existence of the Self
accepted by all, from child to elder

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
suṣuptāvātma-sad-bhāve pramāṇaṃ paṇḍitottamāḥ|
viduḥ sva-pratyabhijñānam ā-bāla-vṛddha-sammatam||

units.label: Verse 605
units.deva:
प्रत्यभिज्ञायमानत्वं लिङ्गमत्रानुमापकम्।
स्मर्यमाणस्य सद्भावः सुखमस्वाप्समित्ययम्॥
units.translation: Being recognized is the inferential sign here: what is remembered must have existed—“I slept happily.”
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
pratyabhijñāyamānatvaṃ liṅgam atra anumāpakam|
smaryamāṇasya sad-bhāvaḥ sukham asvāpsam ityayam||

units.label: Verse 606
units.deva:
पुरानुभूतो नो चेत् तु स्मृतेर् अनुदयो भवेत्।
इत्यादि-तर्क-युक्तिश्च सद्-भावे मानम् आत्मनः॥
units.translation: If it had not been experienced before, memory would not arise. This and similar reasoning is evidence for the Self’s existence.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
purānubhūto no cet tu smṛter anudayo bhavet|
ityādi-tarka-yuktiśca sad-bhāve mānam ātmanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 607
units.deva:
यत्रात्मनोऽकामयितृत्व-बुद्धिः
स्वप्नानवेक्षापि च तत् सुषुप्तम्।
इत्यात्म-सद्-भाव उदीर्यतेऽत्र
श्रुत्यापि तस्माच् छ्रुतिर् अत्र मानम्॥
units.translation: Deep sleep is the state in which there is awareness of the Self’s absence of desire and also no observation of dreams. Thus Śruti declares the Self’s existence here, so Śruti is evidence.

gloss.en: the awareness of absence of desire

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
yatrātmano’kāmayitṛtva-buddhiḥ
svapnānavekṣāpi ca tat suṣuptam|
ityātma-sad-bhāva udīryate’tra
śrutyāpi tasmāc chrutir atra mānam||

units.label: Verse 608
units.deva:
अकामयितृता स्वप्नादर्शनं घटते कथम्।
अविद्यमानस्य तत आत्मास्तित्वं प्रतीयते॥
units.translation: How could the absence of desire and of dreams occur if the Self were nonexistent? From this, the Self’s existence is inferred.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
akāmayitṛtā svapnādarśanaṃ ghaṭate katham|
avidyamānasya tata ātmāstitvaṃ pratīyate||

units.label: Verse 609
units.deva:
एतैः प्रमाणैर् अस्तीति ज्ञातः साक्षितया बुधैः।
आत्मायं केवलः शुद्धः सच्-चिद्-आनन्द-लक्षणः॥
units.translation: Through these means of knowledge, the wise know that this Self exists as the witness: alone, pure, and characterized by being, consciousness, and bliss.

gloss.en: characterized by being, consciousness, and bliss

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
etaiḥ pramāṇair astīti jñātaḥ sākṣitayā budhaiḥ|
ātmāyaṃ kevalaḥ śuddhaḥ sac-cid-ānanda-lakṣaṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 610
units.deva:
सत्त्व-चित्त्वानन्दतादि लक्षणं प्रत्यग्-आत्मनः।
काल-त्रयेऽप्यबाध्यत्वं सत्त्वं नित्य-स्वरूपतः॥
units.translation: Being, consciousness, bliss, and the like characterize the inward Self. Its existence is never negated in any of the three times, because its nature is eternal.

gloss.en: being, consciousness, bliss, and the like

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
sattva-cittvānandatādi lakṣaṇaṃ pratyag-ātmanaḥ|
kāla-traye’pyabādhyatvaṃ sattvaṃ nitya-svarūpataḥ||

units.label: Verse 611
units.deva:
शुद्ध-चैतन्य-रूपत्वं चित्त्वं ज्ञान-स्वरूपतः।
अखण्ड-सुख-रूपत्वाद् आनन्दत्वम् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: Its nature as pure consciousness is called consciousness because its essence is knowledge. Because it is undivided happiness, it is said to be bliss.

gloss.en: having the form of pure consciousness

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
śuddha-caitanya-rūpatvaṃ cittvaṃ jñāna-svarūpataḥ|
akhaṇḍa-sukha-rūpatvād ānandatvam itīryate||

units.label: Verse 612
units.deva:
अनुस्यूतात्मनः सत्ता जाग्रत्-स्वप्न-सुषुप्तिषु।
अहम् अस्मीत्यतो नित्यो भवत्यात्मायम् अव्ययः॥
units.translation: The existence of the continuous Self runs through waking, dream, and deep sleep. From the cognition “I am,” this Self is eternal and undecaying.

gloss.en: in waking, dream, and deep sleep

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
anusyūtātmanaḥ sattā jāgrat-svapna-suṣuptiṣu|
aham asmītyato nityo bhavatyātmāyam avyayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 613
units.deva:
सर्वदाप्यासम् इत्येवाभिन्न-प्रत्यय ईक्ष्यते।
कदापि नासम् इत्यस्माद् आत्मनो नित्यता मता॥
units.translation: The undivided cognition “I have always existed” is seen. Since no one ever thinks “I did not exist,” the Self is held to be eternal.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
sarvadāpyāsam ityevābhinna-pratyaya īkṣyate|
kadāpi nāsam ityasmād ātmano nityatā matā||

units.label: Verse 614
units.deva:
आयातासु गतासु शैशव-मुखावस्थासु जाग्रन्-मुखास्व्
अन्यास्वप्यखिलासु वृत्तिषु धियो दुष्टास्वदुष्टास्वपि।
गङ्गा-भङ्ग-परम्परासु जलवत् सत्तानुवृत्तात्मनस्
तिष्ठत्येव सदा स्थिरा अहमहमित्येकात्मता साक्षिणः॥
units.translation: As states beginning with infancy and all other states of mind—waking and the rest, faulty or not—come and go, the stable oneness of the witness, “I, I,” always remains, like water amid successive waves of the Ganges.

gloss.en: in successive waves of the Ganges
of the Self whose existence continues

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
āyātāsu gatāsu śaiśava-mukhāvasthāsu jāgran-mukhāsv
anyāsvapyakhilāsu vṛttiṣu dhiyo duṣṭāsvaduṣṭāsvapi|
gaṅgā-bhaṅga-paramparāsu jalavat sattānuvṛttātmanas
tiṣṭhatyeva sadā sthirā aham aham ity ekātmatā sākṣiṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 615
units.deva:
प्रतिपदम् अहम्-आदयो विभिन्नाः
क्षण-परिणामितया विकारिणस् ते।
न परिणतिर् अमुष्य निष्कलत्वाद्
अयम् अविकार्य् अत एव नित्य आत्मा॥
units.translation: The “I” and other changing states are distinct at every moment. This Self undergoes no transformation because it is partless; therefore the Self is changeless and eternal.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
pratipadam aham-ādayo vibhinnāḥ
kṣaṇa-pariṇāmitayā vikāriṇas te|
na pariṇatir amuṣya niṣkalatvād
ayam avikāry ata eva nitya ātmā||

units.label: Verse 616
units.deva:
यः स्वप्नम् अद्राक्षम् अहं सुखं यो
ऽस्वाप्सं स एवास्म्यथ जागरूकः।
इत्येवम् अच्छिन्नतयानुभूयते
सत्तात्मनो नास्ति हि संशयोऽत्र॥
units.translation: “I who saw a dream, who slept happily, am that same one now awake.” The Self’s existence is experienced without interruption; there is no doubt about it.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
yaḥ svapnam adrākṣam ahaṃ sukhaṃ yo
’svāpsaṃ sa evāsmyatha jāgarūkaḥ|
ityevam acchinnatayānubhūyate
sattātmano nāsti hi saṃśayo’tra||

units.label: Verse 617
units.deva:
श्रुत्युक्ताः षोडश-कलाश् चिद्-आभासस्य नात्मनः।
निष्कलत्वान् नास्य लयस् तस्मान् नित्यत्वम् आत्मनः॥
units.translation: The sixteen parts stated in Śruti belong to reflected consciousness, not to the Self. Because the Self is partless, it does not dissolve; therefore it is eternal.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
śrutyuktāḥ ṣoḍaśa-kalāś cid-ābhāsasya nātmanaḥ|
niṣkalatvān nāsya layas tasmān nityatvam ātmanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 618
units.deva:
जड-प्रकाशकः सूर्यः प्रकाशात्मैव नो जडः।
बुद्ध्यादि-भासकस् तस्माच् चित्-स्वरूपस् तथा मतः॥
units.translation: The sun illumines inert things and is itself light-natured, not inert. Likewise, because it illumines the intellect and the rest, the Self is held to be consciousness-natured.

gloss.en: the illuminer of the intellect and the rest

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
jaḍa-prakāśakaḥ sūryaḥ prakāśātmaiva no jaḍaḥ|
buddhyādi-bhāsakas tasmāc cit-svarūpas tathā mataḥ||

units.label: Verse 619
units.deva:
कुड्यादेः तु जडस्य नैव घटते भानं स्वतः सर्वदा
सूर्यादि-प्रभया विना क्वचिद् अपि प्रत्यक्षम् एतत् तथा।
बुद्ध्यादेर् अपि न स्वतोऽस्त्यणुर् अपि स्फूर्तिर् विनैवात्मना
सोऽयं केवल-चिन्मय-श्रुति-मतो भानुर् यथा रुङ्मयः॥
units.translation: An inert thing such as a wall never shines by itself; plainly it needs sunlight or other light. Likewise, the intellect and the rest have not even the slightest manifestation without the Self. According to Śruti, this Self is made only of consciousness, as the sun is made of radiance.

gloss.en: of a wall and the like
by the light of the sun and the like
of the intellect and the rest

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
kuḍyādeḥ tu jaḍasya naiva ghaṭate bhānaṃ svataḥ sarvadā
sūryādi-prabhayā vinā kvacid api pratyakṣam etat tathā|
buddhyāder api na svato’styaṇur api sphūrtir vinaivātmanā
so’yaṃ kevala-cinmaya-śruti-mato bhānur yathā ruṅmayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 620
units.deva:
स्व-भासने वान्य-पदार्थ-भासने
नार्कः प्रकाशान्तरम् ईषद् इच्छति।
स्व-बोधने वाप्यहम्-आदि-बोधने
तथैव चिद्-धातुर् अयं परात्मा॥
units.translation: For shining by itself or illuminating other objects, the sun needs not the slightest other light. Likewise, this supreme Self, the substance of consciousness, needs none either to know itself or to make the “I” and the rest known.

gloss.en: for knowing the “I” and the rest

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
sva-bhāsane vānya-padārtha-bhāsane
nārkaḥ prakāśāntaram īṣad icchati|
sva-bodhane vāpyaham-ādi-bodhane
tathaiva cid-dhātur ayaṃ parātmā||

units.label: Verse 621
units.deva:
अन्य-प्रकाशं न किम् अप्यपेक्ष्य
यतोऽयम् आभाति निजात्मनैव।
ततः स्वयं-ज्योतिर् अयं चिद्-आत्मा
न ह्यात्म-भाने पर-दीप्त्यपेक्षा॥
units.translation: This consciousness shines by its own nature without depending on any other light. Therefore it is self-luminous; no other light is needed for the Self to shine.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
anya-prakāśaṃ na kim apyapekṣya
yato’yam ābhāti nijātmanaiva|
tataḥ svayaṃ-jyotir ayaṃ cid-ātmā
na hyātma-bhāne para-dīptyapekṣā||

units.label: Verse 622
units.deva:
यं न प्रकाशयति किञ्चिद् इनोऽपि चन्द्रः
नो विद्युतः किम् उत वह्निर् अयं मिताभः।
यं भान्तम् एतम् अनुभाति जगत् समस्तं
सोऽयं स्वयं स्फुरति सर्व-दशासु चात्मा॥
units.translation: The sun, moon, lightning, and—what need be said—even this faint fire do not illumine that Self. When it shines, the whole world shines after it; this Self shines by itself in every state.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
yaṃ na prakāśayati kiñcid ino’pi candraḥ
no vidyutaḥ kim uta vahnir ayaṃ mitābhaḥ|
yaṃ bhāntam etam anubhāti jagat samastaṃ
so’yaṃ svayaṃ sphurati sarva-daśāsu cātmā||

units.label: Verse 623
units.deva:
आत्मनः सुख-रूपत्वाद् आनन्दत्वं स्व-लक्षणम्।
पर-प्रेमास्पदत्वेन सुख-रूपत्वम् आत्मनः॥
units.translation: Because the Self is happiness in nature, bliss is its own defining mark. Because it is the object of supreme love, the Self is happiness in nature.

gloss.en: because it is happiness in nature
because it is the object of supreme love

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
ātmanaḥ sukha-rūpatvād ānandatvaṃ sva-lakṣaṇam|
para-premāspadatvena sukha-rūpatvam ātmanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 624
units.deva:
सुख-हेतुषु सर्वेषां प्रीतिः सावधिर् ईक्ष्यते।
कदापि नावधिः प्रीतेः स्वात्मनि प्राणिनां क्वचित्॥
units.translation: For all people, affection for things that bring happiness is seen to have a limit. But the affection of living beings for their own Self has no limit anywhere or at any time.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
sukha-hetuṣu sarveṣāṃ prītiḥ sāvadhir īkṣyate|
kadāpi nāvadhiḥ prīteḥ svātmani prāṇināṃ kvacit||

units.label: Verse 625
units.deva:
क्षीणेन्द्रियस्य जीर्णस्य सम्प्राप्तोत्क्रमणस्य वा।
अस्ति जीवितुम् एवाशा स्वात्मा प्रियतमो यतः॥
units.translation: Even for one whose senses are weakened, who is aged, or who has reached the point of departure, there is still a wish to live, because one’s own Self is dearest.

gloss.en: of one whose senses are weakened
of one who has reached the point of departure

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
kṣīṇendriyasya jīrṇasya samprāptotkramaṇasya vā|
asti jīvitum evāśā svātmā priyatamo yataḥ||

units.label: Verse 626
units.deva:
आत्मातः परम-प्रेमास्पदः सर्व-शरीरिणाम्।
यस्य शेषतया सर्वम् उपादेयत्वम् ऋच्छति॥
units.translation: Therefore the Self is the greatest object of love for all embodied beings; everything else becomes worth taking up only as subordinate to it.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
ātmātaḥ parama-premāspadaḥ sarva-śarīriṇām|
yasya śeṣatayā sarvam upādeyatvam ṛcchati||

units.label: Verse 627
units.deva:
एष एव प्रियतमः पुत्राद् अपि धनाद् अपि।
अन्यस्माद् अपि सर्वस्माद् आत्मायं परमान्तरः॥
units.translation: This Self alone is dearest—more than a son, more than wealth, more than anything else. This Self is the innermost of all.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
eṣa eva priyatamaḥ putrād api dhanād api|
anyasmād api sarvasmād ātmāyaṃ paramāntaraḥ||

units.label: Verse 628
units.deva:
प्रियत्वेन मतं यत् तु तत् सदा नाप्रियं नृणाम्।
विपत्तावपि सम्पत्तौ यथात्मा न तथापरः॥
units.translation: What is regarded as dear is not always dear to people. In adversity or prosperity, no other thing is like the Self.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
priyatvena mataṃ yat tu tat sadā nāpriyaṃ nṛṇām|
vipattāvapi sampattau yathātmā na tathāparaḥ||

units.label: Verse 629
units.deva:
आत्मा खलु प्रियतमोऽसु-भृतां यदर्था
भार्यात्मजाप्त-गृह-वित्त-मुखाः पदार्थाः।
वाणिज्य-कर्षण-गवावन-राजसेवा-
भैषज्यक-प्रभृतयो विविधाः क्रियाश्च॥
units.translation: The Self is indeed dearest to living beings. Things such as wife, children, friends, home, and wealth are for its sake; so too are activities such as trade, farming, tending cattle, serving the king, and medicine.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
ātmā khalu priyatamo’su-bhṛtāṃ yadarthā
bhāryātmajāpta-gṛha-vitta-mukhāḥ padārthāḥ|
vāṇijya-karṣaṇa-gavāvana-rājasevā-
bhaiṣajyaka-prabhṛtayo vividhāḥ kriyāśca||

units.label: Verse 630
units.deva:
प्रवृत्तिश्च निवृत्तिश्च यच्च यावच् च चेष्टितम्।
आत्मार्थम् एव नान्यार्थं नातः प्रियतमः परः॥
units.translation: Every engagement and withdrawal, and every action one undertakes, is for the sake of the Self alone, not for another purpose. Nothing is dearer than the Self.

gloss.en: for the sake of the Self

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
pravṛttiśca nivṛttiśca yacca yāvac ca ceṣṭitam|
ātmārtham eva nānyārthaṃ nātaḥ priyatamaḥ paraḥ||

units.label: Verse 631
units.deva:
तस्माद् आत्मा केवलानन्द-रूपो
यः सर्वस्माद् वस्तुनः प्रेष्ठ उक्तः।
यो वा अस्मान् मन्यतेऽन्यं प्रियं यं
सोऽयं तस्माच् छोकम् एवानुभुङ्क्ते॥
units.translation: Therefore the Self is said to be the form of undivided bliss, and dearest of all things. Whoever considers something other than the Self to be dear experiences only sorrow from that.

gloss.en: of the form of undivided bliss

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
tasmād ātmā kevalānanda-rūpo
yaḥ sarvasmād vastunaḥ preṣṭha uktaḥ|
yo vā asmān manyate’nyaṃ priyaṃ yaṃ
so’yaṃ tasmāc chokam evānubhuṅkte||

units.label: Verse 632
units.deva:
अपरः क्रियते प्रश्नो मयायं क्षम्यतां प्रभो।
अज्ञ-वाग् अपराधाय कल्पते न महात्मनाम्॥
units.translation: I ask another question; please forgive me, Lord. The speech of the ignorant does not become an offense to great-souled people.

gloss.en: the speech of an ignorant person

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
aparaḥ kriyate praśno mayāyaṃ kṣamyatāṃ prabho|
ajña-vāg aparādhāya kalpate na mahātmanām||

units.label: Verse 633
units.deva:
आत्मान्यः सुखम् अन्यच् च नात्मनः सुख-रूपता।
आत्मनः सुखम् आशास्यं यतते सकलो जनः॥
units.translation: The Self is one thing and happiness another; the Self is not happiness in nature. Yet everyone strives, hoping for happiness from the Self.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
ātmānyaḥ sukham anyac ca nātmanaḥ sukha-rūpatā|
ātmanaḥ sukham āśāsyaṃ yatate sakalo janaḥ||

units.label: Verse 634
units.deva:
आत्मनः सुख-रूपत्वे प्रयत्नः किमु देहिनाम्।
एष मे संशयः स्वामिन् कृपयैव निरस्यताम्॥
units.translation: If the Self is happiness in nature, why do embodied beings strive? Lord, please dispel this doubt of mine through your compassion.

gloss.en: if it is happiness in nature

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
ātmanaḥ sukha-rūpatve prayatnaḥ kimu dehinām|
eṣa me saṃśayaḥ svāmin kṛpayaiva nirasyatām||

units.label: Verse 635
units.deva:
आनन्द-रूपम् आत्मानम् अज्ञात्वैव पृथग्-जनः।
बहिः-सुखाय यतते न तु कश्चिद् विदन् बुधः॥
units.translation: Not knowing the Self as the form of bliss, an ordinary person strives for happiness outside. No wise person who knows does so.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
ānanda-rūpam ātmānam ajñātvaiva pṛthag-janaḥ|
bahiḥ-sukhāya yatate na tu kaścid vidan budhaḥ||

units.label: Verse 636
units.deva:
अज्ञात्वैव हि निक्षेपं भिक्षाम् अटति दुर्मतिः।
स्व-वेश्मनि निधिं ज्ञात्वा को नु भिक्षाम् अटेत् सुधीः॥
units.translation: Not knowing of the treasure, a foolish person wanders begging. What wise person would beg after knowing of the treasure in their own home?
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
ajñātvaiva hi nikṣepaṃ bhikṣām aṭati durmatiḥ|
sva-veśmani nidhiṃ jñātvā ko nu bhikṣām aṭet sudhīḥ||

units.label: Verse 637
units.deva:
स्थूलं च सूक्ष्मं च वपुः स्व-भावतो
दुःखात्मकं स्वात्मतया गृहीत्वा।
विस्मृत्य च स्वं सुख-रूपम् आत्मनो
दुःख-प्रदेभ्यः सुखम् अज्ञ इच्छति॥
units.translation: Taking the gross and subtle bodies, by their nature sources of suffering, to be the Self, and forgetting the Self’s own nature as happiness, the ignorant seek happiness from things that bring suffering.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
sthūlaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ ca vapuḥ sva-bhāvato
duḥkhātmakaṃ svātmatayā gṛhītvā|
vismṛtya ca svaṃ sukha-rūpam ātmano
duḥkha-pradebhyaḥ sukham ajña icchati||

units.label: Verse 638
units.deva:
न हि दुःख-प्रदं वस्तु सुखं दातुं समर्हति।
किं विषं पिबतो जन्तोर् अमृतत्वं प्रयच्छति॥
units.translation: An object that brings suffering cannot give happiness. Does poison give immortality to the person who drinks it?
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
na hi duḥkha-pradaṃ vastu sukhaṃ dātuṃ samarhati|
kiṃ viṣaṃ pibato jantor amṛtatvaṃ prayacchati||

units.label: Verse 639
units.deva:
आत्मान्यः सुखम् अन्यच् चेत्येवं निश्चित्य पामरः।
बहिः-सुखाय यतते सत्यम् एव न संशयः॥
units.translation: Having concluded that the Self is one thing and happiness another, a foolish person truly strives for happiness outside; there is no doubt about it.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
ātmānyaḥ sukham anyac cetyevaṃ niścitya pāmaraḥ|
bahiḥ-sukhāya yatate satyam eva na saṃśayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 640
units.deva:
इष्टस्य वस्तुनो ध्यान-दर्शनाद्युपभुक्तिषु।
प्रतीयते य आनन्दः सर्वेषाम् इह देहिनाम्॥
units.translation: The joy that all embodied beings perceive while contemplating, seeing, and enjoying a desired object.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
iṣṭasya vastuno dhyāna-darśanādyupabhuktiṣu|
pratīyate ya ānandaḥ sarveṣām iha dehinām||

units.label: Verse 641
units.deva:
स वस्तु-धर्मो नो यस्मान् मनस्येवोपलभ्यते।
वस्तु-धर्मस्य मनसि कथं स्याद् उपलम्भनम्॥
units.translation: Since it is perceived only in the mind, it is not a property of an object. How could an object’s property be perceived in the mind?
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
sa vastu-dharmo no yasmān manasyevopalabhyate|
vastu-dharmasya manasi kathaṃ syād upalambhanam||

units.label: Verse 642
units.deva:
अन्यत्र त्वन्य-धर्माणाम् उपलम्भो न दृश्यते।
तस्मान् न वस्तु-धर्मोऽयम् आनन्दस् तु कदाचन॥
units.translation: The properties of one thing are not seen elsewhere. Therefore, this bliss is never a property of an object.

gloss.en: of the properties of other things

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
anyatra tvanya-dharmāṇām upalambho na dṛśyate|
tasmān na vastu-dharmo’yam ānandas tu kadācana||

units.label: Verse 643
units.deva:
नाप्येष धर्मो मनसोऽसत्यर्थे तद्-अदर्शनात्।
असति व्यञ्जके व्यङ्ग्यं नोदेतीति न मन्यताम्॥
units.translation: Nor is this happiness a property of the mind, since it is not seen when the object is absent. Do not think that what is to be manifested fails to arise when the manifestor is absent.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
nāpyeṣa dharmo manaso’satyarthe tad-adarśanāt|
asati vyañjake vyaṅgyaṃ nodetīti na manyatām||

units.label: Verse 644
units.deva:
सत्यर्थेऽपि च नोदेति ह्यानन्दस् तूक्त-लक्षणः।
सत्यपि व्यञ्जके व्यङ्ग्यानुदयो नैव सम्मतः॥
units.translation: Even when the object is present, the happiness just described does not arise. The absence of what is to be manifested is not accepted when the manifestor is present.

gloss.en: the non-arising of what is to be manifested

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
satyarthe’pi ca nodeti hyānandas tūkta-lakṣaṇaḥ|
satyapi vyañjake vyaṅgyānudayo naiva sammataḥ||

units.label: Verse 645
units.deva:
दुरदृष्टादिकं नात्र प्रतिबन्धः प्रकल्प्यताम्।
प्रियस्य वस्तुनो लाभे दुरदृष्टं न सिध्यति॥
units.translation: Do not suppose that bad fortune and the like are an obstacle here. When a desired object is obtained, bad fortune is not established.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
duradṛṣṭādikaṃ nātra pratibandhaḥ prakalpyatām|
priyasya vastuno lābhe duradṛṣṭaṃ na sidhyati||

units.label: Verse 646
units.deva:
तस्मान् न मानसो धर्मो निर्गुणत्वान् न चात्मनः।
किं तु पुण्यस्य सांनिध्याद् इष्टस्यापि च वस्तुनः॥
units.translation: Therefore happiness is not a property of the mind, nor of the Self, because the Self is without qualities. Rather, it arises from the presence of merit and of the desired object.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
tasmān na mānaso dharmo nirguṇatvān na cātmanaḥ|
kiṃ tu puṇyasya sāṃnidhyād iṣṭasyāpi ca vastunaḥ||

units.label: Verse 647
units.deva:
सत्त्व-प्रधाने चित्तेऽस्मिंस् त्वात्मैव प्रतिबिम्बति।
आनन्द-लक्षणः स्वच्छे पयसीव सुधा-करः॥
units.translation: In this mind, where sattva predominates, the Self itself is reflected, marked by bliss, like the moon in clear water.
units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
sattva-pradhāne citte’smiṃs tvātmaiva pratibimbati|
ānanda-lakṣaṇaḥ svacche payasīva sudhā-karaḥ||

units.label: Verse 648
units.deva:
सोऽयम् आभास आनन्दश् चित्ते यः प्रतिबिम्बितः।
पुण्योत्कर्षापकर्षाभ्यां भवत्युच्चावचः स्वयम्॥
units.translation: This apparent bliss is the bliss reflected in the mind. By the increase or decrease of merit, it becomes greater or lesser.

gloss.en: through the increase or decrease of merit

units.sectionTitle: You are Only that Ultimate Reality
units.iast:
so’yam ābhāsa ānandaś citte yaḥ pratibimbitaḥ|
puṇyotkarṣāpakarṣābhyāṃ bhavatyuccāvacaḥ svayam||

units.label: Verse 649
units.deva:
सार्व-भौमादि-ब्रह्मान्तं श्रुत्या यः प्रतिपादितः।
स क्षयिष्णुः सातिशयः प्रक्षीणे कारणे लयम्॥
