युक्तः सः श्रवणे सताम् अभिमतो मुख्याधिकारी द्विजः॥
units.translation: The twice-born who has pleased God by performing with faith and devotion all the rituals enjoined by the Vedas, who by the grace of God has earned merit in his previous birth, and as a result of it has now become fit and has been endowed with the requisite means to attain liberation, such as discrimination, renunciation and dispassion, it is such a person who becomes fit to comprehend what the Vedānta teaches. Such is the opinion of the good and wise.
units.iast:
śraddhā-bhakti-puraḥ-sareṇa vihitenaiveśvaraṃ karmaṇā
santoṣyārjita-tat-prasāda-mahimā janmāntareṣveva yaḥ|
nityānitya-viveka-tīvra-virati-nyāsādibhiḥ sādhanair
yuktaḥ saḥ śravaṇe satām abhimato mukhyādhikārī dvijaḥ||

units.label: Verse 797
units.deva:
अध्यारोपापवाद-क्रमम् अनुसरता देशिकेनात्र
वेत्त्र-वाक्यार्थे बोध्यमाने सति सपदि सतः शुद्ध-बुद्धेर् अमुष्य।
नित्यानन्दाद्वितीयं निरुपमम् अमलं यत् परं तत्त्वम् एकं
तद् ब्रह्मैवाहम् अस्मीत्युदयति परमाखण्डताकार-वृत्तिः॥
units.translation: No sooner is the meaning of the sentence ‘That thou art’ made known to the aspirant by the teacher of Vedānta, who follows the method of superimposition (adhyāropa) and of negation (apavāda) then there arises in the man of pure intellect that supreme mental modification which knows no change, and he realizes, ‘I am that Brahman who is of the nature of eternal bliss, without a second, incomprehensible, untainted, the One Supreme Reality.’
units.iast:
adhyāropāpavāda-kramam anusaratā deśikenātra
vettra-vākyārthe bodhyamāne sati sapadi sataḥ śuddha-buddher amuṣya|
nityānandādvitīyaṃ nirupamam amalaṃ yat paraṃ tattvam ekaṃ
tad brahmaivāham asmītyudayati paramākhaṇḍatākāra-vṛttiḥ||

units.label: Verse 798
units.deva:
अखण्डाकार-वृत्तिः सा चिद्-आभास-समन्विता।
आत्माभिन्नं परं ब्रह्म विषयी-कृत्य केवलम्॥
units.translation: The indivisible pure consciousness makes itself manifest in all that it reflects upon. It pervades everything. Inasmuch as Brahman is not other than the Ātman, it follows that it is only by means of Brahman that the veil of avidyā may be lifted.
units.iast:
akhaṇḍākāra-vṛttiḥ sā cid-ābhāsa-samanvitā|
ātmābhinnaṃ paraṃ brahma viṣayī-kṛtya kevalam||

units.label: Verse 799
units.deva:
बाधते तद्-गताज्ञानं यद् आवरण-लक्षणम्।
अखण्डाकारया वृत्त्या त्वज्ञाने बाधिते सति॥
units.translation: As a result of the dawning of the supreme knowledge, when the veil of avidyā is rent asunder, in all the levels of consciousness, that power veiling the Supreme Being which was but the product of ignorance, also ceases to function.
units.iast:
bādhate tad-gatājñānaṃ yad āvaraṇa-lakṣaṇam|
akhaṇḍākārayā vṛttyā tvajñāne bādhite sati||

units.label: Verse 800
units.deva:
तत्-कार्यं सकलं तेन समं भवति बाधितम्।
तन्तु-दाहे तु तत्-कार्य-पट-दाहो यथा तथा॥
units.translation: When once ignorance is removed along with it, that sense of separateness which was the effect of ignorance is also removed. If every fibre of the veil should be set on fire, would not the whole fabric become burnt? In the same way, that which was the effect of ignorance, viz. the state of the individual self, also becomes negated.
units.iast:
tat-kāryaṃ sakalaṃ tena samaṃ bhavati bādhitam|
tantu-dāhe tu tat-kārya-paṭa-dāho yathā tathā||

units.label: Verse 801
units.deva:
तस्य कार्यतया जीव-वृत्तिर् भवति बाधिता।
उपप्रभा यथा सूर्यं प्रकाशयितुम् अक्षमा॥
units.translation: Like a pale lamp that fades into insignificance before the bright blaze of the mid-day sun, the flickering light of limited consciousness, which is all that avidyā allows, becomes insignificant in the presence of the knowledge of the infinite, self-effulgent Brahman. ((BrhUEng.4.3.7) (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
tasya kāryatayā jīva-vṛttir bhavati bādhitā|
upaprabhā yathā sūryaṃ prakāśayitum akṣamā||

units.label: Verse 802
units.deva:
तद्वद् एव चिद्-आभास-चैतन्यं वृत्ति-संस्थितम्।
स्व-प्रकाशं परं ब्रह्म प्रकाशयितुम् अक्षमम्॥
units.translation: That reflected light of the individual consciousness which is all that is revealed by the intellect does not in any way add to the light of the supreme consciousness.
units.iast:
tadvad eva cid-ābhāsa-caitanyaṃ vṛtti-saṃsthitam|
sva-prakāśaṃ paraṃ brahma prakāśayitum akṣamam||

units.label: Verse 803
units.deva:
प्रचण्डातप-मध्यस्थ-दीपवन् नष्ट-दीधितिः।
तत् तेजसाभिभूतं सल् लीनोपाधितया ततः॥
units.translation: It is as though one should hold a tiny lamp in order to throw light upon the mid-day sun. When the light of the supreme consciousness shines, one’s limited individual knowledge is of little avail. That is because the adjuncts then become merged in pure consciousness.
units.iast:
pracaṇḍātapa-madhyastha-dīpavan naṣṭa-dīdhitiḥ|
tat tejasābhibhūtaṃ sal līnopādhitayā tataḥ||

units.label: Verse 804
units.deva:
बिम्ब-भूत-पर-ब्रह्म-मात्रं भवति केवलम्।
यथापनीते त्वादर्शे प्रतिबिम्ब-मुखं स्वयम्॥
units.translation: When the adjuncts merge in the Supreme Brahman, which is reflected in them, what remains finally is the light of pure consciousness. That is the light of the supreme Brahman, which alone had been reflected in all of them.
units.iast:
bimba-bhūta-para-brahma-mātraṃ bhavati kevalam|
yathāpanīte tvādarśe pratibimba-mukhaṃ svayam||

units.label: Verse 805
units.deva:
मुख-मात्रं भवेत् तद्वद् एतच् चोपाधि-सङ्क्षयात्।
घटाज्ञाने यथा वृत्त्या व्याप्तया बाधिते सति॥
units.translation: It is only as long as a mirror is there that it reflects the face. But when once the mirror is removed, the reflection becomes one with the face. In the same way, when the limiting adjuncts have ceased to function, all that remains is the one pure consciousness.
units.iast:
mukha-mātraṃ bhavet tadvad etac copādhi-saṅkṣayāt|
ghaṭājñāne yathā vṛttyā vyāptayā bādhite sati||

units.label: Verse 806
units.deva:
घटं विस्फुरयत्येष चिद्-आभासः स्व-तेजसा।
न तथा स्व-प्रभे ब्रह्मण्याभास उपयुज्यते॥
units.translation: A pot, for instance, is made known through the mental modifications, as long as one is in a state of ignorance. But when one has attained knowledge, the same pot is made manifest by the light of consciousness. But the analogy does not hold good in regard to the self-effulgent Brahman, because Brahman cannot be made manifest by its reflection.
units.iast:
ghaṭaṃ visphurayatyeṣa cid-ābhāsaḥ sva-tejasā|
na tathā sva-prabhe brahmaṇyābhāsa upayujyate||

units.label: Verse 807
units.deva:
अत एव मतं वृत्ति-व्याप्यत्वं वस्तुनः सताम्।
न फल-व्याप्यता तेन न विरोधः परस्-परम्॥
units.translation: That is why the learned hold that Reality, or Brahman, is capable of pervading all the mental modifications; but it does not follow that the reflection of pure consciousness can make Brahman an object of manifestation. Consequently, there is no self-contradiction in what the Śruti says. ((KenU.2.3) (Kena Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
ata eva mataṃ vṛtti-vyāpyatvaṃ vastunaḥ satām|
na phala-vyāpyatā tena na virodhaḥ paras-param||

units.label: Verse 808
units.deva:
श्रुत्योदितं ततो ब्रह्म ज्ञेयं बुद्ध्यैव सूक्ष्मया।
प्रज्ञामान्द्यं भवेद् येषां तेषां न श्रुति-मात्रतः॥
units.translation: Brahman should therefore be known by the subtle intellect. But those persons whose understanding is limited cannot directly attain that mental attitude merely by listening to what the Śruti says. Such persons should recollect in mind what the Śruti says and meditate upon it.
units.iast:
śrutyoditaṃ tato brahma jñeyaṃ buddhyaiva sūkṣmayā|
prajñāmāndyaṃ bhaved yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ na śruti-mātrataḥ||

units.label: Verse 809
units.deva: श्रवणान् मननाद् ध्यानात् तात्पर्येण निरन्तरम्॥
units.translation: Śravaṇa-Manana-Dhyāna It is only by constantly hearing and thinking as well as by meditating upon what the Śruti says, that the intellect becomes endowed with the power of ascertaining that which is subtle. It is only then, and not till then, that the Reality is known.
units.iast: śravaṇān mananād dhyānāt tātparyeṇa nirantaram||

units.label: Verse 810
units.deva:
बुद्धेः सूक्ष्मत्वम् आयाति ततो वस्तूपलभ्यते।
मन्द-प्रज्ञावतां तस्मात् करणीयं पुनः पुनः॥
units.translation: That supreme reality is attained only by means of the subtle intellect. Those who are lacking in intellectual sharpness should therefore repeatedly hear and meditate over what the Śruti says, in order to attain the right knowledge. ((BrhUEng.4.4.19) (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
buddheḥ sūkṣmatvam āyāti tato vastūpalabhyate|
manda-prajñāvatāṃ tasmāt karaṇīyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ||

units.label: Verse 811
units.deva:
श्रवणं मननं ध्यानं सम्यग् वस्तूपलब्धये।
सर्व-वेदान्त-वाक्यानां षड्भिर् लिङ्गैः सद्-अद्वये॥
units.translation: The expression ‘hearing what the Śruti says’ is explained by the learned in the following way. It means the ascertainment of the meaning of what the Śruti says, by availing oneself of the six valid means of knowledge (ṣaḍ-liṅgas), until one attains the knowledge of the Supreme Being, the One without a second.
units.iast:
śravaṇaṃ mananaṃ dhyānaṃ samyag vastūpalabdhaye|
sarva-vedānta-vākyānāṃ ṣaḍbhir liṅgaiḥ sad-advaye||

units.label: Verse 812
units.deva:
परे ब्रह्मणि तात्पर्य-निश्चयं श्रवणं विदुः।
श्रुतस्यैवाद्वितीयस्य वस्तुनः प्रत्यग्-आत्मनः॥
units.translation: By resorting to all these aids, the aspirant finds out the meaning of the Śruti, until he comes to realize the Supreme Being, Brahman as pure existence, the One without a second. Such is the meaning of the word ‘hearing (śravaṇa)’.
units.iast:
pare brahmaṇi tātparya-niścayaṃ śravaṇaṃ viduḥ|
śrutasyaivādvitīyasya vastunaḥ pratyag-ātmanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 813
units.deva:
वेदान्त-वाक्यानुगुण-युक्तिभिस् त्वनुचिन्तनम्।
मननं तच्-छ्रुतार्थस्य साक्षात्-करण-कारणम्॥
units.translation: Similarly the word ‘thinking (manana)’ means pondering over the content of what the Śruti says and trying to understand the nature of the inmost Ātman. With the help of reason one should try to know that non-dual Reality, in so far as reason is not opposed to Vedānta. It is in this way that the Ātman is realized, and the Supreme Reality is attained.
units.iast:
vedānta-vākyānuguṇa-yuktibhis tvanucintanam|
mananaṃ tac-chrutārthasya sākṣāt-karaṇa-kāraṇam||

units.label: Verse 814
units.deva:
विजातीय-शरीरादि-प्रत्यय-त्याग-पूर्वकम्।
सजातीयात्म-वृत्तीनां प्रवाह-करणं यथा॥
units.translation: Likewise the word ‘meditation’ implies that the current of thought should flow steadily like a jet of oil, to the exclusion of all other ideas, such as the consciousness of one’s physical body and the like. It is in this way that the mind should be wholly absorbed in the consciousness of the Ātman and be permeated by it.
units.iast:
vijātīya-śarīrādi-pratyaya-tyāga-pūrvakam|
sajātīyātma-vṛttīnāṃ pravāha-karaṇaṃ yathā||

units.label: Verse 815
units.deva:
तैल-धारावद् अच्छिन्न-वृत्त्या तद् ध्यानम् इष्यते।
तावत् कालं प्रयत्नेन कर्तव्यं श्रवणं सदा॥
units.translation: Therefore, let the aspirant listen diligently to what the Vedānta says, until all doubts are removed, and until there comes the awareness that Śruti is the only valid means of knowledge.
units.iast:
taila-dhārāvad acchinna-vṛttyā tad dhyānam iṣyate|
tāvat kālaṃ prayatnena kartavyaṃ śravaṇaṃ sadā||

units.label: Verse 816
units.deva:
प्रमाण-संशयो यावत् स्व-बुद्धेर् न निवर्तते।
प्रमेय-संशयो यावत् तावत् तु श्रुति-युक्तिभिः॥
units.translation: One should turn to the Śruti with the help of reason and ascertain the truth of the Ātman. One should have all one’s doubts cleared by means of continuous thinking, until one realizes the nature of that which is to be proved.
units.iast:
pramāṇa-saṃśayo yāvat sva-buddher na nivartate|
prameya-saṃśayo yāvat tāvat tu śruti-yuktibhiḥ||

units.label: Verse 817
units.deva:
आत्म-याथार्थ्य-निश्चित्त्यै कर्तव्यं मननं मुहुः।
विपरीतात्म-धीर् यावन् न विनश्यति चेतसि।
तावन् निरन्तरं ध्यानं कर्तव्यं मोक्षम् इच्छता॥
units.translation: One who desires to attain liberation should therefore practice meditation unceasingly, until all the wrong ideas that arise in the mind as to the nature of the Ātman are completely eradicated.
units.iast:
ātma-yāthārthya-niścittyai kartavyaṃ mananaṃ muhuḥ|
viparītātma-dhīr yāvan na vinaśyati cetasi|
tāvan nirantaraṃ dhyānaṃ kartavyaṃ mokṣam icchatā||

units.label: Verse 818
units.deva:
यावन् न तर्केण निरासितोऽपि
दृश्य-प्रपञ्चस् त्वपरोक्ष-बोधात्।
विलीयते तावद् अमुष्य भिक्षोर्
ध्यानादि सम्यक् करणीयम् एव॥
units.translation: A man of renunciation should therefore resort to meditation and also avail himself of the other means of knowledge. Then, the world of external objects which have been proved formally to be unreal would no longer interfere with all one’s thought; and the immediate knowledge of the Ātman will be attained.
units.iast:
yāvan na tarkeṇa nirāsito’pi
dṛśya-prapañcas tvaparokṣa-bodhāt|
vilīyate tāvad amuṣya bhikṣor
dhyānādi samyak karaṇīyam eva||

units.label: Verse 819
units.deva:
स-विकल्पो निर्-विकल्प इति द्वेधा निगद्यते।
समाधिः सविकल्पस्य लक्षणं वच्मि तच् छृणु॥
units.translation: Samādhi, the relative kind There are two kinds of samādhi. Of them, one is known as the savikalpa samādhi. It represents deep concentration at the relative plane. The other is the nirvikalpa samādhi which is at the absolute plane of consciousness. We shall now describe the nature of savikalpa samādhi; listen attentively.
units.iast:
sa-vikalpo nir-vikalpa iti dvedhā nigadyate|
samādhiḥ savikalpasya lakṣaṇaṃ vacmi tac chṛṇu||

units.label: Verse 820
units.deva:
ज्ञात्राद्यविलयेनैव ज्ञेये ब्रह्मणि केवले।
तद्-आकाराकारितया चित्त-वृत्तेर् अवस्थितिः॥
units.translation: In the relative plane of consciousness, one is aware of Brahman as permeating the whole of one’s field of consciousness. Inasmuch as one has yet to establish complete identity with that which one contemplates, it is called ‘relative’.
units.iast:
jñātrādyavilayenaiva jñeye brahmaṇi kevale|
tad-ākārākāritayā citta-vṛtter avasthitiḥ||

units.label: Verse 821
units.deva:
सद्भिः स एव विज्ञेयः समाधिः सविकल्पकः।
मृद एवावभानेऽपि मृण्मय-द्विप-भानवत्॥
units.translation: A clay elephant reminds us of a living one, even though it is only clay. In the same way, the apparent distinction of the knower, the known and the knowledge of it, although unreal, yet helps one to realize the ultimate Truth; and such is the nature of savikalpa samādhi.
units.iast:
sadbhiḥ sa eva vijñeyaḥ samādhiḥ savikalpakaḥ|
mṛda evāvabhāne’pi mṛṇmaya-dvipa-bhānavat||

units.label: Verse 822
units.deva:
सन्मात्र-वस्तु-भानेऽपि त्रि-पुटी भाति सन्मयी।
समाधिर् अत एवायं सविकल्प इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: It is called ‘samādhi’ because it is helpful in leading to the transcendent Reality. It is called ‘savikalpa’ which means ‘subject to modification,’ because there still linger the three-fold modifications of the knower, knowing and the known (i.e. it is parokṣa, away from one’s identity).
units.iast:
sanmātra-vastu-bhāne’pi tri-puṭī bhāti sanmayī|
samādhir ata evāyaṃ savikalpa itīryate||

units.label: Verse 823
units.deva:
ज्ञात्रादि-भावम् उत्सृज्य ज्ञेय-मात्र-स्थितिर् दृढा।
मनसो निर्विकल्पः स्यात् समाधिर् योग-संज्ञितः॥
units.translation: Samādhi, the absolute kind That stage of awareness is known as the nirvikalpa samādhi, in which, after having cast off the idea that one is the knower, one is firmly established in that on which one contemplates.
units.iast:
jñātrādi-bhāvam utsṛjya jñeya-mātra-sthitir dṛḍhā|
manaso nirvikalpaḥ syāt samādhir yoga-saṃjñitaḥ||

units.label: Verse 824
units.deva:
जले निक्षिप्त-लवणं जल-मात्रतया स्थितम्।
पृथङ् न भाति किं न्व् अम्भ एकम् एवावभासते॥
units.translation: It is as though the salt that has been thrown into water has lost its separateness, and remains in the form of water only.
units.iast:
jale nikṣipta-lavaṇaṃ jala-mātratayā sthitam|
pṛthaṅ na bhāti kiṃ nv ambha ekam evāvabhāsate||

units.label: Verse 825
units.deva:
यथा तथैव सा वृत्तिर् ब्रह्म-मात्रतया स्थिता।
पृथङ् न भाति ब्रह्मैवाद्वितीयम् अवभासते॥
units.translation: When our individuality merges in the absolute Brahman, from which it has emerged, it loses its sense of separateness, and all that remains is the one non-dual Brahman.
units.iast:
yathā tathaiva sā vṛttir brahma-mātratayā sthitā|
pṛthaṅ na bhāti brahmaivādvitīyam avabhāsate||

units.label: Verse 826
units.deva:
ज्ञात्रादि-कल्पनाभावान् मतोऽयं निर्विकल्पकः।
वृत्तेः सद्-भाव-बाधाभ्याम् उभयोर् भेद इष्यते॥
units.translation: On account of the absence of the knowledge of the knower and the like, this type of deep concentration is referred to as the ‘absolute’. It is the presence or the absence of the mental modifications that distinguishes the savikalpa from the nirvikalpa samādhi.
units.iast:
jñātrādi-kalpanābhāvān mato’yaṃ nirvikalpakaḥ|
vṛtteḥ sad-bhāva-bādhābhyām ubhayor bheda iṣyate||

units.label: Verse 827
units.deva:
समाधि-सुप्त्योर् ज्ञानं चाज्ञानं सुप्त्यात्र नेष्यते।
सविकल्पो निर्विकल्पः समाधी द्वाव् इमौ हृदि॥
units.translation: In relative concentration, there is the knowledge of (or about) Brahman. In deep sleep (where there are no vṛttis) there is the ignorance of Brahman. But deep concentration at the absolute plane differs from both these levels of consciousness.
units.iast:
samādhi-suptyor jñānaṃ cājñānaṃ suptyātra neṣyate|
savikalpo nirvikalpaḥ samādhī dvāv imau hṛdi||

units.label: Verse 828
units.deva:
मुमुक्षोर् यत्नतः कार्यौ विपरीत-निवृत्तये।
कृतेऽस्मिन् विपरीताया भावनाया निवर्तनम्॥
units.translation: An aspirant after liberation should therefore practise in mind both these aspects of samādhi, the savikalpa and the nirvikalpa, and he should continue the practice until all wrong ideas have been utterly effaced.
units.iast:
mumukṣor yatnataḥ kāryau viparīta-nivṛttaye|
kṛte’smin viparītāyā bhāvanāyā nivartanam||

units.label: Verse 829
units.deva:
ज्ञानस्याप्रतिबद्धत्वं सदानन्दश्च सिध्यति।
दृश्यानुविद्धः शब्दानुविद्धश्चेति द्विधा मतः॥
units.translation: When all the wrong ideas have come to an end, there are no more obstacles to the attainment of the highest knowledge. In this way it is that bliss is realized.
units.iast:
jñānasyāpratibaddhatvaṃ sadānandaśca sidhyati|
dṛśyānuviddhaḥ śabdānuviddhaśceti dvidhā mataḥ||

units.label: Verse 830
units.deva:
सविकल्पस् तयोर् यत् तल् लक्षणं वच्मि तच् छृणु।
कामादि-प्रत्ययैर् दृश्यैः संसर्गो यत्र दृश्यते॥
units.translation: There are two varieties of savikalpa samādhi. One type of it is in association with the consciousness of the body (dṛśya-anuviddha). The other is in association with the maxims of the Śruti (śabdha-anuviddha). I shall now explain them to you in this order; listen attentively.
units.iast:
savikalpas tayor yat tal lakṣaṇaṃ vacmi tac chṛṇu|
kāmādi-pratyayair dṛśyaiḥ saṃsargo yatra dṛśyate||

units.label: Verse 831
units.deva:
सोऽयं दृश्यानुविद्धः स्यात् समाधिः सविकल्पकः।
अहं ममेदम् इत्यादि-काम-क्रोधादि-वृत्तयः॥
units.translation: The first type of savikalpa samādhi is that which is blended with the objects of knowledge. There are faint traces of one’s ego consciousness, such as the ideas of ‘I and mine’, as also the impression of one’s likes and dislikes.
units.iast:
so’yaṃ dṛśyānuviddhaḥ syāt samādhiḥ savikalpakaḥ|
ahaṃ mamedam ityādi-kāma-krodhādi-vṛttayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 832
units.deva:
दृश्यन्ते येन सन्दृष्टा दृश्याः स्युर् अहम्-आदयः।
कामादि-सर्व-वृत्तीनां द्रष्टारम् अविकारिणम्॥
units.translation: There is at the same time a realization of the Ātman as the unchanging witness, who alone is the seer, and the perceiver of the ‘me’ consciousness, and of one’s likes and dislikes.
units.iast:
dṛśyante yena sandṛṣṭā dṛśyāḥ syur aham-ādayaḥ|
kāmādi-sarva-vṛttīnāṃ draṣṭāram avikāriṇam||

units.label: Verse 833
units.deva:
साक्षिणं स्वं विजानीयाद् यस् ताः पश्यति निष्क्रियः।
कामादीनाम् अहं साक्षी दृश्यन्ते ते मया ततः॥
units.translation: One should identify oneself with the Ātman, the seer, who does not take part in any kind of activity, by thinking, ‘I am the witness of the likes and dislikes; they are the objects of my knowledge’.
units.iast:
sākṣiṇaṃ svaṃ vijānīyād yas tāḥ paśyati niṣkriyaḥ|
kāmādīnām ahaṃ sākṣī dṛśyante te mayā tataḥ||

units.label: Verse 834
units.deva:
इति साक्षितयात्मानं जानात्यात्मनि साक्षिणम्।
दृश्यं कामादि सकलं स्वात्मन्येव विलापयेत्॥
units.translation: It is in this way that one comes to identify oneself with the witnessing consciousness, and merging in that consciousness all which one conceives within oneself, such as one’s likes and dislikes.
units.iast:
iti sākṣitayātmānaṃ jānātyātmani sākṣiṇam|
dṛśyaṃ kāmādi sakalaṃ svātmanyeva vilāpayet||

units.label: Verse 835
units.deva:
नाहं देहो नाप्यसुर् नाक्ष-वर्गो
नाहङ्कारो नो मनो नापि बुद्धिः।
अन्तस् तेषां चापि तद्-विक्रियाणां
साक्षी नित्यः प्रत्यग् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: One knows oneself thus: I am neither the body, nor vital force, nor the sense organs, nor the ego, nor the mind, nor the intellect, for I am within all these; I am the eternal inmost witnessing consciousness, who is the seer of the changing phenomena, and I am other than all of them.
units.iast:
nāhaṃ deho nāpyasur nākṣa-vargo
nāhaṅkāro no mano nāpi buddhiḥ|
antas teṣāṃ cāpi tad-vikriyāṇāṃ
sākṣī nityaḥ pratyag evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 836
units.deva:
वाचः साक्षी प्राण-वृत्तेश्च साक्षी
बुद्धेः साक्षी बुद्धि-वृत्तेश्च साक्षी।
चक्षुः-श्रोत्रादीन्द्रियाणां च साक्षी
साक्षी नित्यः प्रत्यग् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: I am the eternal inmost witness of the functioning of the organ of speech, the vital force, and the intellect. I am the seer of all the modifications that take place in the intellect, as well as of all that which the eye sees and the ear hears.
units.iast:
vācaḥ sākṣī prāṇa-vṛtteśca sākṣī
buddheḥ sākṣī buddhi-vṛtteśca sākṣī|
cakṣuḥ-śrotrādīndriyāṇāṃ ca sākṣī
sākṣī nityaḥ pratyag evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 837
units.deva:
नाहं स्थूलो नापि सूक्ष्मो न दीर्घो
नाहं बालो नो युवा नापि वृद्धः।
नाहं काणो नापि मूको न षण्डः
साक्षी नित्यः प्रत्यग् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: I am neither fat nor lean, neither a child, nor a youth nor an old person, I am neither a one-eyed person, nor a dumb one, nor am I a eunuch. The inmost witnessing consciousness – that I am.
units.iast:
nāhaṃ sthūlo nāpi sūkṣmo na dīrgho
nāhaṃ bālo no yuvā nāpi vṛddhaḥ|
nāhaṃ kāṇo nāpi mūko na ṣaṇḍaḥ
sākṣī nityaḥ pratyag evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 838
units.deva:
नास्म्यागन्ता नापि गन्ता न हन्ता
नाहं कर्ता न प्रयोक्ता न वक्ता।
नाहं भोक्ता नो सुखी नैव दुःखी
साक्षी नित्यः प्रत्यग् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: I neither come nor go; I do not kill anyone; nor do I cause anyone to be killed. I am neither a doer, nor an employer, nor a speaker, nor an experiencer. I am neither happy, nor miserable; for I am none other than the eternal, inmost witnessing consciousness. ((BhG.18.17) (Bhagavad Gītā))
units.iast:
nāsmyāgantā nāpi gantā na hantā
nāhaṃ kartā na prayoktā na vaktā|
nāhaṃ bhoktā no sukhī naiva duḥkhī
sākṣī nityaḥ pratyag evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 839
units.deva:
नाहं योगी नो वियोगी न रागी
नाहं क्रोधी नैव कामी न लोभी।
नाहं बद्धो नापि युक्तो न मुक्तः
साक्षी नित्यः प्रत्यग् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: I am neither a yogī, nor the reverse of it; I am neither angry, nor lustful nor greedy; I am not bound by anything, nor am I free of anything. I am none other than the eternal, innermost witnessing consciousness.
units.iast:
nāhaṃ yogī no viyogī na rāgī
nāhaṃ krodhī naiva kāmī na lobhī|
nāhaṃ baddho nāpi yukto na muktaḥ
sākṣī nityaḥ pratyag evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 840
units.deva:
नान्तः-प्रज्ञो न बहिः-प्रज्ञको वा
नैव प्रज्ञो नापि चाप्रज्ञ एषः।
नाहं श्रोता नापि मन्ता न बोद्धा
साक्षी नित्यः प्रत्यग् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: The fact is that the Ātman is not conscious of anything either within it or outside of it, either one at a time or both simultaneously, nor is the Ātman non-consciousness. Therefore I am neither a hearer nor a thinker; nor a knower of anything; I am the eternal, inmost witnessing consciousness.
units.iast:
nāntaḥ-prajño na bahiḥ-prajñako vā
naiva prajño nāpi cāprajña eṣaḥ|
nāhaṃ śrotā nāpi mantā na boddhā
sākṣī nityaḥ pratyag evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 841
units.deva:
न मेऽस्ति देहेन्द्रिय-बुद्धि-योगोन
पुण्य-लेशोऽपि न पाप-लेशः।
क्षुधा-पिपासादि-षड्-ऊर्मि-दूरः
सदा विमुक्तोऽस्मि चिद् एव केवलः॥
units.translation: I am not limited either by the body, or the sense organs, or the intellect. Virtue and sin affect me not in the least. Old age and death, hunger and thirst, grief and delusion – all these are far from me. I am none other than pure consciousness, the ever-free.
units.iast:
na me’sti dehendriya-buddhi-yogona
puṇya-leśo’pi na pāpa-leśaḥ|
kṣudhā-pipāsādi-ṣaḍ-ūrmi-dūraḥ
sadā vimukto’smi cid eva kevalaḥ||

units.label: Verse 842
units.deva:
अपाणि-पादोऽहम् अवाग् अचक्षुः
अप्राण एवास्म्यमना ह्यबुद्धिः।
व्योमेव पूर्णोऽस्मि विनिर्मलोऽस्मि
सदैक-रूपोऽस्मि चिद् एव केवलः॥
units.translation: I am neither the hands nor the feet, neither the organ of speech nor the eyes, neither the vital force nor the mind, nor the intellect. Like unto the universal space, I am that which is all pervading, the unchanging pure consciousness.
units.iast:
apāṇi-pādo’ham avāg acakṣuḥ
aprāṇa evāsmyamanā hyabuddhiḥ|
vyomeva pūrṇo’smi vinirmalo’smi
sadaika-rūpo’smi cid eva kevalaḥ||

units.label: Verse 843
units.deva:
इति स्वम् आत्मानम् अवेक्षमाणः
प्रतीत-दृश्यं प्रविलापयन् सदा॥
जहाति विद्वान् विपरीत-भावं
स्वाभाविकं भ्रान्ति-वशात् प्रतीतम्॥
units.translation: The knower of Brahman who knows the Ātman in this manner merges all the objects of knowledge that are experienced by him in the consciousness of the Ātman. It is in this way that he frees himself from all wrong ideas for they are but the products of delusion. ((MunU.2.2.7) (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
iti svam ātmānam avekṣamāṇaḥ
pratīta-dṛśyaṃ pravilāpayan sadā||
jahāti vidvān viparīta-bhāvaṃ
svābhāvikaṃ bhrānti-vaśāt pratītam||

units.label: Verse 844
units.deva:
विपरीतात्मता-स्फूर्तिर् एव मुक्तिर् इतीर्यते।
सदा समाहितस्यैव सैषा सिध्यति नान्यथा॥
units.translation: Therefore the word ‘mukti’ comes to mean freedom from the bondage of ignorance. In itself it means awareness of the Ātman (i.e. means the awareness that is the Ātman); and this may be realized only by means of samādhi, or deep concentration.
units.iast:
viparītātmatā-sphūrtir eva muktir itīryate|
sadā samāhitasyaiva saiṣā sidhyati nānyathā||

units.label: Verse 845
units.deva:
न वेष-भाषाभिर् अमुष्य मुक्तिर् या
केवलाखण्ड-चिद्-आत्मना स्थितिः।
तत्-सिद्धये स्वात्मनि सर्वदा स्थितो
जह्याद् अहन्तां ममताम् उपाधौ॥
units.translation: It is neither by the dress that a person wears, nor by the language that he speaks, that anyone can attain liberation. Liberation lies in being established in the Ātman, which is at once indivisible and conscious. It is only by giving up all ideas of ‘I and mine’ inasmuch as they belong to the adjuncts or the upādhis, and by being established in the Ātman, that one might realize it.
units.iast:
na veṣa-bhāṣābhir amuṣya muktir yā
kevalākhaṇḍa-cid-ātmanā sthitiḥ|
tat-siddhaye svātmani sarvadā sthito
jahyād ahantāṃ mamatām upādhau||

units.label: Verse 846
units.deva:
स्वात्म-तत्त्वं समालम्ब्य कुर्यात् प्रकृति-नाशनम्।
तेनैव मुक्तो भवति नान्यथा कर्म-कोटिभिः॥
units.translation: It is only knowledge that destroys ignorance; and knowledge alone confers liberation. That is why liberation cannot be attained by the mere performance of rituals, even though they should be repeated crores of times.
units.iast:
svātma-tattvaṃ samālambya kuryāt prakṛti-nāśanam|
tenaiva mukto bhavati nānyathā karma-koṭibhiḥ||

units.label: Verse 847
units.deva:
ज्ञात्वा देवं सर्व-पाशापहानिः
क्षीणैः क्लेशैर् जन्म-मृत्यु-प्रहानिः।
इत्येवैषा वैदिकी वाग् ब्रवीति
क्लेश-क्षत्यां जन्म-मृत्यु-प्रहाणिम्॥
units.translation: It is only the knowledge of the self-effulgent Brahman that can destroy all the bonds. When all the kleśas are destroyed, the cycle of birth and death comes to an end. That is what the Śruti says. ((SvetU.1.11) (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
jñātvā devaṃ sarva-pāśāpahāniḥ
kṣīṇaiḥ kleśair janma-mṛtyu-prahāniḥ|
ityevaiṣā vaidikī vāg bravīti
kleśa-kṣatyāṃ janma-mṛtyu-prahāṇim||

units.label: Verse 848
units.deva:
भूयो जन्माद्यप्रसक्तिर् विमुक्तिः
क्लेश-क्षत्यां भाति जन्माद्यभावः।
क्लेश-क्षत्या हेतुर् आत्मैक-निष्ठा
तस्मात् कार्या ह्यात्म-निष्ठा मुमुक्षोः॥
units.translation: It is the absence of the possibility of rebirth that constitutes liberation; and by the destruction of the kleśas, all such possibilities are put an end to. That is why the aspirant after liberation should be ever devoted to the Ātman.
units.iast:
bhūyo janmādyaprasaktir vimuktiḥ
kleśa-kṣatyāṃ bhāti janmādyabhāvaḥ|
kleśa-kṣatyā hetur ātmaika-niṣṭhā
tasmāt kāryā hyātma-niṣṭhā mumukṣoḥ||

units.label: Verse 849
units.deva:
क्लेशाः स्युर् वासना एव जन्तोर् जन्मादि-कारणम्।
ज्ञान-निष्ठाग्निना दाहे तासां नो जन्म-हेतुता॥
units.translation: The kleśas constitute the sources of rebirth; for they are the subtle forms of desire. When the kleśas become parched in the fire of the knowledge of the Ātman, they can no longer be a source of rebirth.
units.iast:
kleśāḥ syur vāsanā eva jantor janmādi-kāraṇam|
jñāna-niṣṭhāgninā dāhe tāsāṃ no janma-hetutā||

units.label: Verse 850
units.deva:
बीजान्यग्नि-प्रदग्धानि न रोहन्ति यथा पुनः।
ज्ञान-दग्धैस् तथा क्लेशैर् नात्मा सम्पद्यते पुनः॥
units.translation: Just as the seeds that have been parched in the fire lose their power of germination, so also the kleśas which have their origin in thought lose all their potency when once the knowledge of Ātman has been attained.
units.iast:
bījānyagni-pradagdhāni na rohanti yathā punaḥ|
jñāna-dagdhais tathā kleśair nātmā sampadyate punaḥ||

units.label: Verse 851
units.deva:
तस्मान् मुमुक्षोः कर्तव्या ज्ञान-निष्ठा प्रयत्नतः।
निःशेष-वासना-क्षत्यै विपरीत-निवृत्तये॥
units.translation: Therefore, let the aspirant after knowledge pursue it with devotion and diligence, so that he might be able to overcome all desires, and dispel all wrong ideas as to the nature of the Ātman.
units.iast:
tasmān mumukṣoḥ kartavyā jñāna-niṣṭhā prayatnataḥ|
niḥśeṣa-vāsanā-kṣatyai viparīta-nivṛttaye||

units.label: Verse 852
units.deva:
ज्ञाननिष्ठातत्परस्य नैव कर्मोपयुज्यते।
कर्मणो ज्ञाननिष्ठाया न सिध्यति सहस्थितिः॥
units.translation: In the pursuit of knowledge, ritual is of no use To one who is devoted to the pursuit of knowledge, the observance of rituals is of no use. The reason for it is that the observance of rituals and the devotion to knowledge cannot co-exist.
units.iast:
jñānaniṣṭhātatparasya naiva karmopayujyate|
karmaṇo jñānaniṣṭhāyā na sidhyati sahasthitiḥ||

units.label: Verse 853
units.deva:
परस्-पर-विरुद्धत्वात् तयोर् भिन्न-स्वभावयोः।
कर्तृत्व-भावना-पूर्वं कर्म ज्ञानं विलक्षणम्॥
units.translation: There is considerable incompatibility between knowledge and rituals inasmuch as their natures are entirely antithetical. It is only he who regards himself as the agent of action that can preform the rituals. But the nature of knowledge is altogether different and it dispels all such ideas.
units.iast:
paras-para-viruddhatvāt tayor bhinna-svabhāvayoḥ|
kartṛtva-bhāvanā-pūrvaṃ karma jñānaṃ vilakṣaṇam||

units.label: Verse 854
units.deva:
देहात्म-बुद्धेर् विच्छित्त्यै ज्ञानं कर्म विवृद्धये।
अज्ञान-मूलकं कर्म ज्ञानं तूभय-नाशकम्॥
units.translation: All the wrong ideas beginning with the idea of regarding one’s physical body as the Ātman are eradicated by knowledge. It is only as long as one is ignorant of the Ātman that rituals have a place. But the knowledge of the Ātman destroys both ignorance and the love of rituals.
units.iast:
dehātma-buddher vicchittyai jñānaṃ karma vivṛddhaye|
ajñāna-mūlakaṃ karma jñānaṃ tūbhaya-nāśakam||

units.label: Verse 855
units.deva:
ज्ञानेन कर्मणो योगः कथं सिध्यति वैरिणा।
सह-योगो न घटते यथा तिमिर-तेजसोः॥
units.translation: How is it possible for one to perform the prescribed rituals while engaged in the pursuit of knowledge, inasmuch as they are incompatible? It is as impossible as that light and darkness should co-exist.
units.iast:
jñānena karmaṇo yogaḥ kathaṃ sidhyati vairiṇā|
saha-yogo na ghaṭate yathā timira-tejasoḥ||

units.label: Verse 856
units.deva:
निमेषोन्मेषयोर् वापि तथैव ज्ञान-कर्मणोः।
प्रतीचीं पश्यतः पुंसां कुतः प्राची-विलोकनम्।
प्रत्यक्-प्रवण-चित्तस्य कुतः कर्मणि योग्यता॥
units.translation: No one can keep one’s eyes open and closed at the same time. It is equally impossible to combine knowledge and rituals. Can one who is looking eastwards see what is in the west? Is it ever possible for one whose mind is directed towards the innermost Ātman to take part in external activities?
units.iast:
nimeṣonmeṣayor vāpi tathaiva jñāna-karmaṇoḥ|
pratīcīṃ paśyataḥ puṃsāṃ kutaḥ prācī-vilokanam|
pratyak-pravaṇa-cittasya kutaḥ karmaṇi yogyatā||

units.label: Verse 857
units.deva:
ज्ञानैक-निष्ठा-निरतस्य भिक्षोर्
नैवावकाशोऽस्ति हि कर्म-तन्त्रे।
तद् एव कर्मास्य तद् एव सन्ध्या
तद् एव सर्वं न ततोऽन्यद् अस्ति॥
units.translation: A man of renunciation, who is solely intent upon the pursuit of knowledge, has nothing to gain from the Śāstras which enjoin the observance of rituals. He observes no ritual other than the pursuit of knowledge; that alone is his ‘Sandhyā (bath)’; but alone is his all in all and there is nothing else.
units.iast:
jñānaika-niṣṭhā-niratasya bhikṣor
naivāvakāśo’sti hi karma-tantre|
tad eva karmāsya tad eva sandhyā
tad eva sarvaṃ na tato’nyad asti||

units.label: Verse 858
units.deva:
बुद्धि-कल्पित-मालिन्य-क्षालनं स्नानम् आत्मनः।
तेनैव शुद्धिर् एतस्य न मृदा न जलेन च॥
units.translation: The removal of all the impurities which the intellect has deposited upon the Ātman constitutes his bath. It is only in this way that he may purify himself, and not by resorting to the use of earth and water.
units.iast:
buddhi-kalpita-mālinya-kṣālanaṃ snānam ātmanaḥ|
tenaiva śuddhir etasya na mṛdā na jalena ca||

units.label: Verse 859
units.deva:
स्व-स्व-रूपे मनः-स्थानम् अनुष्ठानं तद् इष्यते।
करण-त्रय-साध्यं यत् तन् मृषा तद्-असत्यतः॥
units.translation: By putting his mind in its real nature, he performs all the Vedic duties that are enjoined upon him. When the instruments of knowledge and action, such as the karmendriyas and the jñānendriyas as well as the mind are all unreal, anything that may be achieved by means of them must be equally unreal.
units.iast:
sva-sva-rūpe manaḥ-sthānam anuṣṭhānaṃ tad iṣyate|
karaṇa-traya-sādhyaṃ yat tan mṛṣā tad-asatyataḥ||

units.label: Verse 860
units.deva:
विनिषिध्याखिलं दृश्यं स्व-स्व-रूपेण या स्थितिः।
सा सन्ध्या तद् अनुष्ठानं तद् दानं तद्धि भोजनम्॥
units.translation: When one is established in one’s real nature and has excluded from one’s mind the phenomena of the world, that constitutes the performance of ‘Sandhyā’, the observance of religious duties, the offering of gifts, and even the taking of one’s food.
units.iast:
viniṣidhyākhilaṃ dṛśyaṃ sva-sva-rūpeṇa yā sthitiḥ|
sā sandhyā tad anuṣṭhānaṃ tad dānaṃ taddhi bhojanam||

units.label: Verse 861
units.deva:
विज्ञात-परमार्थानां शुद्ध-सत्त्वात्मनां सताम्।
यतीनां किम् अनुष्ठानं स्वानुसन्धिं विनापरम्॥
units.translation: To one whose heart is pure and who has renounced one’s all, there is no other spiritual discipline necessary. It would be enough if one should seek and realize the nature of the Supreme Reality.
units.iast:
vijñāta-paramārthānāṃ śuddha-sattvātmanāṃ satām|
yatīnāṃ kim anuṣṭhānaṃ svānusandhiṃ vināparam||

units.label: Verse 862
units.deva:
तस्मात् क्रियान्तरं त्यक्त्वा ज्ञान-निष्ठा-परो यतिः।
सदात्म-निष्ठया तिष्ठेन् निश्चलस् तत्-परायणः॥
units.translation: Therefore, let the man of renunciation who is devoted to knowledge give up all other actions and rituals. Let him be ever absorbed and be established in the Supreme Ātman.
units.iast:
tasmāt kriyāntaraṃ tyaktvā jñāna-niṣṭhā-paro yatiḥ|
sadātma-niṣṭhayā tiṣṭhen niścalas tat-parāyaṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 863
units.deva:
कर्तव्यं स्वोचितं कर्म योगम् आरोढुम् इच्छता।
आरोहणं कुर्वतस् तु कर्म नारोहणं मतम्॥
units.translation: He who desires to attain the goal of yoga, and has not yet attained it, must necessarily perform his obligatory duties. The learned however are of the opinion that such a course is not incumbent upon him who has attained the goal. ((BhG.6.3) (Bhagavad Gītā))
units.iast:
kartavyaṃ svocitaṃ karma yogam āroḍhum icchatā|
ārohaṇaṃ kurvatas tu karma nārohaṇaṃ matam||

units.label: Verse 864
units.deva:
योगं समारोहति यो मुमुक्षुः
क्रियान्तरं तस्य न युक्तम् ईषत्।
क्रियान्तर्-आसक्त-मनाः पतत्य् असौ
ताल-द्रुमारोहण-कर्तृवद् ध्रुवम्॥
units.translation: The aspirant after liberation who has attained the goal of yoga becomes unfit to perform the rituals, even though they happen to be of a minor nature. He is as sure to fall as one who tries to climb up a palm tree while his mind is wanting elsewhere.
units.iast:
yogaṃ samārohati yo mumukṣuḥ
kriyāntaraṃ tasya na yuktam īṣat|
kriyāntar-āsakta-manāḥ pataty asau
tāla-drumārohaṇa-kartṛvad dhruvam||

units.label: Verse 865
units.deva:
योगारूढस्य सिद्धस्य कृत-कृत्यस्य धीमतः।
नास्त्येव हि बहिर्-दृष्टिः का कथा तत्र कर्मणाम्।
दृश्यानुविद्धः कथितः समाधिः सविकल्पकः॥
units.translation: The perfected person is the wise one has attained the goal of yoga. He has achieved all that which has to be be achieved. His mind is not turned towards external objects, nor can he perform actions in the external world. Such is the nature of savikalpa samādhi, considered in association with the objects of knowledge.
units.iast:
yogārūḍhasya siddhasya kṛta-kṛtyasya dhīmataḥ|
nāstyeva hi bahir-dṛṣṭiḥ kā kathā tatra karmaṇām|
dṛśyānuviddhaḥ kathitaḥ samādhiḥ savikalpakaḥ||

units.label: Verse 866
units.deva:
शुद्धोऽहं बुद्धोऽहं प्रत्यग्-रूपेण नित्य-सिद्धोऽहम्।
शान्तोऽहम् अनन्तोऽहं सतत-परानन्द-सिन्धुर् एवाहम्॥
units.translation: Speaking of the Ātman, the Śruti says, ‘I am the pure, inmost Ātman, untouched by ignorance, and ever existent. I am at once tranquil and limitless. I am an ocean of eternal bliss.
units.iast:
śuddho’haṃ buddho’haṃ pratyag-rūpeṇa nitya-siddho’ham|
śānto’ham ananto’haṃ satata-parānanda-sindhur evāham||

units.label: Verse 867
units.deva:
आद्योऽहम् अनाद्योऽहं वाङ्-मनसा साध्य-वस्तु-मात्रोऽहम्।
निगम-वचो-वेद्योऽहम् अनवद्याखण्ड-बोध-रूपोऽहम्॥
units.translation: I have existed prior to all else. I am without a beginning. All which may be comprehended by means of words and by the mind, that I am. I am comprehended only by the Śruti. Pure knowledge, perfect and indivisible – such is my nature. ((KenU.1.5) (Kena Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
ādyo’ham anādyo’haṃ vāṅ-manasā sādhya-vastu-mātro’ham|
nigama-vaco-vedyo’ham anavadyākhaṇḍa-bodha-rūpo’ham||

units.label: Verse 868
units.deva:
विदिताविदितान्योऽहं माया-तत्-कार्य-लेश-शून्योऽहम्।
केवल-दृग्-आत्मकोऽहं संविन्-मात्रः सकृद्-विभातोऽहम्॥
units.translation: I differ from the known and I am other than the unknown. I am free from Māyā and all its effects. I am the witnessing consciousness; I am pure knowledge, ever effulgent.
units.iast:
viditāviditānyo’haṃ māyā-tat-kārya-leśa-śūnyo’ham|
kevala-dṛg-ātmako’haṃ saṃvin-mātraḥ sakṛd-vibhāto’ham||

units.label: Verse 869
units.deva:
अपरोऽहम् अनपरोऽहं बहिर् अन्तश् चापि पूर्ण एवाहम्।
अजरोऽहम् अक्षरोऽहं नित्यानन्दोऽहम् अद्वितीयोऽहम्॥
units.translation: I am neither the effect nor the cause of anything. Within me and around me there is nothing other than the infinite Ātman. Old age, decay and death are not for me. I am imperishable, for I am Bliss Eternal; I am the one without a second. ((BrhUEng.2.5.19) (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
aparo’ham anaparo’haṃ bahir antaś cāpi pūrṇa evāham|
ajaro’ham akṣaro’haṃ nityānando’ham advitīyo’ham||

units.label: Verse 870
units.deva:
प्रत्यग्-अभिन्नम् अखण्डं सत्य-ज्ञानादि-लक्षणं शुद्धम्।
श्रुत्यवगम्यं तथ्यं ब्रह्मैवाहं परं ज्योतिः॥
units.translation: I am Brahman which is at once the supreme light, and the supreme reality, and which is in no way other than the innermost Ātman, which is indivisible, and ever pure, which is of the nature of sat-cid-ānanda and which is comprehended only by what the Śruti says.
units.iast:
pratyag-abhinnam akhaṇḍaṃ satya-jñānādi-lakṣaṇaṃ śuddham|
śrutyavagamyaṃ tathyaṃ brahmaivāhaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥ||

units.label: Verse 871
units.deva:
एवं सन्-मात्र-गाहिन्या वृत्त्या तन्-मात्र-गाहकैः।
शब्दैः समर्पितं वस्तु भावयेन् निश्चलो यतिः॥
units.translation: It is in this way that the man of renunciation should meditate through all the diverse modifications of the mind, upon the nature of pure existence as the sole object of thought, in so far as it is indirectly presented through the words of the Śruti.
units.iast:
evaṃ san-mātra-gāhinyā vṛttyā tan-mātra-gāhakaiḥ|
śabdaiḥ samarpitaṃ vastu bhāvayen niścalo yatiḥ||

units.label: Verse 872
units.deva:
कामादि-दृश्य-प्रविलाप-पूर्वकं
शुद्धोऽहम् इत्यादिक-शब्द-मिश्रः।
दृश्येव निष्ठस्य य एष भावः
शब्दानुविद्धः कथितः समाधिः॥
units.translation: In the first instance, one begins with the following concept: ‘I am the witness of the desires that arise in me’. Then step by step, one comes to realize, as pointed out by the Śruti. ‘I am pure’. It is in this way that one should meditate upon the Ātman with entire devotion. Such is the process by which one attains savikalpa samādhi, in association with the words of the Śruti.
units.iast:
kāmādi-dṛśya-pravilāpa-pūrvakaṃ
śuddho’ham ityādika-śabda-miśraḥ|
dṛśyeva niṣṭhasya ya eṣa bhāvaḥ
śabdānuviddhaḥ kathitaḥ samādhiḥ||

units.label: Verse 873
units.deva:
दृश्यस्यापि च साक्षित्वात् समुल्लेखनम् आत्मनि।
निवर्तक-मनोऽवस्था निर्विकल्प इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: Nirvikalpa samādhi Where the mind functions (the reality of the vṛttis is) no longer, where there are no (real) objects of knowledge, and where the Ātman, the witnessing consciousness, is the sole reality, there arises the experience of nirvikalpa samādhi.
units.iast:
dṛśyasyāpi ca sākṣitvāt samullekhanam ātmani|
nivartaka-mano’vasthā nirvikalpa itīryate||

units.label: Verse 874
units.deva:
सविकल्प-समाधिं यो दीर्घ-कालं निरन्तरम्।
संस्कार-पूर्वकं कुर्यान् निर्विकल्पोऽस्य सिध्यति॥
units.translation: One who has practised savikalpa samādhi for a long time becomes at long last fit to attain nirvikalpa samādhi, by virtue of the residual impression of what he has practised previously, at an earlier stage.
units.iast:
savikalpa-samādhiṃ yo dīrgha-kālaṃ nirantaram|
saṃskāra-pūrvakaṃ kuryān nirvikalpo’sya sidhyati||

units.label: Verse 875
units.deva:
निर्विकल्पक-समाधि-निष्ठया
तिष्ठतो भवति नित्यता ध्रुवम्।
उद्भवाद्यपगतिर् निर्-अर्गला
नित्य-निश्चल-निरस्त-निर्वृतिः॥
units.translation: It is certain that one who is solely intent upon the realization of Brahman in nirvikalpa samādhi becomes the eternal Brahman. For such the vicious cycle of birth and death has come to an end. Such a person attains the bliss that knows no obstacles, but which is eternal in nature, changeless and continuous.
units.iast:
nirvikalpaka-samādhi-niṣṭhayā
tiṣṭhato bhavati nityatā dhruvam|
udbhavādyapagatir nir-argalā
nitya-niścala-nirasta-nirvṛtiḥ||

units.label: Verse 876
units.deva:
विद्वान् अहम् इदम् इति वा किञ्चिद्
बाह्याभ्यन्तर-वेदन-शून्यः।
स्वानन्दामृत-सिन्धु-निमग्नस्
तूष्णीम् आस्ते कश्चिद् अनन्यः॥
units.translation: Rare indeed are the knowers of Brahman; for they are not other than Brahman. They are not conscious of anything within them such as the idea of ‘I and mine’; nor are they conscious of anything outside them such as ‘this or that’. They are lost, as it were, in the infinite ocean of bliss, which is the bliss of the inmost Ātman, and they remain for ever absorbed in a grand silence.
units.iast:
vidvān aham idam iti vā kiñcid
bāhyābhyantara-vedana-śūnyaḥ|
svānandāmṛta-sindhu-nimagnas
tūṣṇīm āste kaścid ananyaḥ||

units.label: Verse 877
units.deva:
निर्विकल्पं परं ब्रह्म यत् तस्मिन्न् एव निष्ठिताः।
एते धन्या एव मुक्ता जीवन्तोऽपि बहिर्-दृशाम्॥
units.translation: They are indeed the most fortunate who have lost their individuality in that Supreme Being. They alone are liberated, even though they might seem to be (walking, talking) embodied beings as far as the others are concerned.
units.iast:
nirvikalpaṃ paraṃ brahma yat tasminn eva niṣṭhitāḥ|
ete dhanyā eva muktā jīvanto’pi bahir-dṛśām||

units.label: Verse 878
units.deva:
यथा समाधि-त्रितयं यत्नेन क्रियते हृदि।
तथैव बाह्य-देशेऽपि कार्यं द्वैत-निवृत्तये॥
units.translation: All these three types of samādhi, the savikalpa either in association with the objects of knowledge, or with the Śruti, and the nirvikalpa should be practised diligently. By such diligent observance, all that is within oneself, and all that which is without become negated; and it is only then that all duality comes to an end.
units.iast:
yathā samādhi-tritayaṃ yatnena kriyate hṛdi|
tathaiva bāhya-deśe’pi kāryaṃ dvaita-nivṛttaye||

units.label: Verse 879
units.deva:
तत्प्रकारं प्रवक्ष्यामि निशामय समासतः।
अधिष्ठानं परं ब्रह्म सच्-चिदानन्द-लक्षणम्॥
units.translation: I shall now recapitulate briefly the nature of samādhi. Listen with attention. The Supreme Brahman is of the nature of existence-knowledge-bliss and is the substratum of all.
units.iast:
tatprakāraṃ pravakṣyāmi niśāmaya samāsataḥ|
adhiṣṭhānaṃ paraṃ brahma sac-cidānanda-lakṣaṇam||

units.label: Verse 880
units.deva:
तत्राध्यस्तम् इदं भाति नाम-रूपात्मकं जगत्।
सत्त्वं चित्त्वं तथानन्द-रूपं यद् ब्रह्मणस् त्रयम्॥
units.translation: The universe of name and form seems to exist only in so far as it is superimposed upon Brahman. In reality, it is upon the triune nature of Brahman as sat-cid-ānanda that they have their being.
units.iast:
tatrādhyastam idaṃ bhāti nāma-rūpātmakaṃ jagat|
sattvaṃ cittvaṃ tathānanda-rūpaṃ yad brahmaṇas trayam||

units.label: Verse 881
units.deva:
अध्यस्त-जगतो रूपं नाम-रूपम् इदं द्वयम्।
एतानि सच्-चिद्-आनन्द-नाम-रूपाणि पञ्च च॥
units.translation: In addition to those three, two different attributes are added from the world of phenomena viz. name and form. All these five entities become blended together. Thus name, form, existence, consciousness and bliss become intermingled.
units.iast:
adhyasta-jagato rūpaṃ nāma-rūpam idaṃ dvayam|
etāni sac-cid-ānanda-nāma-rūpāṇi pañca ca||

units.label: Verse 882
units.deva:
एकी-कृत्योच्यते मूर्खैर् इदं विश्वम् इति भ्रमात्।
शैत्यं श्वेतं रसं द्राव्यं तरङ्ग इति नाम च॥
units.translation: Those who are unenlightened, mix together the real (existence, consciousness and bliss) and the unreal (name and form): and they refer to the combination of the two as ‘this universe’. It is as though one should put together the diverse factors such as coldness, whiteness, taste, liquidity, and the name ‘wave’ and describe it all together and say, ‘This is a wave’.
units.iast:
ekī-kṛtyocyate mūrkhair idaṃ viśvam iti bhramāt|
śaityaṃ śvetaṃ rasaṃ drāvyaṃ taraṅga iti nāma ca||

units.label: Verse 883
units.deva:
एकी-कृत्य तरङ्गोऽयम् इति निर्दिश्यते यथा।
आरोपिते नाम-रूपे उपेक्ष्य ब्रह्मणस् ततः॥
units.translation: It is only by superimposing the name (nāma) and the form (rūpa) that people say, ‘This is a wave’. It is in the same way that people superimpose name and form upon Brahman also. But when these superimpositions are taken away, what remains is Brahman alone.
units.iast:
ekī-kṛtya taraṅgo’yam iti nirdiśyate yathā|
āropite nāma-rūpe upekṣya brahmaṇas tataḥ||

units.label: Verse 884
units.deva:
स्व-रूप-मात्र-ग्रहणं समाधिर् बाह्य आदिमः।
सच्-चिद्-आनन्द-रूपस्य सकाशाद् ब्रह्मणो यतिः॥
units.translation: Therefore, a man of renunciation should separate name and form from Brahman, in order to realize Brahman which is of the nature of existence-consciousness-bliss by means of concentration.
units.iast:
sva-rūpa-mātra-grahaṇaṃ samādhir bāhya ādimaḥ|
sac-cid-ānanda-rūpasya sakāśād brahmaṇo yatiḥ||

units.label: Verse 885
units.deva:
नाम-रूपे पृथक् कृत्वा ब्रह्मण्येव विलापयन्।
अधिष्ठानं परं ब्रह्म सच्-चिद्-आनन्दम् अद्वयम्।
यत् तद् एवाहम् इत्येव निश्चितात्मा भवेद् ध्रुवम्॥
units.translation: It is in this way that by merging everything in Brahman that the man of renunciation becomes convinced, and knows for certain, ‘I am undoubtedly the Supreme Brahman, non-dual, of the nature of existence-knowledge-blīss, and that which constitutes the substratum of all names and forms.
units.iast:
nāma-rūpe pṛthak kṛtvā brahmaṇyeva vilāpayan|
adhiṣṭhānaṃ paraṃ brahma sac-cid-ānandam advayam|
yat tad evāham ityeva niścitātmā bhaved dhruvam||

units.label: Verse 886
units.deva:
इयं भूर् न सन् नापि तोयं न तेजो
न वायुर् न खं नापि तत्-कार्य-जातम्।
यद् एषाम् अधिष्ठान-भूतं विशुद्धं
सद् एकं परं सत् तद् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: Neither earth, nor water, nor fire, nor air, nor space, nor their products constitute Brahman. As for me, I am none other than the non-dual Brahman, who is pure existence and the substratum of all.
units.iast:
iyaṃ bhūr na san nāpi toyaṃ na tejo
na vāyur na khaṃ nāpi tat-kārya-jātam|
yad eṣām adhiṣṭhāna-bhūtaṃ viśuddhaṃ
sad ekaṃ paraṃ sat tad evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 887
units.deva:
न शब्दो न रूपं न च स्पर्शको वा
तथा नो रसो नापि गन्धो न चान्यः।
यद् एषाम् अधिष्ठान-भूतं विशुद्धं
सद् एकं परं सत् तद् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: I am neither sound, nor form, nor touch, nor smell, nor taste, nor even anything other than these. I am none other than the supreme non-dual Brahman, who is pure existence and the substratum of all.
units.iast:
na śabdo na rūpaṃ na ca sparśako vā
tathā no raso nāpi gandho na cānyaḥ|
yad eṣām adhiṣṭhāna-bhūtaṃ viśuddhaṃ
sad ekaṃ paraṃ sat tad evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 888
units.deva:
न सद् द्रव्य-जातं गुणा न क्रिया वा
न जातिर् विशेषो न चान्यः कदापि।
यद् एषाम् अधिष्ठान-भूतं विशुद्धं
सद् एकं परं सत् तद् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: Neither the dravyas, nor the guṇas, nor the kriyās, nor jāti, nor viśeṣa, nor anything else constitute Brahman. Therefore I am none other than the supreme non-dual Brahman who is pure existence and the substratum of all.
units.iast:
na sad dravya-jātaṃ guṇā na kriyā vā
na jātir viśeṣo na cānyaḥ kadāpi|
yad eṣām adhiṣṭhāna-bhūtaṃ viśuddhaṃ
sad ekaṃ paraṃ sat tad evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 889
units.deva:
न देहो न चाक्षाणि न प्राण-वायुर्
मनो नापि बुद्धिर् न चित्तं ह्यहन्-धीः।
यद् एषाम् अधिष्ठान-भूतं विशुद्धं
सद् एकं परं सत् तद् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: I am neither the body, nor the senses, nor the vital force, nor the mind, nor the intellect, nor the thinking faculty, nor the ego. I am none other than the non-dual Brahman who is pure existence and the substratum of all.
units.iast:
na deho na cākṣāṇi na prāṇa-vāyur
mano nāpi buddhir na cittaṃ hyahan-dhīḥ|
yad eṣām adhiṣṭhāna-bhūtaṃ viśuddhaṃ
sad ekaṃ paraṃ sat tad evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 890
units.deva:
न देशो न कालो न दिग् वापि सत् स्यान्
न वस्त्वन्तरं स्थूल-सूक्ष्मादि-रूपम्।
यद् एषाम् अधिष्ठान-भूतं विशुद्धं
सद् एकं परं सत् तद् एवाहम् अस्मि॥
units.translation: Neither space, nor time, nor the directions, nor other things, nor the gross world, nor the subtle constitute Brahman. I am none other than the non-dual Brahman, who is pure existence, and is the substratum of all.
units.iast:
na deśo na kālo na dig vāpi sat syān
na vastvantaraṃ sthūla-sūkṣmādi-rūpam|
yad eṣām adhiṣṭhāna-bhūtaṃ viśuddhaṃ
sad ekaṃ paraṃ sat tad evāham asmi||

units.label: Verse 891
units.deva:
एतद् दृश्यं नाम-रूपात्मकं यो
ऽधिष्ठानं तद् ब्रह्म सत्यं सद् एति॥
गच्छंस् तिष्टन् वा शयानोऽपि नित्यं
कुर्याद् विद्वान् बाह्य-दृश्यानुविद्धम्॥
units.translation: The wise man who is ever absorbed in the practice of concentration, and to whom the whole of the external world of knowledge becomes blended in the consciousness of Brahman, knows at all times, whether he is walking, or standing or lying down, that in reality the universe of name and form is none other than Brahman, who alone exists and is the substratum of all.
units.iast:
etad dṛśyaṃ nāma-rūpātmakaṃ yo
’dhiṣṭhānaṃ tad brahma satyaṃ sad eti||
gacchaṃs tiṣṭan vā śayāno’pi nityaṃ
kuryād vidvān bāhya-dṛśyānuviddham||

units.label: Verse 892
units.deva:
अध्यस्त-नाम-रूपादि-प्रविलापेन निर्मलम्।
अद्वैतं परमानन्दं ब्रह्मैवास्मीति भावयेत्॥
units.translation: One should therefore meditate in the following manner; ‘I am Brahman, the non-dual Supreme Bliss’. One should merge in Brahman all name and form, for they are superimposed on Brahman.
units.iast:
adhyasta-nāma-rūpādi-pravilāpena nirmalam|
advaitaṃ paramānandaṃ brahmaivāsmīti bhāvayet||

units.label: Verse 893
units.deva:
निर्विकारं निराकारं निरञ्जनम् अनामयम्।
आद्यन्त-रहितं पूर्णं ब्रह्मैवाहं न संशयः॥
units.translation: That unchanging, formless, untainted Brahman, who knows no sorrow and who is without a beginning and an end, and is all-pervading, That I am; and there is no doubt about it.
units.iast:
nirvikāraṃ nirākāraṃ nirañjanam anāmayam|
ādyanta-rahitaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahmaivāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 894
units.deva:
निष्कलङ्कं निरातङ्कं त्रिविध-च्छेद-वर्जितम्।
आनन्दम् अक्षरं मुक्तं ब्रह्मैवास्मीति भावयेत्॥
units.translation: One should meditate in the following manner: ‘I am Brahman, who is taintless, who is free from fear; and also free from the three kinds of limitations imposed by time, space and the nature of things, and who is ever blissful, imperishable and free.’
units.iast:
niṣkalaṅkaṃ nirātaṅkaṃ trividha-ccheda-varjitam|
ānandam akṣaraṃ muktaṃ brahmaivāsmīti bhāvayet||

units.label: Verse 895
units.deva:
निर्विशेषं निराभासं नित्य-मुक्तम् अविक्रियम्।
प्रज्ञानैक-रसं सत्यं ब्रह्मैवास्मीति भावयेत्॥
units.translation: One should therefore meditate in the following manner: ‘I am Brahman who is free from all attributes, whose nature is not reflected in anything else, who is ever free, who undergoes no change, and who is of the nature of pure knowledge, and of nothing else, and who is ever existing.’
units.iast:
nirviśeṣaṃ nirābhāsaṃ nitya-muktam avikriyam|
prajñānaika-rasaṃ satyaṃ brahmaivāsmīti bhāvayet||

units.label: Verse 896
units.deva:
शुद्धं बुद्धं तत्त्व-सिद्धं परं प्रत्यग् अखण्डितम्।
स्व-प्रकाशं पराकाशं ब्रह्मैवास्मीति भावयेत्॥
units.translation: One should therefore meditate thus: ‘I am Brahman, who is ever pure, who is untainted by ignorance; who is realizable only by means of the right knowledge of Brahman, who is the supreme, the inmost and indivisible, the self-effulgent.’
units.iast:
śuddhaṃ buddhaṃ tattva-siddhaṃ paraṃ pratyag akhaṇḍitam|
sva-prakāśaṃ parākāśaṃ brahmaivāsmīti bhāvayet||

units.label: Verse 897
units.deva:
सुसूक्ष्मम् अस्तिता-मात्रं निर्विकल्पं महत्तमम्।
केवलं परमाद्वैतं ब्रह्मैवास्मीति भावयेत्॥
units.translation: One should therefore meditate in the following manner: ‘I am the supreme non-dual Brahman, whose nature is very subtle, who is pure existence, the absolute, the greatest of the great and ever pure.’
units.iast:
susūkṣmam astitā-mātraṃ nirvikalpaṃ mahattamam|
kevalaṃ paramādvaitaṃ brahmaivāsmīti bhāvayet||

units.label: Verse 898
units.deva:
इत्येवं निर्विकारादि-शब्द-मात्र-समर्पितम्।
ध्यायतः केवलं वस्तु लक्ष्ये चित्तं प्रतिष्ठति॥
units.translation: One who thus meditates upon that pure reality, whose nature is indicated by such expressions as being devoid of change and the like, has one’s mind established in Brahman, the goal.
units.iast:
ityevaṃ nirvikārādi-śabda-mātra-samarpitam|
dhyāyataḥ kevalaṃ vastu lakṣye cittaṃ pratiṣṭhati||

units.label: Verse 899
units.deva:
ब्रह्मानन्द-रसावेशाद् एकी-भूय तद्-आत्मना।
वृत्तेर् या निश्चलावस्था स समाधिर् अकल्पकः॥
units.translation: That firm state in which the intellect is absorbed in the bliss of Brahman and has become identical with the real nature of Brahman is known as nirvikalpa samādhi. lt is called ecstasy, or deep concentration at the absolute plane.
units.iast:
brahmānanda-rasāveśād ekī-bhūya tad-ātmanā|
vṛtter yā niścalāvasthā sa samādhir akalpakaḥ||

units.label: Verse 900
units.deva:
उत्थाने वाप्यनुत्थानेऽप्यप्रमत्तो जितेन्द्रियः।
समाधि-षट्कं कुर्वीत सर्वदा प्रयतो यतिः॥
units.translation: A man of renunciation should therefore give up all carelessness; he should have firm control over his senses, and practise with diligence the six types of concentration, whether he is standing or lying down.
units.iast:
utthāne vāpyanutthāne’pyapramatto jitendriyaḥ|
samādhi-ṣaṭkaṃ kurvīta sarvadā prayato yatiḥ||

units.label: Verse 901
units.deva:
विपरीतार्थ-धीर् यावन् न निःशेषं निवर्तते।
स्व-रूप-स्फुरणं यावन् न प्रसिध्यत्यनर्गलम्।
तावत् समाधि-षट्केन नयेत् कालं निरन्तरम्॥
units.translation: One should therefore spend all one’s time in the unceasing practice of all these six varieties of concentration, until all the wrong ideas as to the nature of the Ātman have been eliminated, and until there is an uninterrupted realization of one’s ultimate nature.
units.iast:
viparītārtha-dhīr yāvan na niḥśeṣaṃ nivartate|
sva-rūpa-sphuraṇaṃ yāvan na prasidhyatyanargalam|
tāvat samādhi-ṣaṭkena nayet kālaṃ nirantaram||

units.label: Verse 902
units.deva:
न प्रमादोऽत्र कर्तव्यो विदुषा मोक्षम् इच्छता।
प्रमादे जृम्भते माया सूर्यापाये तमो यथा॥
units.translation: While engaged in the practice of concentration, the learned aspirant after liberation should be on guard against being careless. The reason is that when one is careless, Māyā settles down like the onset of darkness at nightfall.
units.iast:
na pramādo’tra kartavyo viduṣā mokṣam icchatā|
pramāde jṛmbhate māyā sūryāpāye tamo yathā||

units.label: Verse 903
units.deva:
स्वानु-भूतिं परित्यज्य न तिष्ठन्ति क्षणं बुधाः।
स्वानु-भूतौ प्रमादो यः स मृत्युर् न यमः सताम्॥
units.translation: The wise one should not therefore rest even for a moment or abstain from the pursuit of the knowledge of the Ātman. To a good man, Yama is not the cause of death, but it is indifference regarding the knowledge of the Ātman that brings about his death.
units.iast:
svānu-bhūtiṃ parityajya na tiṣṭhanti kṣaṇaṃ budhāḥ|
svānu-bhūtau pramādo yaḥ sa mṛtyur na yamaḥ satām||

units.label: Verse 904
units.deva:
अस्मिन् समाधौ कुरुते प्रयासं
यस् तस्य नैवास्ति पुनर् विकल्पः।
सर्वात्म-भावोऽप्यमुनैव सिध्येत्
सर्वात्म-भावः खलु केवलत्वम्॥
units.translation: But if one should endeavour to practise concentration in the prescribed manner, none of the doubts can assail him. It is only in this way that one could attain sarvātma-bhava, and realize the unity of the Ātman which underlies all beings. To be aware of this oneness is indeed the culmination of spiritual realization.
units.iast:
asmin samādhau kurute prayāsaṃ
yas tasya naivāsti punar vikalpaḥ|
sarvātma-bhāvo’pyamunaiva sidhyet
sarvātma-bhāvaḥ khalu kevalatvam||

units.label: Verse 905
units.deva:
सर्वात्म-भावो विदुषो ब्रह्म-विद्या-फलं विदुः।
जीवन्-मुक्तस्य तस्यैव स्वानन्दानुभवः फलम्॥
units.translation: The knowledge of Brahman brings with it the realization of the unity of the Ātman that underlies all beings; so say the learned. One who has attained Brahman remains a jīvan-mukta, liberated in life, and such a person realizes as a result of it the bliss of the Ātman.
units.iast:
sarvātma-bhāvo viduṣo brahma-vidyā-phalaṃ viduḥ|
jīvan-muktasya tasyaiva svānandānubhavaḥ phalam||

units.label: Verse 906
units.deva:
योऽहं-ममेत्याद्यसद्-आत्म-गाहको
ग्रन्थिर् लयं याति स वासनामयः।
समाधिना नश्यति कर्म-बन्धो
ब्रह्मात्म-बोधोऽप्रतिबन्ध इष्यते॥
units.translation: It is in the stage of samādhi that all the knots of the heart are cut asunder. These so-called knots of the heart are only compact forms of desire, and are the nature of the ideas of ‘I and mine’. They are the sources of unreal knowledge. When they are cut asunder, one’s bondage of the past comes to an end. At the same time all the obstacles that lie in the path of the unity of the Ātman and Brahman come to to an end. ((ChanU.8.12.3) (Chāndogya Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
yo’haṃ-mametyādyasad-ātma-gāhako
granthir layaṃ yāti sa vāsanāmayaḥ|
samādhinā naśyati karma-bandho
brahmātma-bodho’pratibandha iṣyate||

units.label: Verse 907
units.deva:
एष निष्कण्टकः पन्था मुक्तेर् ब्रह्मात्मना स्थितेः।
शुद्धात्मनां मुमुक्षूणां यत् सद्-एकत्व-दर्शनम्॥
units.translation: Only that path by travelling along which one comes to realize that the Ātman is identical with Brahman, is free from the thorns of life. By no other path could the aspirant reach the goal, the realization of pure consciousness.
units.iast:
eṣa niṣkaṇṭakaḥ panthā mukter brahmātmanā sthiteḥ|
śuddhātmanāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ yat sad-ekatva-darśanam||

units.label: Verse 908
units.deva:
तस्मात् त्वं चाप्यप्रमत्तः समाधीन्
कृत्वा ग्रन्थिं साधु निर्दह्य युक्तः।
नित्यं ब्रह्मानन्द-पीयूष-सिन्धौ
मज्जन् क्रीडन् मोदमानो रमस्व॥
units.translation: Be thou ever more intent upon practising the deep concentration of samādhi. Burn up once for all the obstacles that are caused by delusion. Take your fill of delight in the bliss of the eternal which is the nectar of immortality.
units.iast:
tasmāt tvaṃ cāpyapramattaḥ samādhīn
kṛtvā granthiṃ sādhu nirdahya yuktaḥ|
nityaṃ brahmānanda-pīyūṣa-sindhau
majjan krīḍan modamāno ramasva||

units.label: Verse 909
units.deva:
निर्विकल्प-समाधिर् यो वृत्तिर् नैश्चल्य-लक्षणा।
तम् एव योग इत्याहुर् योग-शास्त्रार्थ-कोविदाः॥
units.translation: Yoga or union with Brahman It is only in the state of nirvikalpa samādhi that all the ripples of thought that arise in the mind are stilled and there reigns complete tranquility. Such is the state of yoga or union with Brahman, according to those who are well versed in the yoga śāstra. ((MunU.2.2.7) (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
nirvikalpa-samādhir yo vṛttir naiścalya-lakṣaṇā|
tam eva yoga ityāhur yoga-śāstrārtha-kovidāḥ||

units.label: Verses 910–912
units.deva:
अष्टावङ्गानि योगस्य यमो नियम आसनम्।
प्राणायामस् तथा प्रत्याहारश् चापि च धारणा॥
ध्यानं समाधिर् इत्येव निगदन्ति मनीषिणः।
सर्वं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञानाद् इन्द्रिय-ग्राम-संयमः॥
यमोऽयम् इति सम्प्रोक्तोऽभ्यसनीयो मुहुर् मुहुः।
सजातीय-प्रवाहश्च विजातीय-तिरस्-कृतिः॥
units.translation: The eight constituent aspects of yoga There are eight constituent aspects of yoga. They are respectively known as yama, niyama, āsana, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇa, dhyāna and samādhi. The wise say that the control of the senses that follows from the knowledge that all is Brahman… …That is indeed yama, or self-restraint and they say that this should be practised persistently. When the current of thought flows constantly in one direction, when it is seen that all are forms of the one Ātman, and when all other thoughts are excluded…
units.iast:
aṣṭāvaṅgāni yogasya yamo niyama āsanam|
prāṇāyāmas tathā pratyāhāraś cāpi ca dhāraṇā||
dhyānaṃ samādhir ityeva nigadanti manīṣiṇaḥ|
sarvaṃ brahmeti vijñānād indriya-grāma-saṃyamaḥ||
yamo’yam iti samprokto’bhyasanīyo muhur muhuḥ|
sajātīya-pravāhaśca vijātīya-tiras-kṛtiḥ||

units.label: Verses 913–914
units.deva:
नियमो हि परानन्दो नियमात् क्रियते बुधैः।
सुखेनैव भवेद् यस्मिन्न् अजस्रं ब्रह्म-चिन्तनम्॥
आसनं तद् विजानीयाद् इतरत् सुख-नाशनम्।
चित्तादि-सर्व-भावेषु ब्रह्मत्वेनैव भावनात्॥
units.translation: …That state is known as niyama. It is in this way that the learned derive supreme bliss. That state of mind in which there is a continuous stream of meditation upon Brahman is known as āsana, and it is this that leads to the destruction of all other pleasures.
units.iast:
niyamo hi parānando niyamāt kriyate budhaiḥ|
sukhenaiva bhaved yasminn ajasraṃ brahma-cintanam||
āsanaṃ tad vijānīyād itarat sukha-nāśanam|
cittādi-sarva-bhāveṣu brahmatvenaiva bhāvanāt||

units.label: Verse 915
units.deva:
निरोधः सर्व-वृत्तीनां प्राणायामः स उच्यते।
निषेधनं प्रपञ्चस्य रेचकाख्यः समीरणः॥
units.translation: When all the thoughts that arise in the mind are held under restraint by the one idea that all other factors such as the mind and the like are nothing but Brahman, that indeed is known as prāṇāyāma. In such prāṇāyāma, the negation of the universe is to be regarded as the equivalent of rechaka or the exhaling of the breath.
units.iast:
nirodhaḥ sarva-vṛttīnāṃ prāṇāyāmaḥ sa ucyate|
niṣedhanaṃ prapañcasya recakākhyaḥ samīraṇaḥ||

units.label: Verse 916
units.deva:
ब्रह्मैवास्मीति या वृत्तिः पूरको वायुर् ईरितः।
ततस् तद्-वृत्ति-नैश्चल्यं कुम्भकः प्राण-संयमः॥
units.translation: When the idea ‘I am Brahman’ permeates all the modifications of the mind it is the equivalent of pūraka or the inhaling of breath. When all the modifications of the mind are stilled, that is the state of kumbaka, or the equivalent of the retention of the breath.
units.iast:
brahmaivāsmīti yā vṛttiḥ pūrako vāyur īritaḥ|
tatas tad-vṛtti-naiścalyaṃ kumbhakaḥ prāṇa-saṃyamaḥ||

units.label: Verse 917
units.deva:
अयं चापि प्रबुद्धानाम् अज्ञानां प्राण-पीडनम्।
विषयेष्वात्मतां त्यक्त्वा मनसश् चिति मज्जनम्॥
units.translation: The enlightened make use of kumbaka in order to retain the vital force, whereas the ignorant merely inflict pain upon themselves by resorting to it. To withdraw the mind from all the objects of knowledge, and to cease to identify oneself with them by making the mind merge in pure consciousness…
units.iast:
ayaṃ cāpi prabuddhānām ajñānāṃ prāṇa-pīḍanam|
viṣayeṣvātmatāṃ tyaktvā manasaś citi majjanam||

units.label: Verse 918
units.deva:
प्रत्याहारः स विज्ञेयोऽभ्यसनीयो मुमुक्षुभिः।
यत्र यत्र मनो याति ब्रह्मणस् तत्र दर्शनात्॥
units.translation: …This is known as pratyāhāra. Every aspirant after liberation should diligently practise it. To hold the mind under restraint and to look upon all that the mind conceives as Brahman…
units.iast:
pratyāhāraḥ sa vijñeyo’bhyasanīyo mumukṣubhiḥ|
yatra yatra mano yāti brahmaṇas tatra darśanāt||

units.label: Verse 919
units.deva:
मनसो धारणं चैव धारणा सा परा मता।
ब्रह्मैवास्मीति सद्-वृत्त्या निरालम्बतया स्थितिः॥
units.translation: …Is to be deemed as the highest type of dhāraṇa. To remain in the highest stage of awareness, unsupported by any external agency, through which there runs the one idea, ‘I am Brahman’ which permeates the whole mind…
units.iast:
manaso dhāraṇaṃ caiva dhāraṇā sā parā matā|
brahmaivāsmīti sad-vṛttyā nirālambatayā sthitiḥ||

units.label: Verse 920
units.deva:
ध्यान-शब्देन विख्याता परमानन्द-दायिनी।
निर्विकारतया वृत्त्या ब्रह्माकारतया पुनः॥
units.translation: …Should be regarded as dhyāna, and this is known to all. Dhyāna is also the giver of the highest type of bliss. When all the modifications that take place in the mind have been completely effaced, and when the mind is filled with an unchanging awareness of the form of Brahman…
units.iast:
dhyāna-śabdena vikhyātā paramānanda-dāyinī|
nirvikāratayā vṛttyā brahmākāratayā punaḥ||

units.label: Verses 921–922
units.deva:
वृत्ति-विस्मरणं सम्यक् समाधिर् ध्यान-संज्ञिकः।
समाधौ क्रियमाणे तु विघ्ना ह्यायान्ति वै बलात्॥
अनुसन्धान-राहित्यम् आलस्यं भोग-लालसम्।
भयं तमश्च विक्षेपस् तेजः-स्पन्दश्च शून्यता॥
units.translation: …That indeed is the stage of samādhi, the fulfilment of meditation. As is well-known, there are many obstacles in the path of yoga. The lack of enquiry into the nature of Brahman, laziness, the desire for enjoyment, fear, ignorance, distraction, a sense of trembling felt all over the body, and a feeling of the void or śūnya, all these constitute some of the obstacles which intervene during the practice of yoga.
units.iast:
vṛtti-vismaraṇaṃ samyak samādhir dhyāna-saṃjñikaḥ|
samādhau kriyamāṇe tu vighnā hyāyānti vai balāt||
anusandhāna-rāhityam ālasyaṃ bhoga-lālasam|
bhayaṃ tamaśca vikṣepas tejaḥ-spandaśca śūnyatā||

units.label: Verse 923
units.deva:
एवं यद् विघ्न-बाहुल्यं त्याज्यं तद् ब्रह्मविज्-जनैः।
विघ्नान् एतान् परित्यज्य प्रमाद-रहितो वशी।
समाधि-निष्ठया ब्रह्म साक्षाद् भवितुम् अर्हसि॥
units.translation: Every aspirant after the knowledge of Brahman should overcome all these obstacles. He should avoid them by ceasing to be careless, by the restraint of the senses, and by the exclusive devotion to the practice of concentration in samādhi. In this way, may you become fit to be Brahman itself.
units.iast:
evaṃ yad vighna-bāhulyaṃ tyājyaṃ tad brahmavij-janaiḥ|
vighnān etān parityajya pramāda-rahito vaśī|
samādhi-niṣṭhayā brahma sākṣād bhavitum arhasi||

units.label: Verse 924
units.deva:
इति गुरु-वचनाच् छ्रुति-प्रमाणात्
परम् अवगम्य स्व-तत्त्वम् आत्म-युक्त्या।
प्रशमित-करणः समाहितात्मा क्वचिद्
अचलाकृतिर् आत्म-निष्ठितोऽभूत्॥
units.translation: The student’s direct experience gained by means of right knowledge With his senses made tranquil, with his mind controlled and body motionless, the disciple sat somewhere, and devoted himself exclusively to the pursuit of the Ātman. In the light of what the teacher said, and supported by the evidence of the Śruti he came to realize the supreme truth of the Ātman as himself.
units.iast:
iti guru-vacanāc chruti-pramāṇāt
param avagamya sva-tattvam ātma-yuktyā|
praśamita-karaṇaḥ samāhitātmā kvacid
acalākṛtir ātma-niṣṭhito’bhūt||

units.label: Verse 925
units.deva:
बहु-कालं समाधाय स्व-स्व-रूपे तु मानसम्।
उत्थाय परमानन्दाद् गुरुम् एत्य पुनर् मुदा॥
units.translation: After having spent a long time in such ecstasy, and after having attained self-realization, the disciple came down to the normal plane of consciousness. He approached his guru, radiant in ineffable bliss…
units.iast:
bahu-kālaṃ samādhāya sva-sva-rūpe tu mānasam|
utthāya paramānandād gurum etya punar mudā||

units.label: Verses 926–927
units.deva:
प्रमाण-पूर्वकं धीमान् सगद्गदम् उवाच ह।
नमो नमस् ते गुरवे नित्यानन्द-स्वरूपिणे॥
मुक्त-सङ्गाय शान्ताय त्यक्ताहन्ताय ते नमः।
दया-धाम्ने नमो भूम्ने महिम्नः पारम् अस्य ते।
नैवास्ति यत्-कटाक्षेण ब्रह्मैवाभवम् अद्वयम्॥
units.translation: And spoke to him thus in a voice chocked with emotion. “O Revered Sir, guided by you, I have known that which may be realized only by means of the Śruti. O my preceptor! you are the embodiment of bliss eternal. Deign to accept this, my salutation to you. To you who are devoid of all attachment, who are tranquil, who have transcended the ego-consciousness, and who are the abode of grace, I offer my salutation. Your glory envelops the world. There is nothing that is greater than that. One gracious look from you is enough to make me one with the non-dual Brahman.
units.iast:
pramāṇa-pūrvakaṃ dhīmān sagadgadam uvāca ha|
namo namas te gurave nityānanda-svarūpiṇe||
mukta-saṅgāya śāntāya tyaktāhantāya te namaḥ|
dayā-dhāmne namo bhūmne mahimnaḥ pāram asya te|
naivāsti yat-kaṭākṣeṇa brahmaivābhavam advayam||

units.label: Verse 928
units.deva:
किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि किं गृह्णामि त्यजामि किम्।
यन् मया पूरितं विश्वं महा-कल्पाम्बुना यथा॥
units.translation: What is there for me to do? Whither shall I go? What is there for me either to accept or to reject? I find that the whole universe is like an infinite expanse of water at the end of great cycles, and that is enveloped by the Ātman within me.
units.iast:
kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kiṃ gṛhṇāmi tyajāmi kim|
yan mayā pūritaṃ viśvaṃ mahā-kalpāmbunā yathā||

units.label: Verse 929
units.deva:
मयि सुख-बोध-पयो-धौ महति ब्रह्माण्ड-बुद्बुद-सहस्रम्।
मायामयेन मरुता भूत्वा भूत्वा पुनस् तिरोधत्ते॥
units.translation: In that ocean of immortality, in that sea of consciousness, mighty worlds rise and roll away due to Māyā, like the scudding foam drifting before the wind.
units.iast:
mayi sukha-bodha-payo-dhau mahati brahmāṇḍa-budbuda-sahasram|
māyāmayena marutā bhūtvā bhūtvā punas tirodhatte||

units.label: Verse 930
units.deva:
नित्यानन्द-स्वरूपोऽहम् आत्माहं त्वद्-अनुग्रहात्।
पूर्णोऽहम् अनवद्योऽहं केवलोऽहं च सद्-गुरो॥
units.translation: Thanks to the grace that has been bestowed by you, I have realized the Ātman. I have realized bliss eternal. I am the infinite, innermost Ātman, which is all-pervading, taintless and pure.
units.iast:
nityānanda-svarūpo’ham ātmāhaṃ tvad-anugrahāt|
pūrṇo’ham anavadyo’haṃ kevalo’haṃ ca sad-guro||

units.label: Verse 931
units.deva:
अकर्ताहम् अभोक्ताहम् अविकारोऽहम् अक्रियः।
आनन्द-घन एवाहम् असङ्गोऽहं सदा-शिवः॥
units.translation: I am neither the doer, nor the enjoyer of the fruits of action. I know no change, I am not the product of any kind of creative activity. I am compact of bliss. I am the Ātman, the one without a second, and the ever-auspicious.
units.iast:
akartāham abhoktāham avikāro’ham akriyaḥ|
ānanda-ghana evāham asaṅgo’haṃ sadā-śivaḥ||

units.label: Verse 932
units.deva:
त्वत्-कटाक्ष-वर-चान्द्र-चन्द्रिकापात-धूत-भवतापज-श्रमः।
प्राप्तवान् अहम् अखण्ड-वैभव-
आनन्दम् आत्म-पदम् अक्षयं क्षणात्॥
units.translation: Like a weary traveller tramping under the midday sun, I have been wandering through the cyclic changes of birth and death; and your benignant glance has been to me as refreshing as moonlight to the weary. I have attained in an instant the knowledge of the imperishable Ātman, and realized its inherent glory and bliss indivisible.
units.iast:
tvat-kaṭākṣa-vara-cāndra-candrikāpāta-dhūta-bhavatāpaja-śramaḥ|
prāptavān aham akhaṇḍa-vaibhava-
ānandam ātma-padam akṣayaṃ kṣaṇāt||

units.label: Verse 933
units.deva:
छायया स्पृष्टम् उष्णं वा शीतं वा दुष्ठु सुष्ठु वा।
न स्पृशत्येव यत्-किञ्चित् पुरुषं तद्-विलक्षणम्॥
units.translation: None of these things which are external, such as heat and cold, or good and bad, ever affect me; for, they are but reflex forms of pure consciousness, whereas the nature of the Ātman is altogether different from all of them.
units.iast:
chāyayā spṛṣṭam uṣṇaṃ vā śītaṃ vā duṣṭhu suṣṭhu vā|
na spṛśatyeva yat-kiñcit puruṣaṃ tad-vilakṣaṇam||

units.label: Verse 934
units.deva:
न साक्षिणं साक्ष्य-धर्मा न स्पृशन्ति विलक्षणम्।
अविकारम् उदासीनं गृह-धर्माः प्रदीपवत्॥
units.translation: I am one with that witnessing consciousness whose nature is not stained by what it perceives. It is like a lamp that throws its light indifferently on the diverse objects in a home, itself remaining unaffected by that which it illumines.
units.iast:
na sākṣiṇaṃ sākṣya-dharmā na spṛśanti vilakṣaṇam|
avikāram udāsīnaṃ gṛha-dharmāḥ pradīpavat||

units.label: Verse 935
units.deva:
रवेर् यथा कर्मणि साक्षि-भावो
वह्नेर् यथा वायसि दाहकत्वम्।
रज्जोर् यथारोपित-वस्तु-सङ्गस्
तथैव कूटस्थ-चिद्-आत्मनो मे॥
units.translation: Like unto the sun who is the sole witness of all that takes place under his light or like a red-hot ball of iron as it burns its way, although it is not the iron as such that burns, and like unto a rope which out of superimposition is mistaken to be something else, I am that pure consciousness which is untainted and which remains unchanged, although whatever is manifest is superimposed upon it.
units.iast:
raver yathā karmaṇi sākṣi-bhāvo
vahner yathā vāyasi dāhakatvam|
rajjor yathāropita-vastu-saṅgas
tathaiva kūṭastha-cid-ātmano me||

units.label: Verse 936
units.deva:
इत्युक्त्वा स गुरुं स्तुत्वा प्रश्रयेण कृतानतिः।
मुमुक्षोर् उपकाराय प्रष्टव्यांशम् अपृच्छत॥
units.translation: After having offered to the guru his need of praise as a token of his abounding grace, the disciple bowed low and offered his salutation to his master. He then requested his preceptor to enlighten him further on the various types of liberation, for the benefit of all spiritual aspirants.
units.iast:
ityuktvā sa guruṃ stutvā praśrayeṇa kṛtānatiḥ|
mumukṣor upakārāya praṣṭavyāṃśam apṛcchata||

units.label: Verse 937
units.deva:
जीवन्-मुक्तस्य भगवन्न् अनुभूतेश्च लक्षणम्।
विदेह-मुक्तस्य च मे कृपया ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः॥
units.translation: Be pleased to enlighten me, Revered Sir, and give me the right kind of knowledge as to the nature of the experience attained in jīvan-mukti, or liberation in life, and how it differs from videha-mukti or liberation that endures when the body has been shuffled off.
units.iast:
jīvan-muktasya bhagavann anubhūteśca lakṣaṇam|
videha-muktasya ca me kṛpayā brūhi tattvataḥ||

units.label: Verse 938
units.deva:
ज्ञान-भूमिका-लक्षणम्
वक्ष्ये तुभ्यं ज्ञान-भूमिकाया लक्षणम् आदितः।
ज्ञाते यस्मिंस् त्वया सर्वं ज्ञातं स्यात् पृष्टम् अद्य यत्॥
units.translation: The seven planes of the mind The spiritual guide says: At the outset, I shall define for you the various levels of consciousness, which lead ultimately to the right knowledge. By knowing it, whatever you have asked will also be known.
units.iast:
jñāna-bhūmikā-lakṣaṇam
vakṣye tubhyaṃ jñāna-bhūmikāyā lakṣaṇam āditaḥ|
jñāte yasmiṃs tvayā sarvaṃ jñātaṃ syāt pṛṣṭam adya yat||

units.label: Verse 939
units.deva:
ज्ञान-भूमिः शुभेच्छा स्यात् प्रथमा समुदीरिता।
विचारणा द्वितीया तु तृतीया तनु-मानसी॥
units.translation: The first step to right knowledge is the desire to know, and it is known as the good intention. The second step is reflection, and the third is the diminution of all attachment felt by the mind toward external objects.
units.iast:
jñāna-bhūmiḥ śubhecchā syāt prathamā samudīritā|
vicāraṇā dvitīyā tu tṛtīyā tanu-mānasī||

units.label: Verse 940
units.deva:
सत्त्वापत्तिश् चतुर्थी स्यात् ततोऽसंसक्ति-नामिका।
पदार्थाभावना षष्ठी सप्तमी तुर्यगा स्मृता॥
units.translation: The realization of sattva-guṇa is the fourth step. The next, the fifth, is non-attachment, and the sixth is the absence of the consciousness of all external objects. The seventh and the last step is that which leads to the stage of the turya, or the transcendent.
units.iast:
sattvāpattiś caturthī syāt tato’saṃsakti-nāmikā|
padārthābhāvanā ṣaṣṭhī saptamī turyagā smṛtā||

units.label: Verse 941
units.deva:
स्थितः किं मूढ एवास्मि प्रेक्ष्योऽहं शास्त्र-सज्जनैः।
वैराग्य-पूर्वम् इच्छेति शुभेच्छा चोच्यते बुधैः॥
units.translation: The good intention As soon as there is an awakening of vairāgya, one feels, ‘How ignorant I am, whereas the wise and good are well versed in the Śāstras’. That is the beginning of the desire to learn, and it is called the good intention.
units.iast:
sthitaḥ kiṃ mūḍha evāsmi prekṣyo’haṃ śāstra-sajjanaiḥ|
vairāgya-pūrvam iccheti śubhecchā cocyate budhaiḥ||

units.label: Verse 942
units.deva:
शास्त्र-सज्जन-सम्पर्क-वैराग्याभ्यास-पूर्वकम्।
सद्-आचार-प्रवृत्तिर् या प्रोच्यते सा विचारणा॥
units.translation: The stage of reflection When as a result of being dispassionate one tends to practise good conduct, resorts to holy company and studies the Śāstras, it constitutes the second step and it is known as the stage of reflection.
units.iast:
śāstra-sajjana-samparka-vairāgyābhyāsa-pūrvakam|
sad-ācāra-pravṛttir yā procyate sā vicāraṇā||

units.label: Verse 943
units.deva:
विचारणा-शुभेच्छाभ्याम् इन्द्रियार्थेषु रक्तता।
यत्र सा तनुताम् एति प्रोच्यते तनु-मानसी॥
units.translation: Diminished mental attachment That plane in which all attachment to external objects drop off, where sense pleasure diminishes, as a result of the ripening of good intention and reflection, is known as the plane of diminished mental attachment.
units.iast:
vicāraṇā-śubhecchābhyām indriyārtheṣu raktatā|
yatra sā tanutām eti procyate tanu-mānasī||

units.label: Verse 944
units.deva:
भूमिका-त्रितयाभ्यासाच् चित्तेऽर्थ-विरतेर् वशात्।
सत्त्वात्मनि स्थिते शुद्धे सत्त्वापत्तिर् उदाहृता॥
units.translation: The realization of sattva In the fourth plane the mind attains purity and turns away from all objects of desire. There arises a sense of indifference as a cumulative result of the virtues practised in the three earlier stages. The fourth stage is therefore known as the plane of the realization of sattva.
units.iast:
bhūmikā-tritayābhyāsāc citte’rtha-virater vaśāt|
sattvātmani sthite śuddhe sattvāpattir udāhṛtā||

units.label: Verse 945
units.deva:
दशा-चतुष्टयाभ्यासाद् असंसर्ग-फला तु या।
रूढ-सत्त्व-चमत्-कारा प्रोक्ता संसक्ति-नामिका॥
units.translation: The plane of non-attachment The fifth plane is that in which sattva is unusually predominant. This comes as a result of the virtues practised in the earlier stages, and it leads to vairāgya. It is known as the plane of non-attachment.
units.iast:
daśā-catuṣṭayābhyāsād asaṃsarga-phalā tu yā|
rūḍha-sattva-camat-kārā proktā saṃsakti-nāmikā||

units.label: Verse 946
units.deva:
भूमिका-पञ्चकाभ्यासात् स्वात्मारामतया भृशम्।
आभ्यन्तराणां बाह्यानां पदार्थानाम् अभावनात्॥
units.translation: The total absence of the consciousness of external objects The sixth is the plane of padārtha-abhāvanā. In that stage there is a total absence of the consciousness of external objects. This stage is arrived at when the earlier stages become perfected, and when one is so deeply absorbed in the bliss of the Ātman that one does not feel that there is anything either within or without.
units.iast:
bhūmikā-pañcakābhyāsāt svātmārāmatayā bhṛśam|
ābhyantarāṇāṃ bāhyānāṃ padārthānām abhāvanāt||

units.label: Verse 947
units.deva:
पर-प्रयुक्तेन चिर-प्रयत्नेनावबोधनम्।
पदार्थाभावना नाम षष्ठी भवति भूमिका॥
units.translation: When one is at that stage of consciousness, it is only as the result of prolonged effort on the part of others that one may be brought down, with great difficulty, to the normal plane of consciousness.
units.iast:
para-prayuktena cira-prayatnenāvabodhanam|
padārthābhāvanā nāma ṣaṣṭhī bhavati bhūmikā||

units.label: Verse 948
units.deva:
षड्-भूमिका-चिराभ्यासाद् भेदस्यानुपलम्भनात्।
यत् स्व-भावैक-निष्ठत्वं सा ज्ञेया तुर्य-गा गतिः॥
