units.translation: Establishing in one’s own ultimate nature In this way we come to the seventh plane in which one is finally established in one’s own ultimate nature. This stage is the resultant of sustained effort maintained through all the earlier stages. Here, all consciousness of difference is totally lost. This leads to turya, which transcends waking, dreaming and deep sleep.
units.iast:
ṣaḍ-bhūmikā-cirābhyāsād bhedasyānupalambhanāt|
yat sva-bhāvaika-niṣṭhatvaṃ sā jñeyā turya-gā gatiḥ||

units.label: Verse 949
units.deva:
इदं ममेति सर्वेषु दृश्य-भावेष्वभावना।
जाग्रज्-जाग्रद् इति प्राहुर् महान्तो ब्रह्मवित्तमाः॥
units.translation: The waking aspect of waking consciousness To the mahātmā, who is the best of the knowers of Brahman, all such ideas as ‘this’ or ‘mine’ do not arise; for there is a total absence of the consciousness of external objects. It is the waking aspect of waking consciousness.
units.iast:
idaṃ mameti sarveṣu dṛśya-bhāveṣvabhāvanā|
jāgraj-jāgrad iti prāhur mahānto brahmavittamāḥ||

units.label: Verse 950
units.deva:
विदित्वा सच्-चिद्-आनन्दे मयि दृश्य-परम्-पराम्।
नाम-रूप-परित्यागो जाग्रत्-स्वप्नः समीर्यते॥
units.translation: The dream aspect of waking consciousness When one rejects all name and form after coming to know that all objects of knowledge are but superimpositions upon one’s own Ātman, whose nature is existence-consciousness-bliss, that is the dream aspect of waking consciousness.
units.iast:
viditvā sac-cid-ānande mayi dṛśya-param-parām|
nāma-rūpa-parityāgo jāgrat-svapnaḥ samīryate||

units.label: Verse 951
units.deva:
परिपूर्ण-चिद्-आकाशे मयि बोधात्मतां विना।
न किञ्चिद् अन्यद् अस्तीति जाग्रत्-सुप्तिः समीर्यते॥
units.translation: The deep-sleep aspect of waking consciousness When one comes to know that nothing exists except pure consciousness, which permeates every thing as the paripūrṇa-cid-ākāśa as the all-permeating consciousness, infinite as space, that is the deep-sleep aspect of waking consciousness.
units.iast:
paripūrṇa-cid-ākāśe mayi bodhātmatāṃ vinā|
na kiñcid anyad astīti jāgrat-suptiḥ samīryate||

units.label: Verse 952
units.deva:
मूलाज्ञान-विनाशेन कारणाभास-चेष्टितैः।
बन्धो न मेऽतिस्वल्पोऽपि स्वप्न-जाग्रद् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: The waking aspect of dream consciousness With the destruction of mūlāvidyā or the primordial ignorance, one comes to know that all actions are but the product of causes that are unreal, and which are only apparent. At that stage, when one is no longer bound even to the slightest extent, it is to be regarded as the waking aspect of dream consciousness.
units.iast:
mūlājñāna-vināśena kāraṇābhāsa-ceṣṭitaiḥ|
bandho na me’tisvalpo’pi svapna-jāgrad itīryate||

units.label: Verse 953
units.deva:
कारणाज्ञान-नाशाद् यद् द्रष्टृ-दर्शन-दृश्यता।
न कार्यम् अस्ति तज् ज्ञानं स्वप्न-स्वप्नः समीर्यते॥
units.translation: The dream aspect of dream consciousness The distinction between the seer, the process of seeing and the seen is all due to ignorance. When ignorance is destroyed, knowledge destroys the effects of ignorance. That is the dream aspect of dream consciousness.
units.iast:
kāraṇājñāna-nāśād yad draṣṭṛ-darśana-dṛśyatā|
na kāryam asti taj jñānaṃ svapna-svapnaḥ samīryate||

units.label: Verse 954
units.deva:
अतिसूक्ष्म-विमर्शेन स्व-धी-वृत्तिर् अचञ्चला।
विलीयते यदा बोधे स्वप्न-सुप्तिर् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: The deep sleep aspect of dream consciousness When the intellect becomes calm and motionless, as a result of subtle reflection it becomes merged in pure consciousness, it is to be regarded as the deep sleep aspect of dream consciousness.
units.iast:
atisūkṣma-vimarśena sva-dhī-vṛttir acañcalā|
vilīyate yadā bodhe svapna-suptir itīryate||

units.label: Verse 955
units.deva:
चिन्मयाकार-मतयो धी-वृत्ति-प्रसरैर् गतः।
आनन्दानुभवो विद्वन् सुप्ति-जाग्रद् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: The waking aspect of deep sleep O Learned one, when as a result of the expanding of the mind the individual intellect becomes one with pure intelligence, the bliss of the Ātman is attained. The realization of that bliss is the waking aspect of deep sleep.
units.iast:
cinmayākāra-matayo dhī-vṛtti-prasarair gataḥ|
ānandānubhavo vidvan supti-jāgrad itīryate||

units.label: Verse 956
units.deva:
वृत्तौ चिरानुभूतान्तरानन्दानुभव-स्थितौ।
समात्मतां यो यात्येष सुप्ति-स्वप्न इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: The dream aspect of deep sleep When as a result of the prolonged experience of the bliss within, the mind ceases to function and all its modifications are no longer perceived, one comes to realize a state which is similar to that of the Ātman. That is to be regarded as the dream aspect of deep sleep.
units.iast:
vṛttau cirānubhūtāntarānandānubhava-sthitau|
samātmatāṃ yo yātyeṣa supti-svapna itīryate||

units.label: Verse 957
units.deva:
दृश्य-धी-वृत्तिर् एतस्य केवली-भाव-भावना।
परं बोधैकतावाप्तिः सुप्ति-सुप्तिर् इतीर्यते॥
units.translation: The deep sleep aspect of deep sleep When the object of knowledge, Brahman, whose nature is one of supremely pure consciousness, pervades the whole field of the intellect and all that takes place in it, there is nothing left except the concept of one-ness. That is the deep sleep aspect of deep sleep.
units.iast:
dṛśya-dhī-vṛttir etasya kevalī-bhāva-bhāvanā|
paraṃ bodhaikatāvāptiḥ supti-suptir itīryate||

units.label: Verse 958
units.deva:
पर-ब्रह्मवद् आभाति निर्विकारैक-रूपिणी।
सर्वावस्थासु धारैका तुर्याख्या परिकीर्तिता॥
units.translation: The fourth in relation to the other three When the modifications of the mind remain ever the same, and when the flow of awareness remains unchanged through all the levels of consciousness, and when it assumes one unchanging pattern, the pattern of the supreme Brahman, that is the turya or the transcendent. It is called the fourth in relation to the other three.
units.iast:
para-brahmavad ābhāti nirvikāraika-rūpiṇī|
sarvāvasthāsu dhāraikā turyākhyā parikīrtitā||

units.label: Verse 959
units.deva:
इत्यवस्था-समुल्लासं विमृशन् मुच्यते सुखी।
शुभेच्छादि-त्रयं भूमि-भेदाभेद-युतं स्मृतम्॥
units.translation: Those who become liberated by virtue of the splendour that animates the various stages of awareness are indeed happy. Beginning with the good intention in the first three of the seven steps in yoga, there is a sense of difference, as well as of non-difference. The first three steps of yoga may together be compared to the waking stage of consciousness. Just as people are aware of the sense of difference in the world, the yogī also has a proper knowledge of difference, though he is firmly convinced of non-difference.
units.iast:
ityavasthā-samullāsaṃ vimṛśan mucyate sukhī|
śubhecchādi-trayaṃ bhūmi-bhedābheda-yutaṃ smṛtam||

units.label: Verse 960
units.deva:
यथावद् भेद-बुद्ध्येदं जगज्-जाग्रद् इतीर्यते।
अद्वैते स्थैर्यम् आयाते द्वैते च प्रशमं गते॥
units.translation: Where there is an unshaken perception of the sense of one-ness and where all duality has come to an end, the yogī rises to the fourth plane of consciousness. It may be likened to the dream stage.
units.iast:
yathāvad bheda-buddhyedaṃ jagaj-jāgrad itīryate|
advaite sthairyam āyāte dvaite ca praśamaṃ gate||

units.label: Verse 961
units.deva:
पश्यन्ति स्वप्नवल् लोकं तुर्य-भूमि-सुयोगतः।
पञ्चमीं भूमिम् आरुह्य सुषुप्ति-पद-नामिकाम्॥
units.translation: When the yogī rises to the fifth plane of consciousness it is as though he has entered the stage of deep sleep. All the special traits of the yogī vanish, and he remains absorbed in non-duality.
units.iast:
paśyanti svapnaval lokaṃ turya-bhūmi-suyogataḥ|
pañcamīṃ bhūmim āruhya suṣupti-pada-nāmikām||

units.label: Verse 962
units.deva:
शान्ताशेष-विशेषांशस् तिष्ठेद् अद्वैत-मात्रके।
अन्तर्-मुखतया नित्यं षष्ठीं भूमिम् उपाश्रितः॥
units.translation: On rising to the sixth plane of consciousness the mind of the yogī is ever turned inward, and to all appearance it looks as though out of fatigue he has fallen into the stage of deep sleep.
units.iast:
śāntāśeṣa-viśeṣāṃśas tiṣṭhed advaita-mātrake|
antar-mukhatayā nityaṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ bhūmim upāśritaḥ||

units.label: Verse 963
units.deva:
परिश्रान्ततया गाढ-निद्रालुर् इव लक्ष्यते।
कुर्वन्न् अभ्यासम् एतस्यां भूम्यां सम्यग् विवासनः॥
units.translation: As a result of constant practice in the sixth place, the best among the yogīs becomes completely freed from all desires, and he gradually ascends to the seventh plane of consciousness. This is the turya or the transcendent.
units.iast:
pariśrāntatayā gāḍha-nidrālur iva lakṣyate|
kurvann abhyāsam etasyāṃ bhūmyāṃ samyag vivāsanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 964
units.deva: विदेह-मुक्तिर् एवात्र तुर्यातीत-दशोच्यते॥
units.translation: Videha-mukti Even beyond the state of turya is the state of videha-mukti.
units.iast: videha-muktir evātra turyātīta-daśocyate||

units.label: Verse 965
units.deva:
यत्र नासन् न सच् चापि नाहं नाप्यनहङ्-कृतिः।
केवलं क्षीण-मनन आस्तेऽद्वैतेऽतिनिर्भयः॥
units.translation: In that state there is neither existence nor non-existence. There is neither the ego nor the non-ego. The yogī then becomes totally devoid of fear, and rising free of all intellectual ideations, remains in absolute non-duality.
units.iast:
yatra nāsan na sac cāpi nāhaṃ nāpyanahaṅ-kṛtiḥ|
kevalaṃ kṣīṇa-manana āste’dvaite’tinirbhayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 966
units.deva:
अन्तः-शून्यो बहिः-शून्यः शून्य-कुम्भ इवाम्बरे।
अन्तः-पूर्णो बहिः-पूर्णः पूर्ण-कुम्भ इवार्णवे॥
units.translation: His state may be likened to that of an empty pot set in empty space, so that there is nothing but emptiness within and without; or to a full vessel set in the full ocean, so that there is nothing but fullness inside and out.
units.iast:
antaḥ-śūnyo bahiḥ-śūnyaḥ śūnya-kumbha ivāmbare|
antaḥ-pūrṇo bahiḥ-pūrṇaḥ pūrṇa-kumbha ivārṇave||

units.label: Verse 967
units.deva:
यथा-स्थितम् इदं सर्वं व्यवहारवतोऽपि च।
अस्तं गतं स्थितं व्योम स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: Although the jīvan-mukta is apparently engaged in the various activities of life as usual he is not affected by them. In his view the vast space around and the universe with it have ceased to be. Of such a person it is said that he is liberated in life.
units.iast:
yathā-sthitam idaṃ sarvaṃ vyavahāravato’pi ca|
astaṃ gataṃ sthitaṃ vyoma sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 968
units.deva:
नोदेति नास्तम् आयाति सुख-दुःखे मनः-प्रभा।
यथा-प्राप्त-स्थितिर् यस्य स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person in whose mind the feelings of pleasure and pain neither well up into a crest nor fall into a trough, and whose life is in harmony with circumstances, is indeed liberated in life.
units.iast:
nodeti nāstam āyāti sukha-duḥkhe manaḥ-prabhā|
yathā-prāpta-sthitir yasya sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 969
units.deva:
यो जागर्त्ति सुषुप्ति-स्थो यस्य जाग्रन् न विद्यते।
यस्य निर्वासनो बोधः स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person who is awake in the spirit, even when he is laid asleep in the flesh and who has no other waking state as such, and who is free from all residual desires, is indeed said to be liberated in life.
units.iast:
yo jāgartti suṣupti-stho yasya jāgran na vidyate|
yasya nirvāsano bodhaḥ sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 970
units.deva:
राग-द्वेष-भयादीनाम् अनुरूपं चरन्न् अपि।
योऽन्तर् व्योमवद् अत्यच्छः स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person whose heart is as pure as space, even though his actions seem to be in conformity (like us) with the ordinary feelings of likes and dislikes, as well as, of fear and the like, is indeed liberated in life.
units.iast:
rāga-dveṣa-bhayādīnām anurūpaṃ carann api|
yo’ntar vyomavad atyacchaḥ sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 971
units.deva:
यस्य नाहङ्-कृतो भावो बुद्धिर् यस्य न लिप्यते।
कुर्वतोऽकुर्वतो वापि स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person whose mind is free from egoism, and from attachment, whether (like us) at work or at rest, is said to be liberated in life.
units.iast:
yasya nāhaṅ-kṛto bhāvo buddhir yasya na lipyate|
kurvato’kurvato vāpi sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 972
units.deva:
यः समस्तार्थ-जालेषु व्यवहार्यपि शीतलः।
परार्थेष्विव पूर्णात्मा स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person whose nature is as all-pervading as Brahman, and who even though (like us) he is engaged in the various activities of life remains free of all attachment as though they were the affairs of other people, is indeed liberated in life.
units.iast:
yaḥ samastārtha-jāleṣu vyavahāryapi śītalaḥ|
parārtheṣviva pūrṇātmā sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 973
units.deva:
द्वैत-वर्जित-चिन्-मात्रे पदे परम-पावने।
अक्षुब्ध-चित्त-विश्रान्तः स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person who is endowed with an unperturbed mind, and who is at ease, after having attained the goal, Brahman, who is the greatest of purifiers, and who finds peace in the pure consciousness which is devoid of all duality, is indeed liberated in life.
units.iast:
dvaita-varjita-cin-mātre pade parama-pāvane|
akṣubdha-citta-viśrāntaḥ sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 974
units.deva:
इदं जगद् अयं सोऽयं दृश्य-जातम् अवास्तवम्।
यस्य चित्ते न स्फुरति स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person in whose mind all concepts such as ‘this world’ or ‘this person’, or ‘he is such’ have completely vanished, for they relate to unreal objects, is indeed said to be liberated in life.
units.iast:
idaṃ jagad ayaṃ so’yaṃ dṛśya-jātam avāstavam|
yasya citte na sphurati sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 975
units.deva:
चिद्-आत्माहं परात्माहं निर्गुणोऽहं परात् परः।
आत्म-मात्रेण यस् तिष्ठेत् स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person who lives as the pure Ātman, and who knows ‘I am the Ātman, whose nature is pure consciousness’, ‘I am the supreme Ātman’ and ‘I am superior to the superiors’, is said to be liberated in life.
units.iast:
cid-ātmāhaṃ parātmāhaṃ nirguṇo’haṃ parāt paraḥ|
ātma-mātreṇa yas tiṣṭhet sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 976
units.deva:
देह-त्रयातिरिक्तोऽहं शुद्ध-चैतन्यम् अस्म्यहम्।
ब्रह्माहम् इति यस्यान्तः स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person who knows at heart ‘I am beyond the three bodies – the gross, the subtle and the causal’ – and who knows ‘I am pure consciousness; I am Brahman’ is indeed said to be liberated in life.
units.iast:
deha-trayātirikto’haṃ śuddha-caitanyam asmyaham|
brahmāham iti yasyāntaḥ sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 977
units.deva:
यस्य देहादिकं नास्ति यस्य ब्रह्मेति निश्चयः।
परमानन्द-पूर्णो यः स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person who is devoid of the consciousness of body or the mind, and who has the firm conviction that all this is Brahman, and who is full of Supreme Bliss, is said to be liberated in life.
units.iast:
yasya dehādikaṃ nāsti yasya brahmeti niścayaḥ|
paramānanda-pūrṇo yaḥ sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 978
units.deva:
अहं ब्रह्मास्म्यहं ब्रह्मास्म्यहं ब्रह्मेति निश्चयः।
चिद् अहं चिद् अहं चेति स जीवन्-मुक्त उच्यते॥
units.translation: That person who is firmly convinced, ‘I am Brahman, and nothing else; I am pure consciousness, and nothing else’ is indeed liberated in life.
units.iast:
ahaṃ brahmāsmyahaṃ brahmāsmyahaṃ brahmeti niścayaḥ|
cid ahaṃ cid ahaṃ ceti sa jīvan-mukta ucyate||

units.label: Verse 979
units.deva:
जीवन्-मुक्ति-पदं त्यक्त्वा स्व-देहे कालसात्कृते।
विशत्यदेह-मुक्तित्वं पवनोऽस्पन्दताम् इव॥
units.translation: In the course of time, when the person who has attained liberation in life gives up his physical body, he enters videha-mukti, and is devoid of the consciousness of the body. His state may be compared to the wind becoming calm.
units.iast:
jīvan-mukti-padaṃ tyaktvā sva-dehe kālasātkṛte|
viśatyadeha-muktitvaṃ pavano’spandatām iva||

units.label: Verse 980
units.deva:
ततस् तत् सम्बभूवासौ यद् गिराम् अप्यगोचरम्।
यच् छून्य-वादिनां शून्यं ब्रह्म ब्रह्म-विदां च यत्॥
units.translation: One then enters that state which is beyond thought and expression. It is referred to as the void by those who believe in the void, and as Brahman by the knowers of Brahman.
units.iast:
tatas tat sambabhūvāsau yad girām apyagocaram|
yac chūnya-vādināṃ śūnyaṃ brahma brahma-vidāṃ ca yat||

units.label: Verse 981
units.deva:
विज्ञानं विज्ञान-विदां मलानां च मलात्मकम्।
पुरुषः साङ्ख्य-दृष्टीनाम् ईश्वरो योग-वादिनाम्॥
units.translation: It is knowledge, for the upholders of the doctrine of knowledge, is dirt no bigger than the body for some Jaina mendicants, it is the Puruṣa for the Sāṅkhya school and it is Īśvara, for the followers of Yoga doctrine.
units.iast:
vijñānaṃ vijñāna-vidāṃ malānāṃ ca malātmakam|
puruṣaḥ sāṅkhya-dṛṣṭīnām īśvaro yoga-vādinām||

units.label: Verse 982
units.deva:
शिवः शैवागम-स्थानां कालः कालैक-वादिनाम्।
यत् सर्व-शास्त्र-सिद्धान्तं यत् सर्व-हृदयानुगम्।
यत् सर्वं सर्वगं वस्तु तत् तत्त्वं तद् असौ स्थितः॥
units.translation: It is Śiva for the followers of Śaiva āgama. It is Kāla or time for the astrologers who consider time to be supreme. But all the Śāstras agree upon this that it is the Supreme Truth, which enters the heart of all, is in all and all pervading. It is that Supreme Reality that the liberated one is established.
units.iast:
śivaḥ śaivāgama-sthānāṃ kālaḥ kālaika-vādinām|
yat sarva-śāstra-siddhāntaṃ yat sarva-hṛdayānugam|
yat sarvaṃ sarvagaṃ vastu tat tattvaṃ tad asau sthitaḥ||

units.label: Verse 983
units.deva:
ब्रह्मैवाहं चिद् एवाहम् एवं वापि न चिन्त्यते।
चिन्-मात्रेणेव यस् तिष्ठेद् विदेहो मुक्त एव सः॥
units.translation: One who is free from such thoughts as ‘I am Brahman’ and ‘I am knowledge alone’ is established in pure consciousness only and is undoubtedly liberated in life.
units.iast:
brahmaivāhaṃ cid evāham evaṃ vāpi na cintyate|
cin-mātreṇeva yas tiṣṭhed videho mukta eva saḥ||

units.label: Verse 984
units.deva:
यस्य प्रपञ्च-भानं न ब्रह्माकारम् अपीह न।
अतीतातीत-भावो यो विदेहो मुक्त एव सः॥
units.translation: One who has gone beyond the reach of the mind, to whom the world does not exist, to whom Brahman is not an object of knowledge, and who has cast off all the vāsanās or past impressions is liberated, and is undoubtedly free from body consciousness.
units.iast:
yasya prapañca-bhānaṃ na brahmākāram apīha na|
atītātīta-bhāvo yo videho mukta eva saḥ||

units.label: Verse 985
units.deva:
चित्त-वृत्तेर् अतीतो यश् चित्त-वृत्त्यावभासकः।
चित्त-वृत्ति-विहीनो यो विदेहो मुक्त एव सः॥
units.translation: One who has gone even beyond the reach of thought, to whom the reflex ideas that thought presents are no longer valid, and who has gained knowledge by direct intuition is indeed liberated, and is free from the consciousness of the body.
units.iast:
citta-vṛtter atīto yaś citta-vṛttyāvabhāsakaḥ|
citta-vṛtti-vihīno yo videho mukta eva saḥ||

units.label: Verse 986
units.deva:
जीवात्मेति परात्मेति सर्व-चिन्ता-विवर्जितः।
सर्व-सङ्कल्प-हीनात्मा विदेहो मुक्त एव सः॥
units.translation: One who no longer thinks of the individual, the jīvātman as distinct from the Supreme, the Paramātman and who has lost in the consciousness of the Ātman all saṅkalpas or mental resolves, such a one is indeed liberated and is free of the consciousness of the body.
units.iast:
jīvātmeti parātmeti sarva-cintā-vivarjitaḥ|
sarva-saṅkalpa-hīnātmā videho mukta eva saḥ||

units.label: Verse 987
units.deva:
ओङ्कार-वाच्य-हीनात्मा सर्व-वाच्य-विवर्जितः।
अवस्था-त्रय-हीनात्मा विदेहो मुक्त एव सः॥
units.translation: One who has transcended the three levels of consciousness, who has gone beyond all that is connoted by means of words, and who has gone even beyond what is indicated directly by the sacred symbol ‘Om’ is indeed liberated, and is free of the consciousness of the body.
units.iast:
oṅkāra-vācya-hīnātmā sarva-vācya-vivarjitaḥ|
avasthā-traya-hīnātmā videho mukta eva saḥ||

units.label: Verse 988
units.deva:
अहि-निर्ल्वयनी-सर्प-निर्मोको जीव-वर्जितः।
वल्मीके पतितस् तिष्ठेत् तं सर्पो नाभिमन्यते॥
units.translation: Just as a snake does not regard as its own the slough which it has cast off, and which lies mouldering on an ant-hill, so also the liberated one does not identify himself with either the gross body of the subtle body. ((BrhUEng.4.4.7) (Bṛhad-Āraṇyaka Upaniṣad))
units.iast:
ahi-nirlvayanī-sarpa-nirmoko jīva-varjitaḥ|
valmīke patitas tiṣṭhet taṃ sarpo nābhimanyate||

units.label: Verse 989
units.deva:
एवं स्थूलं च सूक्ष्मं च शरीरं नाभिमन्यते।
प्रत्यग्-ज्ञान-शिखि-ध्वस्ते मिथ्या-ज्ञाने सहेतुके॥
units.translation: All false ideas have become burnt up in the fire of knowledge. What remains is pure consciousness alone, and the Śruti points it out by the expression ‘Not Such; Nor such’.
units.iast:
evaṃ sthūlaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ ca śarīraṃ nābhimanyate|
pratyag-jñāna-śikhi-dhvaste mithyā-jñāne sahetuke||

units.label: Verse 990
units.deva:
नेति नेतीत्यरूपत्वाद् अशरीरो भवत्ययम्।
विश्वश्च तैजसश्चैव प्राज्ञश्चेति च ते त्रयम्॥
units.translation: The Ātman has neither form nor shape. To know that and to identify oneself with the Ātman is to go beyond the state of an embodied being. Thus the attributes of Viśva, Taijasa, and Prājña, along with their adjuncts drop off.
units.iast:
neti netītyarūpatvād aśarīro bhavatyayam|
viśvaśca taijasaścaiva prājñaśceti ca te trayam||

units.label: Verse 991
units.deva:
विराड् हिरण्य-गर्भश्च ईश्वरश्चेति ते त्रयम्।
ब्रह्माण्डं चैव पिण्डाण्डं लोका भूर्-आदयः क्रमात्॥
units.translation: The knower of the Ātman goes beyond the concepts of Virāṭ, Hiraṇya-garbha and Īśvara, for they too are aspects of the Ātman when taken along with the adjuncts only. To the knower of the Ātman the whole world and its adjuncts merge in the Ātman.
units.iast:
virāḍ hiraṇya-garbhaśca īśvaraśceti te trayam|
brahmāṇḍaṃ caiva piṇḍāṇḍaṃ lokā bhūr-ādayaḥ kramāt||

units.label: Verse 992
units.deva:
स्व-स्वोपाधि-लयाद् एव लीयन्ते प्रत्यग्-आत्मनि।
तूष्णीम् एव ततस् तूष्णीं तूष्णीं सत्यं न किञ्चन॥
units.translation: In this way, when the adjuncts of the Piṇḍāṇḍa and the Brahmāṇḍa, the microcosm and the macrocosm, merge in the Ātman; all that remains is a grand silence. That silence alone is real; and there is nothing else so real as that.
units.iast:
sva-svopādhi-layād eva līyante pratyag-ātmani|
tūṣṇīm eva tatas tūṣṇīṃ tūṣṇīṃ satyaṃ na kiñcana||

units.label: Verse 993
units.deva:
काल-भेदो वस्तु-भेदो देश-भेदः स्व-भेदकः।
किञ्चिद्-भेदो न तस्यास्ति किञ्चिद् वापि न विद्यते॥
units.translation: All distinctions of time, space, and the nature of things have ceased. Similarly all the distinctions within oneself have also ceased. Where there are no distinctions at all, in reality, there are none to be perceived.
units.iast:
kāla-bhedo vastu-bhedo deśa-bhedaḥ sva-bhedakaḥ|
kiñcid-bhedo na tasyāsti kiñcid vāpi na vidyate||

units.label: Verse 994
units.deva:
जीवेश्वरेति-वाक्ये च वेद-शास्त्रेष्वहं त्विति।
इदं चैतन्यम् एवेत्यहं चैतन्यम् इत्यपि॥
units.translation: It is true that the Śruti speaks of the Jīva and the Īśvara, but the knower of Brahman goes beyond what is indicated by the mere words of the Śruti. To him even the idea ‘I am the pure consciousness’, ‘The pure consciousness is myself’ does not arise.
units.iast:
jīveśvareti-vākye ca veda-śāstreṣvahaṃ tviti|
idaṃ caitanyam evetyahaṃ caitanyam ityapi||

units.label: Verse 995
units.deva:
इति निश्चय-शून्यो यो विदेहो मुक्त एव सः।
ब्रह्मैव विद्यते साक्षाद् वस्तुतोऽवस्तुतोऽपि च॥
units.translation: When the ‘I’ consciousness does not at all arise, the liberated one is undoubtedly devoid of body consciousness. Such a one exists as Brahman, and also otherwise.
units.iast:
iti niścaya-śūnyo yo videho mukta eva saḥ|
brahmaiva vidyate sākṣād vastuto’vastuto’pi ca||

units.label: Verse 996
units.deva:
तद् विद्या-विषयं ब्रह्म सत्य-ज्ञान-सुखात्मकम्।
शान्तं च तद्-अतीतं च परं ब्रह्म तद् उच्यते॥
units.translation: Brahman is an object of knowledge when Brahman is endowed with the attributes of existence-knowledge-bliss. But the Supreme Brahman is not an object of knowledge, and transcends knowledge. ((TaitU.2.1.1) (English Upaniṣad – Taittiriya))
units.iast:
tad vidyā-viṣayaṃ brahma satya-jñāna-sukhātmakam|
śāntaṃ ca tad-atītaṃ ca paraṃ brahma tad ucyate||

units.label: Verse 997
units.deva:
सिद्धान्तोऽध्यात्म-शास्त्राणां सर्वापह्नव एव हि।
नाविद्यास्तीह नो माया शान्तं ब्रह्मैव तद्-विना॥
units.translation: The siddhānta or the sifted truth in relation to the Adhyātma Śāstra, the knowledge relating to the Ātman, is that Brahman is not an object of knowledge. Consequently, avidyā and Māyā, which are also objects of knowledge have no being. All that is, is the supreme tranquil Brahman.
units.iast:
siddhānto’dhyātma-śāstrāṇāṃ sarvāpahnava eva hi|
nāvidyāstīha no māyā śāntaṃ brahmaiva tad-vinā||

units.label: Verse 998
units.deva:
प्रियेषु स्वेषु सुकृतम् अप्रियेषु च दुष्कृतम्।
विसृज्य ध्यान-योगेन ब्रह्माप्येति सनातनम्॥
units.translation: The knower of Brahman thus leaves a legacy of good deeds to those who befriend him, while his evil deeds go to those who think ill. After having realized the eternal Brahman, he becomes one with Brahman in profound meditation. ((BrSEng.3.2.26) (Brahma Sūtras Eng.))
units.iast:
priyeṣu sveṣu sukṛtam apriyeṣu ca duṣkṛtam|
visṛjya dhyāna-yogena brahmāpyeti sanātanam||

units.label: Verse 999
units.deva:
यावद् यावच् च सद्-बुद्धे स्वयं सन्त्यज्यतेऽखिलम्।
तावत् तावत् परानन्दः परमात्मैव शिष्यते॥
units.translation: O wise one! know that it is by giving up all that which is unreal, that one attains what is real. In this way, one realizes the Supreme Being, and attains the Supreme Bliss. That is what is left over, that is the residual value.
units.iast:
yāvad yāvac ca sad-buddhe svayaṃ santyajyate’khilam|
tāvat tāvat parānandaḥ paramātmaiva śiṣyate||

units.label: Verse 1000
units.deva:
यत्र यत्र मृतो ज्ञानी परमाक्षरवित् सदा।
परे ब्रह्मणि लीयेत न तस्योत्क्रान्तिर् इष्यते॥
units.translation: At whatever place the knower of the Supreme Brahman may cast off his body, he invariably merges in Brahman. To him there is no going, and no return, in order to assume a fresh body. ((BrSEng.4.1.14) (Brahma Sūtras Eng.))
units.iast:
yatra yatra mṛto jñānī paramākṣaravit sadā|
pare brahmaṇi līyeta na tasyotkrāntir iṣyate||

units.label: Verse 1001
units.deva:
यद् यत् स्वाभिमतं वस्तु तत् त्यजन् मोक्षम् अश्नुते।
असङ्कल्पेन शस्त्रेण छिन्नं चित्तम् इदं यदा॥
units.translation: By giving up all things that are held dear one attains liberation. Desirelessness is therefore the greatest weapon.
units.iast:
yad yat svābhimataṃ vastu tat tyajan mokṣam aśnute|
asaṅkalpena śastreṇa chinnaṃ cittam idaṃ yadā||

units.label: Verse 1002
units.deva:
सर्वं सर्वगतं शान्तं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते तदा।
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर् वाक्यं शिष्यस् तु छिन्न-संशयः॥
units.translation: It is with that weapon that one cuts asunder all the knots of the heart. One then realizes Brahman, all in all, all-pervading, and tranquil.
units.iast:
sarvaṃ sarvagataṃ śāntaṃ brahma sampadyate tadā|
iti śrutvā guror vākyaṃ śiṣyas tu chinna-saṃśayaḥ||

units.label: Verse 1003
units.deva:
ज्ञात-ज्ञेयः सम्प्रणम्य सद्गुरोश् चरणाम्बुजम्।
स तेन समनुज्ञातो ययौ निर्मुक्त-बन्धनः॥
units.translation: After having heard all that the Guru had to say, the disciple came to know what he should do. All his doubts were dispelled. He had become free of bondage. He prostrated himself at the lotus feet of the good preceptor. With his permission, he took leave of him.
units.iast:
jñāta-jñeyaḥ sampraṇamya sadguroś caraṇāmbujam|
sa tena samanujñāto yayau nirmukta-bandhanaḥ||

units.label: Verse 1004
units.deva:
गुरुर् एष सदानन्द-सिन्धौ निर्मग्न-मानसः।
पावयन् वसुधां सर्वां विचचार निरुत्तरः॥
units.translation: As for the Guru, he whose mind was steeped in the bliss of the divine consciousness, he too left the place, in order to roam over the Earth and purity it by his silence.
units.iast:
gurur eṣa sadānanda-sindhau nirmagna-mānasaḥ|
pāvayan vasudhāṃ sarvāṃ vicacāra niruttaraḥ||

units.label: Verse 1005
units.deva:
इत्याचार्यस्य शिष्यस्य संवादेनात्म-लक्षणम्।
निरूपितं मुमुक्षूणां सुख-बोधोपपत्तये॥
units.translation: In this discourse between the Guru and the disciple the real nature of the Ātman has been brought out. It has been set down in order that it might be easily understood by other aspirants after liberation.
units.iast:
ityācāryasya śiṣyasya saṃvādenātma-lakṣaṇam|
nirūpitaṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ sukha-bodhopapattaye||

units.label: Verse 1006
units.deva:
सर्व-वेदान्त-सिद्धान्त-सार-सङ्ग्रह-नामकः।
ग्रन्थोऽयं हृदय-ग्रन्थि-विच्छित्त्यै रचितः सताम्॥
units.translation: This work entitled ‘The Quintessence of Vedānta’ has been specially composed in order that it might help other aspirants after wisdom in dispelling the doubts that might arise in their hearts.
units.iast:
sarva-vedānta-siddhānta-sāra-saṅgraha-nāmakaḥ|
grantho’yaṃ hṛdaya-granthi-vicchittyai racitaḥ satām||
